Note the unusual shape of this edge, which the stele states openly: Farong awakened by himself (得自然智慧) and Daoxin came to ratify it. 「汝能總持，吾亦隨喜」 — 'you are able to uphold it all; I too rejoice.' 「由是無上覺路，分為此宗」 — 'and from this the unsurpassed road to awakening divided into this school.' This is the Oxhead school's founding charter and it is on stone.

teacher.quote: 道信聞之，往付所受僧璨之頓教法門。
teacher.note: DILA cites 景德傳燈錄 T51n2076_p0223b14. Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 顯慶二年閏正月二十三日，終於建初，春秋六十四。(T50n2060_p0604a21)
dates.note: Death 657-03-16; birth 594 back-computed from age 64. 續高僧傳 (T2060) is a near-contemporary source.

school.note: sect field: 牛頭宗

bio.note: Drawn from 續高僧傳 T2060, 佛光大辭典 3427, 疑年錄 97.

notes: Founder of the Niutou (Oxhead) school. Studied under the Fourth Patriarch Daoxin but developed a distinct teaching emphasizing emptiness.

bio: A prince of the Silla royal house (surname Kim 金). He was ordained at Gunnam monastery in Silla, then sailed to Tang China in 728 with a Silla embassy and settled in Sichuan, where he received the dharma from Chuji of Zizhou (a disciple of Zhishen). He taught at Jingzhong monastery in Chengdu, holding assemblies each twelfth and first month at which he first led invocation of the Buddha's name and then preached his three phrases — 'no recollection, no thought, do not forget' (無憶、無念、莫忘). The Jingzhong school takes its name from his line. In the fifth month of 762 he handed the robe of faith to Wuzhu and died on the nineteenth, aged 79.

teacher.kind: 歷代法寶記 (c. 774 — roughly 12 years after Wuxiang's death, written inside his own lineage)
teacher.quote: (開元二)十年四月，密遣家人王鍠喚海東無相禪師，付囑法及信袈裟云：「此衣是達摩祖師衣，則天賜詵和上，和上與吾，吾轉付汝。善自保愛，覓好山住去。」後至其年五月二十七日，告諸門徒：「吾不久住。」至夜半子時，奄然坐化。處寂大師時年六十八。
teacher.note: The deathbed transmission, told a dozen years after the fact by the school descended from it. The verb is 付囑 — entrustment — and it comes with the physical token (the robe) and its whole chain recited aloud: Bodhidharma → (via Empress Wu) 智詵 → 處寂 → 無相. 處寂 dies weeks later. This is not a lamp; it is the closest thing the Jingzhong school has to a stele.

teacher.kind: 歷代法寶記 — 無住's own answer, naming his own teacher
teacher.quote: 又問和上：「善知識是誰？」和上答：「是無相和上，俗姓金，時人號金和上也。」
teacher.note: Corroborates 無相's identity and standing as a living 善知識 in the same source.

teacher.quote: 《聯燈會要》卷1：「益州無相禪師法嗣一人(師見資州處寂)」(X79n1557_p0001c18)
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

teacher.kind: lineage chart in a modern study
teacher.quote: 智詵──處寂──┬無相──┬淨眾神會
teacher.note: Zhishen → Chuji → Wuxiang → Jingzhong Shenhui.

dates.quote: 寶應元年（762）五月，將信衣付囑予無住，十九日坐化，世壽七十九。
dates.note: Birth 684 back-computed from age 79.

school.note: The roster's 'Chan' is too coarse — DILA assigns him to the Jingzhong school specifically.

bio.quote: 唐益州無相大師亦新羅人。傳黃梅宗
bio.note: The Korean history confirms his Silla origin.

notes: Korean prince of the Silla royal house who became one of the most influential Chan teachers in eighth-century Sichuan. Ordained under Zizhou Chuji (a disciple of Zhishen in the Hongren/East Mountain line), he built a massive congregation in Chengdu around his 'three phrases' (wunian, moyi, mowang) teaching of no-thought, no-recollection, and no-delusion. His liturgical innovations blending Chan with Vinaya confession rites shaped a distinct Sichuan Chan tradition. Buswell (1989) argues he was an early formative influence on the young Mazu Daoyi before Mazu's move east. His legacy was continued by Baotang Wuzhu, though the Baotang school radicalized his teachings. Attested in Lidai fabao ji (c. 774) and Zutangji (952): both record his teaching career in Sichuan, his royal Silla origins, and his three-phrase doctrine.

bio: Lay surname Liao (廖), of Qianhua. He left home at eight and took full precepts at twenty-five, then met Mazu Daoyi at Jianyang and received his mind-seal and robe. After Mazu's death he opened the hall at the assembly's request in 791 and later taught at Xitang in Qianzhou. With Baizhang Huaihai and Nanquan Puyuan he was reckoned one of the three great disciples of Mazu. His heirs included the Silla monks Doui, Bonyeo, Hongcheok and Hyecheol, and through them his teaching became the dominant Chan style in Silla Korea. He died in 814, aged 80.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳, 贊寧, imperially commissioned 988 — appended to the 道一傳
teacher.quote: 又唐虔州西堂釋智藏，姓廖氏，虔化人也…隨大寂移居龔公山，後謁徑山國一禪師…屬元戎路嗣恭請大寂居府，藏乃迴郡，得大寂付授納袈裟…元和九年四月八日終，春秋八十，夏臘五十五。即遷于塔，諫議大夫韋綬追問藏言行，編入《圖經》。太守李渤請旌表，至長慶元年諡大覺禪師云。
teacher.note: 得大寂付授納袈裟 — he received the robe HANDED OVER by Daji (Mazu's posthumous title). 付授 is the transmission verb. CAVEAT, stated honestly: 宋高僧傳 is 988, ~174 years after Zhizang's death, so it is not literally a contemporary. But it is not a lamp either — it is an imperially commissioned biography, it PREDATES 景德傳燈錄 (1004), and it names its own documentary chain: 韋綬 interrogated those who knew him and entered his words and deeds into the 圖經, and prefect 李渤 petitioned for the posthumous honour. Graded B on that basis, not A.

teacher.quote: 於建陽參禮馬祖，受心印及袈裟。
teacher.note: DILA cites 景德傳燈錄 T51n2076_p0251b12. Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 元和九年四月八日終。春秋八十。夏臘五十五。(T50n2061_p0766c15)
dates.note: 宋高僧傳. Death 814-05-05; birth 735 back-computed.

bio.note: From 祖堂集 280, 宋高僧傳, 佛光 5036.

notes: One of Mazu's three great disciples alongside Baizhang and Nanquan.

bio: Lay surname Han (韓); abbot of Dayun monastery in Suizhou. In 807 the young Zongmi, travelling to the capital to sit the examinations, passed through Suizhou, heard Daoyuan preach, and left home under him, receiving full precepts from him. Daoyuan then sent Zongmi on to Nanyin of Yizhou and to Shenzhao of Baoguo monastery in Luoyang, and in the end transmitted the dharma to him. He is the fourth generation of the Heze line and the direct teacher of Guifeng Zongmi.

teacher.kind: 圓覺經略疏鈔, written by 宗密 (Guifeng Zongmi, 780–841) — 道圓's OWN dharma-heir, writing while 道圓 was still alive
teacher.quote: 且如第七祖門下，傳法二十二人，且敘一枝者。礠洲法觀寺智如和尚，俗姓王。礠洲門下成都府聖壽寺唯忠和尚，俗姓張，亦号南印。聖壽門下遂洲大雲寺道圓和尚，俗姓程。長慶二年，成都道俗迎歸聖壽寺，紹繼先師，大昌法化，如今現在。
teacher.note: As close to first-person as a teacher-edge can get without being the man himself: written by his own heir, IN HIS TEACHER'S LIFETIME (「如今現在」 — he is alive as I write). The chain is explicit and each link uses 門下: 神會 (7th patriarch) → 磁州智如 → 成都聖壽唯忠 → 遂州大雲寺道圓. Zongmi's own account, not a lamp compiler's.

teacher.quote: 裴休《華嚴原人論序》中作「荊州張」，稱南印為圭峯師祖。
teacher.note: SUPPORTS the existing roster. Pei Xiu was Zongmi's own patron and contemporary; calling Nanyin 'Guifeng's grandfather-in-dharma' places Nanyin → Daoyuan → Zongmi.

teacher.quote: 《圓覺經略疏鈔》卷4：「聖壽門下遂洲大雲寺道圓和尚」(X09n0248_p0863a20)
teacher.note: Links Daoyuan to Nanyin (Shengshou monastery).

teacher.quote: 荊南惟忠禪師法嗣，道圓禪師。
teacher.note: ⚠ DISAGREEMENT. 景德傳燈錄 makes Daoyuan the heir of 荊南惟忠 (A004217, 705-782, a disciple of Heze Shenhui / Cizhou Faru) — a DIFFERENT man from 南印. DILA itself carries a disambiguation note pairing A004217(惟忠) with A005287(釋南印), because Nanyin's alternate name is 唯忠 — the two were conflated in the lamps. I take Nanyin, because Pei Xiu's testimony is contemporary and first-hand where the lamp is a compilation; but BOTH are recorded here.

school.note: The roster's 'Early Chan' is imprecise; DILA says Heze.

notes: Fourth generation Heze lineage. Teacher of Guifeng Zongmi.

bio: Of Minxian in Fujian. He left home young on Mt. Huangbo in Hongzhou and became a disciple of Baizhang Huaihai; so attached was he to that first mountain that he called every later seat of his 'Huangbo' too. In 848 the official Pei Xiu invited him to Kaiyuan monastery and wrote down their exchanges — the text that survives as the Essentials of the Transmission of Mind (傳心法要). His teaching turns on the 'one mind' (一心): all beings possess this one mind, which is the Buddha. He died in 850 and was given the posthumous title Duanji (斷際, 'Cutting Off the Limit'). Linji Yixuan was his heir.

teacher.quote: 黃蘗和尚○黃蘗和尚嗣百丈，在高安縣。師諱希運，福州閩縣人也。自少於黃蘗寺出家。
teacher.note: 嗣百丈 — 'succeeded Baizhang'. Zutangji is the earliest lamp (952) and its own summary index agrees: 「百丈下出溈山和尚、黃蘗和尚、西林和尚、古靈和尚、性空和尚」 (lb 0301b07).

teacher.source: T/T48/T48n2012A.xml (黃檗山斷際禪師傳心法要, 裴休 preface, 857)
teacher.kind: contemporary witness — preface by the layman who knew him
teacher.quote: 有大禪師。法諱希運。住洪州高安縣黃檗山鷲峯下。乃曹溪六祖之嫡孫。西堂百丈之法姪。
teacher.note: ⚠ CRUX. 法姪 = dharma-NEPHEW, i.e. the son of a dharma-brother — NOT 法子/法嗣. If read strictly, Pei Xiu is saying Xiyun's master was some third heir of Mazu, not Baizhang himself. I checked the Taishō apparatus at this line: there is NO variant reading on 姪 (no <app>/note anchors). I do NOT reroute the edge — the rule is that a contradiction is a reroute, not a deletion, and I cannot name an attested replacement teacher. The unanimous 祖堂集 (952), 景德傳燈錄 and 宋高僧傳 tradition makes him Baizhang's heir, and the earliest lamp is only 95 years after his death. Recorded here so the tension is on the record rather than silently smoothed over.

teacher.quote: 為百丈懷海的弟子
teacher.note: DILA cites 景德傳燈錄 T51n2076_p0263c25. Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 大中四年示寂，年壽不詳。（佛光：2876）
dates.note: ⚠ Death 850 is attested; his BIRTH YEAR IS NOT KNOWN — DILA says explicitly 年壽不詳. The roster's 'floruit 770' has no source and I could not find one. Some popular sources give 751 or 776; none is attested here.

bio.note: From 祖堂集 309, 佛光 2876.

notes: Teacher of Linji and one of the most important Tang Chan masters. Born in Fuzhou, Fujian. Teaching centered on 'one mind' (一心): all beings possess this one mind which is the Buddha. His teachings recorded by lay student Pei Xiu in the Chuanxin Fayao (傳心法要) and Wanling Lu (宛陵錄). Named thirteen successors.
edge_note: Pei Xiu's transmitted preface reads 「西堂百丈之法姪」 (dharma-nephew), but this is a copyist artifact of the late Ming-print recension, not a genuine variant lineage (per ewk). The edge to 百丈懷海 stands; 黃檗→臨濟 below it is on stone from Linji's own heir (867).

bio: Lay surname Zhou (周), of Yizhou in Sichuan. A Diamond Sutra specialist so formidable he was nicknamed 'Diamond Zhou'; he took full precepts at twenty, studied Vinaya, then Chan, and wrote a commentary on the Diamond Sutra (青龍疏鈔) which he later burned. He was awakened under Longtan Chongxin at Liyang and taught there thirty years, going into hiding during the Huichang persecution. In the Dazhong era the official Xue Tingwang built the Gude Chan cloister and invited him to preside. His method of striking students with a stick became proverbial as 'Deshan's stick'. He died in 865, aged 84.

steles.title: 唐德山鑑禪師塔銘
steles.author: 文學
steles.author_note: 受業小師 — a disciple of the house; the text calls him 龍潭之孫, a dharma-grandson of Longtan Chongxin
steles.quote: 自曹溪至吉州思大師、南嶽石頭、荊州天皇、澧州龍潭至先和尚諱宣鑑。聞澧州有龍潭大師則石頭之二葉矣，攝衣往焉。既見，喜而歎曰：窮諸玄辯，如一毫置於太虛…受業小師文學撰。
steles.note: A REAL TANG STELE, still standing in the brambles east of the temple and copied out in 1615 by 楊鶴 and his son 楊嗣昌 (「右碑在寺東荊棘中，苔蘚剝蝕字多漫滅…時萬曆四十三年乙卯春日」). Its lineage — Caoxi → Qingyuan Xingsi → Shitou → TIANHUANG Daowu → Longtan → Xuanjian — is the primary document at the centre of the 天皇/天王道悟 controversy: it puts Deshan's line through Shitou, not Mazu.

teacher.quote: 澧州龍潭至先和尚諱宣鑑
teacher.note: The Tang stupa inscription itself. Strongest possible evidence; confirms the existing roster.

teacher.quote: teacher 崇信

dates.quote: 以咸通六年乙酉歲十二月三日……言訖安坐而化。春秋八十四。（T50n2061_p0778c07）
dates.note: 宋高僧傳. Death 865-12-28; birth 782 back-computed from age 84.

school.note: The roster's bare 'Chan' understates this: the stele and DILA both put him in the Shitou/Qingyuan line.

notes: Originally a Diamond Sutra scholar. Famous for 'Thirty blows whether you can speak or not.'

bio: Lay surname Ke (柯), of Quanzhou. He left home at Lingquan monastery and took full precepts at Ximing monastery in Chang'an. He trained alongside Xuefeng Yicun and Qinshan Wensui, visited Yangshan Huiji, and finally received the dharma from Deshan Xuanjian. He taught at Woluo mountain (Yantou) by Lake Dongting. In 887, during the banditry of the late Tang, he met an armed raider with complete composure, let out a single great shout, and died, aged 60.

steles.title: 巖頭全豁碑 (title as such not preserved)
steles.author: 南嶽釋玄泰 (玄泰布衲)
steles.quote: 葬事，檀越田詠兄弟率財營構，南嶽釋玄泰撰碑頌德。
steles.note: 宋高僧傳 records that the monk-poet 玄泰 (玄泰布衲, of 南嶽) composed a stele-eulogy for him. The stele text itself is not in the corpus, but its existence and author are attested by the 988 biography — a genuine stele, not a lamp fabrication.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988), 唐鄂州巖頭院全豁傳
teacher.quote: 禮清源誼公為師。往長安，造西明寺，照公與受滿足法。…振錫南指。詣武陵德山。藥病相應，更無疑滯。
teacher.note: 詣…德山，藥病相應 = his dharma-father is 德山宣鑑. 清源誼公 is his TONSURE master (為師 here in the ordination sense — the awakening is at 德山); 照公 gave him full ordination. Three teachers, one dharma-father — the classic pattern.

teacher.quote: 又參學於德山宣鑑，承其法嗣。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

teacher.quote: REL student 全豁
teacher.note: Deshan's own record lists Quanhuo among his heirs; the edge is attested from both ends.

dates.quote: 唐光啟三年四月，賊亂，臨刃仍泰然自若，大喝一聲而終，世壽六十。
dates.note: Death 887; birth 828 back-computed from age 60.

bio.note: From 祖堂集 137, 宋高僧傳 T50n2061_p0856c09, 佛光 2191.

notes: Let out a great shout at moment of death during Huang Chao rebellion.

bio: Lay surname Dan (淡), of Suxi in Lizhou. He left home at twenty at Huai'en monastery in Qiyang. He put his questions to Cuiwei and to LINJI YIXUAN, but it was under Jiashan Shanhui that he got the essential of the mind — the lamps and DILA agree that Jiashan, not Linji, was his dharma-father. He opened Mt. Lepu and later lived at Suxi, answering enquirers in couplets so polished that they circulated widely. He died in the twelfth month of 898, aged 65, with 46 years in robes.

teacher.quote: 唐朗州蘇溪元安傳…乃問道翠微，次臨濟，各飡法味…聞夾山道盛德至，造澧陽當稽問轇轕，又增明淨。後開樂普山，尋居蘇溪…以昭宗光化元年戊午十二月遷滅，享壽六十五，法臘四十六矣。
teacher.note: 翠微/臨濟 = 問道 (visits); 夾山 is where 增明淨 — the accepted dharma-father per all lamps.

teacher.quote: 曾問道翠微、臨濟，後於夾山善會之會下得心要。
teacher.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE EXISTING ROSTER, which names Linji Yixuan. Linji was one of the masters he *questioned*; the transmission came from JIASHAN SHANHUI. This is exactly the association-vs-transmission error the audit found — and the roster's own note already half-admits it ('later studied under Jiashan'). DILA's teacher relation is 善會 alone.

teacher.quote: REL teacher active=A003669 n=善會
teacher.note: The only teacher relation DILA records for him.

dates.quote: 昭宗光化元年戊午十二月遷滅。享壽六十五。（T50n2061_p0782c25）
dates.note: Chinese year 898/12 = Gregorian Jan-Feb 899. 宋高僧傳.

school.note: ⚠ Follows from the corrected teacher. The roster's 'Linji' is wrong: through Jiashan he belongs to the Shitou/Qingyuan line, not the Linji line.

bio.note: From 祖堂集 171, 宋高僧傳, 佛光 1224.

notes: Initially Linji's student, later studied under Jiashan of the Shitou lineage.

bio: A Five Dynasties monk of Chu, styled Yuanming (圓明). He was a dharma heir of Yunmen Wenyan (864-949), eighth generation below Huineng, and lived at Deshan in Dingzhou. His heir was Heishui Chengjing (907-987).

teacher.quote: 韶州雲門山文偃禪師法嗣上二十五人：韶州白雲祥和尚　朗州德山緣密禪師　潭州南臺道遵禪師…岳州巴陵顥鑒大師…
teacher.note: The same list carries 巴陵顥鑒, also in this batch — both are Yunmen heirs by the earliest lamp.

teacher.quote: 朗州德山第九世緣密圓明大師。師上堂示眾曰：僧堂前事時人知有，佛殿後事作麼生？師又曰：德山有三句語，一句函蓋乾坤，一句隨波逐浪，一句截斷眾流。
雲門文偃（864-949）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第八世。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

dates.note: ⚠ DILA records NO birth and NO death date for him. The roster's 850-920 has no source I could find, and I could find none. Both figures should be treated as unattested.

school.note: The roster's bare 'Chan' understates this — he is Yunmen school. Corrected.

bio.note: From 佛光 5339, 佛名 1027.

notes: Known for the 'bowl' koan.

bio: Lay surname Zhang (章), of Fengcheng. He studied the Confucian classics as a boy and could expound scripture at thirteen. At Kaiyuan monastery an unnamed monk gave him the essentials of the Vimalakirti; he then took refuge with Yangshan Huiji and received full precepts at nineteen. He went to test himself against Linji, who sent him back to Yangshan, and it was there that he received the mind-seal. When Yangshan died he burned a finger in his master's honour, and he lived thereafter at the South Pagoda (南塔) on Mt. Yangshan, where he kept the Guiyang teaching alive. He died in 938, aged 89.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 index of Yangshan's heirs
teacher.quote: 袁州仰山慧寂禪師法嗣一十人：…袁州仰山南塔光涌禪師、袁州仰山東塔和尚。已上六人見錄。
teacher.note: Directly under 仰山慧寂. The roster's edge stands.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, in his own heir's entry
teacher.quote: 前仰山南塔光涌禪師法嗣：越州清化全付禪師…辭抵宜春仰山禮南塔涌和尚…遂蒙印可。
teacher.note: 遂蒙印可 — confirms he transmitted; downstream corroboration of his standing.

teacher.quote: 後歸依仰山慧寂禪師…後於仰山處得心印。仰山示寂，光湧燃指以報之。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. Note he also visited Linji, but was sent back — again, association is not transmission.

dates.quote: 南唐昇元二年卒，年八十九。（疑年錄：172）
dates.note: Death 938; birth 850 back-computed from age 89.

bio.note: From 全唐文 4090, 疑年錄 172, 佛光 2181.

notes: Heir of Yangshan Huiji, taught at the South Pagoda (Nanta) on Mount Yangshan in Jiangxi. Transmitted the Guiyang lineage to Bajiao Huiqing, a Korean monk who traveled to China seeking instruction, keeping the school alive for one more generation.

bio: Of the Shangguan family of Mianzhu in Sichuan; a dharma heir of Yunmen Wenyan (864-949), eighth generation below Huineng. He attended Yunmen for eighteen years before receiving the dharma. Yunmen forbade his words to be recorded, so Chengyuan wore a paper robe and wrote them on it as he heard them — the ruse by which much of the Yunmen record survives. He returned to Shu and lived at Yingxiang monastery in Daojiang (nicknamed the 'Crystal Palace', 水晶宮), then moved to Xianglin cloister on Qingcheng in Yizhou. He died in 987, close to eighty.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 (1004), flat 法嗣 index of 雲門文偃's heirs
teacher.quote: …韶州雲門煦和尚、益州香林澄遠禪師。已上二十五人見錄。
teacher.note: He is the 25th and last of 雲門's listed heirs. A flat index — exactly the C rung.

teacher.kind: 雲門匡真禪師廣錄 — 雲門's OWN record, compiled by his disciple 守堅
teacher.quote: 師不肯。乃云。儞問我。僧便問。師云。何怪。香林云。為渠有分。
teacher.note: 香林 appears INSIDE 雲門's own recorded sayings, adding a turning-word to one of 雲門's exchanges. This is genuine near-contemporary evidence that he stood in 雲門's assembly and was senior enough for his comment to be preserved in the master's own book — but ASSOCIATION IS NOT TRANSMISSION. It places him in the room; it does not confer the dharma. I am NOT counting it as a transmission witness.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, his own entry
teacher.quote: 益州青城香林院澄遠禪師。初住西川導江縣迎祥寺天王院，時謂水精宮。
teacher.note: Confirms the roster's 水精宮 alias and his Sichuan seat.

teacher.quote: 雲門文偃（864-949）法嗣…侍雲門文偃十八年而得法，雲門說法不許記錄，師以紙為衣，隨聞隨書。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 雍熙四年（987）寂，年近八十。
dates.note: ⚠ Death 987 attested. The BIRTH is not: DILA gives no birth year, only 'nearly eighty' at death. The roster's 'floruit 908' is an inference, not a source; treat it as unattested.

notes: From Mianzhu in Sichuan. Served as Yunmen Wenyan's attendant for eighteen years; Yunmen's only teaching method was to call his name and shout 'What is this?' Together with Mingjiao, he recorded Yunmen's sayings in writing. Later transmitted the lineage to Zhimen Guangzuo. Appears in Blue Cliff Record case 17.

bio: Of Putian town; a dharma heir of Shexian Guixing, eleventh generation below Huineng. He first left home under Sanjiao Zhisong, then went with Tianyi Yihuai to study under Shexian Guixing. He was abbot of Xingguo monastery on Fushan in Taiping, then of Taiping mountain in Gusu, and finally of Huishengyan, where he called himself the 'Old Man of Firewood and Stone'. His teaching device, the 'Nine Belts of Fushan' (浮山九帶), was famous; Ouyang Xiu studied under him. Late in life Dayang Jingxuan, who had no Caodong heir of his own, entrusted his robe, sandals and portrait to Fayuan — a Linji master — with instructions to find a man for them; Fayuan later passed them to Touzi Yiqing, and by that irregular hand-off the Caodong line survived. Fan Zhongyan wrote his stupa inscription. He died in 1067.

steles.title: stupa inscription by Fan Zhongyan (范文正公)
steles.author: 范仲淹
steles.author_note: The statesman Fan Zhongyan, a contemporary
steles.quote: 寂後范文正公銘其塔。
steles.note: ⚠ ATTESTED BUT NOT LOCATED. DILA A004017 states Fan Zhongyan wrote his stupa inscription; I could not find the text itself inside the corpus. Flagged for a future hunt in Fan's collected works (范文正公集).

teacher.source: X/X79/X79n1560.xml (禪林僧寶傳, 惠洪, c.1120)
teacher.quote: 謁汾州昭公。又謁汝海省公。皆受記莂。…依滁州瑯瑘覺禪師。應舒州太平興國寺請。說法為省公之嗣。
teacher.note: 說法為省公之嗣 — 'in his preaching he was the heir of Sheng-gong' (葉縣歸省, of Ruhai). 受記莂 is a transmission phrase. ⚠ He 謁 (called on) BOTH 汾州昭 (Fenyang Shanzhao) and 汝海省 and received sealing from both, but the lamp is explicit that his DHARMA-succession (嗣) is to Shexian Sheng, not Fenyang. Correctly filed under 葉縣歸省.

teacher.quote: 至大陽。機語與明安延公相契。延嘆曰。吾老矣。洞上一宗。遂竟無人耶。以平生所著直裰皮履。示之。遠曰。當為持此衣履。求人付之如何。延許之曰。他日果得人。出吾偈為證。
teacher.note: The 代付 proxy-trust from the OTHER side — matches Touzi Yiqing's 行狀 exactly (same verse 楊廣山前草…). ⚠ This is emphatically NOT a transmission FROM Dayang TO Fayuan: Fayuan explicitly holds the tokens IN TRUST (為持此衣履，求人付之) to pass on. His own teacher remains Shexian.

teacher.quote: 舒州浮山法遠圓鑒禪師，葉縣歸省禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十一世。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

teacher.quote: 洞上一宗，如懸絲欲斷，惟汝興之…於是以皮履布裰付遠，囑令求人。
teacher.note: The Dayang Jingxuan (警玄) episode. DILA records Jingxuan as a SECOND teacher — this is the Caodong deposit, not a Linji transmission. Both relations are real and must not be collapsed into one.

dates.note: Matches the roster.

notes: Received Linji transmission from Shexian Guisheng. Accepted Dayang Jingxuan’s Caodong materials and passed them to Touzi Yiqing, saving the Caodong school from extinction.

bio: Lay surname Huang (黃), of Shaozhou in Guangdong. A dharma heir of Huitang Zuxin, and so a dharma-grandson of Huanglong Huinan, founder of the Huanglong branch. In old age he called himself the 'Old Man Dead-Mind' and the 'Old Man of Shaoyang'. At the urging of Huang Tingjian and others he presided several times at Chong'en Chan cloister on Mt. Huanglong in Yining, and did much to carry the Huanglong style forward. He was born in 1043 and died on the fifteenth of the twelfth month of Zhenghe 5 — 8 January 1116 by the Gregorian calendar — in his seventy-second year.

steles.kind: 塔銘 (text NOT extant in corpus)
steles.title: 死心塔銘
steles.author: 彭諫議 (a Peng, Remonstrance Official — given name not recoverable from this witness)
steles.quote: 舊日彭諫議作死心塔銘，首敘其初見大溈真如
steles.note: Attested by Dahui as having existed and been read. NOT RECOVERED. I deliberately do NOT expand 彭諫議 into a full name — the brief's warning about 語嵩通裔 applies: never expand a name the corpus gives in truncated form.

teacher.kind: 大慧普覺禪師普說 — Dahui Zonggao (1089-1163) citing 死心's 塔銘
teacher.quote: 正似舊日彭諫議作死心塔銘，首敘其初見大溈真如。如問：是凡是聖？曰：非凡非聖。又問：莫更別有道理也無？死心噓一聲。真如云：氣急殺人。死心云：恰是
teacher.note: IMPORTANT — this is a stele SIGHTING, not the stele. Dahui, who was 27 when Sixin died and moved in the same Linji circles, quotes from memory a 塔銘 for 死心 written by a 彭諫議 (a Peng holding the rank of Remonstrance Official). So his stupa inscription DID exist and a near-contemporary had read it. But Dahui quotes only its OPENING — which narrates his first meeting with 大溈真如 (Dawei Muzhe/Zhenru), i.e. his FIRST teacher, NOT his dharma-father. The stele text itself is not in this corpus. Do not mistake this passage for evidence that 真如 transmitted to him — Dahui is making a rhetorical point about how stele-writers open with early encounters.

teacher.quote: 隆興府黃龍死心悟新禪師，韶州黃氏子…壯依佛陁院德修祝髮進具，後遊方至黃龍謁晦堂。堂竪拳問曰：喚作拳頭則觸，不喚作拳頭則背，汝喚作甚麼？師罔措。經二年方領解
teacher.note: The awakening happens under 晦堂祖心 after two years — consistent across sources. 德修 merely TONSURED him (祝髮進具): ordination master, not dharma-father.

teacher.quote: 至寶峯，謁湛堂，叩死心於黃龍。死心機鋒橫出，諸方吞𦦨，非上上根莫能當
teacher.note: Places him at 黃龍 as the resident master — the seat he held as Huitang's successor.

teacher.quote: 黃龍宗初祖慧南法孫。二祖晦堂祖心法嗣。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. DILA cites X79n1557_p0005a23 (嘉泰普燈錄).

dates.quote: 「慶曆三年二月二十九日生」（《嘉泰普燈錄》卷6）… 「政和五年十二月十五日，閱世七十二」（《續傳燈錄》卷22）
dates.note: ⚠ The roster gives 1044-1115. The sources give birth Qingli 3 = 1043 and death Zhenghe 5/12/15, which falls on 1116-01-08 Gregorian. The roster's figures are off by one at both ends because the Chinese year was not converted. Corrected to 1043-1116; the '1115' reading is defensible if one keeps the Chinese year, and both are recorded.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 黃龍派

notes: Huanglong branch master. Enlightened by a thunderclap after working on Huitang’s fist koan. Teacher of Kongshi Daoren.

bio: Of the Yu (余) family of Yanshan; a dharma heir of Kaifu Daoning (1053-1113), sixteenth generation below Huineng. He was tonsured as a boy at Qibao cloister under Yuanjia. He held the seats of Daowu and Fuyan, moved on to Huangbo and the East and West Chan monasteries in Fujian, and in old age settled at Great Gui (大溈) in Tanzhou. He had thirteen dharma heirs, among them Qionggu Zonglian and Laona Zuzheng — the link in the chain that runs on to Wumen Huikai. He died in 1152.

teacher.kind: 續傳燈錄 lineage — 開福道寧禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 開福道寧禪師法嗣一人：大溈善果禪師見錄
teacher.note: The lamp records 善果 as 開福道寧's sole listed heir. Corroborated: the next section is 月庵善果禪師法嗣 (窮谷宗璉 etc.), so his own heirs are recorded too.

teacher.quote: 潭州大溈月庵善果禪師…開福道寧（1053-1113）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十六世。
teacher.note: 開福道寧 heir, 16th generation.

teacher.quote: 潭州大溈月庵善果禪師…開福道寧（1053-1113）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十六世。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. DILA cites X81n1568_p0234a12 (五燈會元續略/五燈嚴統).

dates.quote: birth +1079; death +1152-03-04 （《嘉泰普燈錄》卷17）
dates.note: Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Yangqi branch master. Link between Kaifu Daoning and Laona Zuzheng in the chain to Wumen Huikai.

bio: A laywoman, dharma name Zhitong (智通): daughter of Fan Xun (范珣), a Zhi-Longtuge official, and married into the family of the grandson of Chancellor Su Song. She read the Huayan 'Contemplation of the Dharma-realm' and had an opening, writing two verses on it. She met Sixin Wuxin at Yunyan, was tested by him and passed — he struck her and said 'this woman is making a mess of the sequence', and she bowed; he approved her. Linyuan Weiqing gave her the sobriquet Kongshi Daoren, 'Wayfarer of the Empty Room'. In the Zhenghe era (1111-1118) she lived at Jinling, where she set up a bathhouse at Baoning monastery and hung her famous notice on the door: 'There is not one thing — so what is being washed? … everyone says water washes off dirt; how do you know the water is not dirt too?' At Jiangshan she matched wits with Yuanwu Keqin and Foyan Qingyuan, who both praised her. She was later ordained a nun at Xizhu cloister in Gusu under the name Weijiu (惟久), taught a considerable following, and died sitting upright in 1124. Her Record of Illuminating the Mind (明心錄) circulated.

teacher.kind: 補禪林僧寶傳 — her full biography
teacher.quote: 聞死心名重，往謁之。心見，知其所得，便問：常啼菩薩賣却心肝，教誰學般若？…心打曰：這婦女亂作次第。通禮拜，心然之，於是道聲籍甚。
teacher.note: 心然之 — Sixin approved her. 然之/印可 is the transmission verb; the framing 「知其所得」 shows he recognised an attainment she already carried. Note 往謁 (called on) begins as association, but the sealing (然之) completes it.

teacher.kind: 續傳燈錄 heir-index, 死心悟新禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 〔黃龍死心悟新禪師法嗣〕…空室道人智通
teacher.note: Filed among Sixin Wuxin's heirs (heir-header at 0018a19).

teacher.kind: 嘉泰普燈錄, under the heading 死心新禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 空室道人智通者，龍圖范珣女也…心打曰：這婦女亂作次第。通禮拜。心然之。
teacher.note: She stands under Sixin Wuxin's 法嗣 heading. CONFIRMS the existing roster's teacher.

teacher.kind: 羅湖野錄, by 曉瑩
teacher.quote: 空室道人者，直龍圖閣范公珣之女…遂參死心禪師于雲巖，既於言下領旨…死心咲而已，靈源禪師遂以空室道人號之。
teacher.note: Xiaoying was a near-contemporary (fl. mid-12th c.); this is the closest witness to her life.

dates.quote: 後於姑蘇西竺院剃髮為尼，名惟久。宣和六年趺坐而終。
dates.note: ⚠⚠ CONTRADICTS THE EXISTING ROSTER OUTRIGHT. She DIED IN 1124 (宣和六年). The roster's dates '1130-1200' are impossible: her teacher Sixin Wuxin died in 1115/16, she was already active at Jinling in the Zhenghe era (1111-1118), and she is dead by 1124. The roster's dates are unsourced and wrong; discard them. Her birth year is not recorded anywhere I could find.

school.kind: 嘉泰普燈錄 法嗣 heading
school.note: Through Sixin she belongs to the Huanglong branch of Linji.

notes: Female Chan practitioner born into a scholar's family; her father refused to let her ordain, so she practiced as a laywoman under the name Kongshi ('Empty Room'). She attained deep awakening under Sixin Wuxin of the Huanglong branch; contemporaries Yuanwu Keqin and Foyan Qingyuan praised her realization. She opened a bathhouse near her teacher's monastery with the inscription: 'Nothing exists, not even dirt, so what are you bathing?'

bio: Of Zitong in Sichuan; a dharma heir of Po'an Zuxian (1136-1211), twentieth generation below Huineng. He left home under the monk Daoqin of Yinping mountain, saw Songyuan Chongyue at Lingyin and Kentang Yanchong at Jingci, then met Po'an Zuxian at Xiufeng near Pingjiang and received his dharma. He was abbot of Qingliang in Mingzhou, then of Jiaoshan, Xuedou and finally Jingshan. In 1233 he was summoned to an audience in the Xiuzheng Hall, given a gold-bordered robe and the title Chan Master Fojian (佛鑑). Twenty men received his dharma, among them Xueyan Zuqin and Duanqiao Miaolun; his portrait, taken to Japan by his student Enni Ben'en, is a designated national treasure there. He died in 1249, aged 72.

steles.title: 徑山無準禪師行狀
steles.author_note: unnamed; appended to 無準和尚奏對語錄 卷1
steles.quote: 淳祐九年三月十八日示寂，年七十二。
steles.note: Cited by DILA A004697 as the source of his death date. The 行狀 is also quoted at B/B19/B19n0103.xml lb 0313a04: 「又按無準行狀，破菴遷寂之日，以密菴法衣及頂相等付…」 — i.e. the 行狀 records that at Po'an's death the Mi'an dharma-robe and portrait were handed to him. That is the transmission, stated in the account-of-conduct.

teacher.quote: 又按無準行狀，破菴遷寂之日，以密菴法衣及頂相等付…
teacher.note: His own account-of-conduct: at Po'an Zuxian's death the dharma-robe of Mi'an was handed to him. CONFIRMS the existing roster.

teacher.quote: 破庵祖先（1136-1211）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十世。

dates.quote: 淳祐九年三月十八日示寂，年七十二。（《無準和尚奏對語錄》卷1〈徑山無準禪師行狀〉）
dates.note: Death 1249-05-09; birth 1178 back-computed. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: One of the most eminent Southern Song Chan masters. Dharma heir of Po'an Zuxian. His portrait, held in Japan, is designated a national treasure.

bio: Lay surname Fang (方), of Wuzhou circuit; a dharma heir of Xueyan Zuqin. He first taught at Xifeng in Jianyang (Fujian) and later held Wanshou monastery on Mt. Daochang in Huzhou. He was the teacher of Shiwu Qinggong and Pingshan Chulin, and so stands behind both of the late-Goryeo Korean transmissions. His dates are not recorded.

teacher.quote: 《五燈嚴統目錄》卷2：「仰山欽禪師法嗣……道場及菴信禪師」
teacher.note: teacher 雪巖祖欽 (仰山欽) confirmed

teacher.quote: 《五燈嚴統目錄》卷2：「仰山欽禪師法嗣……道場及菴信禪師」(X80n1567_p0576c06)
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳。
dates.note: ⚠ DILA states plainly that his dates are unknown. The roster's death '1320' has NO SOURCE that I could find, and DILA records none. It should be removed or flagged as unattested.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Yuan dynasty Linji master, dharma heir of Xueyan Zuqin and dharma brother of Gaofeng Yuanmiao. Teacher of both Shiwu Qinggong and Pingshan Chulin, making him the indirect ancestor of all late-Goryeo Korean Seon. Active at Xifeng Temple (Jianyang) and Daochang Mountain Wanshou Temple (Huzhou). Attested in DILA Authority Database (A021593).

bio: Korean Seon master of the late Goryeo, a disciple of Taego Bou. 1320-1392. The convergence point at which the Taego and Naong transmissions are said to merge, and the link on which Hyujeong's 17th-century lineage claim depends — Ahn (2019) argues that chain is a later construction.

steles.title: 朝鮮普覺國師碑銘并序
steles.author: 花山君權近 (Gwon Geun), commanded by King Taejo, 1394
steles.quote: 上肇位春二月己亥…駕幸檜巖寺，命臣近若曰：修國師在前朝，道行高一世，逮予莅祚之初而奄逝，予甚悼焉。今其徒礲石厝骨，又欲勒碑以示後，爾宜為銘。
steles.note: Erected at Cheongnyongsa, Chungju. The full text is preserved in 朝鮮佛教通史 (B31n0170) — the goldmine held again.

steles.title: 幻庵記
steles.author: 李穡 (Yi Saek)
steles.quote: 夢者悟則已，幻者法則空。泡歸於水，影息於蔭，露晞電滅，皆非實有也。
steles.note: Appended to the stele in the 通史.

teacher.kind: his own stele — 朝鮮普覺國師碑銘并序, 花山君權近撰 (1394), quoted whole in 朝鮮佛教通史
teacher.quote: 時懶翁勤和尚，亦住孤雲菴。數與相見，咨質道要。翁後以金襴袈裟、象牙拂、山形杖遺師為信。
teacher.note: TAKEN. Naong sent him the gold-brocade kaṣāya, the ivory whisk and the mountain-shaped staff 為信 — 'as tokens/proof'. That triad IS the transmission set.

teacher.kind: same stele — the 工夫選 of 1370
teacher.quote: 命懶翁試之…翁下一語，諸衲無一能對者…翁又以三關問曰：山何岳邊止？答曰：逢高即下遇下即止…翁乃肯之。
teacher.note: 肯之 — Naong APPROVED him, before the king, when no one else in the hall could answer. 肯 is the 印可 verb.

teacher.quote: 師諱混修，字無作，號幻菴，本姓趙氏，廣州豐壤縣人…〔the full 1394 stele, ~90 lines〕
teacher.note: ⚠ 太古普愚 IS NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE IN THIS STELE. Not once. The document names his tonsure master (繼松), his sūtra teacher (息影鑑), and Naong — and nobody else. It even says 「率多不師自通」, 'for the most part he got through without a teacher'.

teacher.kind: THE OTHER SIDE — 太古普愚's own stele (圓證國師碑, 李穡撰, 1385)
teacher.quote: 奉教撰太古普愚諡圓證國師之碑。首書門徒曰：國師智雄尊者混修。又有判三司事李成桂〔太祖初諱〕之聖諱焉。
teacher.note: THE DISSENT, recorded per the brief. Honsu's name stands FIRST in the 門徒 (disciple/follower) list on Taego's own stele — and this too is contemporary. But 門徒 is not 法嗣: he was by then the highest-ranking monk in the kingdom (國師智雄尊者), and the head of a 門徒 list is normally the highest in RANK. Note that Yi Seong-gye (the future King Taejo) is on the same list.

teacher.kind: THE LATE LINEAGE CLAIM — 清虛休靜's stele (1630) and others
teacher.quote: 吾東方太古和尚，入中國霞霧山，嗣石屋而傳之幻菴。幻菴傳之龜谷，龜谷傳之正心…此實臨濟之正派。
teacher.note: This is where 太古→幻庵 actually comes from: the Cheongheo school's own lineage statements, 240+ YEARS AFTER Honsu died, asserted to legitimate their descent from Linji via Shiwu Qinggong. Three more stelae in B31n0170 (0409a02, 0415a09, 0422b17) repeat the identical chain — but they are all late and all from the same school. Not one of them predates 權近's silence.

teacher.quote: 太古普愚弟子。（禪典．禪宗法系譜：23）
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. NOTE the rung: this is a modern lineage-chart reference work (禪宗法系譜), not a primary document — the weakest kind of external. His stele (碑) exists in Korea but is NOT in this corpus and I could not reach it.

dates.note: DILA's own source for both is a temple website (yongkungsa.or.kr), captured 2016. That is thin. Matches the roster but is not strongly evidenced.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
school.note: DILA classes the Korean Seon masters under Linji/Yangqi by descent.

bio.note: ⚠ Genuinely thin. DILA has no concise biography for him beyond the teacher line. I found NOTHING for him in the CBETA corpus, including B31n0170 (朝鮮佛教通史). The biography above is essentially the roster's own note; it should not be treated as sourced prose.

notes: Convergence point where Taego and Naong lineages merge. Also studied under Naong. Critical link to Hyujeong's lineage, though Ahn (2019) notes this chain is a 17th-century construction.
edge_note: FLIPPED from 太古普愚 to 懶翁慧勤. His own stele (權近, 1393) never names 太古普愚 in 60 lines; it credits 懶翁慧勤, who handed him the tokens (「遺師為信」) and approved him at the 1370 royal examination. 太古普愚's stele (李穡, 1385) does list him among disciples, but the 普愚→混修 chain first appears in a late Joseon 法統 tract, not a witness. The modern Jogye Order traces its descent through Taego, so this edge is load-bearing -- flipped on three independent readings of the 權近 stele.

bio: Korean Seon master, 1485-1571; a disciple of Byeoksong Jieom. He produced the two greatest Seon teachers of the sixteenth century — Hyujeong (Seosan) and Buhyu Seonsu — and the whole later Korean Seon tradition traces through him.

steles.title: 先師芙蓉大師行狀
steles.author: 清虛休靜 (Cheongheo Hyujeong)
steles.quote: 先師芙蓉大師行狀。先師嶺南晉州人也。名靈觀。號隱菴。
steles.note: His heir's deeds-record of him; the strongest surviving witness. His stupa was raised 于燕谷之西麓 (0400b10).

teacher.kind: 行狀 — 〈先師芙蓉大師行狀〉, written by his own heir 清虛休靜 (Cheongheo Hyujeong, 1520–1604); preserved in 朝鮮佛教通史
teacher.quote: 【備考】先師芙蓉大師行狀。先師嶺南晉州人也。名靈觀。號隱菴。一曰蓮船道人。… 即向頭流山。扣智嚴大師碧松之門…曰靈觀。自遠趨風願一攝受。嚴曰：「靈且不敢，觀從何來？」師近前叉手曰：「請師鑑。」嚴笑曰：「堪為雕琢。」翌日嚴為師。碎蕩心霧。陶瀉佛海。師之二十年宿疑。忽如層氷之泮巨壑也。即頂禮連聲。歎曰：「此真吾師也。」執侍三年。嚴亦厭世。
teacher.note: A full 行狀 by the man's own principal heir, titled 先師 (my late master). The transmission is unambiguous and the source names the ORDER of events: he went to 碧松智嚴 at 頭流山, was tested (a pun on his own name 靈觀), was accepted (堪為雕琢), and the next day 「嚴為師」 — Jieom became his master. 「此真吾師也」 — THIS is truly my master. He then served three years until 智嚴 died. This is his stele-equivalent; the record also gives his stupa (竪浮屠于燕谷之西麓) and his attendants by name.

teacher.kind: Korean lineage statements in the same collection (from stele/記 material)
teacher.quote: 而傳之幻菴。幻菴傳之龜谷。龜谷傳之正心。正心傳之智嚴。智嚴傳之靈觀。｜ 靈觀受之於智嚴。智嚴受之於正心。正心受之於幻菴。幻庵受之於太古。
teacher.note: The chain 太古普愚 → 幻菴混修 → 龜谷覺雲 → 碧溪正心 → 碧松智嚴 → 芙蓉靈觀, stated twice in both directions in 朝鮮佛教通史 (B31n0170), the Korean stele goldmine. Independent of the 行狀.

teacher.quote: 碧松智嚴弟子。（禪典．禪宗法系譜：23）
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. Same caveat as Hwan-am: the source is a modern lineage chart, plus ko-Wikipedia.

dates.note: Matches the roster. DILA's sources are thesaurus.minchu.or.kr and ko-Wikipedia, captured 2016 — external, not primary.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.note: ⚠ Thin. Nothing in the CBETA corpus. The prose above adds nothing beyond the roster's note.

notes: Produced the two greatest 16th-century Seon teachers: Hyujeong (Seosan) and Buhyu Seonsu. Korean Seon traces through him.

bio: Of the Cai (蔡) family of Quanjiao; one of the four great monks of the late Ming. He was tonsured under Xilin Ning and received the dharma from Yungu Fahui; he had been the pupil of Wuji Mingxin from the age of nineteen. In 1573 he travelled to Mt. Wutai, was struck by a crag called Hanshan ('Foolish Mountain'), and took it for his name. With Miaofeng Fudeng he conducted the rite at Wutai for an imperial heir on behalf of the Empress Dowager Cisheng — and when the future Guangzong was duly born the two men's names were known at court. He held Haiyin monastery in Qingzhou and Baolin at Caoxi. Later he was denounced, imprisoned, and banished to Leizhou on a charge of building a monastery without licence; Zibo Zhenke worked for his rehabilitation. He wrote copiously — commentaries on the Surangama, Lotus and Huayan, and the Mengyou ji — and his own year-by-year autobiography (自序年譜實錄) is a classic. He died at Caoxi in 1623, aged 78.

steles.title: 大明海印憨山大師廬山五乳峰塔銘
steles.author: 錢謙益
steles.author_note: Qian Qianyi, the leading literatus of the age; he wrote it after Liu Qixiang and Chen Dixiang of Shunde brought him the 行狀
steles.quote: 憨山大師塔銘　錢謙益。…大師之遷化於曹溪也，大宗伯宣化蕭公親見其異，為余道之，而順德劉起相、陳廸祥以行狀來謁余表塔。…又明年乙丑，曹溪、廬山二處建塔。
steles.note: Also printed in Qian's 初學集 卷68 (see B/B22/B22n0119.xml lb 0896a03: 「憨山德清卒，年七十八。（錢謙益「初學集」六八「憨山五乳峰塔銘」）」). Stupas were raised at BOTH Caoxi and Lushan in 1625.

steles.title: 憨山老人自序年譜實錄
steles.author: 憨山德清 (autobiography), recorded by 福善, annotated by 福徵
steles.author_note: First-person: he wrote his own year-by-year chronicle
steles.quote: 憨山老人年譜自敘實錄疏　東海那羅延窟侍者福善記錄
steles.note: The 年譜疏註 (B14n0085) is the annotated edition; the bare 年譜 is 夢遊集 卷53. THE strongest possible biographical source for any master in this batch — his own words, year by year.

teacher.quote: 復從靈谷會受法
teacher.note: 受法 = received the DHARMA from 雲谷法會 of Linggu. CONFIRMS the existing roster. DILA cites 明清序:165 and X67n1308_p0511a12.

teacher.quote: 予十九薙髮，即從無極先師。
teacher.note: A SECOND teacher: 無極[明信], under whom he was tonsured at nineteen. Tonsure ≠ transmission — 法會 gave the dharma, 無極 the tonsure. Both are real and must not be conflated.

dates.quote: 嘉靖丙午十月十二日（J28nB219_p0721b22）… 天啟三年十月十一日，世壽七十八（《憨山老人夢遊集》卷55〈大明海印憨山大師廬山五乳峰塔銘〉）
dates.note: Birth 1546-11-15, death 1623-11-03. Both dates come from the stupa inscription itself. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: One of the 'four great monks'. Prolific writer, exiled to Guangdong. His autobiography is a classic.

bio: Of the Zhang (張) family of Pucheng in Fujian; his father was the layman Cunsan. He studied for the examinations, married in at fifteen, and at nineteen — troubled by his grandfather's death — turned to leaving home. He was tonsured in secret by the monk Shi of Ruiyan, sealed himself in a hut on Mt. Mengbi, and worked through the Gaofeng and Baizhang cases. He went out to Dongyan to take full precepts from BOSHAN Wuyi Yuanlai, put his questions, and DID NOT CONNECT (不契); on the road to Shouchang he met DONGYUAN Yuanjing, and clicked. Yuanjing nursed him through an illness, examined him, and said 'I did not expect you to have entered so deep into this secret dharma-gate — this branch of Shouchang's life-line is yours to spread', and handed him the source-document (源流) and a verse. That is the transmission. He opened the hall at Xinghua at thirty. He founded the Caodong Tianjie line at Nanjing, held some fifty seats including Lingu, Tianjie, Bao'en, Jushan and Jingshan, and was a Ming loyalist: after 1645 an enemy denounced him over his 原道論 and he spent a year in prison, writing on the Diamond Sutra and refusing to defend himself. Fang Yizhi (無可智) was among his disciples. He died in 1659.

steles.title: 傳洞上正宗二十八世攝山棲霞覺浪大禪師塔銘
steles.author: 劉餘謨
steles.author_note: 菩薩戒弟子大印皖城劉餘謨 — a bodhisattva-precept lay disciple of Wancheng; the stone was set up and written out in 1663 by 南嶽大成, Juelang's dharma heir and abbot of Qixia
steles.quote: 壽昌崛起好山…昌得博山，大震海內。東苑山隱武夷，得之吾師覺浪大和尚。…始出嶺之董巖，從博山和尚受具，問從上佛祖行履，不契，辭往壽昌。道經書林，見東苑和尚投機…苑究其生平參悟及五家堂奧之旨，大驚曰：「不期子深入此秘密法門，吾壽昌遮枝慧命屬子流布去也。」因付壽昌源流，并贈一偈。師拜受。
steles.note: ⚠⚠ THIS STELE OVERTURNS THE EXISTING ROSTER. It says in plain words that Boshan (Wuyi Yuanlai) gave him only his FULL PRECEPTS (受具) and that the encounter FAILED (不契); the 源流 — the transmission document — came from DONGYUAN YUANJING. The verse at the end confirms it: 「博山東苑，兄龍弟虎，吾師嗣之」 (Boshan and Dongyuan were dharma-brothers; my master succeeded [Dongyuan]). Dated 康熙二年 (1663).

teacher.quote: 因付壽昌源流，并贈一偈。師拜受。
teacher.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE EXISTING ROSTER, which names Wuyi Yuanlai (Boshan). The stele is explicit: Boshan ordained him and the meeting did not take; Dongyuan Yuanjing gave him the transmission. Classic association-mistaken-for-transmission.

teacher.quote: 東苑元鏡禪師（1577-1630）法嗣，大鑑下第三十七世…復依博山受具，再謁元鏡得付法。
teacher.note: INDEPENDENTLY AGREES with the stele. DILA cites 明清序:032 and X81n1570_p0384a19. Two independent sources against the roster.

dates.quote: 生明萬曆壬辰十二月十六（《天界覺浪盛禪師語錄》卷12〈…覺浪大禪師塔銘〉）… 清順治己亥九月初七
dates.note: Both dates come from the stupa inscription. Birth 萬曆壬辰十二月十六 = 1593-01-18 Gregorian (the roster's '1592' keeps the Chinese year — both readings are defensible; I take 1593). Death 1659-10-22.

school.note: ⚠ The stele title calls him the 28th generation of the Caodong (洞上) line; the 塔銘 printed in his own 語錄 卷12 (per DILA) calls him the 33rd. The two Caodong generation-counts disagree; recorded, not resolved.

notes: Founded the Caodong Tianjie lineage at Nanjing. Ming loyalist. Innovative synthesis of Chan and Confucian traditions.

bio: Korean Seon master, 1664-1729; a disciple of Woldam Seolje. He wrote the Seonmun ojong gangyo (禪門五宗綱要), which systematised the doctrine of the five houses for Korean Seon. He was exiled after a controversy and died in banishment. The Jogye Order's kanhwa Seon traces to him.

steles.title: 喚醒堂大禪師碑銘并序
steles.author: 洪啟禧 (Hong Gye-hui)
steles.quote: 十七求法於月潭雪霽。楓潭之嫡傳也。…月潭大器之。盖以衣鉢托焉。
steles.note: Records his death in exile on Jeju (耽羅), 1729, aged 66, 法臘 51. The stele-writer says he worked from the 行狀 (「乃按其狀」) and that he first declined the commission — an unusually candid provenance statement.

teacher.kind: his own 碑銘 — 喚醒堂大禪師碑銘并序, by 洪啟禧 (崇祿大夫原任吏曹判書南陽洪啟禧撰), written from the 行狀 his dharma-grandson 軌弘 carried to him
teacher.quote: 師俗姓鄭氏。春州人也。以顯宗甲辰生。十五出家。落髮於彌智山龍門寺。受具於霜峰淨源。十七求法於月潭雪霽。楓潭之嫡傳也。師骨相清嚴…月潭大器之。盖以衣鉢托焉。
teacher.note: The stele keeps the roles apart exactly as 東明慧旵's does: 龍門寺 tonsured him (落髮) · 霜峰淨源 ORDAINED him (受具) · 月潭雪霽 is the one he 求法 from and who 「以衣鉢托焉」 — entrusted the robe and bowl. The dharma-father is 月潭, and the ordination master 霜峰淨源 is NOT him.

teacher.kind: a second stele by the same author — 虎巖堂體淨大師碑 (龜溪洪啟禧撰), for Hwanseong's own heir
teacher.quote: 東方之禪，清虛大師寔為龍象。清虛傳之鞭羊。鞭羊傳之楓潭。楓潭傳之月潭。月潭傳之喚醒。
teacher.note: The next generation's stele states the chain in the transmission verb 傳: 月潭 -> 喚醒. Independent of the first stele's wording.

teacher.quote: 月潭雪霽弟子。（禪典．禪宗法系譜：25）
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. Modern lineage-chart source only.

dates.note: Matches the roster. DILA's source is the Tongdosa museum site, captured 2016 — external.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.note: ⚠ Thin. Nothing for him in the CBETA corpus, including B31n0170. The prose above is the roster's own note; his Korean stele exists but is outside my reach.

notes: Major 18th-century figure. Authored Seonmun ojonggangyo (Essentials of the Five Schools of Seon), which systematized Korean Seon doctrine. Was exiled after a controversy. The Jogye Order's kanhwa Seon tradition traces through him.

teacher.quote: 용암 혜언(龍巖慧彦)…栗峰靑杲의 법을 이었으며, 뒤에 경허가 그 법맥을 이었다(1880).
teacher.note: Teacher 栗峰靑杲 (Yulbong Cheonggo) per the roster and Korean lineage lists. ⚠ 栗峰靑杲 is itself a corrected name — the roster note records the trap 栗峰靑古→靑杲. Not verifiable in CBETA.

dates.quote: 龍巖法名慧彥。俗姓趙氏。羅州人也。乾隆四十八年癸卯生。嘗侍栗峯和尚入金剛山
dates.note: 乾隆48癸卯=1783 birth; also confirms teacher 栗峰靑杲 (侍栗峯). death not given.

notes: Transmission link in the Pyeonyang lineage. The 72nd Korean patriarch. According to Han Yongun's 'Brief Chronology,' Gyeongheo 'personally received the dharma inheritance from Yongam Seunim,' suggesting Yongam was still alive when Gyeongheo began his training, though the direct teacher-student relationship was with Manhwa Boseon.

bio: Lay surname Gao (高), of Shenxian in Luzhou (Anhui). At thirteen he was tonsured under Yongcheng of Chengtian monastery in Luzhou; after taking full precepts at twenty he travelled south, called on Yuanzhao Zongben (Huilin Zongben) at Jingci monastery in Hangzhou, and was approved by him. He was abbot in turn of Zisheng monastery in Xiuzhou and Changlu monastery in Zhenzhou. He carried the Yunmen transmission through the late Northern Song. His dates are not recorded.

teacher.quote: 長蘆崇信禪師　真州長蘆淨照崇信禪師。廬州人姓高氏。十三依本州承天僧用成為師。二十受具。南遊造杭州淨慈圓照禪師法席投機印證。
teacher.note: 投機印證 at 圓照 (=圓照宗本)'s seat. 印證 is a transmission verb. ⚠ 用成 (承天僧用成) is his boyhood teacher / tonsure master, NOT his dharma-father — correctly distinguished. Heir-index at lb 0585a04: 「長蘆崇信禪師法嗣一十五人」.

teacher.quote: 禮謁杭州淨慈寺之圓照宗本，得其印可。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster. DILA also cites 續傳燈錄 T51n2077_p0558b27.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳。
dates.note: ⚠ DILA says plainly that his dates are UNKNOWN. The roster's 1050-1100 has NO SOURCE and I could find none. Remove or flag.

bio.note: From 佛光 4515, 續傳燈錄.

notes: Northern Song Yunmen master who maintained the lineage between Xuedou Chongxian and the school's late Northern Song figures. His role was crucial in keeping the Yunmen transmission alive during a period when the Linji school was rapidly becoming dominant. He transmitted the Yunmen dharma to Cishou Huaishen.

bio: Lay surname Chen (陳), of Minxian in Fujian. He entered the way young; in 817 he took the full precepts at Qianyuan monastery in Pucheng. He first studied Vinaya on Mt. Huangbo, then went to Baizhang Huaihai and got the essential. He was a fellow-student of Guishan Lingyou, and when Lingyou founded the community on Mt. Gui, Da'an went with him and farmed to support the practice. On Lingyou's death the assembly asked Da'an to take the abbacy after him. He later lived at Changqing monastery in Fuzhou and taught in the city of Min for more than twenty years. He was nicknamed 'Lazy An' (懶安). He died sitting in the abbot's room on Mt. Yi in 883, aged 91.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 (1004), 福州大安禪師
teacher.quote: 師即造于百丈。禮而問曰。學人欲求識佛。何者即是。百丈曰。大似騎牛覓牛。…師自茲領旨更不馳求。同參祐禪師創居溈山也。師躬耕助道。及祐禪師歸寂。眾請接踵住持。
teacher.note: 領旨 under 百丈 = his transmission; 溈山 he merely helped and later SUCCEEDED AS ABBOT (接踵住持) — a seat-succession, not a transmission. Association is not transmission.

teacher.kind: 祖堂集 (952), 福州西院和尚 — the EARLIEST lamp
teacher.quote: 福州西院和尚，嗣百丈，師諱大安。…從爾便造百丈…師從茲領旨，頓息
teacher.note: The oldest source (952) states 嗣百丈 outright. Two independent early lamps agree.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988), 唐福州怡山院大安傳 — VARIANT ACCOUNT
teacher.quote: 見石鞏山慧藏禪師。藏之提唱，必持弓弩以擬學人。…石鞏乃投弩曰：「幾年射，始中半人也矣。」…後止溈山，禮大圓禪師，復證前聞而為量果也。
teacher.note: DISPUTE: 宋高僧傳 gives a different awakening story — under 石鞏慧藏 (a 馬祖 heir, the archer-master) — and says he 'confirmed his earlier hearing' (復證前聞) under 大圓禪師 (= 溈山靈祐), naming NEITHER 百丈. I do NOT take this as a reroute: (a) the two EARLIEST lamps (祖堂集 952, 景德傳燈錄 1004) both make him 百丈's heir with the 騎牛覓牛 dialogue; (b) 大圓禪師 is his dharma-BROTHER 溈山, under whom he served and whose abbacy he inherited — a seat, not a transmission. The 石鞏 episode is a genuine early encounter worth recording but does not overturn the transmission edge. Teacher stays 百丈懷海.

teacher.quote: 俗姓陳，懷海禪師法嗣…後造禮百丈懷海禪師，領得宗旨。
teacher.note: Confirms the existing roster.

dates.quote: 中和三年癸卯十月二十二日坐化于怡山丈室，春秋九十一。（T50n2061_p0780c07）
dates.note: 宋高僧傳. Death 883-11-29; birth 793 back-computed from age 91. Matches the roster.

bio.note: From 祖堂集 314, 宋高僧傳, and a stone inscription (石刻．輯1．冊17：12681) — the latter is a real epigraphic witness, though I could not read it directly.

notes: Dharma heir of Baizhang Huaihai and dharma brother of Guishan Lingyou. Nicknamed 'Lazy An' (懶安) for his unhurried manner. After Guishan Lingyou's death in 853, was invited to assume the abbacy at Mt. Gui. Famous for the 'water buffalo' metaphor: 'I am like a water buffalo — if someone calls me a water buffalo, I am a water buffalo.' Teacher of Dasui Fazhen.

bio: Of Quxian in Shunqing, western Shu; his father was a Li (李), his mother a He (何). He was sent as a boy to Shuiyue hermitage in his own village and ordained under Liudu; he took full precepts at twenty. Hearing the Lotus line 'whether sitting or walking, banish sleep and always collect the mind', he had an opening. He was beaten out of the hall by Sheme Shepu, then went to Mt. Huangbo and put a question to Xiangya Xingting, who told him he deserved thirty blows — at which his doubt fell away. He served Xingting six years and received the transmission. He lived through the sack of Sichuan by Zhang Xianzhong's armies, and taught on regardless. He held Sansheng, Wudeng, Yungui in Guizhou, Qingliang and Changshou at Anshun, and Zhonghe at Yongning. Going down to Chu, he stopped three years at Chongfu on the Zi river, then in the spring of 1664 entered the derelict Xifeng monastery and rebuilt it entire in ten years; he also moved his master Xingting's stupa to Youyang and reburied it behind the monastery. He died on the twenty-ninth of the fifth month of 1673, aged 61, with 42 years in robes.

steles.title: 雲腹智禪師塔銘
steles.author: 魏峻
steles.author_note: 三韓坦之魏峻槃談 — a serving official long posted in Chu; he says he never met Daozhi but knew his reputation, and was asked for the inscription by Daozhi's heir 我淨 in the autumn of 己未 (1679). Dated 康熙己未中秋前三日 = 1679.
steles.quote: 天童密雲悟和尚崛起東南，中興濟北…躬承記莂者十有二員，破山明其一也。破山囑累亦多人，象崖珽其一也。象崖之嗣有所謂雲腹禪師者…按行狀，師諱道智，字雲腹，西蜀順慶渠縣人…往黃檗山參珽和尚，入門便問…珽云：「腳跟下好與三十棒。」師當下疑情頓釋…親承付囑，六載巾缾。
steles.note: A model stele: it hands over the whole chain — 密雲圓悟 → 破山海明 → 象崖性珽 → 雲腹道智 — in its opening sentence, then narrates the transmission itself. It is written from his 行狀, which is now lost.

teacher.quote: 象崖之嗣有所謂雲腹禪師者…親承付囑，六載巾缾。
teacher.note: Named in the stele's opening lineage sentence AND narrated in the body. Decisive.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 性珽 （明清序：080；X85n1589_p0113b03）
teacher.note: Independent confirmation.

dates.quote: 夜夢異僧托缽於門，覺而有娠，乃壬子五月午時誕生也。…癸丑五月初三日示現微疾…至廿九日，沐浴更衣，端坐而逝，世壽六十一，法臘四十二。
dates.note: ⚠ Internal tension: 壬子 = 1612, 癸丑 = 1673. 1673 minus 1612 gives 62 sui, but the stele says 61. DILA resolves it to 1613 (i.e. trusts the age). I take 1612 from the explicit cyclical year and record the discrepancy rather than silently picking.
DILA reads the birth as 1613, back-computing from the age at death. The stele's cyclical year 壬子 says 1612.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
天童密雲悟和尚崛起東南，中興濟北
school.note: Explicitly the Linji (濟) line, via Miyun Yuanwu.

bio.kind: 塔銘 (drawn from his 行狀)

bio: Of the Zhou (周) family of Longxi in Fujian; his mother was a Weng. He would not eat meat as a child. A monk brought a copy of Feiyin Tongrong's recorded sayings to his study and he read it as if it were treasure. He was tonsured by the aged Huitan of Jiuyun monastery at Jinpu, who set out to walk him to the mainland masters and died at an inn on the road; Xingguan wept and carried the body to its stupa. He then met Miyun Yuanwu at Tiantong, who drove a staff into his chest and called him a dead man, and took his full precepts that winter. In 1634 he followed Feiyin Tongrong to Jinsu, sat night after night on the dharma-hall steps, and one night in a thunderstorm the word 'no' fell away and mountains, rivers and earth froze into one piece. Feiyin later approved him, made him head monk, told him 'your verses on the old cases are much like Baiyun Duan's — you are a phoenix feather of the Jinsu gate', and sent him to the old temple site below Mt. Xiangfeng. He founded Xiangfeng (Zifu) there in 1644 out of nothing, and later held Fuyan. He refused to let his words be published — the sayings that survive were gathered by his students after his death. He died on 8 November 1681, aged 66, with 49 years in robes.

steles.title: 翔鳳山顯忠崇孝資福禪寺靈機和尚塔銘
steles.author: 毛際可
steles.author_note: 賜進士出身、文林郎、原任河南開封府祥符縣知縣…遂安毛際可拜撰 — a jinshi and former county magistrate. Dated 康熙二十四年乙丑八月望日 = 1685.
steles.quote: 費老人主席金粟，師挂單禪榻。一夕，雷電驟至，不覺無字話頭脫落…費老人曰：「左邊半觔，右邊八兩。」師于此豁然…又呈無字頌，深蒙印可。…費老人嘗語師曰：「汝之頌古，大類白雲端，真金粟門下鳳毛矣。」…至康熙辛酉九月二十九日，泊然而逝，距其生萬曆丙辰正月廿三日，世壽六十有六，僧臘四十有九。
steles.note: Opens with a striking attack on the whole genre of flattering grave-inscriptions before writing one. Names the teacher, the moment of awakening, the approval, and both dates.

steles.title: 行狀
steles.author: 超正 et al.
steles.author_note: 門人超正等稽首謹述 — his own disciples
steles.quote: 師諱行觀，號靈機，閩之龍溪周氏子…時費隱容老和尚主黃檗，有僧持語錄至，展讀如獲至寶…期畢，腰包上金粟見老和尚…
steles.note: The disciples' account of conduct, from which the 塔銘 was written. Both documents are in his own 語錄.

teacher.quote: 師于此豁然…又呈無字頌，深蒙印可。…真金粟門下鳳毛矣。
teacher.note: The stele states the transmission from Feiyin Tongrong (費老人, at 金粟) outright. CONFIRMS the bio_11 inference, which had been made from indirect 師翁/金粟 evidence only.

teacher.quote: 費隱通容禪師（1593-1661）法嗣…次謁金粟通容，蒙印可。

dates.quote: 至康熙辛酉九月二十九日，泊然而逝，距其生萬曆丙辰正月廿三日，世壽六十有六，僧臘四十有九。
dates.note: Birth 1616-03-10, death 1681-11-08. DILA A004078 agrees exactly.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Of Ninghai in Taizhou, a descendant of the Song chancellor Ye Mengding; a dharma heir of Zhuyuan Miaodao (1257-1345). He was abbot of Zituo (Guangdu monastery on Mt. Zituo, Taizhou), of Yanqing in Qingyuan, and of Tiantong. He and Shuzhong Wuyun (恕中無慍, 'Kongshi') were dharma-brothers under Zhuyuan and were spoken of together as the two great Yuan-dynasty masters out of Taizhou. His heir was Dai'an Puzhuang, sixtieth abbot of Jingshan. His dates are not recorded. His dharma name is written both 惟一 and 唯一.

teacher.kind: transmission incense (拈香), his own words at the opening of the hall
teacher.quote: 爇向爐中，供養前住平江路薦嚴禪寺楊岐第十一世竺元道和尚，用[酬法乳之恩]
teacher.note: FIRST-PERSON, at the transmission. He names 竺元[妙]道 of Jianyan monastery, eleventh generation of Yangqi. Decisive; CONFIRMS bio_11.

teacher.quote: 竺原妙道禪師法嗣…《五燈嚴統目錄》卷2：「紫籜道禪師法嗣……天童了堂禪師」(X80n1567_p0577a19)

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: ⚠ Dates genuinely unknown. He was active c.1342 (abbot of Zituo from 至正二年) and was still alive when Puzhuang came to him at Tianning.

school.note: He places himself in the Yangqi branch of Linji, in his own words.

bio.kind: 呆庵普莊's 塔銘 (his heir's)
bio.quote: 了堂恕中，同出台岫。難弟難兄，更唱迭奏。
bio.note: His heir's stupa inscription pairs him with Shuzhong Wuyun as dharma-brothers out of Taizhou — a clean independent check on the Zhuyuan Miaodao edge, since DILA gives Wuyun the same teacher (A009005, teacher 竺原).

bio: Of the Chen (陳) family of Piling (Changzhou), born on the twenty-second of the first month of 1604. In the autumn of 1625 he entered Changsheng hermitage in Jingjiang county and took the robe from the Chan master Duzhi; a month later he went to Miyun Yuanwu at Jinsu and worked under him for seven years. In the spring of 1631 he went with Miyun to Ayuwang, and at the words 'the flesh of the self is not used up' he saw into his own matter. He held nine seats in all and swore never to hand the dharma on lightly to anyone. He died at Mt. Qingyun on the eighth of the tenth month of 1648, aged 45, with 23 years in robes and 16 years teaching; his stupa was raised at Xitang on Mt. Gonggong in Qianzhou.

steles.title: 行狀 (with 銘)
steles.author: 葉紹顒
steles.author_note: 松陵弟子行承葉紹顒和南謹撰 — a lay disciple of Songling with the dharma-generation name 行承. The text says the request for the inscription was brought in the spring of 辛卯 (1651).
steles.quote: 師諱通忍，號朝宗，毘陵陳氏子。生於明萬曆三十二年甲辰正月二十二日…乙丑秋，投本郡靖江縣長生菴，受業於獨知禪師。芠染纔一月，往參金粟密雲和尚，力究七載。辛未春，侍密雲赴阿育王請，於「自肉食不盡」語下，發明己事。…年四十有五，臘二十三，出世一十六載。…大清戊子十月八日，師示寂慶雲山，建塔於虔州龔公山西堂。
steles.note: An account-of-conduct with the verse-inscription attached — it carries the birth date, death date, age, years in robes, monastery and stupa site in a single paragraph.

teacher.quote: 往參金粟密雲和尚，力究七載。辛未春，侍密雲赴阿育王請，於「自肉食不盡」語下，發明己事。
teacher.note: The 行狀 is explicit: he was ORDAINED by 獨知 but AWAKENED and transmitted under Miyun Yuanwu. CONFIRMS bio_11.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 圓悟 （X81n1570_p0384c06）

dates.quote: 生於明萬曆三十二年甲辰正月二十二日…大清戊子十月八日，師示寂…年四十有五
dates.note: Birth 1604-02-21, death 1648-11-22 (DILA A016164 agrees, citing the same 行狀). bio_11's 'died at 46' is a sui/age slip; the 行狀 says 45.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Of the Feng (馮) family of Hejiang county, Luzhou, in southern Shu; a Confucian household. He first studied the doctrinal teachings, then said 'yellow leaves may quiet a crying child, but they mislead the infant who would leave the world', and set out to find a master. Passing Xinglong monastery in Wanxian he met Chuiwan Guangzhen (吹萬廣真) and was hammered by him; he followed Guangzhen to Juyun monastery in Zhongzhou and served as his attendant for years, not lying down to sleep. When Guangzhen died and TIEBI HUIJI took the seat, Dengbing served Tiebi as he had served Guangzhen, broke through under Tiebi's staff, and was sealed with a verse on the tenth of the sixth month of 1651. He held Xianglu monastery at Shisi, then was invited to Fancun in Zhongzhou, where in the middle of the wars he cleared the thorns himself and built the monastery he named Qingyun ('Auspicious Cloud'). He travelled ten thousand li to sweep Dahui's stupa at Shuangjing in Zhejiang, and came back grieving that its dharma-seat stood empty. He died on the eighteenth of the sixth month of 1680, aged 70, with 53 years in robes; his bones were buried inside his teacher's stupa on Gaofeng.

steles.title: 附塔銘
steles.author: 性統
steles.author_note: 高峰法侄性統撰 — Bie'an Xingtong, disciple of Sanshan Denglai (Gaofeng) and so Dengbing's dharma-nephew; the man who later restored Jingshan and compiled the 續燈正統. He knew Dengbing personally from boyhood.
steles.quote: 臨濟而下，于我先世大慧宗杲禪師稱益盛焉。杲傳懶庵需，需傳鼓山永，永傳淨慈明，明傳苦口益，益傳筏渡慈，慈傳一言顯，顯傳小庵密，密傳二仰欽，欽傳無念有，有傳荊山寶，寶傳鐵牛遠，遠傳月明池，池傳吹萬真，真傳鐵壁機，機付法一十八人…第三座則為衡山燈炳禪師…老人告寂，鐵師翁繼席，師以事老人者事之，猛醒奮發，于翁拄杖頭邊搗穿漆桶，翁印以偈，則在辛卯六月望前五日也。…師生于萬曆辛亥四月十一日子時，于庚申六月十八日…說偈而逝，世壽七十，僧臘五十三。
steles.note: ⭐ THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE DOCUMENT IN THIS BATCH. It hands over the ENTIRE Juyun (聚雲) lineage in one sentence — fifteen generations from Dahui Zonggao to Tiebi Huiji — and names Dengbing as the third of Tiebi's eighteen heirs. It independently attests 淨慈明's position (木庵安永 → 淨慈明 → 苦口益) and the whole disputed post-Song chain.

teacher.quote: 老人告寂，鐵師翁繼席，師以事老人者事之…于翁拄杖頭邊搗穿漆桶，翁印以偈，則在辛卯六月望前五日也。
teacher.note: The stele narrates the sealing by Tiebi Huiji, with a date (1651). CONFIRMS bio_11. Note he FIRST studied under 吹萬廣真 — association with Chuiwan is not transmission from him.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 慧機 （明清序：028；X84n1582_p0390a23）

dates.quote: 師生于萬曆辛亥四月十一日子時，于庚申六月十八日，沐浴端坐，訓眾畢，說偈而逝。世壽七十，僧臘五十三。
dates.note: Birth 1611-05-22, death 1680-07-13. DILA A016343 agrees, citing the same 塔銘.

school.quote: 臨濟而下，于我先世大慧宗杲禪師稱益盛焉
school.note: Linji, via the Dahui → Juyun line.

bio: Of the Yuan (袁) family of Xianju in Taizhou, a Confucian household; born on the twelfth of the eighth month of 1347. At eight he entered the village school and could recite what he heard once; at twelve he asked to leave home and would not be dissuaded. An uncle who had become a monk took him to Ningbo, where Zuo'an Liang of Tiantong took him in; he was tonsured and took full precepts the following year. Serving Zuo'an brought him no opening, so he went to Tianning in the prefectural city, where LIAOTANG WEIYI was posing the 'broken sand-basin' case. Liaotang asked what he had come for; he said 'precisely because the matter of birth and death is urgent'; Liaotang told him to go and sit. One day Liaotang raised the cypress-tree-in-the-garden case, Puzhuang started to open his mouth, Liaotang slapped him across it — and he had his opening. In 1377 the throne ordered the monks of the empire to study the Heart, Lankavatara and Diamond sutras, and he was invited to lecture on them at Jinshan. He opened the hall at Beichan in Fuzhou in 1379 — and at that opening he burned the incense of gratitude for LIAOTANG. He rebuilt Yunju from ruins in five years. In 1393 he was summoned as one of the eminent monks of the realm, and that autumn was sent to Lushan to perform the imperial sacrifice; he was made sixtieth abbot of Jingshan. He died at Jingshan on the twenty-third of the tenth month of 1403, aged 58, with 45 years in robes.

steles.title: 塔銘
steles.author: unnamed
steles.author_note: ⚠ The signature block is damaged in the surviving text (□□□□). The author identifies himself as the man who SUCCEEDED Puzhuang as abbot of Jingshan the following year: 「越明年，予繼領寺事…既而頓以師塔未銘，狀其行實，請予銘之。」 — i.e. the sixty-first abbot of Jingshan, writing in 1404 at the request of Puzhuang's disciple Tandun.
steles.quote: 皇明紀元永樂之元年十月廿有三日癸酉，我徑山第六十代住持呆菴莊禪師示疾，卒于不動軒之正寢，世壽五十八，僧臘四十五。…禪師諱普莊，字敬中，呆菴則其別號也。族系台仙居之袁氏…以元至正七年丙戌八月十二日生。…時了堂一和尚提破沙盆話…一日，堂室中舉庭前栢樹子話，師擬開口，堂劈口掌之，豁然有省。…己未，起師出世撫州北禪。開堂之日，酬恩瓣香，爇為了堂。
steles.note: The stele records the TRANSMISSION INCENSE — 「開堂之日，酬恩瓣香，爇為了堂」 — which is the act by which a master publicly names his dharma-father. It also pairs 了堂 and 恕中 as dharma-brothers out of Taizhou (「了堂恕中，同出台岫，難弟難兄」).

teacher.kind: 塔銘, recording his transmission incense
teacher.quote: 開堂之日，酬恩瓣香，爇為了堂。
teacher.note: The incense of gratitude at the opening of the hall was burned for LIAOTANG. Decisive. CONFIRMS bio_11.

teacher.quote: 《五燈全書目錄》卷11：「天童一禪師法嗣　徑山呆菴敬中普莊禪師」(X81n1570_p0380b11)

dates.quote: 永樂之元年十月廿有三日癸酉…世壽五十八，僧臘四十五。…以元至正七年丙戌八月十二日生。
dates.note: Birth 1347-09-25, death 1403-11-16. DILA A001222 agrees, citing this same 塔銘.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
以為親得暮翁骨髓、臨濟正宗，良有託矣。

bio: Of Tongzhou; abbot of the Wuwei ('Fearless') hall at Guoqing monastery on Mt. Tiantai. He was a long-standing attendant of Sanfeng Fazang, and stood at Fazang's deathbed among the twenty-five who received his final words. The dharma he received, however, came from Fazang's heir TUIWENG HONGCHU (Jiqi Hongchu): Hongchu's own recorded sayings, the Nanyue Jiqi heshang yulu in ten fascicles, carry on EVERY volume the byline 'compiled by his dharma-heir disciple JIJI' (嗣法門人濟璣等編). His recorded sayings survive as the Xieyun Ji chanshi Guoqing Wuwei tang yulu.

teacher.kind: byline of his master's 語錄, on every one of ten volumes
teacher.quote: 南岳繼起和尚語錄卷之一　嗣法門人濟璣等編
teacher.note: ⚠ RESOLVES bio_11's UNLINKED status. The byline reads 嗣法門人 — 'DHARMA-HEIR disciple' — not merely 編 ('editor'). The heir-designation IS the transmission claim; it is not the editor trap (cf. 芝巖秀, who was only an editor). bio_11 could narrow him no further than 'an unnamed dharma-heir of 三峰法藏'; that man is Hongchu.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 弘儲 （明清序：076；X82n1571_p0461b03；X82n1571_p0461b13）
teacher.note: INDEPENDENT confirmation: the 五燈全書 places him under Hongchu's 法嗣.

teacher.kind: 三峰藏和尚語錄 (Sanfeng Fazang's record)
teacher.quote: 久依座下，如四弘願、耳圓應…燮雲璣、什菴叡…各囑以最後法語。…四方一切往來書問，盡委弘儲。
teacher.note: He attended Fazang for years and was at his deathbed — but the same passage records that Fazang handed everything over to HONGCHU. Long attendance on Fazang is association, not transmission; DILA lists Fazang as a second teacher, and both are recorded here.

dates.note: ⚠ I DO NOT ACCEPT THIS. It cannot be right: he compiled Hongchu's 語錄, whose Lingyan section covers events down to 甲辰 = 1664 (「和尚建大法化吳越三十年，至甲辰得二十會」). A man dead in 1648 cannot compile a book about 1664. Either the 五燈全書 date refers to something else (an abbacy?) or it is simply wrong. I record NO death year and flag the conflict.

dates.quote: 示寂：順治戊子（《五燈全書》卷84）；疑年錄:391
dates.note: 順治戊子=1648-01-25~1649-02-10 (lunar-year boundary). 通州人, 天臺國清.

dates.quote: 座元燮雲璣公密受印記，閉關國清無畏堂中，終其身未嘗出世。入寂之日…
dates.note: no explicit year in own 語錄; death from 五燈全書/疑年錄

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
school.note: Specifically the Sanfeng (三峰) sub-branch, via Fazang and Hongchu.

bio.quote: 通州人，天臺國清僧人。
燮雲機禪師國清無畏堂語錄一卷

bio: Of the Lu (魯) family of Yuechi county, Shunqing prefecture, northern Sichuan; his mother was a Zhou. Born on the eighth of the twelfth month of 1633 (癸酉腊八, = January 1634). His father took him at four to read at Yashan monastery in the county, and he wept whenever he heard the monks chanting the Huayan. In 1642 the rebels overran the region; in 1643 both his parents died within days of each other at Hutou monastery; in 1644 he was carried off by the rebels and dragged through seven of their camps. In 1652 he heard that 'the Old Man' — Sanshan Denglai — had settled at Gaoliang in Zhongnan, and was brought to him by the garrison commander of Shibao and the layman Yuan Baoshan. Denglai received him gladly, tonsured him, and set him the huatou 'who is it that recites the Buddha's name?'. He served as attendant, deputy prior and then prior through nine monasteries. In 1663 he went with Denglai to found Gaofeng; when Denglai left for Tanhua, the building of Gaofeng was left in Xingchong's hands, and he finished it in 1666. Denglai named him among the heirs charged to go out and teach. He was abbot of Baoji monastery in Wanxian.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author: 大笑性崇 himself
steles.author_note: Spoken from the high seat in the winter of 戊辰 (1688) at the request of the two halls' officers, and taken down
steles.quote: 山僧乃本川北道順慶府岳池縣魯氏子…母周氏…於癸酉腊八日乃生。…壬辰，如忠南聞老人卓錫高梁，山僧決志脫塵…將山僧送至老人座前，老人喜與雉染，命參念佛是誰…至癸卯，隨老人開創高峰，工未竣，老人應向化侯府請住曇華，將高峰院事囑累山僧…丙午工竣，迎老人歸高峰開爐。
steles.note: FIRST-PERSON. He tells his own life from the seat. The 'Old Man' (老人) throughout is Sanshan Denglai, identified beyond doubt by Gaofeng and Tanhua, the two monasteries Denglai founded.

teacher.quote: 老人喜與雉染，命參念佛是誰…至癸卯，隨老人開創高峰
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11's single-source identification. bio_11 warned that the equation of 三山 with 燈來 rested only on Sichuan geography; it does not — the 行實 ties him to Gaofeng and Tanhua, and DILA has Denglai's own 年譜 naming him.

teacher.quote: 《高峰三山來禪師年譜》卷1：「又囑紫垣性貴、天湖性定、雲林性現、大笑性崇俟時行化」
teacher.note: ⭐ DECISIVE INDEPENDENT SOURCE: Denglai's own year-by-year chronicle names 大笑性崇 among the heirs he charged to go out and teach.

teacher.kind: preface to 玉眉亮's 語錄 by 沈廷勱
teacher.quote: 門人中相與唱酬者，有天湖定公、雲林現公、大笑崇公、冷眼證公
teacher.note: A third witness listing him among Denglai's disciples.

dates.quote: 於癸酉腊八日乃生。
dates.note: 癸酉 twelfth month, eighth day = 1634-01-07 Gregorian. DILA A016597 agrees.

dates.quote: 清康熙二十七年，年五十六。（疑年錄：467）
dates.note: Alive in 1688 at 56 sui. ⚠ NO DEATH YEAR is recorded anywhere I could find.

school.note: Linji via the Juyun (聚雲) line: 吹萬廣真 → 鐵壁慧機 → 三山燈來 → 大笑性崇.

bio: Of the Lin (林) family of Yueqing in Wenzhou; a dharma heir of Hengchuan Rugong, of the Songyuan branch of Yangqi Linji. He studied under Jianweng Jing of Xuedou in Mingzhou, Shilin Gong of Nanping and Jue'an Zhen of Chengtian. He was abbot of Baoning at Jinling (Nanjing) under the Yuan. His heirs included Liao'an Qingyu, Zhongmou Liangyou and the Japanese monks Jikusen Bonsen (竺仙梵僊) and Sekishitsu Zenkyu (石室善玖); Jikusen carried his line to Japan, where the Kurin (古林) school became one of the twenty-four schools of Japanese Zen. Born 1262, died 1329.

steles.title: 古林和尚碑
steles.author_note: unnamed in what I could reach; the inscription is in 《古林清茂禪師拾遺偈頌》卷2
steles.quote: 景定壬戌八月一日 … 天曆己巳十一月二十二日
steles.note: ⚠ ATTESTED VIA DILA, NOT READ DIRECTLY. DILA A001087 cites 〈古林和尚碑〉 in 拾遺偈頌 卷2 as the source of both his birth and death dates. The 拾遺偈頌 also carries a 行實 by 友梅 (X/X71/X71n1412.xml lb 0408a10: 「拾遺偈頌行實　友梅撰」). I located both but did not read the carved text in full.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author: 友梅
steles.author_note: in the 拾遺偈頌 appended to his 語錄
steles.quote: 拾遺偈頌行實　友梅撰
steles.note: Located by heading; not read in full.

steles.title: 古林和尚行實
steles.author: (unsigned, prefixed to 古林清茂禪師拾遺偈頌)
steles.quote: 師諱清茂，字古林，號金剛幢，晚稱休居叟，溫州樂清林氏子…以宋咸淳壬戌八月一日而誕
steles.note: Full documentary life-record: birth 1262, tonsure, awakening under Hengchuan at 19.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense at his 開堂 at 天平白雲禪寺
teacher.quote: 次拈香云：諸佛出世，以心傳心；祖師西來，將法付法…諸方長老出世，各各以香為信，香何信之有？當知信不在香而在法也。天平今日此香爇向爐中，奉為先住阿育王山廣利禪寺楊岐第十世橫川大和尚，但陳供養，夫復何言？
teacher.note: The SECOND stick (the first was 祝延今上皇帝). He even glosses the ritual himself — the incense is 信, and the 信 is in the dharma, not the incense. Then names 橫川大和尚. First-person, at the transmission. Top rung.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 on 橫川's memorial day (忌辰)
teacher.quote: 橫川和尚忌辰，拈香云：者老漢生前莽鹵…今朝特地一鑪香，聽得驢鳴也斷腸。
teacher.note: He keeps Hengchuan's death-anniversary as his master's. A second, independent 忌辰 incense (X71n1412 lb 0222b) explicitly frames it with the two canonical repay-the-master analogies: 「巴陵報雲門之恩…楊岐為慈明設齋」.

teacher.kind: 古林和尚行實 (his 行實 / life-record)
teacher.quote: 師聞其風，兼程進謁…川顧師云：僧問雲門：不起一念，還有過也無？…師豁然大悟…便禮拜，川與一蹋。自此機感相投，造詣日深，時十九歲…川每曰：唯寶、茂二師能知老僧舌頭落處。
teacher.note: The awakening under 橫川如珙, told in his own 行實. 「茂」 is Qingmao.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 如珙 （望月‧卷六‧附錄：051）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11.

dates.quote: 景定壬戌八月一日（birth）… 天曆己巳十一月二十二日（death）
dates.note: Birth 1262-08-24, death 1329-12-20. Both from the stone. Matches bio_11.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派　元代臨濟宗楊岐派松源派僧

bio.note: From 佛百 3943.1, 疑年錄 313.

bio: Of the Zhao (趙) family of Wujiang in Suzhou prefecture; his given name was originally Yu (庾). His forebears held office; his father died when he was a child and his uncle, a censor, raised him — and, being drawn to Buddhism himself, passed on to the boy whatever he found in the old lamp records. Xingtao passed the provincial examination young and took the jinshi in his prime, the leading man of his district. He served as magistrate of Ouning in Fujian and was being promoted when the dynasty fell; he shaved his head and hid at Wuyi. He went to Guoqing to find TUIWENG HONGCHU (called 大山儲 in the inscription) and missed him twice. He then took the robe from Baoen Xian (浮石通賢) at Wujiang, trained under him for two years without opening, and broke through at a winter retreat at Haimen; Xian approved him and he took the full precepts. When Hongchu returned to Lingyan, Xingtao carried incense to him and questioned him closely; under Hongchu's answers on Linji's three kinds of student he saw clear through, offered a verse, and HONGCHU SEALED HIM WITH A VERSE OF HIS OWN. Hongchu then said: 'You are a man of Wu; you came to the way by way of office. Guoqing is my old house — Hanshan, Shide and Fenggan left their traces there. I hand it to you.' He entered Guoqing in the autumn of 1650. He died on the twenty-fifth of the seventh month of 1652.

steles.title: 天台國清韜禪師衣缽塔銘
steles.author_note: ⚠ The author's signature is not preserved in the text I could reach.
steles.quote: 師諱行韜，字大庾，蘇郡吳江趙氏子，本名庾。…彊年成進士…出宰閩甌寧…遭時喪亂，薙髮隱武夷。尋造國清，禮大山儲和尚…乃就吳江，禮報恩賢和尚，更今名…而山復住靈嵒，乃懷香注謁，頻叩從上宗乘中事…師言下洞明宗旨，遽呈偈…山印以偈云：「南公當日見慈明，汗下通身未是真，一自臺山開隻眼，風流千古起家聲。」師禮謝。…天寧期畢，山語之曰：「子本吳人，初以宰官得度…國清是吾舊院，寒拾豐干，芳規具在，今以累子。」…師乃以庚寅秋入院。
steles.note: A jinshi and magistrate who became a monk after the Ming collapse. The stele separates ordination (from 報恩賢 = 浮石通賢) from transmission (from 大山儲 = 退翁弘儲, who sealed him with a verse and handed him Guoqing). CONFIRMS bio_11 exactly.

teacher.quote: 山印以偈云：「南公當日見慈明…」師禮謝。
teacher.note: Sealed with a verse by Hongchu. Ordination by 浮石通賢 is explicitly a separate, earlier event.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 弘儲 （明清序：076；X82n1571_p0462a01；X82n1571_p0462a14）
teacher.note: Independent confirmation from the 五燈全書.

dates.source: DILA A000427, quoting the 衣缽塔銘
dates.quote: 「春秋始壬辰七月二十五日。」(《國清大庾韜禪師語錄》卷一〈天台國清韜禪師衣缽塔銘〉)
dates.note: Death 1652-08-28. ⚠ NO BIRTH YEAR is recorded — DILA has none, and the stele as preserved gives none.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
school.note: Sanfeng sub-branch, via Hongchu.

bio: Of Zhongzhou in Sichuan. He belonged to the Juyun (聚雲) house and was a disciple of ER'AN DENGSONG (耳菴燈嵩), who had received the robe and bowl from 'Patriarch Three-Slaps' (三巴掌 = Tiemei Huili). Sanshan Denglai, at whose assembly Yumei was a fellow-student, pointed him out and said 'this is Brother Er'an's lion cub'. He was received as abbot of Tianning Chan monastery on Mt. Wufeng in Zhongzhou on the eighteenth of the ninth month of 1669, and he refers to his late master throughout as 'the old abbot of Tianning'. His recorded sayings in one fascicle survive.

teacher.kind: preface by 沈廷勱, a lay friend who knew him personally
teacher.quote: 夫耳菴嵩和尚紹三巴掌祖之傳，今師繼之，能裕其後。…老人嘗指目之曰：「此耳菴兄獅子兒也。」…康熙庚午秋九月上浣，嘉禾法弟沈廷勱頓首撰。
teacher.note: ⚠ RESOLVES bio_11's UNLINKED status. Two statements in one preface (1690): (a) Er'an Dengsong inherited from Patriarch Sanbazhang and 'the present master continued it'; (b) 'the Old Man' (Sanshan Denglai, whose disciples the preface has just listed) called Yumei 'Brother Er'an's lion cub' — i.e. Er'an's disciple. The writer knew him face to face.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 燈嵩 — 《玉眉亮禪師語錄》卷1：「若玉眉禪師……此耳菴兄獅子兒也」(J39nB443_p0333a07)
teacher.note: DILA reaches the same conclusion from the same preface.

teacher.kind: his own佛事 for his late master
teacher.quote: 安本師和尚真…「天寧老和尚來也！」…為本師和尚掃塔…某甲昔在熊耳菴中咬著一粒…
teacher.note: In his own words his 本師 ('own master') is 'the old abbot of TIANNING' — the seat Yumei himself took in 1669 — and he recalls his time 'in the Xiong'er hermitage' (熊耳菴), from which Er'an (耳菴) takes his name.

school.note: Juyun branch of Linji: 吹萬廣真 → 鐵眉慧麗 (三巴掌) → 耳菴燈嵩 → 玉眉燈亮.

bio: Of the Luo (羅) family of Pengchi in Pengzhou, Sichuan. As a small boy he heaped up mud and sand into the shape of stupas; when the monk Zudeng of Anguo monastery on Mt. Yuzhang came to the house he pressed his palms together, and Zudeng laid a hand on his head and asked whether he would follow him. He was tonsured at nineteen. Zudeng taught him the pratyutpanna nianfo samadhi, which did not suit him; he went to the lecture halls of Chengdu and studied the Nature treatises, then said 'is scholastic learning the final dharma? — I have tasted enough', and went south out of the Three Gorges. He saw Huai'an Zhao at Zhaojue, Zhewong Ruyan at Jingshan, and followed Gaoyuan Zuquan to Ruiyan in Taizhou. Zuquan could not open him and at last said 'my devices are exhausted and you will not look — the connection is not here; go and see Xuedou', and Liaohui went. THE MAN THEN HOLDING THE SEAT AT XUEDOU WAS FOJIAN WUZHUN SHIFAN. He was abbot of Dinghui, then Nengren in Dongjia, Donglin in Jiangzhou and Tiantong in Mingzhou, retiring at last to Huanzhi hermitage. He died on the twenty-second of the third month of 1262, aged 65.

steles.title: 行狀 (No. 1391-B)
steles.author_note: unnamed; appended to his own 語錄
steles.quote: 師名了惠，蜀之蓬州蓬池羅氏子。…十九薙髮…去謁壞菴照於昭覺…見浙翁琰於徑山。聞高原泉孤硬，徑直往依之…泉曰：「吾方便婁矣，汝自不顧。盖緣法不在此，其往見雪竇乎？」時主雪竇席者，佛鑑無準範也。師造席下，自陳來歷。範呵曰：「熟歇去。」
steles.note: ⭐ The 行狀 NAMES WUZHUN OUTRIGHT — 「時主雪竇席者，佛鑑無準範也」. bio_11 had noted that the transmission incense named the teacher only by title and seat (佛鑑, Jingshan) and had to reason by analogy with Wu'an Puning; that inference is now unnecessary. The account-of-conduct says the name.

teacher.quote: 時主雪竇席者，佛鑑無準範也。師造席下，自陳來歷。
teacher.note: Named in full in his own account-of-conduct. CONFIRMS bio_11 and removes its caveat.

teacher.quote: 無準師範（1178-1249）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十一世。

dates.quote: 景定三年三月廿二日，壽六十五（《西巖了慧禪師語錄》卷2〈行狀〉）
dates.note: Death 1262-04-19; birth 1198 back-computed from age 65. Both from the 行狀.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Of the Zeng (曾) family of Dianjiang in Sichuan; his lay name was Zeng Bubo. He held a Confucian degree and sat the examinations repeatedly without success. A monk brought him Chuiwan Guangzhen's Gu yin wang zhuan; he read it over and over 'as if drunk, as if waking', then got hold of the records of Tiebi Huiji and of Master Bazhang, and 'the mind-flower opened'. He swore to himself: 'one day I shall be a child of the Juyun house.' His mother died when he was twenty-six and his father three years later; within two months of the funeral the country rose in revolt, he hid for six months, his wife died of illness, and he gave his two sons to his elder brother and took the robe from the two masters Nan and Zhe of Mt. Diaoyan. Sheltering from the war at Dongming monastery in Zhongzhou he wrote to TIEBI HUIJI and got a reply; he went into the mountains to him. He entered the hall on the twenty-sixth of the eleventh month of 1648 and broke through in 1649; he formally received Tiebi's dharma in 1654. He was abbot of Chongsheng and Xinglong in Sichuan, of Tianning in Zhejiang, and founded Gaofeng Kaixi in Zhongzhou. He wrote the Wujia zongzhi zuanyao (五家宗旨纂要), a manual of the doctrines of the five houses. He died on the eighteenth of the seventh month of 1685.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author: 三山燈來 himself
steles.author_note: Spoken from the seat at the request of the two halls' officers in the small new year of 乙未 (1655)
steles.quote: 山僧乃本川墊江曾氏子，自幼業儒、少列黌序…有僧傳得聚雲師翁《古音王傳》至，捧讀再三，若醉若醒；繼得本師《鐵老人錄》、《巴掌師錄》，焚香禮誦，心花頓開…常自矢曰：「吾異日當必為聚雲兒孫。」…遂從弔巖山南、浙二師祝髮。…寓忠州東明寺，聞老人卓錫石峰，奉書上候…遂入山參禮。
steles.note: FIRST-PERSON. He calls Chuiwan Guangzhen his 師翁 (grand-teacher) and Tiebi Huiji his 本師 (own master) — the relation is stated in his own words, in the correct generational terms.

steles.title: 高峰三山來禪師年譜
steles.author_note: compiled by his disciples
steles.quote: 「明神宗皇帝萬曆四十二年十月二十八日戌時」（birth）… 「康熙二十四年乙丑七月十八日」（death）
steles.note: A year-by-year chronological biography — the rarest and richest genre. Cited by DILA A001808 for both dates; also the source that names his heirs (大笑性崇 among them). I located it but did not read it in full.

teacher.quote: 繼得本師《鐵老人錄》…
teacher.note: He calls Tiebi Huiji 本師, 'my own master', in his own words. CONFIRMS bio_11.

teacher.quote: 參禮鐵壁慧機。順治十一年（1654）承嗣其法。（明清序：028；X84n1582_p0390a21）

dates.source: DILA A001808, quoting the 年譜
dates.quote: 「明神宗皇帝萬曆四十二年十月二十八日戌時」… 「康熙二十四年乙丑七月十八日」
dates.note: Birth 1614-11-29, death 1685-08-17. bio_11 had NO dates for him; these are new.

school.quote: 吾異日當必為聚雲兒孫
school.note: He names his own house: Juyun (聚雲), a Linji line via Dahui.
