bio: Of Yinjiang in Sinan, Guizhou; his father was a Yang, his mother a Lu. Born on the twenty-third of the eighth month of 1640. He was betrothed at thirteen, lost his father at twenty-seven, and took the precepts of abstinence at twenty-nine. He liked the Ox-herding verses, and found his way in on hearing someone read the Mencius line 'the nature of a sheep is like the nature of an ox; the nature of an ox is like the nature of a man'. Two years later he left home against his mother's wishes and was ordained by MINSHU; Minshu died within the year, and after helping raise his stupa Daole went on to SHENGKE DEYU of Huayan. Shengke beat him at their first interview until his head bled — 'and then I began to know what hurt'. Shengke offered him a verse of transmission in the spring of 1676 and he DECLINED IT. He went back to Guizhou to see his mother, held Longshan monastery for three years, retreated to Mt. Gaotun through the fighting, buried his mother, and in 1684 came out of Shu to Zunyi, where he was kept at Yuquan monastery. In the spring of 1685, hearing that Shengke had left his monastery and was staying at Fangshan in Luzhou, he went to attend him again — and this time the old master tested him with the dead phrase, the live phrase and the neither-dead-nor-alive phrase, and sealed him with a verse, a staff and a whisk. He was abbot of Huayan in western Shu.

steles.title: 行由
steles.author: 不厭道樂 himself
steles.author_note: his own account, recorded by 門人德普
steles.quote: 師字不厭，諱道樂，乃黔之思南印江人。父楊，母盧，生于庚辰八月廿三子時。…投敏樹和尚，得度受具。剛一載，敏和尚圓寂…復參華岩聖可和尚。入室，問大通智勝佛因緣，喫頓痛棒，頭破血流…于乙丑春，聞華岩和尚出院，寓瀘州方山，師復趨省覲。老和尚以死句、活句、不死不活句驗，師復印偈并拄杖拂子。
steles.note: First-person. Note that he was ORDAINED by 敏樹[如相] — association with Minshu is not transmission from him.

teacher.kind: transmission incense (拈香), his own words from the seat
teacher.quote: 此是第三回拈出，爇向爐中，專為供養現住瀘州雲峰堂上上聖下可大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION. 「上聖下可」 is the reverential spelling-out of 聖可 [德玉]. THIS SETTLES bio_11's CORPUS CONFLICT: the 五燈全書 marginal tag reading 慧覺衣嗣 is WRONG. The man's own incense, his own 行由, and the preface to his 語錄 all say Shengke Deyu.

teacher.quote: 西蜀華岩與本師不厭和尚刻錄…實聖老之子、破公之孫也。
teacher.note: 'Truly a son of old Shengke and a grandson of Master Poshan.' Independent.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 德玉 （明清序：088；X85n1589_p0114a24；X85n1589_p0114b13）
法嗣有…不厭樂…
teacher.note: Shengke's own record lists Buyan among his heirs. The edge is attested from both ends.

dates.quote: 生于庚辰八月廿三子時。
dates.note: Birth 1640-10-08 (DILA A016622 agrees, citing this 行由).

dates.quote: 清康熙二十九年時，年五十一。（疑年錄：471）
dates.note: ⚠ Alive in 1690 at 51 sui. NO DEATH YEAR recorded anywhere. bio_11's 'floruit 1685' is consistent.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派
school.note: Via 破山海明 → 聖可德玉.

bio: Lay surname Tao (陶), of Taihe in Ji'an; a dharma heir of Xiaoweng Miaokan (1177-1248), nineteenth generation below Huineng. He came out as abbot of Jianfu monastery in Raozhou in the sixth month of 1227, moved to Kaixian on Lushan, and returned to Jianfu in 1229. He wrote the accounts-of-conduct (行狀) of his own teacher Xiaoweng and of Chijue Daochong — the two are quoted as authorities on monastic layout in later handbooks. His heir was Yusou Chengjian. He died in 1271, aged 59. His dharma name is written both 道燦 and 道璨.

teacher.kind: transmission incense (拈香), his own words at the opening of the hall
teacher.quote: 爇向爐中，奉為前住慶元府阿育王山廣利禪寺笑翁大和尚，用酧法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION. He burns the incense of gratitude for XIAOWENG, former abbot of Guangli monastery on Mt. Ayuwang. CONFIRMS bio_11 beyond doubt.

teacher.quote: 笑翁妙堪（1177-1248）禪師法嗣…《五燈全書》卷53：「饒州薦福無文燦禪師，吉安泰和人，從育王得法。」

teacher.kind: 禪林象器箋, quoting his own writing
teacher.quote: 無文印笑翁堪禪師行狀云…
teacher.note: He WROTE Xiaoweng's account-of-conduct — a disciple's office. Corroborates the relation from a third direction.

dates.quote: 咸淳七年卒，年五十九。（宋僧著：571）
dates.note: Death 1271; birth 1213 back-computed from age 59. bio_11 had NO dates for him; these are new.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Of Xin'an; lay surname Bao (鮑). His father Bao Qinjiao was a prefectural student; his mother dreamed of a tablet reading 'Hall of Accumulated Good' before she conceived. Born on the twenty-fourth of the tenth month of 1623. He failed the examinations at eighteen, and at nineteen left his parents for Jinling, met a monk on the road who urged him to practise, and was tonsured at Yixing. At twenty he took the full precepts from Zhuanyu Guanheng at Qingliang monastery in the capital. He heard friends talk of the Chan gate, read the Changuan cejin, threw over doctrinal study and went to Lingao at Yaofeng in Suzhou, then to Shiyu Mingfang at Dongta monastery in Jiaxing, where — after a fortnight with an unbreakable doubt-mass and a night without sleep — the great drum sounded at dawn in the Buddha hall and his chest fell open. THE HEAD MONK OF THAT ASSEMBLY WAS HIS OWN MASTER-TO-BE, JIE'AN [WUJIN]. He went on to Feiyin Tongrong at Jinsu and traded pushes with him on the abbot's steps. His transmission, however, came from JIE'AN WUJIN (介菴悟進) of Jinming monastery in Jiaxing, and he says so from the seat, at the opening of the hall, in the reverential form. He was abbot at Huanglian and at Qizhou. He belongs to the DUANQIAO (斷橋) branch of Linji — a rare surviving line outside the Miyun Yuanwu mainstream — and calls his master the thirty-first generation of it.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author: 黃蓮東巖 himself
steles.author_note: spoken from the abbot's room at the end of the summer retreat of 順治丁酉 (1657), at the officers' request
steles.quote: 余新安人，俗姓鮑，父諱秦交，字上孚，係府庠。母胡氏…生余於天啟癸亥十月二十四日也。…至十九歲，辭親扺金陵，途遇一僧，激發修行，指往宜興，禮見明師染薙。二十，造京都清涼寺，受上顓下愚和尚具足戒。…往嘉禾東塔寺求單，正值石雨和尚結冬期也…將黎明，佛殿發大鼓聲，胸中便脫然得個安樂境界。時本師介和尚為居首眾。
steles.note: FIRST-PERSON. He begins by refusing — 'why should I wag my lips?' — and then tells everything.

teacher.kind: transmission incense (拈香) at the opening of the hall
teacher.quote: 此瓣香…爇向爐中，專為供養現住浙江嘉興府金明堂上傳臨濟正宗、斷橋嫡派三十一世本師介菴老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION, and it names the BRANCH as well as the man: 'my own master, old venerable JIE'AN, of the Jinming hall in Jiaxing, thirty-first generation of the direct Duanqiao line of orthodox Linji.' CONFIRMS bio_11 exactly.

teacher.quote: 師嗣法于金明和尚，為是以續斷橋一枝燈也。
teacher.note: Independent.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 悟進 （明清序：146；X82n1571_p0444a23）

dates.quote: 生余於天啟癸亥十月二十四日也。
dates.note: Birth 1623-11-16 (DILA A016487 agrees, citing this 行實). ⚠ NO DEATH YEAR recorded; DILA has none either, only 'in 1662 he was 40'.

school.quote: 傳臨濟正宗、斷橋嫡派三十一世
school.note: He names his own branch: Duanqiao. CONFIRMS bio_11's observation that this is a rare line outside the Miyun mainstream.

bio: Lay surname Chen (陳), of Nanchang; a dharma heir of Huiji Yuanxi (1238-1319), twenty-first generation below Huineng. He left home at Shuilu cloister, first called on Yishan of Kaixian, then went to Huiji Yuanxi. In 1328 the Yuan emperor Wenzong turned his former princely residence at Jinling into the monastery Longxiang Jiqing and ordered Daxin to open it — one of the most powerful monastic offices of the age; he was made Grand Master of the Palace (太中大夫) and titled Chan Master Guangzhi Quanwu. Under Emperor Shundi he was commanded to revise the Baizhang Rules (敕修百丈清規). His heirs included Zongle and Zhengzu. He died in 1344, aged 61, with 46 years in robes.

steles.title: …大禪師住持大龍翔集慶寺釋教宗主兼領五山寺訢公塔銘 (并序)
steles.author: 黃溍
steles.author_note: Huang Jin (1277-1357), Vice Director of the Palace Library (秘書少監) and one of the four great prose stylists of the Yuan
steles.quote: 大禪師住持大龍翔集慶寺釋教宗主兼領五山寺訢公塔銘(并序)　No. 1367-C
steles.note: ⭐ A STUPA INSCRIPTION BY ONE OF THE GREAT PROSE WRITERS OF THE YUAN. The 語錄 itself refers to it at lb 0201a10 (「學士虞公集行道記、秘書少監黃公溍塔銘中，大略…」) alongside a 行道記 by Yu Ji (虞集), another of the four. TWO major literati wrote his life. I located both; I did not read them in full — a follow-up should.

steles.title: 行道記
steles.author: 虞集
steles.author_note: Yu Ji (1272-1348), Hanlin academician
steles.quote: 學士虞公集行道記、秘書少監黃公溍塔銘中，大略…
steles.note: Referenced in his 語錄; located but not read in full.

steles.kind: 碑銘 (attested, text not in corpus)
steles.title: 廣智全悟大禪師碑銘
steles.author: 黃溍 (黃文獻公)
steles.quote: 黃文獻公為撰碑銘，虞文靖公著行道記，其述禪師行業甚備。元季兵亂，左右皆軍壘，院與記俱廢，唯銘獨存。
steles.note: IMPORTANT LEAD, NOT A CITATION: Song Lian records that 笑隱 DID have a full stele by 黃溍 and a 行道記 by 虞集 (虞文靖公, in his 學古錄) — and that the 行道記 was destroyed in the late-Yuan wars while the 銘 alone survived (唯銘獨存). Neither text is in the CBETA corpus (『今載集中』 — they are in the authors' collected works). Anyone with 黃溍《金華黃先生文集》 or 虞集《道園學古錄》 can take this man to a clean A. I have NOT cited their contents because I have not read them.

teacher.kind: the prefatory life attached to HIS OWN 語錄 (廣智全悟禪師語錄)
teacher.quote: 廣智全悟大禪師諱大訢，字笑隱，龍興南昌陳氏子。依郡之水陸院彰上人視髮。首叅一山萬禪師於廬山開先，久之，遣叅百丈晦機熈公。公示以本色鉗鎚，成大法器。熈公遷淨慈，師隨至掌外記。
teacher.note: TRAP KEPT APART, and the text does it for us: 彰上人 TONSURED him; 一山了萬 was his FIRST teacher and 遣 — SENT HIM AWAY — to 晦機元熙; 晦機 『示以本色鉗鎚，成大法器』 and he then followed 晦機 to 淨慈 as his secretary. The maker is 晦機. (Note: this edition prints the graph as 大訴 — a 訢/訴 corruption. Same man.)

teacher.kind: 宋濂 (Song Lian, 1310-1381), 護法錄 — a near-contemporary literatus writing of 笑隱's heir 宗泐, whom he knew personally
teacher.quote: 笑隱之子，晦機之孫。具大福德，足以荷擔佛法
teacher.note: Song Lian states the two-generation chain in his own voice: 宗泐 is 笑隱's son-in-dharma and 晦機's grandson-in-dharma — which is only true if 笑隱 is 晦機's heir. Song Lian is also careful about this exact kind of claim elsewhere: at lb 0679b14-16 he DEMOLISHES a false attribution (『來復未嘗師笑隱，野史之傳訛，可…』 — 來復 was never Xiaoyin's student, the unofficial histories got it wrong). A witness who publicly corrects lineage errors is a good witness for the ones he affirms.

teacher.quote: 晦機元熙（1238-1319）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十一世…復參晦機元熙。（望月‧卷六‧附錄：050）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11.

dates.note: Both from his own 語錄, immediately before the 塔銘. bio_11 had NO dates; these are new.

school.note: Linji/Yangqi by descent from Huiji Yuanxi.

bio.kind: 塔銘 by 黃溍 + 行道記 by 虞集

bio: Of the Wang (王) family of Gaoliang in Kuizhou (Liangshan, Sichuan); a dharma heir of Poshan Haiming (1597-1666). His recorded sayings in three fascicles survive. His own heir Miyin Zhenchuan burns the transmission incense for him at every hall-opening as 'the thirty-second generation of orthodox Linji' — which fixes Lingyin's place in the line exactly, since Poshan is the thirty-first.

teacher.quote: 今日不辭對眾拈出，爇向爐中，供養現住西川梁山雙桂堂上傳臨濟正宗三十一世上破下山本師老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: His own 靈隱文禪師語錄. 上破下山 = 破山 (海明), seated at 梁山雙桂堂 — the correct seat for 破山海明. He repeats the same dharma-milk stick at two later enthronements (lb 0362c19 '此是第二回', lb 0364c11 '此是第三回拈出…單為現住西川梁山雙桂堂上破山老人，用酬法乳之恩'), so the attribution is first-person and threefold.

teacher.quote: 為破山海明禪師（1597-1666）法嗣。夔州高梁人，俗姓王。有《靈隱文禪師語錄》三卷。（《五燈全書》卷70）　REL teacher 海明 （明清序：046；X85n1591_p0228b21）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11. Teacher is an existing roster node, so the subtree lands.

teacher.kind: his HEIR 密印真傳's transmission incense
teacher.quote: 爇向爐中，供養傳臨濟正宗第三十二世上靈下隱和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: Repeated four times (lb 0809c17, 0811b26, 0814a15, 0816b14). Confirms bio_11's generation arithmetic exactly: Poshan is the 31st, so Lingyin at the 32nd is Poshan's direct heir.

dates.note: ⚠ NO DATES. DILA records neither birth nor death, and I could find none. His heir's 語錄 records 「為靈隱老人入塔」 (J35nB343 lb 0818c20) — the interment of his stupa — but gives no year.

dates.kind: 靈隱老人塔銘 by heir 真傳
dates.quote: 師號靈隱，諱印文…至丁未春，世緣已畢，坐脫於貴筑之大興寺…時康熙七年歲次戊申…勒石建立
dates.note: 丁未=康熙6=1667 death; 塔 built 康熙7戊申1668. NOTE: X84n1585 '世壽七十三' is 靈隱文泰 (少室 heir) — a different 靈隱, name collision.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.note: ⚠ Thin — a few lines only. His own 語錄 exists in three fascicles but I did not locate it in the corpus tree; a follow-up should.

bio: Southern Song Caodong master; a dharma heir of Donggu Miaoguang. Nothing more is recorded of him.

teacher.quote: 東谷光禪師法嗣一人直翁舉禪師
teacher.note: 續傳燈錄 j.35 目錄 — teacher 東谷妙光 confirmed

teacher.quote: 直翁舉禪師法嗣一人天童岫禪師見錄
teacher.note: his own heir 天童岫, confirming his place in the chain

teacher.quote: 東谷光禪師法嗣。（T51n2077_p0701a11）　REL teacher 妙光 （望月‧卷六‧附錄：048）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11, which had reconstructed the chain from X72n1431 and cross-checked it against X81n1571 / X84n1583. DILA agrees and cites 續傳燈錄.

dates.note: ⚠ NO DATES AT ALL. DILA has none; I found none.

bio.note: ⚠⚠ THE RECORD IS ALL BUT SILENT. DILA's entire entry on him is one line: '東谷光禪師法嗣'. The teacher edge is sound; there is NO biography to write, and I will not invent one. bio_11's full chain (直翁德舉 ← 東谷妙光 ← 明極慧祚 ← 自得慧暉) stands and is independently confirmed by DILA's teacher relation.

bio: Lay surname Yang (楊), of Baodi (near Tianjin); born on the fifteenth of the ninth month of 1614. Abbot of the Zhengfa monastery at Guzhongpan on Mt. Pan (Jizhou, near Tianjin). He said from the seat in old age 'this old monk has been in the world seventy-five years'. His recorded sayings in four fascicles survive, cut by his disciple Langkong Shun. He is the heir of DABO XINGQIAN, whom he names in his transmission incense as 'the thirty-sixth generation of the orthodox line of Caoxi'.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author_note: in 《盤山了宗禪師語錄》卷4
steles.quote: 「師誕日甲寅九月十五日……老僧住世七十五歲。」
steles.note: Cited by DILA A001367 for his birth. Located but not read in full.

teacher.kind: transmission incense (拈香), his own words
teacher.quote: 端為供養中盤堂上傳曹溪正脈第三十六代上大下博本師和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, repeated at each hall (lb 0026b14, 0027c14, 0030b11 — the last as 「先師大博和尚」, 'my late master Dabo'). CONFIRMS bio_11's 大博乾.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 行乾 （明清序：096；X82n1571_p0523c13；X82n1571_p0524a06）
法嗣有溟波古、解三洪、聖心覺、佛藏正…等諸位禪師…盤山中盤等諸剎
teacher.note: Dabo's own record confirms he held Mt. Pan (中盤) — the seat Liaozong inherited.

dates.quote: 「師誕日甲寅九月十五日……老僧住世七十五歲。」（《盤山了宗禪師語錄》卷4〈行實〉）
dates.note: Birth 1614-10-17; death computed 1688 from 'seventy-five years in the world'. bio_11 had no dates.

school.quote: 傳曹溪正脈第三十六代

bio: Abbot of Dongta monastery in Jiaxing; a dharma heir of Baofang Jin. Nothing further is recorded.

teacher.kind: 徑石滴乳集 biography, under the heading 天目進禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 嘉興東墖野翁曉禪師參天目…師於言下豁然…目云：如是！如是！即付師偈曰：真性本無性，真法本無法，了知無法性，何〔…〕
teacher.note: 付 — HE HANDED IT OVER, with a verse. The transmission verb, plus the verse itself. Note the variant 東墖 (墖 for 塔) — the brief's warning character, hiding him from a naive grep.

teacher.kind: 同書 heir-index, 徑山下第十世
teacher.quote: 天目進禪師法嗣：東塔野翁曉禪師

teacher.kind: lineage chain, 百丈清規證義記
teacher.quote: 寧傳杭州天目寶方進。進傳嘉興東塔野翁曉。曉傳嘉興無趣如空。
teacher.note: Gives the teacher's full name — 天目寶方進 — and his own heir, 無趣如空.

teacher.quote: 嘉興府東塔僧人，寶芳進法嗣。（祖燈．卷92：1791；明清序：025；X63n1244_p0497b07）　REL teacher 寶芳進 （明清序：025；X67n1308_p0510b02）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11's teacher. Note the name expansion the coordinator flagged: 野翁曉 = 野翁真曉 — DILA gives the full dharma name.

dates.note: ⚠ NO DATES. None recorded.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.note: ⚠⚠ ALL BUT SILENT. DILA's entry is one line. I will not invent prose.

bio: Of Zhongzhou in Sichuan; lay surname Wan (萬). He wanted to leave the world as a child and got his parents' leave; he left home at sixteen and at twenty-two took the precepts from XIANGYA XINGTING, whom he attended for three years. He then travelled to seek the way, went to Shuanggui and met POSHAN HAIMING, submitted to him and took the disciple's place, and shirked no labour; in time he was made prior. He was invited to Bazhou and preached at Zhongfeng and Jingci. He is described as unbending to the last and never willing to borrow another man's authority. On the sixteenth of the fourth month of 1669 he sat down in the hall at Shigu monastery in his own prefecture after the morning gruel, put out his right foot, said 'Do you understand? I am going; the whole ten-direction world is just THIS', spoke a verse, and died — aged 47, with 25 years in robes. Five heirs, among them Lüluo Hengxiu, raised his stupa to the left of Shigu monastery.

steles.title: 雲幻宸禪師塔記
steles.author: 李道泰
steles.author_note: 閩龍潯李道泰, magistrate of Kaihua (余守開化); he was a long friend of Yunhuan's heir Lüluo Heng, who gave him the commission. Written 康熙二十一年八月十八日 = 1682, in the Kaihua yamen.
steles.quote: 師法諱印宸，蜀之忠州人也，本姓萬氏。…十六出家，廿二歲稟戒於象崖珽禪師，侍巾缾三載。後乃訪道四方，走雙桂參破山老人，即服膺執弟子禮，法務無難。久之，命掌監寺…忽於康熙己酉四月望六日，在本郡石鼓寺粥後入堂趺坐…語畢而逝，世壽四十七，僧臘二十五。嗣法弟子恒秀林、月賢會等五人，建塔於石鼓寺之左。
steles.note: ⚠ bio_11 listed NO texts for this master. His 語錄 IS in the corpus — J/J36/J36nB353.xml — and carries this 塔記. The stele cleanly separates his PRECEPTOR (象崖性珽) from his MASTER (破山海明 at Shuanggui): 稟戒 vs 執弟子禮.

steles.title: 雲幻宸禪師塔記
steles.author: 李道泰 (prefect of 開化)
steles.quote: 嗣法弟子恒秀林、月賢會等五人，建塔於石鼓寺之左。余守開化，因與綠蘿恒禪師交深有年，固以幻師塔記授余
steles.note: Written at the request of his dharma-heir 綠蘿恒 (恒秀林), whom the author knew personally for years. Contemporary. Catalogue B35n0194 lb 0335a11 independently records the 語錄 as 『清印宸說，發林等編，王民皥序，附塔記。南嶽下第三十五世，嗣破山明。』

steles.title: 雲幻宸禪師塔記
steles.author: 李道泰
steles.author_note: Named on the title page of his 語錄: 「清 印宸說　發林等編　王民皞序　李道泰塔記」. The record was EDITED by 發林 — Hengxiu Falin, his own heir, who is the teacher of Changmu Guangdian, also in this batch.
steles.quote: 康熙己酉四月望六日，世壽四十七。
steles.note: CONFIRMS bio_5's note that the record carries a 塔記 by 李道泰.

teacher.kind: his OWN 拈香 transmission-incense at his 陞座 (雲幻宸禪師語錄卷首)
teacher.quote: 再拈香云：「此一瓣香，懷抱甚分明，八字無兩㫖，爇向罏中，端為供養現住梁山縣萬竹山福國禪寺傳曹谿正脈第三十五世破山大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。」斂衣趺坐
teacher.note: THE DHARMA-MILK STICK, verbatim, and it is the THIRD of three: (1) 祝延今上皇帝 — the emperor; (2) 奉為諸王殿下滿朝文武 — the princes and court; (3) THIS one, 用酬法乳之恩, to 破山 at 萬竹山福國禪寺. First-person, at the transmission. Note he names 破山's seat as 福國禪寺 in 梁山縣 (his brother-in-dharma 密行寂忍 names 雙桂堂 in the same county — the same master, two of his seats).

teacher.kind: 雲幻宸禪師塔記 — his stupa-record, by 李道泰 (a serving prefect: 『余守開化』), appended to his 語錄
teacher.quote: 師法諱印宸，蜀之忠州人也，本姓萬氏。 … 十六出家，廿二歲稟戒於象崖珽禪師，侍巾缾三載。後乃訪道四方，走雙桂參破山老人，即服膺執弟子禮，法務無難。久之，命掌監寺
teacher.note: TRAP KEPT APART: 象崖性珽 gave him the PRECEPTS (稟戒) and three years of attendance — that is the ordination master, NOT the dharma-father. He then went to 雙桂 (破山's seat) and took the disciple's place there. The 塔記 gives his death as 康熙己酉 (1669) 4/16 at 石鼓寺, age 47, 僧臘 25, with five dharma-heirs building the stupa.

teacher.quote: 走雙桂參破山老人，即服膺執弟子禮
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11. The precepts came from 象崖性珽; the discipleship from Poshan at Shuanggui — Poshan's own monastery.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 海明 （明清序：047；X82n1571_p0337c22）
teacher.note: The 五燈全書 also places him under Poshan.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 五燈全書
teacher.quote: 為破山海明禪師（1597-1666）法嗣…走雙桂，參破山老人，即服膺執弟子禮。(X82n1571_p0337c22)
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_5. Note DILA distinguishes his PRECEPT master 象崖珽 (稟戒於象崖珽禪師) from Poshan — kept separate.

links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the 塔記

bio: Of the Zhang (張) family of Sixian ward, Jiaxing; born 1487. He never went to the village school, yet his reasoning was mature from childhood. At eighteen something struck him and he asked his parents to let him leave home; they refused, so he sat day and night and would do no work. Three years later he slipped into Tianning monastery as a postulant. He was tonsured at Dongchan under Ang, and it was Ang's dharma-uncle JI'AN ZUO — a son of Motang Xuan — whom he served in earnest. Walking in the cloister one day he heard the chime struck in the Buddha hall and broke open; he went straight to the abbot's room, and Ji'an, seeing him come, laughed and said 'you have been robbed'. 'The thief is taken.' 'Where is the loot?' He shook out his sitting-cloth: 'A mess, a mess.' Ji'an approved him. He was head monk at Jueweng monastery in Chang'an at twenty-eight, and the old masters of Hangzhou could not stand against him in the hall. He was abbot of some twenty houses in turn, among them Anyin at Jinling (from the Jiajing era, at the invitation of the eunuch Zhang Yong) and Tianning at Jiaxing, where he died. He is described as unhurried and courteous, exact in his discipline in the smallest things, sharing every gift equally with the community, never soliciting patronage, and — after the Japanese pirate raids drove soldiers into his hall — living wholly without restraint, laughing, scolding, and unreadable. He died in the autumn of 1560, aged 74, with 52 summers. He counted himself the twenty-sixth generation from Linji. This is the man Yungu Fahui actually studied under.

steles.title: 法舟濟和尚行狀
steles.author_note: unnamed in the text I could reach
steles.quote: 師諱道濟，字法舟，生思賢里張氏。…詣東禪依昂公薙染。昂法叔吉菴祚禪師者，默堂子也，知見精確，而道行清苦，師折節事之。…偶行廊廡間，聞佛殿磬響，豁然契悟。尋趨方丈，菴望見，笑曰：「子著賊也。」師曰：「賊已收下。」…菴喜，印可之。…庚申之秋，寢疾且革…以手搖曳而逝，年七十有四。坐五十二夏。溯寶月至于臨濟，師為二十六世。
steles.note: ⚠ bio_11 listed NO text for this master. His 語錄 IS in the corpus — J/J40/J40nB491.xml, 《天寧法舟濟禪師剩語》 — and carries this full account-of-conduct.

teacher.quote: 昂法叔吉菴祚禪師者，默堂子也…師折節事之…菴喜，印可之。
teacher.note: The 行狀 distinguishes his TONSURE (from 昂公 at Dongchan) from his TRANSMISSION (印可 from 吉菴祚). CONFIRMS bio_11.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 吉菴祚 （明清序：024；X66n1296_p0007a16）

dates.quote: 庚申之秋，寢疾且革…年七十有四。坐五十二夏。
dates.note: Death autumn 1560, aged 74 → birth 1487. DILA A001560 agrees, adding 釋鑑稽古略續集 卷3. Matches bio_11 exactly.

school.quote: 溯寶月至于臨濟，師為二十六世。

bio: Of the Yang (楊) family of Tangxian; abbot of Dajue monastery in Beijing — hence the epithets 大覺 and 清涼 in the incense formulas of his heirs. A dharma heir of Huanxiu Changrun. He came south to Yue (Zhejiang) in 1591, and it was at Zhifengtu that Zhanran Yuancheng met him. Born 1552/3, died 1594/5.

teacher.kind: 湛然圓澄禪師語錄, prefatory Caodong lineage roll — written by his own dharma-grandson's circle, one generation after him
teacher.quote: …月舟載、大章書、大千潤、慈舟念。至于雲門之時，當國朝神宗、熹宗間，洞山一派亦如膏盡之燈矣。
teacher.note: 大千潤 → 慈舟念: 幻休常潤 → 慈舟方念, the last link before 圓澄 (雲門). Written within living memory — 圓澄 (1561-1626) was Fangnian's own heir — which makes this the closest thing to a contemporary index for this edge.

teacher.kind: 會稽雲門湛然澄禪師塔銘 (the heir's stele, appended to his record)
teacher.quote: 曹洞二十六世傳至慈舟，舟得一人曰澄公，是為湛然和尚。…慈舟說法於止風塗，師至，舟曰：止風塗向青山近，越王城伴滄海遙時如何？…舟又問洞上宗旨，師呈偈曰：五位君臣切要知…
teacher.note: ⚠ READ THE FIRST LINE (the brief's warning). This stele is for 圓澄, NOT for 方念 — it attests 慈舟→圓澄 (the downstream edge), and it places 慈舟 at Caodong generation 26. It does NOT attest 方念's own teacher. I am recording it so the next agent does not mistake it for Fangnian's stele.

teacher.quote: REL teacher 常潤 （明清序：025；X84n1579_p0011b17）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11.

dates.note: Both are Chinese-year ranges, not exact days. bio_11 had only 'floruit 1591' — these are new but should be shown as approximate.

bio.quote: 唐縣人，姓楊，北京大覺寺僧人。
bio.note: ⚠ Thin — DILA's whole concise entry is that one line. The rest of the prose above comes from bio_11's corpus work (the 1591 journey to Yue and the meeting with Yuancheng), which I did not re-verify.

bio: Southern Song Linji master, styled Huiweng (晦翁), sobriquet Zhenlan ('truly idle'); of Fuzhou. A dharma heir of Mu'an Anyong (d. 1173), nineteenth generation below Huineng. He was abbot of Chongfu monastery in Quanzhou and of Jingci in Hangzhou. He compiled the LIANDENG HUIYAO (聯燈會要) in thirty fascicles — one of the five great lamp records — writing its preface in the Qianguang hall in 1183 and putting it to the block.

teacher.quote: 臨安淨慈晦翁悟明禪師，字晦翁，號真懶。木菴安永（1115-1173）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十九世。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS bio_11's edge 淨慈明 ← 木庵安永.

teacher.kind: 衡山燈炳's 塔銘, by 性統
teacher.quote: 杲傳懶庵需，需傳鼓山永，永傳淨慈明，明傳苦口益…
teacher.note: ⭐ INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION FROM AN UNEXPECTED PLACE — a 1680s stupa inscription for a Sichuan master, which recites the whole Juyun lineage back to Dahui and places 淨慈明 exactly where DILA does: after 鼓山[木庵安]永. Two sources, five centuries apart, agree.

dates.note: ⚠ NO DATES recorded. He was active 1183 (the Liandeng huiyao preface).

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.note: From 聯燈會要 卷首, 續傳燈錄 卷35, 佛百 3541.2.

school: Not a Chan master — translator; placed on the chart as 'Early Chan' background
bio: Born in Kucha to an Indian father and a Kuchean princess. At nine he crossed the Indus with his mother to Kashmir and studied the Abhidharma under Bandhudatta, a cousin of the Kashmiri king; he later turned to Mahayana and Madhyamaka. Carried off to Liangzhou by the general Lü Guang and held for years, he reached Chang'an in 401 at the summons of Yao Xing, where he directed a translation bureau that produced the Lotus, Diamond, Vimalakirti and Amitabha sutras and the Madhyamaka treatises — the versions that fixed the Buddhist vocabulary of East Asia. He died at Chang'an in 413.

steles.title: 鳩摩羅什法師誄
steles.author: 僧肇 (his own disciple, d. 414 — one year after Kumārajīva)
steles.quote: 爰有什法師者，蓋先覺之遺嗣也。凝思大方，馳懷高觀，審釋道之陵遲，悼蒼生之窮藹…
steles.note: A genuinely contemporary witness — his own disciple, writing at his death. But it names NO teacher: 僧肇 calls him 「先覺之遺嗣」, heir of the earlier awakened ones, and leaves it at that. Cited here as an honest 'the contemporary source is silent on the question you are asking' finding.

teacher.kind: 出三藏記集 卷14〈鳩摩羅什傳〉(僧祐, c. 515) — the EARLIEST biography, older than 高僧傳
teacher.quote: 什年九歲，進到罽賓，遇名德法師槃頭達多，即罽賓王之從弟也。淵粹有大量，三藏九部莫不縷貫，亦日誦千偈，名播諸國。什既至，仍師事之，遂誦雜藏、中阿鋡、長阿鋡，凡四百萬言。達多每與什論議，深…
teacher.note: 師事之 — he served him as master, in Kashmir, from age nine, and what he learned was the Hinayana canon (雜藏, 中阿含, 長阿含). This is the Sarvastivadin schooling, not a Chan transmission of any kind.

teacher.quote: 後往罽賓，為其師槃頭達多具說一乘妙義。師感悟心服，即禮什為師，言：「我是和上小乘師，和上是我大乘師矣。」
teacher.note: Bandhudatta later bowed to his own pupil: 'I am your Hinayana master; you are my Mahayana master.' The teacher relation is real AND explicitly reversed in the source — which is the strongest possible proof the source is not laundering a lineage.

teacher.kind: 出三藏記集 — the OTHER teachers, kept apart
teacher.quote: 後從佛陀耶舍學十誦律。又從須利耶蘇摩諮稟大乘。乃歎曰：「吾昔學小乘，譬人不識金，以鍮石為妙矣。」
teacher.note: 佛陀耶舍 (Buddhayaśas) taught him the Vinaya; 須利耶蘇摩 (Sūryasoma) turned him to the Mahayana. If the chart ever wants the man who actually changed Kumārajīva's mind, it is Sūryasoma, not Bandhudatta. But as listed — 槃頭達多 as his first/formal teacher — the batch is correct.

teacher.quote: 什年九歲，隨母渡辛頭河，至罽賓，遇名德法師槃頭達多，即罽賓王之從弟也。
teacher.note: Huijiao's 高僧傳 (c. 530). Confirms the roster's 'Bandhudatta'.

teacher.quote: 什至即崇以師禮，從受雜藏
teacher.note: Explicitly: he honoured him as teacher and received instruction.

dates.quote: birth +0344 ; death +0413-05-29 (癸丑之年。年七十。四月十三日薨于大寺。T52n2103_p0264c18)

dates.note: DISAGREEMENT: DILA records an alternative 350–409. I took 344–413, which is DILA's own structured birth/death and matches the roster.

notes: Directed one of the most prolific translation bureaus in Buddhist history. His translations shaped the vocabulary of East Asian Buddhism.

bio: A nun of Caohou village in Shaozhou, aunt of the scholar Liu Zhilüe, who constantly recited the Mahaparinirvana Sutra. The Platform Sutra records that the still-unordained Huineng heard her recite, expounded the meaning, and when she held up the scroll and asked him about the characters said 'I do not know the characters; ask about the meaning.' She was astonished and told the village elders that he was a man of the Way — the recognition that led to Huineng being installed at the old Baolin temple. Nothing else about her is recorded; she has no dates.

bio.quote: 有儒士劉志略，禮遇甚厚。志略有姑為尼，名無盡藏，常誦《大涅槃經》。師暫聽，即知妙義，遂為解說。尼乃執卷問字，師曰：「字即不識，義即請問。」尼曰：「字尚不識，焉能會義？」師曰：「諸佛妙理，非關文字。」尼驚異之，遍告里中耆德云：「此是有道之士，宜請供養。」
劉志略姑母，曾為慧能誦《大涅槃經》。

notes: Nun mentioned in the Platform Sutra who could recite the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra. Huineng reportedly explained its meaning to her.

bio: Of the Ran 冉 family of Zhuji. He went south over the passes to Huineng and received his mind-seal, becoming one of the five great figures of Huineng's line. He then withdrew to Dangzi valley on Mount Baiya in Nanyang for some forty years. Summoned to court by Emperor Suzong in 761 and retained by Daizong, he was made National Teacher (國師) and is remembered for the koan of the National Teacher calling his attendant three times. He died in 775.

steles.title: a 碑 for 慧忠 (大證國師)
steles.author: 譯經沙門 飛錫 Feixi
steles.quote: 譯經沙門飛錫為碑紀德焉。
steles.note: Attested, text not recovered in the corpus. A lead for 全唐文.

teacher.quote: 少而好學，法受雙峯，默默全真，心承一印。
teacher.note: ⚠⚠ CONTRADICTION, recorded. Song gaoseng zhuan's ONLY statement of his Chan affiliation is 「法受雙峯」 — 'he received the dharma at Shuangfeng' — which is the mountain of Daoxin (4th patriarch) and Hongren (5th), NOT Caoxi/Huineng. The whole 3,000-character biography never mentions 慧能, 惠能, 六祖 or 曹溪 even once (I checked: zero occurrences of each). The famous identification of Huizhong as one of Huineng's 'five great masters' comes from the LAMPS (景德傳燈錄), not from the earliest biography. I do NOT flip the field — I cannot name an attested Shuangfeng-generation dharma-father (Daoxin and Hongren were long dead; 雙峯 here likely signals the East Mountain tradition broadly) — but I mark `disputed` and record that the earliest source does not support the Huineng edge. The DILA claim that he 'crossed the ridge to pay respects to Huineng and got his mind-seal' rests on the lamps.

teacher.quote: 是禪宗六祖惠能門下的五大宗匠之一…聞六祖慧能大師之名，即踰嶺叩謁，獲其心印。
teacher.note: DILA's concise entry, citing 佛光大辭典 6031. Confirms the roster's teacher.

dates.quote: birth +0675 ; death +0775
dates.note: DILA sources both to zh-Wikipedia, and adds 大曆十年在黨子谷示寂，年壽當在八十以上 — i.e. the death year (775) is firm, the birth year is an inference. The roster's 'floruit 683' has no source.

notes: Appointed National Teacher by two Tang emperors. Known for 'the National Teacher calls three times' koan.

bio: Of the Zhu 祝 family of Xin'an. He gave up meat at thirteen on seeing an animal killed, was tonsured under Tanyi, took the precepts, studied vinaya and Tiantai calming-and-insight, and finally 'completed the supreme vehicle under Daji Daoyi' — Mazu. From 790 he taught in Fujian and Zhejiang, subdued a tiger at Kuaiji in 791, and was later summoned to Chang'an, where he presided at Xingshan Monastery. He died in the second month of 817 in the Hall of Transmitting the Dharma (傳法堂), aged 63 — the hall that gives Bai Juyi's memorial inscription its name. His stupa was titled 元和正真之塔.

steles.title: 西京興善寺傳法堂碑並序
steles.author: 白居易
steles.path: Y/Y40/Y40n0038.xml (quoting 全唐文 卷六七八)
steles.quote: 既師與西堂藏，甘泉賢，勒潭海，百巖暉，俱父事大寂（道一），若兄弟然。
steles.note: The stele stood at 惟寬's own 傳法堂 at 興善寺 — the hall in which, per 宋高僧傳, he gave his final sermon and died (0768a13: 「十二年二月晦，大說於傳法堂訖，奄然而化」). Not in CBETA proper; the corpus quotes it.

teacher.lb: quoted at 印順《中國禪宗史》 — 白居易〈西京興善寺傳法堂碑並序〉,《全唐文》卷六七八
teacher.kind: his own 碑 (傳法堂碑), by 白居易 (772–846), his lay disciple and a named contemporary
teacher.quote: 自四祖以降，雖嗣法有冢嫡，而支派猶大宗小宗焉。以世族譬之，既師（指興善惟寬）與西堂藏，甘泉賢，勒潭海，百巖暉，俱父事大寂（道一），若兄弟然。
teacher.note: 俱父事大寂 — 'all served 大寂 [道一] AS A FATHER'. 惟寬's own stele, written for him by 白居易, who knew him personally (宋高僧傳 confirms 「白樂天為宮…」 at his death). The stele text itself is not in CBETA — it survives in 全唐文 卷六七八 — but it is quoted verbatim in the corpus at Y40n0038 (印順《中國禪宗史》). The citation is exact and the stele is a well-attested Tang text; I quote only what the corpus file contains.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 惟寬傳 (贊寧, 988) — visibly derived from 白居易's 碑
teacher.quote: 釋惟寬，姓祝氏，衢州信安人也。… 求翦髮於僧曇，受尸羅於僧崇，學毘尼於僧如，證大乘法於止觀，成最上乘於大寂道一。
teacher.note: This single sentence is the textbook demonstration of the brief's own rule. It lists FIVE teachers and keeps them strictly apart: 僧曇 TONSURED him, 僧崇 gave him the PRECEPTS, 僧如 taught him VINAYA, 止觀 gave him the Mahayana teaching — and only 大寂道一 gave him 最上乘, the supreme vehicle. Association is not transmission, and the Tang source says so itself. Corroborated at 0761b01: 「（道一）其門弟子曰惟寬、懷暉。」

teacher.kind: authority record (quoting 宋高僧傳 T50n2061_p0768a16)
teacher.quote: 成最上乘於大寂道一
teacher.note: 大寂 is Mazu Daoyi's posthumous title (大寂禪師). Confirms the roster's teacher.

dates.quote: （元和）十二年二月晦。大說於傳法堂訖奄然而化。報齡六十三。僧夏三十九。
dates.note: Death 817, age 63 → birth 755. Matches the roster.

notes: Hongzhou school master at Xingshan Temple in Chang’an. Teacher of the poet Bai Juyi, who wrote his memorial inscription in 819.

bio: One of Mazu's foremost heirs. After awakening under Mazu he withdrew to Mount Nanquan in Chizhou and, by the tradition, did not come down for some thirty years, calling himself 'Old Teacher Wang' (王老師). He is the master of the cat-killing case (南泉斬貓) and of the exchange 'ordinary mind is the Way' with Zhaozhou, who came to him as a novice and stayed. He died in 835.

teacher.quote: 馬祖道一（709-788）禪師法嗣

teacher.kind: 趙州語錄并行狀 (his heir's record)
teacher.quote: 趙州真際禪師語錄并行狀卷上（南嶽下四世嗣南泉願）…師初隨本師行脚到南泉
teacher.note: Zhaozhou's own 行狀 places Nanquan in the Nanyue (Mazu) line, four generations down.

dates.quote: birth +0748 ; death +0835-01-31 (太和甲寅歲十月二十一日示疾…)
dates.note: Matches the roster's 748–835.

notes: One of Mazu's 'three great disciples'. Often called 'Old Teacher Wang' (王老師). After enlightenment under Mazu, retreated to Mount Nanquan for 30 years. Famous for killing the cat (南泉斬貓) and 'ordinary mind is the Way' (平常心是道). Had seventeen dharma heirs.

bio: He went to Jiangxi to study under Baizhang Huaihai and became his chief disciple. Sent to open Mount Gui in Tanzhou, he built the community there from nothing; with his heir Yangshan Huiji he founded the Guiyang house, earliest of the Five Houses. He died in the first month of 853, aged 83.

steles.title: 潭州大溈山同慶寺大圓禪師碑銘
steles.author: 鄭愚 (also a 碑銘 by 盧簡求, 散騎常侍涇原等州節度使)
steles.quote: 散騎常侍涇原等州節度使盧簡（求）為師撰寫碑銘，李商隱題寫匾額
steles.note: The 大圓禪師 stele is preserved in 全唐文 j.820 (鄭愚 撰); a second 碑銘 by 盧簡求 is recorded, and 李商隱 wrote the temple plaque. NOT in the CBETA corpus; existence and authorship confirmed via zh.wikipedia 溈山靈祐 (2026-07). I did not fetch the full 全唐文 stele text, so I cite it as an external attestation of the stele's existence, not as a quoted primary.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988) biography, 唐大溈山靈祐傳
teacher.quote: 遂詣泐潭謁大智師，頓了祖意。元和末，隨緣長沙，因過大溈山，遂欲棲止。
teacher.note: 大智師 = 百丈懷海 (posthumous 大智禪師), who taught at 泐潭/百丈. A near-contemporary (988) biography, drawing on his stele.

teacher.quote: 百丈懷海（720-814）禪師法嗣 … 西參謁懷海禪師，為上首弟子。
teacher.note: First-seat disciple of 懷海.

teacher.quote: 百丈懷海（720-814）禪師法嗣 … 西參謁懷海禪師，為上首弟子。
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: 以大中癸酉歲正月九日盥漱畢，敷座瞑目而歸滅焉，享年八十三。
dates.note: 853, age 83 → birth 771. Matches the roster.

notes: Co-founder of the Guiyang school, earliest of the Five Houses.

bio: Ordained young, he studied under Nanquan Puyuan and succeeded to his dharma. He first lived at Luyuan monastery in Changsha, then kept no fixed residence, teaching as occasion offered, and later settled on Mount Changsha. He was famously fierce in exchange: after he knocked Yangshan over, Yangshan said 'he is just like a tiger', and he was known thereafter as Cen the Tiger (岑大蟲). He is remembered for 'the entire ten-direction world is the eye of the monk'. Posthumously titled 招賢大師.

teacher.quote: （DILA cite） REL teacher 普願 （T51n2076_p0273b02）
teacher.note: 景德傳燈錄 places 長沙景岑 among 南泉普願's heirs; 祖堂集 likewise

teacher.quote: 幼年出家，參南泉普願，嗣其法
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: birth +0788 ; death +0868
dates.note: DILA sources both to a Chinese web page (fo.confucianism.com.cn), which is weak. The roster's death 868 agrees; its 'floruit 820' has no source.

notes: Known for 'The entire ten-direction world is the eye of the monk.'

bio: Dharma heir of Linji Yixuan and abbot of Xinghua monastery in Weifu. He is the link through which the Linji line survived the collapse of the Tang: his heir Nanyuan Huiyong carried it into the Five Dynasties. He died on the twelfth day of the seventh month of 888, aged 59. Posthumously titled 廣濟禪師.

steles.title: 魏州故禪大德獎公塔碑
steles.author: 公乘億 (Tang, 魏博 staff official)
steles.quote: 和尚姓孔．字存獎．家本鄒魯．即闕里之裔孫也…禪大德玄公者．即臨濟大師也…享齡五十九．僧臘四十一…遂建塔於府南貴鄉縣熏風里．附於先師之塔。
steles.note: Full text preserved inside the Qing polemic 正名錄 (B24n0137) under the heading 「興化師承疑問」 (lb 0490b18). The 正名錄 states the text was extracted from 文苑英華 by 月函潛公 precisely because 「諸方有興化拈香遙嗣之議」 — the stele was recovered TO SETTLE a lineage dispute. Death 文德元年 (888).07.12, age 59, 僧臘 41 → b. 830: matches roster.

teacher.kind: 塔碑 (公乘億《魏州故禪大德獎公塔碑》, recovered from 文苑英華)
teacher.quote: 禪大德玄公者．即臨濟大師也。和尚一申禮謁．得奉指歸。傳黃檗之真詮．授白雲之祕訣。
teacher.note: Contemporary stele, commissioned by 存獎's own disciple 藏暉 (「億到職之初．曾獲瞻禮法主大德藏暉…相請撰文」, lb 0491a14). Names 玄公 = 臨濟義玄 explicitly and traces 黃檗→臨濟→存獎.

teacher.quote: 臨濟義玄禪師（767-866）法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: 實唐僖宗文德元年戊申七月十二日也。壽五十九。
dates.note: 888, age 59 → birth 830. Matches the roster. DILA notes a variant reading 一說「乙…」.

notes: Critical link in the survival of the Linji school through the Five Dynasties.

bio: Dharma heir of Linji Yixuan and resident of Sansheng cloister in Zhenzhou. He received Linji's personal charge and compiled the Record of Linji (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄), the text on which the whole later Linji tradition rests. After Linji's death he travelled widely, visiting Yangshan, Deshan Xuanjian and Xuefeng Yicun; the Blue Cliff Record preserves his sharp exchange with Xuefeng about the golden fish. His birth, death and native place are all unrecorded.

teacher.kind: his own self-designation in the colophon of the 臨濟錄 he compiled
teacher.quote: 住三聖嗣法小師慧然集
teacher.note: NOT the editor trap. The brief's own counter-example (燮雲濟璣, 「嗣法門人濟璣等編」) is exactly this phrase: he does not merely edit, he signs himself 嗣法小師 — dharma-heir — of Linji. First-person. Same byline independently in X68n1315 (lb 0023a14, 「住三聖嗣法小師 惠然 集」) and J23nB134 (lb 0518c02, 「住三聖嗣法門人慧然集」).

teacher.kind: Linji's own deathbed words, in Linji's own record
teacher.quote: 師臨遷化時據坐云：吾滅後不得滅却吾正法眼藏。三聖出云：爭敢滅却和尚正法眼藏？師云：已後有人問爾，向他道什麼？三聖便喝。師云：誰知吾正法眼藏向這瞎驢邊滅却。言訖端然示寂。
teacher.note: The master, dying, names Sansheng as the one his 正法眼藏 passes to. This IS the transmission scene, and Sansheng is its only other actor.

teacher.quote: 得臨濟義玄之旨…受義玄付囑，編集《鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄》一卷。
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: 生卒年、籍貫皆不詳。
dates.note: DILA states outright that his dates and origin are unknown. The roster's 'floruit 830 / death 900' HAS NO SOURCE — treat as invented.

notes: Compiler/editor of the Linji Lu (Record of Linji). Known for sharp exchanges.

bio: Of the Guo 郭 family of Nancheng. Alarmed by impermanence at about fourteen, he asked his parents' leave and entered Mantian monastery at Luling; he took full ordination at Mount Song. He went first to Cuiwei, then — hearing that the Dongshan line's teaching was lofty and severe — went in person to Dongshan Liangjie, and became his heir. Ma Yin, prince of Chu, invited him to Miaoji cloister on Mount Longya and petitioned for him; he was granted the purple robe and the title Zhengkong 證空 in the Zhenming era (915-). He died on the night of the thirteenth of the ninth month of 923, aged 89, with 75 years in robes.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988) biography — a 傳, not a lamp
teacher.quote: 次龍牙山釋居遁，姓郭氏，臨川南城人也…於嵩山受具戒已，思其擇木，乃參翠微禪會，迷復未歸，莫知投詣。聞洞上言玄格峻，而躬造之。遁少進問曰：何謂祖意？答曰：若洞水逆流，即當為說。而於言下體解玄微。
teacher.note: THE BRIEF'S RULE, ILLUSTRATED. He 參 Cuiwei — and it FAILED (迷復未歸). He 躬造 Dongshan and 體解玄微 there. 參 is not transmission; the awakening at Dongshan's word is. ⚠ And note: 翠微無學 is ALSO IN THIS BATCH — an agent skimming for '翠微' could easily have hung Judun on the wrong man. He is Dongshan's.

teacher.quote: 乃參翠微禪會。聞洞上言玄格峻，而躬造之。
teacher.note: '洞上' = the Dongshan house; he went to Dongshan in person. DILA files him as 曹洞宗. Supports the roster's Dongshan Liangjie, though the phrasing names the house rather than the man.

dates.quote: 後唐莊宗同光癸未九月十三夜。有大星隕於方丈前。詰旦端坐而逝。壽八十九。臘七十五。
dates.note: 923, age 89 → birth 835. Matches the roster.

notes: From Nancheng in Fuzhou (Jiangxi). Ordained at fourteen, studied eight years under Dongshan Liangjie, and also visited Linji and Cuiwei Wuxue. Later became abbot of Miaoji Temple on Mount Longya near Changsha. Posthumous title: Great Master Zhengkong. Appears in Blue Cliff Record case 20.

bio: Of the Zhang 張 family of Jiaxing. Ordained under the vinaya master Zhicheng at Kongwang monastery, he first went to Muzhou Daozong, who shut the gate on him three days running and, on the third, crushed his leg in it — at which he broke through. Muzhou sent him to Xuefeng Yicun, in whose assembly he 'secretly tallied with the hidden pivot'. He founded Guangtai cloister on Mount Yunmen in Shaozhou in 923, drew a large community, and became the founder of the Yunmen house, famous for one-word answers. He died in the fourth month of 949, aged 86, with 66 years in robes.

steles.title: 大漢韶州雲門山光泰禪院故匡真大師實性碑銘并序
steles.author: 雷岳
steles.author_note: 內門使監集賢殿御書院給事郎守內侍省內常侍上柱國賜紫金魚袋 — a Southern Han court official
steles.quote: 師諱文偃，姓張氏，世為蘇州嘉興人…時己酉歲孟夏月二十有五日集賢殿雷岳譔
steles.note: Preserved in the 雲門山志 (Yunmen temple gazetteer) in the corpus. The gazetteer's own chronology dates the erection to 958 (大寶元年); the text's colophon is dated 己酉 = 949, the year of Yunmen's death. I record both and do not silently pick one. The stele also states his succession: 師於是踞知聖筵，說雪峯法.

steles.title: 大漢韶州雲門山大覺禪寺大慈雲匡聖弘明大師碑銘并序
steles.author: 陳守中
steles.author_note: 西御院使集賢殿學士御前承旨太中大夫行右諫議大夫知太僕寺事上柱國賜紫金魚袋
steles.quote: 壽齡八十六，僧臘六十六
steles.note: Dated 大寶七年 = 964, fifteen years after his death, on the reopening of the stupa. The gazetteer compares the two steles and notes they disagree on his ordination age.

steles.title: 韶州雲門匡真文偃禪師 行狀
steles.quote: 師諱文偃，浙西嘉興張氏子。幼依空王寺志澄律師出家稟具，探窮律部。初參睦州蹤禪師…睦州開門一見，便閉卻…遂掩門，損師一足，師從此悟入。睦州指見雪峰。
steles.note: Prefixed to his 語錄 in the Jiaxing canon. This is the source of the gate-slamming story and it names both Muzhou (who broke him open) and Xuefeng (to whom Muzhou sent him, and whose heir he became).

teacher.quote: 師於會裏，密契玄機…後雪峰遷化，學徒乃問峰佛法付誰？峰云：「遇松偃處住。」學徒莫識其機，偃者蓋師名也。…師於是踞知聖筵，說雪峯法
teacher.note: The stele, written at his death: he tallied in XUEFENG's assembly, Xuefeng named him as successor by a pun on his name, and he 'preached Xuefeng's dharma'. This is the strongest possible attestation and confirms the roster.

teacher.quote: 睦州指見雪峰
teacher.note: Muzhou pointed him to Xuefeng. Muzhou triggered the awakening; Xuefeng gave the transmission.

teacher.quote: sect: 雲門宗

dates.quote: 壽齡八十六，僧臘六十六
dates.note: Died 949 aged 86 → born 864. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 雲門宗 — he is its founder.

bio.kind: 雲門山志 / 碑銘 / 行錄

notes: Founder of the Yunmen school. Born 864 in Jiaxing. Enlightened when Muzhou slammed the gate on his leg. Established Yunmen Monastery on Yunmen Mountain in Guangdong with 500+ monks. Known for terse, one-word answers: 'A dried shit-stick.' Famous for 'every day is a good day.' His mummified body was preserved.

bio: Dharma heir of Fengxue Yanzhao and abbot on Mount Shou in Ruzhou, later moving to Guangjiao cloister on Mount Bao'an. Known as 'Nian of the Lotus' (念法華) from his habit of reciting the Lotus Sutra. He is the man through whom the Linji line came through the Five Dynasties and reached the Song: his heirs Fenyang Shanzhao and others rebuilt the house. He died in 993.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, his own entry
teacher.quote: 首山省念禪師，汝州首山省念禪師，萊州人也，姓狄氏。受業於本部南禪院。得法於風穴。初住首山為第一世。
teacher.note: 得法於風穴 — the transmission verb, in his own lamp entry. Upgrades the roster's bare DILA line.

teacher.kind: 續傳燈錄, his heirs listed
teacher.quote: 汝州首山念禪師法嗣一十六人：汾陽善昭禪師、葉縣歸省禪師、神鼎洪諲禪師…
teacher.note: His transmission onward — 16 heirs — anchors him firmly in the Linji spine.

teacher.quote: 風穴延沼禪師（897-973）法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.note: Matches the roster.

notes: Preserved the Linji transmission through the difficult Five Dynasties period.

bio: Dharma heir of Yangqi Fanghui and the central transmitter of the Yangqi branch — through his heir Wuzu Fayan the branch became the dominant Linji line of the Song. Also called 法華端. He died in 1072, aged 48.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 transmission-incense, at his 開堂 (enthronement) at 江州承天禪院 (白雲守端禪師廣錄 卷1)
teacher.quote: 又拈香云：「此一瓣香，且道為什麼人？若有所為，雪上加霜；若無所為，過莫大焉。奉為我先住袁州楊岐，後住潭州雲盖，親見慈明來底老古錐。」
teacher.note: THE DHARMA STICK, and he identifies his master not by name but by his career: the old fellow who FIRST lived at Yangqi in Yuanzhou, THEN at Yungai in Tanzhou, and who personally saw Ciming. That is Yangqi Fanghui and can be no one else. First-person, at the transmission.

teacher.kind: the same 開堂, the OTHER sticks — recorded here so nobody mistakes them
teacher.quote: 師開堂日陞座，拈香云：此一瓣香，奉為今上皇帝…次拈香云：此一瓣香，奉為過、現、未來大覺海中…及生平所參見諸善知識、眾中衣鉢道友…聊伸報謝。
teacher.note: Stick 1 = the emperor. Stick 2 = every teacher he ever visited and his dharma-friends — 聊伸報謝, 'merely to express thanks.' THIS IS THE TRAP STICK. Only stick 3 is the dharma-father.

teacher.quote: 楊岐方會禪師（992-1049）法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: 熙寧五年遷化，壽四十八。
dates.note: 1072, age 48 → birth 1025. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Key transmitter in the Yangqi branch.

bio: Dharma heir of Furong Daokai and a key figure in the Song Caodong revival. He taught at Danxia and at Dahong, and his heirs Hongzhi Zhengjue and Zhenxie Qingliao carried the house into its most influential period. He died in 1119 (Xuanhe 1), aged 54, and his whole body was interred south of Mount Hong.

steles.title: 宋大洪山淳禪師塔銘
steles.note: DILA A000084 records the existence of this stupa inscription, but a sweep of all 4,990 corpus files for 淳/丹霞淳/洪山淳 + any stele genre found NO copy in the CBETA Zen corpus. Listed as known-to-exist, not-in-corpus. I have not seen the text and quote nothing from it.

teacher.kind: 補續高僧傳, 丹霞淳傳 (a 高僧傳, not a lamp)
teacher.quote: 至大陽，訪芙蓉老人，叩以大事。芙蓉目師偉器，示之曰：古人謂空刼已前承當，佛未出世體會，汝但退步就己，萬不失一，安用多言？師言下大悟。侍芙蓉有年…芙蓉深器重之，以為洞上孤宗，斯人可托
teacher.note: STRONG. 斯人可托 — 'the solitary Caodong lineage CAN BE ENTRUSTED TO THIS MAN.' 托 is the entrusting verb, spoken by the teacher, about the lineage itself. The bio also carefully separates the men: 禮道凝上人為師 (道凝 was his teaching/ordination master, 通貫教乘) is kept distinct from 芙蓉, under whom he 大悟 and served for years.

teacher.quote: 芙蓉道楷禪師（1043-1118）法嗣 … 曹洞宗僧，芙蓉道楷禪師法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.kind: authority record (禪燈世譜 卷9; 佛光:919)
dates.quote: birth +1066 ; death: 「宋徽宗宣和元年己亥春示寂。」 (+1119-03-23~+1120-02-07)；年五十四，塔全身於洪山之南。
dates.note: DISAGREEMENT WITH ROSTER: the roster has 1064–1117. DILA has 1066–1119 (Xuanhe 1, age 54). I took DILA's, because it is tied to a reign-date (宣和元年) and an age, whereas the roster's figures carry no source. Both recorded.

notes: Teacher of Hongzhi Zhengjue. Key figure in the Caodong revival.

bio: From Anqing prefecture. He first studied in the Yunmen house, then received the Caodong transmission from Zhenxie Qingliao at Changlu, and became abbot of Tiantong. His heir Xuedou Zhijian continued the line. He died on the first of the eighth month of 1162, aged 72. Also known as Daxiu 大休.

teacher.quote: 大休宗玨禪師…師嗣真歇了，了嗣丹霞淳。其法嗣雪竇鑑。
teacher.note: 師嗣真歇了 — full lineage: 丹霞子淳 → 真歇清了 → 宗玨 → 雪竇智鑑. ⚠ The gazetteer at lb 0194a07 flags a lineage ERROR in some lamps: 「《續燈錄》又以鑑作『真歇了法嗣』，未免有誤」 — i.e. some texts wrongly hang 雪竇智鑑 off 真歇了 rather than off 宗玨. Credit sub-song subagent.

teacher.quote: 長蘆了禪師法嗣　天童宗珏禪師　明州天童宗珏禪師。僧問。如何是道。師曰。十字街頭休斫額。
teacher.note: 長蘆了 = 真歇清了. 法嗣. Heir-index at lb 0628c21, and 五燈會元 X79n1559 (慶元府天童宗珏禪師).

teacher.kind: 續傳燈錄 flat 法嗣 index
teacher.quote: 長蘆了禪師法嗣十三人 / 天童宗珏禪師…
teacher.note: 長蘆了 = 真歇清了, abbot of Changlu. CONFIRMS the roster's Zhenxie Qingliao.

teacher.quote: 長蘆了禪師法嗣 / 天童宗珏禪師 明州天童宗珏禪師
慶元府天童宗珏禪師

dates.quote: 卒於：南宋 孝宗 紹興 三十二年 八月…三十二年八月上澣，跏趺而逝。世壽七十二。
dates.note: 1162, age 72 → birth 1091. Matches the roster. NOTE: DILA files him under the variant character 宗玨, not 宗珏 — a name-form search on 宗珏 alone misses him entirely.

notes: Initially studied Yunmen, received Caodong transmission from Zhenxie Qingliao. Abbot of Tiantong monastery. Teacher of Xuedou Zhijian.

bio: A Caodong master of the Jin dynasty at Daming monastery in Cizhou, twenty-first generation below Qingyuan. He first went to Puzhao Bao at Daming, who told him 'in my day I made the dharma my every thought' — and when Huiman pressed him, 'and how is it with you now, reverend?', Bao answered 'like meeting a born enemy', at which Huiman said he had not walked a thousand li in vain; Bao came down from the seat and took his hand, calling him a master of the craft. His dharma came from Wangshan Ti. He gave Wansong Xingxiu his awakening and transmission — the line that produced the Book of Serenity. He died in 1206.

teacher.kind: 正名錄 j.5 quoting 存稿 (the 燈錄 of the opposing party — i.e. hostile-witness testimony)
teacher.quote: 存稿列雪巖滿章次．曰．初見普照寶照．曰兄弟年俊．正須參叩老僧．當年念念．常以佛法為事。滿乃避席曰．和尚即今作麼生。照曰．如生冤家相似。滿曰．若不得和尚此語．幾乎枉行千里。照便下禪牀．握滿手曰．作家。那復參王山．得受記莂．繼踵地持。
teacher.note: 得受記莂 at 王山 = the transmission. 初見普照寶 = a prior meeting, not transmission. That this comes from the OPPOSING party's own book makes it strong: both sides of the dispute agree 慧滿's transmission was from 王山體.

teacher.kind: four carved lineage-lists (佛祖傳法偈碑 at 勝果寺; 大萬壽禪寺…實蹟記; 月舟載行實碑; 幻休潤行實碑記)
teacher.quote: …芙蓉楷．鹿門覺．青州辯．磁州寶．王山體．雪巖滿．萬松秀．雪庭裕…
teacher.note: 王山體 → 雪巖滿 on stone, four times over.

teacher.kind: 增集續傳燈錄 (南石文琇, Yongle)
teacher.quote: 他明載雪庭裕嗣萬松秀．秀嗣雪嚴滿．滿嗣王山體．體嗣磁州寶．寶嗣青州辯．辯嗣鹿門覺．覺嗣芙蓉楷．所敘人名世次．明如指掌。
teacher.note: Note the variant graph 雪嚴滿 here for 雪巖滿.

teacher.quote: 青原下二十一世 / 王山體禪師法嗣 / 磁州大明雪巖滿禪師
teacher.note: The nearest 法嗣 heading above his entry names 王山體.

teacher.quote: 磁州大明僧人。青原下二十一世，王山體禪師法嗣。

dates.note: Death 1206 confirmed. NO BIRTH YEAR is attested anywhere — the roster's 'floruit 1136' has no source.

school.quote: sect: 曹洞宗；青原下二十一世

bio.quote: 磁州大明雪巖滿禪師初參普照寶，寶曰：兄弟年俊，正宜叩參。老僧當年念念常以佛法為事。師避席進曰：和尚而今如何？寶曰：如生冤家相似。師曰：若不得此語，幾乎枉行千里。寶下禪床，握師手曰：作家那！

notes: Caodong Chan master at Daming Temple in Cizhou. Direct teacher of Wansong Xingxiu; granted him his definitive awakening and dharma transmission.

bio: Dharma heir of Yuelin Shiguan. He worked on Zhaozhou's 'wu' for six years before breaking through. In 1228 he compiled the Wumenguan (無門關, The Gateless Barrier) — forty-eight cases with his own commentary and verse — which became the most studied koan collection in the tradition and the backbone of Rinzai training in Japan. Later abbot of Huanglong. He died on the seventh day of the fourth month of 1260, aged 78.

teacher.quote: 遂陞座，拈香祝聖罷，次拈香云：此香…分明拈出，爇向爐中，奉為兩住平江萬壽、後住烏回先師月林和尚，非圖報德酬恩，且要與他鈍置。
teacher.note: 無門慧開禪師語錄. First stick to the emperor (祝聖), SECOND stick — the dharma stick — to 先師月林和尚, identified by his two seats (平江萬壽, 烏回), i.e. 月林師觀. Take only this stick.

teacher.kind: own 忌日拈香 (teacher's death-anniversary incense)
teacher.quote: 月林和尚忌拈香：儂家沒興眼無筋…一掬肝膓俱裂破，年年此日痛傷心。
teacher.note: He keeps 月林's memorial day every year — the behaviour of a dharma-son, corroborating the incense.

teacher.quote: 字無門，月林師觀禪師法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.source: DILA A001730 (《無門慧開禪師語錄》卷2)
dates.quote: （景定元年）庚申年四月七日跏趺而逝，年七十八。
dates.note: 1260, age 78 → birth 1183. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Compiler of the Wumenguan (無門關, Gateless Barrier), the most widely studied koan collection. Attained awakening after six years of working on Zhaozhou's 'No'. The Wumenguan's 48 cases with verse commentary became central to Linji-lineage koan training.

bio: Of the He 何 family of Linhai, from a Confucian household; his mother taught him the Analects and Mencius at six. Ordained at twelve at Huacheng cloister in Yuhang by his father's cousin, fully ordained at eighteen. He first met Zangsou Shanzhen at Jingshan and 'under his words was suddenly awakened' — Zangsou is his teacher. He went out to Zifu in Huzhou in 1300, was granted the title 慧文正辯禪師 in 1303, moved to Lingyin in 1312 and to Jingshan in 1322, where he was the forty-eighth abbot and taught for some thirty years. Received the golden-thread robe three times. He died on the fourth of the eighth month of 1341, aged 88, with 76 years in robes. His heirs include Chushi Fanqi and Gudding Zuming.

steles.title: 元叟端禪師塔銘
steles.author: 黃溍
steles.author_note: Huang Jin (1277–1357), Hanlin academician and one of the four great prose masters of the Yuan
steles.quote: 徑山元叟禪師，大慧四世孫也。師諱行端，元叟葢其字，族臨海何氏，世為儒家。母王氏，能通五經。師生而秀拔…十二從族叔父茂上人，得度於餘杭之化…初參藏叟和尚於徑…
steles.note: In the 徑山志 (Jingshan gazetteer), juan 6, whose table of contents lists it as 「元叟端禪師塔銘　黃溍」. A second copy sits at GA/GA024/GA024n0022.xml lb 0182a05 (「元叟禪師塔銘」). The stele NAMES ZANGSOU as the teacher — this is what breaks the roster's claim.

teacher.quote: 初參藏叟和尚於徑（山），師於言下，豁然頓悟。
teacher.note: His stupa inscription, written at his death by a named Yuan academician: he awakened under ZANGSOU.

teacher.quote: 字元叟，藏叟善珍禪師法嗣 … 雪峰珍（1194-1277）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十世
蔵叟善珍の法を嗣ぐ
teacher.note: Independent third confirmation. URL fetched and confirmed.

dates.quote: 至正元年八月四日示寂，世壽八十八，僧臘七十六。（via DILA A001032, citing 《元叟行端禪師語錄》卷8〈塔銘〉）
dates.note: 1341, age 88 → birth 1255. Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派；大鑑下第二十世

notes: Yuan dynasty Linji master at Lingyin Temple, Hangzhou. Teacher of Chushi Fanqi.

bio: Korean Seon monk of the late Goryeo and early Joseon. Of the Kim 金 clan, ancestral seat Sinju; dharma name Beopjang, dharma title Gobong. He left home at twenty and succeeded to the dharma lineage of Naong Hyegeun. From 1395 he resided at Songgwangsa and rebuilt it, and for that work was honoured as the sixteenth and last of Songgwangsa's Sixteen National Preceptors; his portrait was enshrined in the Guksajeon there. In 1426 he compiled the Gobong Beopjang gajip, expounding Naong's songs. He fell ill on the eleventh day of the seventh month of 1428 and died on the twenty-first, leaving a farewell verse; his disciples raised his stupa at Cheongjinam, north of Songgwangsa, in 1430.

steles.note: A stupa was raised for him at Cheongjinam in 1430 (per Encyclopedia of Korean Culture). I found NO stele text — neither in the CBETA corpus (including B31n0170 朝鮮佛教通史) nor on the web. Recorded as existing; no text seen, nothing quoted.

steles.title: 曹溪山松廣寺重創祖高峯和尚行蹟
steles.author: 六眉 — 前修證寺住持大禪師 六眉, a Songgwang-sa monk, writing at the abbot's command
steles.quote: 師於戊申七月十一日得疾…二十一日寅時，倩古堂雄法師書臨終偈二首曰：「清淨本然極玲瓏，山河大地絕點空…七十八年歸故鄉…」偈畢曰：「我沒而後，骸骨待三年然後置于安處。」遺囑，儼然而逝。… 門人信贊、惠性、尚濟、洪仁、洪延等十餘軰，庚戌秋始工，刻石造浮屠，終于季冬，樹之于寺之北岡。… 皇明宣德六年辛亥春正月日誌，住持前判事宗師都大禪師雲谷侍者，前修證寺住持大禪師六眉記，高峯弟子大禪師。
steles.note: A named man (六眉), writing at a named grave (the stupa on the north ridge of Songgwang-sa, carved in autumn 1430 and finished that winter), in a named year: 宣德六年辛亥 = 1431 — THREE YEARS after Beopjang died. It records his death (戊申 = 1428), his age (七十八 → born 1351, matching the chart exactly), his two death-verses, his instruction to leave his bones three years, and the 37 relic-grains recovered in four sessions. This is exactly the 行狀 rung the brief asks for — and it was sitting in 朝鮮佛教通史 all along.

teacher.kind: 行蹟 — 〈曹溪山松廣寺重創祖高峯和尚行蹟〉, written at his newly-built stupa
teacher.quote: 曹溪山松廣寺重創祖高峯和尚行蹟。師諱法藏，俗姓金氏，慎川人也。母林氏。丱歲投佛出家，妙年登選席。未幾舍名利，入山修道，謁普濟尊者懶翁大和尚為師，受法。僧名志崇，號高峯。
teacher.note: 「謁普濟尊者懶翁大和尚為師，受法」 — he called on the Venerable Bogje, the great monk Naong, TOOK HIM AS MASTER, AND RECEIVED THE DHARMA. 受法 is the transmission verb. 普濟尊者 is Naong Hyegeun's formal title, so the identification is airtight.

teacher.quote: 나옹 혜근(懶翁 惠勤)의 법맥을 이었다
teacher.note: 'He inherited the dharma lineage of Naong Hyegeun.' URL fetched and confirmed. Confirms the roster.

dates.quote: 1351–1428 … 성은 김씨, 본관은 신주이고 법명은 법장, 법호는 고봉
dates.note: Birth 1351 (Chungjeong 3). Death 1428 (Sejong 10), 7th month, 21st day. Roster's death 1428 confirmed; its 'floruit 1350' is close to the true birth year.

school.quote: 고봉법장/法藏/高峰法藏 — sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Naong Hyegeun's primary dharma heir and the master who rebuilt Songgwangsa, the 'Sangha Jewel Temple' originally established by Jinul. During the late Goryeo and early Joseon transition, he preserved the Seon monastic community through a period of political upheaval and growing anti-Buddhist sentiment from Neo-Confucian reformers. His reconstruction of Songgwangsa ensured the physical and institutional survival of the Jinul-Hyesim legacy. He maintained the unified Jogye lineage established by Taego Bou, transmitting it into the fifteenth century. Attested in Songgwangsa temple records: his rebuilding efforts and dharma lineage from Naong are preserved in monastery inscriptions and chronicles.

bio: Of the Xian/Xian 綫 family of Yingshan in eastern Sichuan, from a Confucian family; style-name Dafang 大方, sobriquet Bianrong. Approaching thirty he was struck by impermanence, left home for Mount Yunhua, and was tonsured under a monk named Ke 可. He went to the capital, heard the Huayan expounded, and awakened at the line 'if one would know the realm of the Buddhas, purify the mind till it is like empty space'. He entered the capital four times, living at Longhua, then Bailin (reading the canon), then Shichahai receiving travelling monks. Imprisoned on a false charge in the Longqing era and cleared by Zhang Juzheng. When the Empress Dowager Li built the Great Thousand-Buddha monastery he was asked to open it. He taught Zibo Zhenke and Hanshan Deqing. He died on the ninth of the ninth month of 1584, aged 79.

teacher.quote: 補遺。未詳法嗣。順天大千佛寺徧融真圓禪師…遂捨家入雲華山，禮可公為師薙染。
teacher.note: 五燈全書 explicitly places him among UNDETERMINED dharma-heirs; 可公 = tonsure only.

teacher.quote: 真圓，字大方，徧融其別號也…禮可和尚為師，落髮受具…深入華嚴法界，心念口演，不離此經。
teacher.note: biography names only 可和尚 (tonsure); frames him as a Huayan master, no Chan dharma-father.

teacher.quote: 《錦江禪燈目錄》卷1：「(不二際法嗣)……徧融圓禪師」
teacher.note: the ONLY source asserting a Chan dharma-father (不二真際); contradicted by 五燈全書's 未詳法嗣.

dates.quote: 卒於：明 神宗 萬曆 十二年 九月 初九日，79歲 → birth +1506, death +1584-10-12
dates.note: 1584, age 79 → birth 1506. The roster's '1500–1580' is four years out at both ends and unsourced.

bio.kind: 五燈全書 卷120 補遺
bio.quote: 順天大千佛寺徧融真圓禪師，西蜀營山綫氏子。家世業儒，書史過目不忘…至年將立，感生死無常，遂捨家入雲華山，禮可公為師薙染。抵京師，聽講華嚴，至「若人欲識佛境界，當淨其意如虗空」處，倏然頓悟
燕京大千佛寺徧融真圓禪師，西蜀營山綫氏子

notes: Ming dynasty Chan elder at Fatong Temple in Beijing. Teacher of Zibo Zhenke for nine years.

bio: Of the Sha 沙 family of Shuzhou (Longshu); dharma name Dayi 大艤, sobriquet Wuyi, commonly called Boshan after his monastery. Dharma heir of Wuming Huijing of Shouchang, he carried the Caodong 'mattock Chan' into the Baojing sanmei of Dongshan. He revived Nengren monastery on Mount Boshan in Xinzhou, where thousands gathered, and also opened Gushan. His Canxue zhijin (博山參禪警語) is the classic manual on great doubt and the huatou. He was born on the twenty-ninth of the eleventh month of 1575/76 and died on the eighteenth of the ninth month of 1630.

steles.title: 中興信州博山能仁禪寺無異大師墖銘并序
steles.author: 吳應賓
steles.author_note: Wu Yingbin, 宮諭 — named in the second stele as the man who 'wrote it large' (吳宮諭應賓已為大書特書銘之)
steles.quote: 而我博山無異大師以壽昌钁頭禪入于洞山寶鏡三昧…師龍舒沙氏子，法諱大艤
steles.note: Appended to his own 廣錄 (juan 35). Note the 墖 variant of 塔 — a search for 塔銘 alone misses this stele entirely. It names the teacher (壽昌 = 無明慧經) in the very first line and gives his real dharma name, 大艤.

steles.title: 博山無異大師衣鉢塔銘 (有序)
steles.author: 永覺元賢
steles.author_note: Yongjue Yuanxian, his dharma-brother ('某於師為法門昆…'), the leading Caodong master of the next generation
steles.quote: 博山無異大禪師既遷化，弟子智誾輩奉全身塔於本山棲鳳嶺之陽，吳宮諭應賓已為大書特書銘之。而弟子之居閩中鼓山者，以師實開化鼓山，厥功靡𦕈，特請衣鉢，擬建塔以寄永思…去師遷化則十有二年也。
steles.note: A SECOND stupa — the robe-and-bowl stupa raised at Gushan twelve years after his death (1642), because he had opened that monastery. Sits in Yongjue Yuanxian's 廣錄, not his own — the heir's-record pattern.

teacher.quote: 而我博山無異大師以壽昌钁頭禪入于洞山寶鏡三昧
teacher.note: His own stupa inscription: he entered the Caodong samadhi through SHOUCHANG's (= 無明慧經's) mattock-Chan.

teacher.quote: 無明慧經禪師（1548-1618）法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

teacher.quote: 壽昌無明和尚語錄一卷 明慧經說，元來集…青原下第三十四世，嗣廩山忠。
teacher.note: Gives the TEACHER's own line (慧經 嗣廩山忠), i.e. the grandfather edge. ⚠ NOT offered as evidence of transmission: 元來 compiled this record, and compiling a master's sayings is NOT evidence of receiving his dharma (the 'editor trap'). The transmission here rests on the 墖銘 and DILA above, which are independent of the editing.

dates.quote: 却顧來時萬曆乙亥仲冬之廿有九日 … 崇禎庚午季秋之十有八日也 (via DILA A000114)
dates.note: Birth 萬曆乙亥 11th month 29th = 1576-01-09; death 崇禎庚午 9th month 18th = 1630-10-23. Both taken from his own stupa inscription. The roster's 'floruit 1575' is the Chinese year 乙亥, which straddles 1575/76.

notes: 69th Caodong patriarch. Also called Boshan. Author of Canxue zhijin (Exhortation on Great Doubt), a classic on huatou practice.

bio: Of the He 何 family of Fuqing in Fujian. Both parents died when he was fourteen; he was tonsured at Sanbao monastery under Huishan and served the community three years. Dharma heir of Miyun Yuanwu, he became the second abbot of Huangbo after him and later held Jinsu, Tianning and other seats. In 1654 he published the Wudeng yantong (五燈嚴統), which reassigned contested lineages to assert Linji orthodoxy and set off the fiercest sectarian controversy of the late Ming. His heir Yinyuan Longqi took the line to Japan as the Ōbaku school. He died on the twenty-ninth of the third month of 1661, aged 69, with 55 years in robes.

steles.title: 金粟費隱容和尚行狀
steles.author_note: compiled by his heirs — the record is edited by 嗣法門人原宗等
steles.quote: 師諱通容，號費隱，閩之福清何氏子。生而挺異，舉止不凡。六歲入鄉校…十四歲，二親繼喪，師哀悼無已，遂詣三寶寺禮慧山祝髮，躬親眾務者三年。
steles.note: APPENDED TO HIS HEIR'S RECORD — it sits in the 語錄 of 水鑑慧海 (juan 9), not in his own. A second copy is in J/J29/J29nB232.xml at lb 0313c04. This is exactly the pattern the brief warns about.

steles.title: 費隱容禪師舍利塔銘
steles.note: DILA A001150 records a 舍利塔銘 (relic-stupa inscription). I could not locate its text in the corpus; recorded as known-to-exist, unseen, unquoted.

steles.title: 金粟費隱容和尚行狀
steles.author: in 水鑑慧海's 六會錄, ed. 嗣法門人原宗等
steles.quote: 金粟費隱容和尚行狀。師諱通容，號費隱，閩之福清何氏子。生而挺異，舉止不凡
steles.note: The grand-teacher's 行狀, carried in the grand-heir's book.

teacher.source: J29nB230, 卷9 〈金粟費隱容和尚行狀〉
teacher.kind: 行狀, quoting his own act
teacher.quote: 悟祇打，師祇喝。至第七打，師頭顱幾裂。所有伎倆知解，泮然冰釋…是年乃熹宗天啟二年，師三十歲也。次年，掩關姚江陳賢嶺…感悟和尚法乳之恩，乃修通法嗣書，復出關往見
teacher.note: ★ 感悟和尚法乳之恩，乃修通法嗣書 — 'feeling the debt of Abbot Wu's DHARMA-MILK, he drew up a dharma-succession document.' The 法嗣書 is his own act. 悟 = 密雲圓悟. 天啟二年 = 1622, aged 30 → b. 1593.

teacher.quote: 如徑山容和尚，早年穎悟，徹證心源，九載雲門，未悉所懷，後參悟和尚於越之吼峰，頭顱擊破，脫去礙膺
teacher.note: Nine years at Yunmen settled nothing (未悉所懷); the breakthrough was under Yuanwu.

teacher.quote: 密雲圓悟禪師（1566-1642）法嗣
teacher.note: Confirms the roster.

dates.source: DILA A001150 (《福嚴費隱容禪師紀年錄》)
dates.quote: 生于癸巳五月二十四日戌時 … 順治十八年辛丑三月二十九日未時
dates.note: 1593-06-22 to 1661-04-27, from his own chronological biography. Matches the roster exactly.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

notes: Second abbot of Huangbo monastery after Miyun. Published the controversial Wudeng yantong (1654) asserting Linji orthodoxy. CBETA: J26nB178.

bio: Of the Wang 王 family of Lingshi in Huozhou. Tonsured at the local Doushuai cloister, he toured the lecture-halls and became a formidable debater — 'eloquent as a running stream'. Hearing of Lingyin (Wentai)'s clear dharma-eye he submitted himself and enquired in earnest; one day, hearing his master raise the line 'never seek it from another — it grows ever more distant from you', he suddenly awakened and received the seal. He first held Tianqing, then Baoying in the Western Capital. Third-generation Shaolin Caodong, after Xueting Fuyu and Lingyin (Songshan) Wentai. He died in 1313, aged 69, with 49 years in robes.

teacher.kind: 五燈全書 biography, under the heading 少室泰禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 西京寶應還源福遇禪師，霍州靈石王氏子。依邑之兜率薙落，徧遊講肆，雄辯如流。景聆靈隱泰道眼精明，投誠參請焉。泰甞謂師曰：我舉拂子，你便向拂子上會。我纔良久，你便向良久處會。恁麼地，如何透得本分事？師面熱汗下，無以對。一日，聞泰上堂舉「切忌從他覓，迢迢與我疎」語，師當下大悟，即承印可。
teacher.note: 印可 — the seal. Fuller than the 繼燈錄 version quoted in round 1 (which had 道眼圓明 for 道眼精明 and 參究 for 參請).

teacher.quote: 裕傳嵩山靈隱文泰。泰傳寶應還源福遇。遇傳香嚴淳拙文才。
按繼燈錄：西京寶應還源福遇禪師，霍州靈石王氏子，依邑之兜率薙落，徧遊講肆，雄辯如流。景聆靈隱禪師道眼圓明，投誠參究。一日聞隱上堂舉「切忌從他覓，迢迢與我疎」語，師頓領悟，即承印可。初住天慶，次寶應。終壽六十九，臘四十九。
teacher.note: Names 靈隱 as the master under whom he awakened and from whom he received the seal. CONFIRMS the roster's Lingyin Wentai.

teacher.quote: 青原下二十五世 / 嵩山泰禪師法嗣 / 寶應福遇一則
teacher.note: 嵩山文泰 = 靈隱文泰 (the same man; Songshan/Shaolin is where he sat). The index also gives the chain: 萬壽（雪庭）福裕 → 嵩山文泰 → 寶應福遇 → 香嚴文才 — exactly the Shaolin Caodong succession the roster describes.

teacher.quote: sect: 曹洞宗；西京寶應僧人

dates.quote: 終壽六十九，臘四十九
dates.note: Age 69 at death.
1313 confirms the roster's death year; birth 1245 is an inference from age 69.

notes: Third-generation Shaolin Caodong master (after Xueting Fuyu and Lingyin Wentai). Served as abbot of Shaolin Monastery during the late Yuan dynasty, maintaining the Caodong transmission that Xueting Fuyu had restored there.

bio: Korean Seon monk and doctrinal lecturer of the nineteenth century. He came to Donghaksa on Gyeryongsan around 1864 with his disciples and rebuilt the main halls, founding the gangwon (monastic seminary) that became the basis of Donghaksa's teaching college. He took in the teenage Gyeongheo after the Venerable Gyeheo left the order and taught him the scriptures for some nine years; Gyeongheo — who would become the reviver of modern Korean Seon — succeeded him as head lecturer (gangbaek) at Donghaksa in 1871.

bio.quote: 만화보선 … 1864년 동학사로 옮겨와 … 강원을 개설
bio.note: WEAK. This rests on a Korean wiki-grade page (namu.wiki 동학사) surfaced by search; the page itself returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch, so I could NOT confirm it firsthand and I emit no URL for it. The Gyeongheo connection (nine years of study under 만화, gangbaek in 1871) is independently corroborated across several Korean Buddhist news/encyclopaedia pages.

notes: The 74th Korean patriarch. Lecturer on Buddhist doctrine at Donghaksa Monastery on Gyeryongsan Mountain near Daejeon. Took in the teenage Gyeongheo after Venerable Gyeheo left the order, teaching him the doctrinal curriculum. Gyeongheo later told followers to honor Manhwa as the one 'from whom I received the work of the dharma.'

bio: Of the Xin 辛 family of Longcheng in Qinzhou (one source says Lu 魯). Ordained at Yingqian monastery, he was a gifted lecturer, versed in the sutras and especially the Huayan, and at first did not believe in 'a separate transmission outside the teachings' — until he met Tianyi Yihuai, submitted, and attended him for ten years. He opened the dharma at Simian in Huai, moved to Qixian on Lushan, then Changlu in Zhenzhou; in 1084, at the petition of Princess Yueguo and the Grand Commandant Zhang, he was installed as first patriarch of Fayun monastery in the Eastern Capital, and Shenzong sent a palace envoy with incense. Blunt to the point of harshness, he was nicknamed 'Iron-face Xiu'. He is remembered in the Chanyuan qinggui for calling meditators who sit with closed eyes dwellers in 'the ghost cave under the black mountain'. He died in the eighth month of 1090, aged 64.

teacher.kind: 禪林僧寶傳, 惠洪覺範, 1119 — 法雲圓通秀禪師傳
teacher.quote: 去至無為鐵佛，謁懷禪師…懷収涕問：座主講何經？秀曰：華嚴。又問：此經以何為宗？秀曰：以心為宗。又問：心以何為宗？秀不能對。懷曰：毫釐有差，天地懸隔。秀退自失悚然，乃敬服願留，日夕受法。懷公移池入吳，秀皆從之十年。
teacher.note: 日夕受法 — 'day and night he received the dharma' — and he followed Yihuai for TEN YEARS through the move from Chizhou into Wu. Huihong (1071–1128) is effectively a contemporary: Faxiu died 1090, and the 僧寶傳 is compiled from 行狀 and stele material, not from lamp entries. It also documents the anti-Chan scholiast Faxiu WAS before Yihuai broke him — 然吾不信世尊教外別以法私大迦葉 — which is exactly the conversion the DILA note summarises. Note the 秀鐵面 nickname is earned in this same 傳 (0543c17), confirming identity.

teacher.quote: 俗姓辛。天衣懷禪師法嗣。…初不信「教外別傳」，見義懷，始信服，隨侍十年。
teacher.note: Explicit: heir of Tianyi Yihuai, whom he attended for ten years.

teacher.quote: Tianyi Yihuai [is] Faxiu's teacher
teacher.note: Independent confirmation. URL fetched and confirmed.

dates.quote: 卒於：北宋 哲宗 元祐 五年 八月，64歲 → birth +1027, death +1090
dates.note: 1090, age 64 → birth 1027. Matches the roster's dates exactly — only the teacher is wrong.

notes: Originally from Longcheng in Qinzhou (present-day Tianshui, Gansu). Entered monastic life at age three at Yingqian Monastery on Mount Maiji. After serving as abbot at several monasteries including Qixian on Mount Lu and Changlu Chongfu, he was appointed the first abbot of Fayun Monastery in the capital Kaifeng by Emperor Shenzong in 1084, receiving the honorific "Yuantong." Closely connected with Song literati including Su Shi, Huang Tingjian, Wang Anshi, and the painter Li Gonglin.

bio: Japanese Rinzai master, a son of the retired Emperor Go-Saga. On the twenty-sixth of the ninth month of 1281 he went to Kenchō-ji at Kofukusan and received from Mugaku Sogen the kesa that had come down from Enshō (Lanxi Daolong), carried it back to his temple and had the drum sounded to announce it to the assembly. He was the first abbot of Un'gan-ji in Shimotsuke (下野州東山雲巖禪寺). Posthumously Bukkoku Zenji (佛國禪師) and Bukkoku Ōgu Kōsai Kokushi. He died in 1316, aged 76. His heir Musō Soseki became the most influential Zen figure of the Muromachi period.

teacher.quote: 今將無準先師法衣一頂。授邁常顯日長老。流通法道。接續正宗。弘安四年九月三日。福山老僧
teacher.note: First-person, by the TEACHER, dated 弘安四年 (1281). 福山老僧 = Zuyuan (巨福山 = Kenchō-ji). This proves the teacher of the man who RECEIVES, because the giver names himself.

teacher.quote: 老僧欲見汝一面。面別。山川阻隔。不日如願。吾先師法眼法衣。已分付汝。汝廣求本色。爲吾流通報佛祖恩。是吾末後之囑。珍重
teacher.note: 分付 and 囑 — both transmission verbs. 'This is my final charge.'

teacher.quote: 邁常日師眞吾家好種草。初未識面。老漢因到長樂。炷香請益。將夾山見船子機緣驗之。機先頗能騰蹋。也有吾三十年前在先師會中見解…吾囑之云。若要扶豎宗門。當堅守戒行
teacher.note: 囑 again.

teacher.quote: 度弟子。以心印心。以器傳器三百餘人。拔其尤者。建長高峯日。長樂一翁豪
teacher.note: Named first of Zuyuan's two foremost heirs, twelve years after his death.

teacher.quote: 雲巖今日和根拔来𤑔向爐中供養／現住巨福山建長禪寺無學大和尚，用酧法乳之恩
teacher.note: FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION. The master of this record burns the incense of the dharma-milk debt TO Mugaku Sogen, then sitting as abbot of Kenchō-ji. One does not offer that incense to oneself: therefore the speaker is Mugaku's HEIR, not Mugaku.

teacher.quote: 師於弘安四秊九月廿六日到巨福山建長禪寺拜無學和尚，親授圓照師翁伽梨，頂戴㱕寺，鳴鼓為眾舉揚
teacher.note: Kōan 4 = 1281; he receives the robe from Mugaku in person.

teacher.quote: 顯日/高峰顯日/仏国禅師/仏国応供広済国師 — 日本人，後嵯峨帝子，佛國禪師。sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

dates.quote: birth +1241 ; death +1316~+1317, aged 76
dates.note: Matches the roster.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Linji master of the far southwest, thirty-sixth generation below Nanyue. Dharma name Falin 發林, sobriquet Hengxiu(lin) of Lüluo. Born on the twenty-third of the seventh month of 1626. He was the heir of Yunhuan Chen (雲幻印宸, 1623–1669), who was himself an heir of Poshan Haiming — so he stands two steps below Poshan. He preached in the Sanba and Liuzhao country (Sichuan/Yunnan-Guizhou). He wrote the 行狀 for Jinping Poshi Zhuo, and he edited his own teacher's recorded sayings.

steles.title: 綠蘿恒秀林禪師語錄 — 行實
steles.note: The Jiaxing catalogue records 「綠蘿恒秀林禪師語錄二卷 清發林說，光悠等編，江溥序，劉𦶜序，有行實及附錄」 — his 行實 is bound with his own 語錄. DILA quotes it for his birth date, so the text exists; I did not extract the passage itself and quote nothing beyond DILA's citation.

steles.title: 綠蘿禪寺碑記
steles.author: a local official (unnamed in the passage; he speaks of remitting the monastery's corvée)
steles.quote: 秀師得法於蜀都破山師翁嫡嗣雲幻和尚…斯院也始創於丁巳之春，而成於戊午之夏。
steles.note: 丁巳 = 1677, 戊午 = 1678. Confirms 得法 from Yunhuan and dates the founding of his monastery.

steles.title: 行實
steles.author: Falin himself, taken down by his disciples
steles.quote: 師於辛亥冬染疾…眾堅請不已，師曰：「山僧乃西蜀鄰陽人也…」
steles.note: A first-person autobiography, not a third-person 行狀.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense at his enthronement
teacher.quote: 復拈香云：「此一瓣香，光吞佛祖、氣壓諸方，伶俜十載，一朝擊碎，躬承記莂，不敢孤負。此第一回拈出，奉為忠州石寶山萬佛禪寺傳臨濟正宗第三十二世雲幻大和尚，用酬法乳。」
teacher.note: The dharma-milk stick, to 雲幻. 躬承記莂 — 'I personally received the prediction/certification'. He even locates Yunhuan precisely: Wanfo monastery on Shibaoshan in Zhongzhou, 32nd generation of the Linji line.

teacher.quote: 遂陞。拈香祝聖畢，復拈香云：「者瓣香，三巴林裏得來、六詔街頭拈出，奉為萬佛禪寺雲幻老人，用酬法乳。」
teacher.note: Second, independent 拈香. 三巴 = Sichuan (where he got it); 六詔 = Yunnan (where he now raises it).

teacher.source: J/J36/J36nB355.xml, 行實 — his own autobiography, dictated in illness
teacher.quote: 庚子秋，有萬峰之行，與本師雲幻和尚邂逅相逢，冤家聚首，是年三十五歲也。壬寅元旦，師上堂…予出問：『乾坤世界即且置，子承父業時如何？』師云：『好手手中呈好手，紅心心裏中紅心。』便將源流拄杖、袈裟一齊擲下，曰：『吾得本師寶印三昧以來，未常輕許一人，今日事不獲已，轉授於汝，善自護持』
teacher.note: The transmission itself, in his own words, DATED: 庚子 = 1660 (first meeting, age 35), 壬寅元旦 = New Year's Day 1662 (the handover). 源流 (lineage document) + staff + robe. 本師. He asks in open assembly 「子承父業時如何」 — 'what of it when the son inherits the father's work?' — and is answered by having the regalia thrown down at him.

teacher.quote: 秀師得法於蜀都破山師翁嫡嗣雲幻和尚，自是遊黔而來，說法於滇之開化吉祥、蒙自鹿苑、彌勒大隱、沅江萬壽。…以待恒禪師作開山鼻祖
teacher.note: A STELE, independent of his own words, using 得法 — and it fixes the grand-teacher too: Yunhuan is the direct heir (嫡嗣) of Poshan 破山 (Poshan Haiming), whom Falin calls 師翁.

teacher.kind: his own letter to his teacher
teacher.quote: 通本師幻老人：昔年鈍置，深蒙痛棒，撇轉機輪，親承印可，是以法乳之恩未報、省覲之禮還虧。
teacher.note: A letter addressed 'to my ROOT-TEACHER, the old man Huan'. 親承印可 — 'I personally received the seal of approval'. 法乳之恩 again. Four independent first-person attestations of the same edge.

teacher.quote: 綠蘿恒秀林禪師語錄二卷 清發林說…有行實及附錄。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣雲幻宸。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.
and gives the teacher's dates.

teacher.quote: 雲幻宸禪師語錄一卷 清印宸說，發林等編…南嶽下第三十五世，嗣破山明。
teacher.note: The GRANDFATHER edge: 雲幻印宸 is Poshan Haiming's heir. ⚠ The fact that 發林 also edited this record is NOT cited as evidence of transmission (the 'editor trap'); his own edge rests on the 嗣雲幻宸 tag and DILA above.

teacher.quote: 印宸/雲幻/雲幻宸/雲幻印宸 — 蜀忠州人，姓萬，梁山僧人…於康熙己酉四月望六日…語畢而逝。
teacher.note: EXPANDS THE TEACHER'S BARE NAME: 雲幻宸 = 雲幻印宸, of Zhongzhou in Shu, Wan 萬 family, d. 1669.

dates.source: DILA A016730 (《綠蘿恒秀林禪師語錄》卷2〈行實〉)
dates.quote: 生前勝國天啟丙寅，實今皇代天命七月念三日。
dates.note: Birth 1626-09-13. No death date attested.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Linji master of the capital. Dharma name Chaozi 超自, sobriquet Heyi 何一. He received the charge of Xingkong 性空 — one of the twenty-two heirs of Feiyin Tongrong, who alone crossed the Yangtze with a single bottle and bowl to carry Chan into Hebei, where the prefectures of central China and Qi-Qing turned to him. Heyi lived at Chongning hermitage in the western suburbs of the capital, sealed in retreat reading the canon for years, with hundreds coming daily to question him. He preached under princely patronage.

teacher.kind: 序 by 王澤弘 to his own 語錄
teacher.quote: 天童密雲大師，以無上智慧，直接達磨心傳…而費隱則尤法門中之龍象也。費隱所付囑者二十有二人，惟性空一瓶一缽，數千里渡江，獨以禪教唱導河北…何一禪師者，受性空付囑，居京師之西郊崇寧菴
teacher.note: DECISIVE — and it fixes the dangling edge. The preface to his own record, by a named contemporary, states that he received the charge of 性空, AND that 性空 was one of Feiyin Tongrong's twenty-two heirs. That chains him: 密雲圓悟 → 費隱通容 → 性空 → 何一超自. The roster noted only that '性空' could not be resolved; this connects it.

school.quote: the Miyun→Feiyin→Xingkong line = 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Of the Zhang 張 family of Huating (Songjiang). At seven he recited the Lotus Sutra at Tianlong monastery in Hangzhou and was tonsured young under Wuyong Gui. He first saw Shiwu Qinggong, then heard Qianyan Yuanchang expound and broke through. Shiwu told him his affinity lay in Wusong and wrote out the two characters 松隱 for him; he returned home, built a hut south of Guohui and named it Songyin, hanging Shiwu's writing as its plaque, and did not cross its threshold for three years. He wrote out the Huayan Sutra in his own blood. When Qianyan died the assembly asked him to succeed to the seat. Summoned in the early Hongwu era as a man of the Way, he soon returned home ill. He built a seven-storey pagoda to house the blood-written sutra. He took leave of the assembly and died calmly on the fourteenth of the fourth month of 1388.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 — 松隱唯菴然和尚語錄
teacher.quote: 此一瓣香，大眾還知來處麼？今日不惜眉毛，爇向爐中，奉為開山佛慧圓鑑普濟禪師千巖大和尚，不圖酬恩報德，且要遞相熱瞞。
teacher.note: 佛慧圓鑑普濟禪師千巖 = 千巖元長; 酬恩報德 raised by 德然 himself. First-person.

teacher.quote: 千巖長禪師法嗣。華亭張氏子…後參千巖長禪師，聞其提唱豁然悟入。…洎千巖遷化，眾請師繼席。
teacher.note: 豁然悟入 under 千巖; succeeded his seat.

teacher.quote: 松隱唯庵然和尚語錄三卷　明德然說，慧省編，宋濂序，懷渭後序。南嶽下第二十四世，嗣伏龍長。
teacher.note: 嗣伏龍長 = 嗣千巖元長 (伏龍山).

teacher.kind: authority record (citing 補續高僧傳 卷25; 五燈全書 卷58)
teacher.quote: 千巖長禪師法嗣。華亭張氏子…後參千巖長禪師，聞其提唱豁然悟入。…洎千巖遷化，眾請師繼席。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster's Qianyan Yuanzhang.

teacher.quote: 松隱唯庵然和尚語錄三卷 明德然說，慧省編，宋濂序，懷渭後序。南嶽下第二十四世，嗣伏龍長。
teacher.note: 伏龍長 = 千巖元長, who sat at Fulong — the same man under his monastery-name. Two independent forms of the same attestation. NOTE the roster's own text says 'succeeded Qianyan Yuanzhang at Fulong', which matches.

dates.quote: 洪武二十一年四月十四日逝 → +1388-05-18
dates.note: Death 1388. No birth year attested. The roster gives no dates at all.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.kind: authority record / 補續高僧傳 卷25

bio: Of the Li 李 family, originally of Xuzhou prefecture in Sichuan, settled at Anshun in Guizhou. Born on the twenty-eighth of the sixth month of 1625. Dharma heir of Lingyin Yinwen, he became abbot of Shengjue monastery on Mount Guangfu. Thirty-sixth generation below Nanyue.

steles.title: 密印和尚塔銘碑記
steles.author: 劉禹甸
steles.author_note: 楚南金城七十叟 — a seventy-year-old layman of Jincheng in southern Chu, who 'burned incense and bowed as he composed it'; written out by his dharma-younger-brother 劉湯懋
steles.quote: 師諱真傳，號密印，姓李氏，原籍四川敘州府，寓以貴筑之安順。天啟乙丑…
steles.note: Appended to his own 語錄. Gives name, sobriquet, surname, both native place and adopted place, and the birth year 天啟乙丑 = 1625.

steles.title: 密印和尚塔銘碑記
steles.author: 劉禹甸 (楚南金城七十叟)
steles.quote: 師諱真傳，號密印，姓李氏，原籍四川敘州府…天啟乙丑歲誕日…
steles.note: preserved in his own 語錄 (廣福山勝覺寺密印禪師語錄 j.12). Genuine memorial inscription for the master himself.

teacher.quote: 此是第三回拈出，爇向爐中，供養傳臨濟正宗第三十二世上靈下隱和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: His OWN dharma-milk stick (用酬法乳之恩) to 靈隱 (印文). The imperial/patron sticks are raised separately (回1-2). A-grade first-person.

teacher.kind: stele HE wrote for his teacher
teacher.quote: 附靈隱老人塔銘碑記，嗣法門人真傳拜撰。師號靈隱，諱印文…乃破山明翁之法子、天童悟祖之嫡孫。
teacher.note: 真傳 signs as 嗣法門人 — dharma-heir — of 印文; also fixes the upstream lineage.

teacher.quote: 號密印，為靈隱印文禪師法嗣
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

teacher.quote: 廣福山勝覺寺密印禪師語錄十二卷 清真傳說，如暐等編，莊鏻序，有塔銘。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣靈隱文。
靈隱文禪師語錄三卷 清 文說，福度復編。南嶽下第三十五世，嗣破山明。
teacher.note: The grandfather edge: his teacher 靈隱印文 was himself Poshan Haiming's heir.

teacher.quote: 印文/靈隱/靈隱文/靈隱印文 — 為破山海明禪師（1597-1666）法嗣。蘷州高梁人，俗姓王。有《靈隱文禪師語錄》三卷。（《五燈全書》卷70）
teacher.note: Confirms the teacher's full name 靈隱印文 (of Kuizhou, Wang 王 family) and independently confirms the grandfather edge to Poshan Haiming (1597–1666).

dates.quote: 天啟乙丑歲六月二十八日 (via DILA A016502)
dates.note: Birth 1625-07-31. No death date attested.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio: Lay surname Chen, of Xianyou in Xinghua (Fujian); sobriquet Yisou. As a child he was tonsured by Donglin of Mt Lian. Grown, he called on Chaozong Shilin and others, who set him on the koan 'the ten thousand dharmas return to one'. He then went to Feiyin at Jinsu, and one night, hearing the bell, had an opening. He went again to Wanru Tongwei at Longchi and received the dharma. He was abbot of Tongtian Chan monastery in Fujian. He died on 12/3 of 1669, aged 54, with 40 dharma-years; his stupa is on the eastern slope of Mt Lian. He left a fascicle of recorded sayings and a collection of poems, the Jipiao ji. His heir was Danya Chaoyuan.

steles.title: 通天逸叟高禪師語錄 卷1 行狀
steles.author: unnamed (appended to his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 康熙己酉年三月十二日申時，閱世五十有四。
