His first abbacy was Xingsheng in 1229; he then held Bao'en, Xianxiao, Ruiyan, Yanfu and Baolin, became the 43rd abbot of Ayuwang in 1258, and by imperial decree took Jingci in 1264 and finally Jingshan. Honoured by both Lizong and Duzong, he died seated in 1269, aged 85, with 53 summers. His recorded sayings became foundational for the later Linji tradition, and through his Japanese heir Nanpo Jomyo his line carries the whole of Japanese Rinzai: every abbot of Daitokuji and Myoshinji descends from him.

steles.title: 虛堂智愚禪師語錄 卷10 〈行狀〉
steles.author: not named in the sources reached
steles.note: The canon catalogue confirms an 行狀 is appended to his own recorded sayings: B35n0194 「虛堂智愚禪師語錄十卷…附行狀。南嶽下第二十世，嗣運庵巖。」

steles.title: 虛堂和尚行狀
steles.author: 法雲 (嗣法小師)
steles.quote: 師諱智愚。四明象山陳氏子…春秋八十五。夏臘五十三…咸淳十年十月十一日…嗣法小師法雲謹狀。
steles.note: a full 行狀 (life-record, the stele-genre) by his dharma-heir, preserved in his own 語錄.

teacher.quote: 爇向爐中。奉為前住安吉州道場山護聖萬歲禪寺。先師運庵和尚。用酬法乳。
teacher.note: His OWN dharma-milk stick (用酬法乳) to 運庵 (普巖) — raised at multiple enthronements (報恩, 顯孝 etc.). Imperial/patron sticks raised separately. A-grade first-person.

teacher.quote: 是時運庵師祖…携師過霅上。薙染為不釐務侍者…造方丈。通見解…庵云。何不合取狗口。
teacher.note: 行狀 by heir 法雲: transmission narrative under 運庵.

teacher.quote: 虛堂智愚禪師語錄十卷，宋智愚說，妙源、可宣等編…附行狀。南嶽下第二十世，嗣運庵巖。
teacher.note: ⭐ Heir of Yun'an Yan, 20th generation. And the neighbouring entry: 「運庵普巖禪師語錄一卷…附行實。南嶽下第十九世，嗣松源嶽。」 — the chain Songyuan → Yun'an → Xutang is laid out in three consecutive catalogue entries.

teacher.quote: 運菴巖（1156-1226）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十一世…首參雪竇煥、中庵皎，後謁運菴巖得旨。

dates.quote: 咸淳五年十月初七日…春秋八十五，夏臘五十三

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.quote: 明州象山陳氏子…住興聖、寶恩、顯孝、瑞巖、延福、寶林、育王、淨慈、徑山

links.label: Terebess (Kido)
links.confirms: teacher Yun'an Puyan 1156-1226; the Nanpo Jomyo transmission to Japan

notes: Late Song Linji master whose recorded sayings became profoundly influential in the later Linji tradition. Dharma heir of Yunan Puyan (not Wuzhun Shifan as sometimes misattributed).

bio: A Changshu man of the Wen clan, ordained at Xingjiao Chongfu monastery in his home prefecture and fully ordained at twenty. He first went to GAOFENG YUANMIAO at Tianmu, who gave him the huatou 'the myriad things return to one' and whom he served for three years — until Gaofeng himself sent him away: 'In Wen there is a blind donkey; in Huai there is Ji'an. You should go and see him.' He went to West Peak in Jianyang and consulted JI'AN ZONGXIN, who tested him ('Where there is a Buddha, do not stay; where there is no Buddha, hurry past — what does it mean?'), rejected his first answer as a dead phrase, and finally approved him, calling him 'a golden fish that has passed through the net.' He lived at Fuyuan monastery on Mt Xiawu. He died in 1352 and was titled Chan Master Fociezhao; his relics were interred at Tianhu and DELIBERATELY PAIRED WITH JI'AN'S STUPA, 'to show he did not forget the shared niche.' He transmitted to the Korean Taego Bou, who carried his line to Korea.

steles.title: 石屋清珙禪師語錄 附塔銘
steles.author: not named in the sources reached
steles.path: 《石屋清珙禪師語錄》二卷 (嘉興續藏)
steles.note: The canon catalogue confirms: B35n0194 「石屋清珙禪師語錄二卷，元清珙說，至柔等編，明來復序，清鄉野序，附塔銘，又云佛慈照禪師語錄，內題福源石屋珙禪師語錄。」 A 塔銘 is appended to his own recorded sayings.

steles.title: 石屋和尚塔銘
steles.author: 釋元旭 (前四明延壽禪寺沙門元旭), 洪武九年 (1376)
steles.quote: 師諱清珙，字石屋，蘇之常熟人也，俗姓溫…其徒至柔刊行于世，且以師之行狀徵予銘之。予昔見師於福源，臞然其形，道韵可掬，今已四十餘年矣。
steles.note: The stele sits inside 吳都法乘, a Suzhou gazetteer — NOT in his own 語錄 (X70n1399 has no 行狀/塔銘 at all). Classic 'the stele is in somebody else's book'. The author states he personally saw Shiwu at Fuyuan some forty years earlier, and worked from a 行狀 by the disciple 至柔. Also records the Korean heir 愚太[古] 太古普愚 and the posthumous title 佛慈慧照禪師.

teacher.kind: 石屋和尚塔銘 (his stupa inscription) by 元旭, who had met him
teacher.quote: 師發憤棄去，途中忽舉首見風亭，豁然有省…菴頷之。久乃辭去，菴送之門，囑曰：已後與汝同龕…惠朗之孫，及菴之子。
teacher.note: The stele's verb is 囑 — the charge. And its lineage line is explicit: 「及菴之子」, son of Ji'an. It also records that his relics were interred 「以及菴之塔配之，示不忘同龕之師意也」 — buried beside Ji'an's stupa to keep the master's promise. Grave, verb, and burial all agree.

teacher.kind: same stele — on 高峰原妙, the OTHER candidate
teacher.quote: 峰嘿噐之，授萬法歸一之語，服勤三年，大事未明，忽辭他行。峰曰：溫有瞎驢，淮有及菴，宜徃見之。
teacher.note: TRAP DISARMED. The stele is explicit that under 高峰原妙 the great matter was NOT settled (大事未明) — Gaofeng himself sent him away to Ji'an. Association, study, three years of service — but not transmission. Anyone reading the lamp's 「首叅高峰」 as a teacher-edge is reading a visit as a transmission.

teacher.kind: 繼燈錄 via 古今圖書集成
teacher.quote: 嘉興府福源寺石屋清珙禪師，蘇之常熟溫氏子，依本州興教崇福寺出家，二十祝髮具戒。後首叅高峰，授以萬法歸一話，服勤三年。次住建陽西峰，叅及菴。菴問：有佛處不得住，無佛處急走過，意旨如何？師答不契。菴曰：者箇亦是死句。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE PRIMARY TEXT, IN THE CORPUS. Gaofeng FIRST (three years); THEN Ji'an at West Peak, who rejects his answer and later approves him. The sequence is explicit.

teacher.quote: [TEACHER] 及庵宗信. 首參天目高峰原妙和尚，服勤三年。妙公曰：「溫有瞎驢，淮有及菴，宜往見之。」珙直走見及菴。至溫建陽西峰，參及菴，及菴肯之。
teacher.note: ⭐ GAOFENG PERSONALLY SENT HIM AWAY. Cited to 《五燈會元續略》卷1：「道場信禪師法嗣，福源清珙禪師」(X80, no.1566, p.449, b19-20) — a 法嗣 index entry filing him under JI'AN.

teacher.quote: 宗信/及庵宗信/及庵信/道場信 — 元代臨濟宗僧。俗姓方，為雪岩祖欽之法嗣。初於建陽（福建）之西峰弘法。 [TEACHER 祖欽]
teacher.note: ⭐ Ji'an was an heir of XUEYAN ZUQIN — and so was Gaofeng. That makes Shiwu Gaofeng's dharma-NEPHEW. This is EXACTLY why the two get conflated. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

bio.quote: 塔于天湖之原，以及菴之塔配之，示不忘同龕
bio.note: ⭐ His stupa was PAIRED WITH JI'AN'S — a physical monument to the transmission the roster gets wrong.

bio.quote: 師生楊根郡大元里，遊學中國，嗣臨濟十八代孫石屋清珙禪師之法，則於臨濟為十九代之孫也。石屋贈法衣禪杖以表相契。東還，玄陵禮以為王師，尋加國師。
bio.note: ⭐ On TAEGO BOU: he 'inherited the dharma of Chan master Shiwu Qinggong, 18th-generation Linji descendant, thus becoming the 19th generation. Shiwu gave him a dharma-robe and Chan staff to mark their accord.' Confirms Shiwu → Taego Bou from the Korean side.

links.label: DILA Authority A007799
links.confirms: teacher Ji'an Zongxin; Gaofeng sent him away; stupa paired with Ji'an's

links.label: DILA Authority A021593 (Ji'an Zongxin)
links.confirms: Ji'an is an heir of Xueyan Zuqin — hence Shiwu is Gaofeng's dharma-nephew

links.label: Wikipedia (Shiwu)
links.confirms: 1272-1352; Gaofeng first, 'Chi-an' second and the effective teacher

notes: Yuan dynasty Linji Chan master, dharma heir of Gaofeng Yuanmiao. Significant for Korean Seon history as the Chinese teacher who transmitted to both Taego Bou and Baegun Gyeonghan, linking Korean Seon to mainstream Chinese Linji lineage. Also received teaching from Ji'an Zongxin, a dharma brother of Gaofeng.

bio: Born Yu Su-i into an aristocratic Korean family, he studied at the Seonggyungwan, the Confucian academy. At twenty-one, shaken by a friend's death, he abandoned Confucian study for Buddhism, and about 1397 came to Hoeamsa to study under Muhak Jacho, the last National Preceptor of his generation — through whom he received a Linji-derived Seon transmitted from Naong Hyegeun. He wrote the Hyeonjeongnon, the major Buddhist reply to Neo-Confucian attack, along with commentaries on the Diamond Sutra and the Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment. He restored Bongamsa on Huiyangsan in 1431 and died there on the first day of the fourth month, 1433. Grand Prince Hyoryeong ordered his relics divided, and stupas were raised at Hyeondeungsa, Bongamsa and Jeongsusa.

steles.title: 涵虛堂得通塔 / 涵虛堂得通之塔
steles.note: Three stupas exist (Hyeondeungsa, Bongamsa, Jeongsusa) from the division of his relics. I found no inscription TEXT and no named author. Recorded as monuments, not as evidence.

steles.title: 涵虛堂得通和尚行狀
steles.author: 門人埜夫 (his disciple Yabu)
steles.quote: 師諱己和。號得通。舊名守伊。號無準。所居室曰涵虛堂。俗姓劉氏。中原人也。 … 考諱聽。官至典客寺事。母方氏。 … 以洪武九年丙辰十一月十有七日生焉。
steles.note: Died 宣德八年癸丑 (1433) 4/1. The compiler 尚玄 appends an argument (in-line note) that 中原 = 忠州 and that Gihwa was Korean, not Chinese — settling an old dispute. The 行狀 also records that the name 己和／得通 was given to him in a DREAM at 五臺山 in 1420, after he made offerings before 懶翁's portrait.

teacher.kind: 〈涵虛堂得通和尚行狀〉 by his own disciple 埜夫 (門人埜夫錄), quoted in full in 朝鮮佛教通史
teacher.quote: 越明年丁丑早春。到檜巖寺。初叅王師無學妙嚴尊者。親聞法要。於是辭退。游歷諸山。戰戰勤修。又甲申仲春。再到檜巖。獨居一室。杜絕視聽。
teacher.note: READ THIS EXACTLY. The 行狀 — written by his own disciple, the closest witness there is — attests only 叅 (a visit) and 親聞法要 (he personally heard the essentials of the dharma) in spring 1397, followed by 辭退 (he took his leave). It does NOT say 嗣法, 付法, 印可 or 得法. His awakening (『行行忽迴首，山骨立雲中』; the wash-bucket, 『惟此一事實，餘二則非真』) comes SEVEN YEARS LATER (甲申 1404) at 檜巖, alone in a shut room — and Muhak was long gone from there by then. I am reporting what the document says, not what the lineage charts want it to say.

teacher.kind: 法統 lineage statement in the same compilation
teacher.quote: 慧勤是也。勤得妙嚴無學。學得涵虗得通。遂止不傳。
teacher.note: The Korean transmission-line index DOES assert the edge (懶翁慧勤 → 無學自超 → 涵虛得通), and adds 『遂止不傳』 — the line then STOPPED. This is the index rung, and it is the only place the edge is asserted as a transmission.

teacher.quote: arrived at Hoeam-sa c. 1397 to study under Muhak Jacho (1327-1405), 'the National Preceptor of the generation.'
he had the fortune of becoming the disciple of the last Korean national teacher, Muhak
teacher.note: Kihwa received a Linji-derived Seon transmitted through Muhak, who was taught by Naong Hyegeun.

dates.quote: 1376-1433; died 'the first day of the fourth month, 1433'

bio.quote: born Yu Su-i into an aristocratic family, studied at the Seonggyungwan; at 21, after a friend's death, abandoned Confucian study for Buddhism

links.label: Terebess (Kihwa)
links.confirms: born Yu Su-i, Seonggyungwan, Hoeamsa c.1397 under Muhak Jacho, died 1433 at Bongamsa

notes: Also known as Hamheo Deuktong. Wrote Hyeonjeong non defending Buddhism against Neo-Confucian attacks. Commentaries on Diamond Sutra and Sutra of Perfect Enlightenment. No known dharma heirs.

bio: A Beijing (Jintai) man of the Wu clan, ordained at Guanghui cloister under Daji Neng. He consulted some thirty teachers north and south before receiving the dharma from Wuwen Mingcong (also known as Longquan Cong), abbot of Longquan monastery at Guanziling in Suizhou. He was abbot of Gaozuo, Niushou and Yuantong, and his teaching featured the stick and the thunderous shout. His recorded sayings survive as the Xiaoyan ji in four juan. Through his heir Huanyou Zhengchuan he is the dharma-grandfather of Miyun Yuanwu, and thus stands at the head of the entire late-Ming Linji revival.

teacher.quote: 據笑巖行實自敘．初見關子嶺無聞有省．次依襄陽大覺。而關嶺無聞嘗有書與大覺．欲覺警策笑巖．又以書寄勉笑巖．二書俱刻夢說錄中。未幾．笑巖再見關嶺無聞．始受記莂
teacher.note: 受記莂 = transmission verb. His OWN account of his own life. Note the trap avoided: 大覺 of Xiangyang was a station on the way, not the father.

teacher.quote: 况笑巖集中．有舉僧問關嶺無聞佛降誕及本來面目兩則機緣．與夢說錄中所載相同。且著語拈之．代之發明其旨
teacher.note: he quotes and comments on his own teacher's koans — the two texts interlock

teacher.quote: 笑巖得法於無聞明聰．今收嗣正聰．其訛四
teacher.note: 得法於 = transmission verb. The 禪燈世譜 filed him under Zhengcong; that is the error.

teacher.kind: preface to 笑巖北集 by 三際廣通 — his own closest disciple and the recorder of his 語錄 — quoted in 正名錄
teacher.quote: 三際廣通禪師作笑巖北集序曰．師得絕學老人不傳之旨．望臨濟二十六代之祖。俱載笑嵓集中。曇芝廣通事笑巖最久．而偈序皆巖在時所作．
teacher.note: 廣通 served 笑巖 longest and wrote this preface WHILE 笑巖 WAS ALIVE (偈序皆巖在時所作) — a contemporary, first-hand witness. Transmitted at one remove (quoted inside 智楷's 正名錄), because 笑巖集 itself is NOT in the CBETA corpus.

teacher.kind: 正名錄 (智楷著) — a critical source that examined the 笑巖集 first-hand
teacher.quote: 焭絕集所載．臨潼無聞聰．館陶絕學聰．延安無聞聰．雖非笑巖之師．實是天奇之嗣。夢說錄所載．光澤無聞聰．雖非天奇之嗣．實是笑巖之師。
teacher.note: 智楷 affirms elsewhere 「紀笑巖面稟親承於明聰。是矣」 — that 笑巖 received face-to-face from 明聰 is CORRECT — and 「笑巖無聞之子．芝通無聞之孫」 (lb 0471b10). The teacher edge 笑巖 ← 無聞明聰 is therefore not in dispute.

teacher.kind: Jiaxing canon catalogue entry for his own collection
teacher.quote: 月心笑巖寶祖南北集二卷　明德寶說，廣通等錄，南嶽下第三十一世，嗣關嶺聰
teacher.note: 嗣關嶺聰 — 關子嶺 龍泉寺 is 無聞明聰's seat. Independent of 正名錄.

teacher.quote: 龍泉明聰禪師法嗣
teacher.note: 龍泉聰 is Mingcong by his monastery.

teacher.quote: 無聞明聰 / 絕學正聰 / 龍泉聰, d. 1543, 隨州關子嶺龍泉寺, heir of 天奇本瑞. [弟子] 德寶
teacher.note: Confirmed from the far side — his teacher's record lists him as disciple. Same man; no namesake problem.

dates.note: ⚠ DILA's Gregorian conversion reads 1513-01-31 because the lunar birthdate 正德七年十二月十五日 falls in Jan 1513. DILA's own prose writes 笑巖德寶（1512-1581）. The conventional 1512 is correct.

bio.quote: 金臺 (Beijing) man, surname 吳; abbot of 高座, 牛首, 圓通; heirs 龍池正傳 (幻有正傳), 東臺瑞峯, 靈谷曇芝

bio.source: DILA A000273 (幻有正傳) and A003688 (密雲圓悟)
bio.quote: 幻有正傳 (1549-1614): 「為笑巖德寶禪師（1512-1581）法嗣」; 密雲圓悟 (1567-1642) is Huanyou's heir
bio.note: Confirms the roster's claim that he stands two generations above Miyun. Beata Grant independently: 'by Miyun Yuanwu's Dharma grandfather, Xiaoyan Debao (1512-1581)'.

links.label: DILA Authority A001697
links.confirms: dates 1512-1581, teacher Wuwen Mingcong, heir Huanyou Zhengchuan

notes: Ming dynasty Linji master. Teacher of Yunqi Zhuhong. His teaching featured the stick and thunderous shout.

bio: A Wuxi man of the Su clan. In 1624 he came to Jinsu monastery and received the dharma from Miyun Yuanwu. He opened Sanfeng Qingliang Chan monastery — hence 'Fazang of Sanfeng' — and later held Jingci, Beichan and Zhenru. He then clashed with his own teacher over the interpretation of Linji's teaching, a doctrinal quarrel (centred on his Wuzong yuan) that split the late-Ming Linji revival and rumbled on for a century after both men were dead. He died in 1635, aged 63. His heirs included Yimo Hongcheng and Wenshi Hongcheng — and, through Jiqi Hongchu, a large Suzhou-centred line.

steles.title: 三峰和尚年譜
steles.author: not named in the sources reached
steles.quote: 萬曆元年十月七日 / 崇禎八年乙亥七月廿二日，壽六十三
steles.note: A year-by-year chronological biography appended to his own recorded sayings — the strongest class of source after a stele. DILA sources BOTH his birth and death dates to it.

steles.title: 蘇州三峰漢月藏禪師塔銘
steles.author: 黃宗羲 (Huang Zongxi, 1610–1695)
steles.quote: 師諱法藏，字漢月，號於密，晚改天山，無錫蘇氏子也
steles.note: ⚠ AUTHOR CORRECTION: the brief expected a 董其昌 stele. Huang Zongxi's stele NAMES an earlier 董宗伯 (董其昌) inscription and says it was 'not complete' (董宗伯所撰亦未備), which is why Jiqi Xingchu asked Huang to write a fuller one. So a 董其昌 stele DID exist but Huang's is the fuller, extant text. NAME: 蘇州 in the title is where his seat was; he was a 無錫 man, surname 蘇 (蘇氏子).

teacher.source: 黃梨洲文集, 蘇州三峰漢月藏禪師塔銘, by 黃宗羲 (Huang Zongxi)
teacher.quote: 密雲悟公以臨濟第十三世開法金粟，師徘徊而就之，雲大喜…又十年而後嗣法於密雲
teacher.note: 嗣法於密雲 — his FORMAL succession is to Miyun Yuanwu, Linji 13th generation. This is the recorded edge.

teacher.source: 黃梨洲文集, same 塔銘
teacher.quote: 師從寂音遺書悟之…讀高峰語錄，入手恍然如出己口…師又上書於雲曰：藏得心於高峰，印法於寂音，和尚一棒血流，三番大滅，瓣香總炷一爐
teacher.note: ⚠ DISPUTED / BOOK-TRANSMISSION — the heart of the 17th-c. controversy, and exactly the brief's 'evidence quality and relation type are SEPARATE'. Fazang told Miyun to his face that he 'GOT HIS MIND from Gaofeng [Yuanmiao's recorded sayings] and SEALED THE DHARMA from Jiyin [= Juefan Huihong's 智證傳]' — i.e. from two BOOKS by men long dead — and only combined the incense into one censer with Miyun's. Miyun rejected this and wrote the 辟妄七書 against him: 「天下視其師弟子之間若水火焉」. I record the teacher as 密雲圓悟 (the formal 嗣法) but mark transmission `disputed`/book, because the master himself asserted the substance came from Gaofeng and Huihong's writings, not from Miyun.

teacher.source: 黃梨洲文集, same 塔銘, Miyun's own words on the seat
teacher.quote: 雲…上堂告眾曰：漢公悟處真實，出世先我，所以屈身來此者，為臨濟源流耳
teacher.note: Miyun publicly: 'Hanyue's awakening is genuine; he came out before me, and stooped to come here only FOR THE LINJI SOURCE-STREAM.' Even the acknowledged edge is framed as Fazang seeking the lineage certificate, not the awakening.

teacher.quote: 密雲圓悟（1567-1642）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第三十五世。天啟四年（1624），至金粟寺參詣圓悟得其法。
Miyun's twelve dharma heirs: 五峰學、漢月藏、破山明、費隱容、石車乘、朝宗忍、萬如微、木陳忞、石奇雲、牧雲門、浮石賢、林野奇
teacher.note: ⭐ ONE SENTENCE that simultaneously confirms Hanyue Fazang, Muyun Tongmen, Fushi Tongxian, Linye Tongqi AND Shiche Tongcheng (Qiyuan Xinggang's teacher) — five edges in this batch.

dates.source: DILA A003668, quoting the 年譜

bio.quote: 無錫人，俗姓蘇；開三峰清涼禪寺；後住淨慈、北禪、真如。法嗣一默弘成、問石弘乘。

links.label: DILA Authority A003668
links.confirms: dates 1573-1635 (from his 年譜), teacher Miyun Yuanwu, transmission at Jinsu in 1624

notes: Clashed with his teacher over Linji's teaching, splitting the late Ming Linji revival.

bio: A Yuan-dynasty Caodong master of the Yao clan, tonsured at Fuyan monastery in Jiangzhou. He received the dharma from Huanyuan Fuyu, abbot of Shaolin. He was himself abbot of SHAOLIN twice: from 1324, retiring to Xiangyan monastery in 1329, and again from 1345. He died in 1352, aged 80. His heirs — Ziyan, Foyan Ren, Zhu'an Ziren, Huayan Yu — carried the Shaolin Caodong line that persisted there for centuries; the lamp records call it 'the dharma heirs of Chan master Cai of Shaoshi.'

teacher.kind: 五燈會元續略 biography, under the heading 寶應遇禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 鄧州香嚴淳拙文才禪師，平陽臨汾姚氏子…長依絳明福嚴普公出家。甞讀證道歌，至「幻化空身即法身」之句，欣然契悟。乃謁還源禪師，呈所解，源可之。閱藏於龍門山三載。泰定甲子，主少室。尋隱香嚴…
teacher.note: 可之 — approved. Note the two masters again: 普公 tonsured him (出家); 還源 approved him (可之).

teacher.quote: 寶應遇禪師法嗣：少室文才禪師　／　青原下二十七世：少室才禪師法嗣：南陽府萬安寺松庭子嚴禪師
遇傳香嚴淳拙文才。才傳南陽萬安松庭子嚴。
參嵩山少林寺住持還源福遇嗣法
福遇 (1245-1313, 寶應福遇). [弟子] 文才
teacher.note: Confirmed from the far side.

teacher.source: 《五燈全書目錄》卷12 (X81 no.1570 p.383 b6-8, via DILA)
teacher.quote: 少室才禪師法嗣

dates.note: ⭐ BIRTH YEAR RECOVERED — the roster had only the death year.

bio.quote: 元泰定元年（1324年），住持少林寺。元天曆二年（1329年），退居香嚴寺。元至正五年（1345年），再次住持少林寺。

links.label: DILA Authority A015502
links.confirms: dates 1273-1352, teacher Huanyuan Fuyu, two Shaolin abbacies

notes: Fourth-generation Shaolin Caodong master, dharma heir of Huanyuan Fuyu. Served as abbot of Shaolin Monastery during the mid-Yuan dynasty, continuing the Caodong lineage that would persist at Shaolin into the Ming.

bio: Born in Tongjin, Gimpo, Gyeonggi, of the Yu clan. He was ordained young under Seongsun on Myohyangsan and took full precepts from Woncheol; he then returned to Myohyangsan and cultivated Seon under PYEONYANG EONGI, awakened to the subtle meaning, and INHERITED THE DHARMA LINEAGE. Over six years he corrected and edited more than 150 fascicles of commentary on the Avatamsaka and the Surangama. He had over five hundred students and some seventy lineage-holders; through his disciples — Sangbong Jeongwon, Woldam Seolje, Woljeo Doan, Bodang Jungi — his 'Pungdam gate' carries the Cheongheo Hyujeong → Pyeonyang mainstream of Korean Seon forward. He died at Jeongyangsa on Geumgangsan in 1665, aged 74, with 58 years in robes.

steles.title: 해남 대흥사 풍담당 의심대사비 (Daeheungsa, Haenam)
steles.author: 金宇亨 Kim Uhyeong
steles.author_note: A Joseon official.
steles.note: Erected 1692, 27 years after his death. A second stupa-and-stele pair survives at Munsusa, Gyeonggi ('문수사 풍담대사 부도 및 비').

steles.title: 金剛山楓潭堂大禪師碑銘并序
steles.author: 李端相 (通訓大夫前行弘文舘典翰知製教兼經筵侍講官春秋舘編修世子侍講院輔德)
steles.quote: 皇明丁未秋，不佞屏居于維楊之靈芥洞中。一日金剛山人俊機、一如、三覆等，踵門而請曰：亡師楓潭子，即清虛之嫡孫，鞭羊之法嗣也。願得公一言，以圖不朽
steles.note: Full text present in 朝鮮佛教通史. Corroborated independently at lb 0417b05, where a later writer recalls having SEEN the stone: 「靜觀李公所撰楓潭義諶碑」.

teacher.kind: his own 碑銘 — 金剛山楓潭堂大禪師碑銘并序
teacher.quote: 亡師楓潭子，即清虛之嫡孫，鞭羊之法嗣也 … 按狀，師法名義諶，楓潭其號也 … 十六從性淳老師落髮受戒。初叅圓徹大師，仍入鞭羊之室，盡得清虛之傳
teacher.note: THE STELE ITSELF, and it is a model of the distinction the brief demands. FOUR men, kept apart: 性淳 TONSURED him (落髮受戒). 圓徹 he merely FIRST VISITED (初叅). 清虛(休靜) is the grand-teacher whose transmission he inherits at one remove. 鞭羊彥機 is the one whose ROOM he entered (入…之室) and whose 法嗣 he is called outright. Author 李端相 (1628-1669), a serving Hongmun'gwan official, writing 皇明丁未 = 1667, two years after Uisim's death (1665), at the request of Uisim's own disciples 俊機/一如/三覆, working 按狀 (from the 行狀 they brought him).

teacher.kind: the 銘 (verse) of the same stele
teacher.quote: 逮至虛羊，禪教合一。師承其授，非肉非骨
teacher.note: 虛羊 = 清虛(休靜) + 鞭羊(彥機). 師承其授 — 'the master received their transmission.' The inscribed verse, on the stone.

teacher.quote: 다시 묘향산으로 들어가 언기의 문하에서 선을 닦아 묘지를 깨치고 법맥을 이었다
teacher.note: 'Entered Myohyangsan again, cultivated Seon UNDER EONGI (彦機 = Pyeonyang Eongi), awakened to the subtle meaning, and INHERITED THE DHARMA LINEAGE.' Explicit transmission.

dates.quote: 1592-1665; died 8th day, 3rd month; age 74, 58 years ordained

bio.quote: born 1592 in Gimpo (Tongjin), Gyeonggi, lay surname 柳; ordained under 성순 性淳; died at Jeongyangsa (正陽寺) on Geumgangsan; five sarira recovered

links.label: EncyKorea 의심
links.confirms: 1592-1665, dharma from Pyeonyang Eongi, died at Jeongyangsa

links.label: Daeheungsa stele (Haenam local culture)
links.confirms: the Pungdam Uisim stele at Daeheungsa, erected 1692, inscription by 金宇亨

notes: Carried the Pyeonyang lineage into mid-17th century. Important link figure in the main trunk of Korean Seon.

bio: Born Song Donguk in Jeonju, he entered monastic life about age nine at Cheonggyesa under Gyeheo, spent five years there, and then studied the scriptures at Donghaksa under MANHWA BOSEON, a lecturer. In 1879, travelling through a plague-stricken village and confronted with death, he found that his command of the sutras was useless to him; he shut himself in and broke through on the phrase 'a cow with no nostrils.' HE HAD NO LIVING TEACHER'S TRANSMISSION. In 1880 he claimed the dharma line descending from Yongam Hyeeon — who had died before Gyeongheo was born — and styled himself the eleventh-generation heir of Cheongheo Hyujeong and the seventh-generation heir of Hwanseong Jian. He is reckoned the seventy-fifth patriarch of Korean Seon and the reviver of the tradition. His last years (1905-1912) are obscure: he lived incognito in the far north, reportedly teaching the Confucian classics, and died at Gapsan in 1912.

steles.title: 先師鏡虛和尚行狀
steles.author: 漢巖 重遠 (his disciple)
steles.path: Woljeongsa 한암일발록 archive (off-corpus); the 鏡虛集 (1943) also carries 行狀 material
steles.quote: 이것을 이은 이가 바로 나의 선사(先師) 경허화상이 그런 분이시다.
steles.note: A disciple's 行狀 — the Korean equivalent of the 塔銘/行狀 rung. Verified by fetching the Woljeongsa page. Notably Hanam's version was OMITTED from the printed 鏡虛集 because it warned against imitating Gyeongheo's unconventional conduct — a documented editorial dispute, recorded here rather than hidden.

teacher.quote: 1880년 용암 혜언(龍巖慧彦)으로부터 이어지는 법맥을 이었으며 … 청허(淸虛) 휴정(休靜)의 11대손, 환성(喚惺) 지안(志安)의 7대손.
teacher.note: His lineage-claim is to 龍巖慧彦, making him 11th-gen from Cheongheo Hyujeong. But this is a REMOTE succession (遙嗣): —

teacher.quote: Yongam Hye'eon had died before Gyeongheo was born … Gyeongheo, like Jinul, [established his own lineage].
teacher.note: Confirms the 龍巖慧彦 link is 遙嗣, not a meeting. This is evidence quality A for a relation-type 遙嗣 — the two are separate axes, and the remote succession is openly, positively attested, not a gap.

teacher.source: 漢巖(Hanam) 鏡虛和尚行狀 (Woljeongsa archive)
teacher.quote: 화상의 휘는 성우요, 어려서 이름은 동욱이며, 경허는 그 호이다. 성은 송씨요, 여산의 후손이다. … 9살 때에 … 계허스님을 은사로 머리를 깎고 … 계룡산 동학사 만화화상[에게] … 만화화상은 당세의 큰 강사였다.
teacher.note: Hanam's 行狀 gives tonsure-master 계허 and scripture-teacher 만화 explicitly — these are his ACTUAL living teachers; the 龍巖慧彦 line is the (remote) dharma-lineage he chose.

teacher.quote: 1880년 용암 혜언(龍巖慧彦)으로부터 이어지는 법맥을 이었으며 … 청허(淸虛) 휴정(休靜)의 11대손, 환성(喚惺) 지안(志安)의 7대손
teacher.note: ⭐ In 1880 he took up the dharma line descending from YONGAM HYEEON, and styled himself 11th-gen heir of Cheongheo Hyujeong and 7th-gen heir of Hwanseong Jian. Manhwa appears in this record only as the DONGHAKSA LECTURER (강백), not as a transmitter.

teacher.quote: Yongam Hye'eon had died before Gyeongheo was born … Gyeongheo, like Jinul, whose enlightenment did not come directly from a master, apparently felt that he had been given the imprimatur to teach and transmit the robe and bowl.
teacher.note: ⭐ THE DECISIVE POINT: the man whose line he claimed was already dead. The claim is RETROACTIVE.

teacher.source: Seung Sahn / Kwan Um popular biography (reproduced on Terebess)
teacher.quote: he went to Zen Master Man Hwa for an interview. Man Hwa gave him Transmission and the Dharma name Kyong Ho.
teacher.note: ⚠ THIS IS THE SOURCE OF THE ROSTER'S CLAIM — and it is NOT what the Korean scholarly sources say. Recorded because the disagreement must be shown, not because I believe it.

dates.quote: EncyKorea: 1846 (헌종 12) – 1912. Terebess: 'born 1846 (alternative dates 1849/1857); died April 25, 1912, aged 64' at Gapsan.
dates.note: ⚠ Birth year disputed. 1846 is preferred by EncyKorea AND Terebess. The roster's 1849 comes from Korean journalistic/wiki-type sources.

bio.quote: his knowledge of Buddhist sutras did not help him with the issues of life and death
bio.note: The 1879 plague-village crisis; awakening on 無鼻孔 ('no nostrils'); 75th Patriarch; obscure final years.

links.label: EncyKorea 성우
links.confirms: 1846-1912; Gyeheo ordination; Manhwa as lecturer; 1880 Yongam Hyeeon line; 7th-gen heir of Hwanseong Jian

links.label: Terebess
links.confirms: Yongam Hyeeon died before Gyeongheo was born; carries the conflicting 'Manhwa gave transmission' account too

links.label: Wikipedia
links.confirms: teachers Gyeheo then Manhwa; 1879 crisis; 'no nostrils' awakening

notes: The 75th Korean patriarch and the reviver of Korean Seon. Born Song Donguk (宋東旭) in Jeonju. Entered monastic life around age 9 under Venerable Gyeheo at Cheonggyesa, then studied under Manhwa at Donghaksa. Attained enlightenment in 1879 after encountering plague victims, which drove him from sutra study to intensive meditation. On November 15, 1887, achieved great awakening. Revived kanhwa Seon (hwadu meditation) and taught at Beomeosa, Haeinsa, and Songgwangsa. In 1905, at age 59, abruptly left the sangha and wandered incognito in northern Korea, reportedly living as a layperson teaching Confucian classics until his death in 1912 at Gapsan. His four great disciples -- Suwol (1855-1928), Hyewol (1861-1937), Mangong (1871-1946), and Hanam (1876-1951) -- became the pillars of 20th-century Korean Buddhism.

bio: A Wuxi man of the Guan clan. At nineteen he went to Daosheng at Chengtian Yong'an in Suzhou, serving ten years before tonsure. He went to Chizhou, met TIANYI YIHUAI, and awakened at a word. He opened the dharma at Ruiguang monastery in Suzhou, then Jingci in Hangzhou, where over a thousand students gathered. In 1082 Emperor Shenzong summoned him to be FIRST PATRIARCH of the newly founded Huilin Chan cloister at the Xiangguo monastery in the capital — hence his name. Zhezong granted him the title Chan Master Yuanzhao; he retired to Lingyan and died in 1099, aged 80, with 52 summers. He was also a major Pure Land figure and appears in the Records of Pure Land Sages.

teacher.quote: 服勤三年。乃辭昇。游方徧參。初至池州景德。謁義懷禪師。言下契悟。…懷笑曰。此子吾家精進幢也。汝輩他日。當依賴之。
teacher.note: 言下契悟 at 義懷's seat, and 義懷 publicly claims him ('the banner of zeal in MY house'). ⚠ Note 道昇 (承天永安道昇) is his TONSURE/service master (師事…道昇 / 剃髮受具), NOT his dharma-father — correctly distinguished from 義懷.

teacher.quote: 慧林宗本禪師別錄一卷…大鑒下第十三世，嗣天衣懷。
teacher.note: 13th generation from Huineng, heir of Tianyi Huai.

teacher.quote: 字無喆，天衣義懷禪師法嗣。常州無錫人，俗姓管。年十九依姑蘇承天永安道昇禪師出家…初至池州謁義懷禪師，言下契悟。

dates.quote: b. 1020; d. 元符二年十二月二十八日 = 1099 (lunar; 1100-02-15 Gregorian), 閱世八十，夏五十二
dates.note: ⚠ The roster's 1020-1099 is right on the Chinese calendar. Note the Gregorian slip if anyone converts.

bio.quote: 1082 神宗 summoned him as 第一祖 of the 慧林禪院 at the 相國寺; 哲宗 granted 圓照禪師; posthumous 法空禪師

links.label: DILA Authority A014482
links.confirms: dates 1020-1099, teacher Tianyi Yihuai, Huilin cloister 1082, title Yuanzhao

notes: Also known as Yuanzhao Zongben. Dharma heir of Tianyi Yihuai who first taught at Ruiguang Monastery in Suzhou, then served as abbot of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou where over a thousand disciples gathered. Later served at imperially sponsored monasteries in the Northern Song capital Kaifeng, including Huilin Monastery. Together with his student Shanben, they were known as "Big and Little Ben." He was one of the most prestigious Buddhist monks of his generation.

bio: A Changshu man of the Zhang clan, tonsured under Poshan Dongwen. He first studied with Boshan (Wuyi Yuanlai), then met Miyun Yuanwu at Jinsu and became his heir — the thirty-first generation of Linji. He was abbot of Gunan at Meili (hence 'the Reverend of Gunan'), then Qizhen at Siming, Meixi at Jiahe, Jile at Xinghua, and finally TIANTONG, retiring to Helin at Jingkou. A calligrapher and poet, he left the Qihui yulu and the Lanzhai bieji, and had ten dharma heirs. He died in 1671.

teacher.kind: own letter (牧雲和尚嬾齋別集) — the 法乳 formula in his own hand
teacher.quote: 某愚鈍無似，入法以來，聞般若種子有生同具，乃不肯自負靈根，行腳浙東，叨沐天童先師法乳，遂過為緇流所目。
teacher.note: 「叨沐天童先師法乳」 — 'I unworthily bathed in the DHARMA-MILK of my late master of Tiantong.' 法乳 in the first person, of his own teacher, in his own correspondence. 天童 is 密雲圓悟's seat.

teacher.kind: own 讚 (牧雲和尚七會語錄, portrait-eulogies)
teacher.quote: 天童本師密老和尚(八首)：「者尊慈，也大奇，本來面不動而變，正顏色不怒而威。杖子用慣，左右未嘗須臾離，但見人來便一錐，老婆心忒煞癡。」
teacher.note: The heading is his own: 天童本師密老和尚 — 'my ROOT MASTER, old monk Mi of Tiantong.' 本師 + the surname 密 名 it beyond doubt. Eight verses of them.

teacher.quote: [TEACHER] 圓悟; 臨濟下三十一世; 破山洞聞 tonsure; met Miyun at Jinsu
Miyun's twelve heirs: 五峰學、漢月藏、破山明、費隱容、石車乘、朝宗忍、萬如微、木陳忞、石奇雲、牧雲門、浮石賢、林野奇
teacher.note: 牧雲門 = Muyun Tongmen, in his teacher's own heir list.

dates.quote: b. 萬曆二十七年 = 1599; d. 康熙十年十一月十五日 = 1671-12-15 (《天童寺志》卷3)

bio.note: His recorded sayings, from which the roster's Gunan/Changshu/Zhang-clan/Dongwen details derive. All independently confirmed by DILA.

links.label: DILA Authority A001148
links.confirms: dates 1599-1671, teacher Miyun Yuanwu, abbot of Gunan then Tiantong

bio: Youngest son of the Jiang clan of Qiyang in southern Hunan; his father was named Chunlong, his mother of the Li clan. He was born in 1633. He never studied as a boy, and about the age of twelve both his parents died; he was tonsured at Tianquan in 1644. In 1653, when the country had quietened, he took leave of his master and travelled to the lecture-halls. He entered QISHAN for the summer retreat in 1654 and was fully ordained that winter under LANFANG, a thirtieth-generation Caodong master at Renrui monastery on Qishan in Hengzhou. During work-practice a monk asked, 'Mountains, rivers and the great earth fully reveal the Dharma-King's body; before us they are vivid and clear — what then is the Dharma-King's body?' and the master answered 'Revealed.' Hearing it from the side, Wenmu Nian suddenly awoke. He later presided at a 'new Danxia'.

steles.title: 文穆念禪師語錄 〈行實〉
steles.author: self-narrated; taken down by 真慧 (compiler of the 語錄)
steles.author_note: Solicited by his disciples, including 騎龍天劍大師, in the winter of 1665.
steles.quote: 余生緣南楚祁陽蔣氏之季子，父諱春龍，母李氏，產於明懷宗癸酉年六月廿三日巳時。… 是甲申歲臘月八日，薙髮埋首天泉。… 至甲午始入岐山結制，是冬圓具。… 和尚領眾出坡，一僧問：『山河及大地，全露法王身。目前山河大地歷歷明明，如何是法王身？』和尚荅：『露。』余傍聞頓惺。
steles.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON. He opens by refusing — 「余未嘗雲水，用說奚為？」 ('I have never wandered; what is there to tell?') — and only yields after three requests. Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「文穆念禪師語錄五卷，清念說，真慧編，劉檝序，有行實。」

teacher.quote: 爇向爐中供養本師，現住湖廣衡州府岐山仁瑞堂上，傳達磨正宗曹洞第三十世上嬾下放太老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION. 'I burn this in the censer to my ORIGINAL MASTER, the Great Old Reverend LANFANG, thirtieth-generation transmitter of the orthodox Bodhidharma CAODONG line, now residing at Renrui hall on Qishan, Hengzhou prefecture, Huguang — to repay the milk of the dharma.' Names the man, the school, the generation and the monastery in one sentence.

teacher.quote: 此一瓣香…爇向爐中，供養本山第一代天然大師。」復懷中取香拈出，云：「…第二回供養岐山仁瑞堂上本師上嬾下放老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⚠ TRAP AVOIDED. He burns FIRST for 天然[函昰] — but as 「本山第一代」, the FOUNDING ABBOT of the mountain he now occupies, a courtesy. He burns SECOND, and explicitly as 本師 ('my original master'), for LANFANG. Reading the first incense as a transmission would have handed him the wrong teacher and the wrong lineage. The 本師 tag is the tell.

dates.quote: 產於明懷宗癸酉年六月廿三日巳時
dates.note: ⭐ BORN 1633 (崇禎癸酉), 6th month 23rd day. Death not recorded in the sources reached.

school.quote: 傳達磨正宗曹洞第三十世
school.note: CAODONG — from his own mouth.

bio: A son of the Lü clan of southern Hunan, born about 1631. Born into civil war, he was TAKEN CAPTIVE AND CARRIED INTO GUIZHOU and pressed into an army camp; at Changshou hermitage in Anshun he heard the Reverend Yunfu give a dharma-talk and conceived the wish to leave the world. When the dynasty's forces retook Yunnan and Guizhou his unit scattered, and he fled to Longtan monastery at Annan and was tonsured under the elder Wuxia. Hearing that SHANQUAN DAWEI was teaching at Wanshou monastery in Longchang, he went and received full ordination; Shanquan took him for a vessel at first sight. He followed Shanquan to Songkui and, while attending him in a discussion of the Surangama, awoke at the passage where the Buddha raises his golden arm. Shanquan deeply approved him. He never left him again, staying at Songkui for over twenty years; when Shanquan died in 1684 the assembly asked him to succeed, and he rebuilt Songkui. He died in the winter of 1697, aged 67, with 40 years in robes, having told his disciples: 'When I am gone, do not trouble with pyre and expense — bury me whole.'

steles.title: 天一悅禪師語錄 〈行實〉
steles.author: self-narrated; recorded by 學愚
steles.quote: 師諱大悅，號天一，楚南呂氏子。生值離亂，被擄入黔… 師秉權命，如是參究，刻無間斷。時權遷松巋，師亦隨之，住經兩載。一日，侍權與官人持論《楞嚴經》，至世尊舉金色臂屈五輪指問阿難處，豁然有醒。… 權深肯之。師自受囑後，總未離權，隨住松巋二十餘載。甲子歲，權示寂… 師世壽六十有七，僧臘四十。
steles.note: ⭐ 'Born into the chaos, he was TAKEN CAPTIVE AND CARRIED INTO GUIZHOU.' The transmission, the twenty years of attendance, and the death are all here.

steles.title: 天一禪師壽塔銘
steles.author: 周名遠 Zhou Mingyuan, style 聲及, of Xiugu (繡谷)
steles.author_note: A lay author. Signed 「繡谷周名遠聲及氏拜撰」.
steles.quote: 禪師本楚南呂氏子，因值兵燹，被擄入營，涉歷艱辛，無不備嘗。第身雖在營，心則出家… 傳善權禪師衣缽，實參默悟… 銘之曰：四大本空，五蘊非有。菩提無樹，懸崖撒手。震撼河山，地中獅吼。一師塔頂，圓光不朽。
steles.note: ⭐ 「傳善權禪師衣缽」 — 'he transmitted the ROBE AND BOWL of Chan master Shanquan.' The teacher, at stele rung. Note this is a 壽塔 — a stupa raised in his lifetime — commissioned by his dharma-brother 善一 [如純]. Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「天一悅禪師語錄一卷，清大悅說，學愚錄，有塔銘。南嶽下第三十八世，嗣善權位。」

teacher.quote: 傳善權禪師衣缽
天一悅禪師語錄一卷…有塔銘。南嶽下第三十八世，嗣善權位。
達位 / 善權 / 善權位 / 善權達位 / 松巋善權 — b. 1619-10-29, d. 1684-10-01. 楚北人，姓瞿，黔南松巋僧人。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE TEACHER'S FULL NAME AND DATES. 善權位 = 善權達位 (1619-1684). His DEATH YEAR 1684 EXACTLY MATCHES the 行實's 「甲子歲，權示寂」 (甲子 = 1684) — and his monastery, SONGKUI in Qiannan, exactly matches the 行實's 「時權遷松巋」. Two documents that never met, agreeing. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

teacher.quote: 善一如純 / 天龍善一純 — [TEACHER] 達位
teacher.note: A second DILA record independently giving 達位 as Shanquan's dharma name.

dates.quote: 時遇丁丑孟冬，偶示微恙…言訖而逝。…師世壽六十有七，僧臘四十。
dates.note: d. 丁丑 = 1697, early winter, aged 67 → b. c.1631.

links.label: DILA Authority A016435 (Shanquan Dawei)
links.confirms: the teacher's full name 善權達位 and dates 1619-1684; Songkui monastery in Qiannan

bio: A son of the Zhao clan, his family from Hulin (Hangzhou) and settled at Danghu. His father was old and childless and prayed for a son; the family declined after his birth. He began school at six under the name Chongguang, but the household grew poor and by seven he was working for a living. At thirteen he gave up meat; at nineteen, when his parents moved to marry him off, he said 'if I do not go now, I shall never get free,' and fled to Putuo, where he was tonsured under Shaozong. He received the novice precepts from the great Yunqi Zhuhong. He studied for years at Jinsu under MIYUN YUANWU, followed him to Fujian, later sealed himself in retreat at Wuyuan, and became Miyun's heir the following year. He was abbot of Qinglian in Zhejiang and of BAO'EN monastery at Wujiang in Suzhou. He died in 1667, aged 75.

steles.title: 浮石禪師語錄 〈行實〉
steles.author: self-narrated, on his birthday in 1648, at the assembly's request
steles.quote: 予乃趙氏子，父文，母李氏，世居虎林，移徙當湖。父年向老，艱於嗣息，禱神得生，生後家業漸凋。六歲破學，學名重光，家益寒。七歲遂經營度日。十三歲，不茹葷…十九歲，父母欲為我完娶，嘆曰：『此時不行，他日難脫矣。』于是背親至南海普陀禮紹宗禪師，薙髮。
steles.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON. Also the wrenching detail that when he came home after three months his mother 「泣絕而甦者幾幾」 — wept until she fainted and revived — and he grew his hair back to comfort her, only leaving for good with her blessing.

teacher.quote: 此瓣香，丹青描不出，千聖覓無蹤，二回拈出，供養天童先師密雲大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON: 'for my LATE MASTER, the Great Reverend MIYUN of Tiantong, to repay the milk of the dharma.'

teacher.quote: [TEACHER] 圓悟
Miyun's twelve heirs include 浮石賢

dates.quote: d. 康熙六年七月二十五日 = 1667-09-12, 閱世七十五 (《五燈全書》卷67)

bio.quote: 當湖 man, surname 趙; tonsured at Putuo under 紹宗; novice precepts from 雲棲祩宏; abbot of 青蓮 and 江蘇吳江報恩寺
bio.note: DILA and the first-person 行實 agree on every detail — surname, Danghu, Putuo, Shaozong, Zhuhong. Independent corroboration.

links.label: DILA Authority A012052
links.confirms: dates 1593-1667, teacher Miyun Yuanwu, Bao'en at Wujiang/Suzhou

bio: Born 1610 in Chongqing department, Chengdu, Sichuan, of the Hu clan; his mother dreamt of a foreign monk carrying a lotus-torch. He was tonsured at nine at Zhongfeng monastery in Guan county and served ten years, and at twenty went to Emei for full ordination. He left Sichuan in 1638 and travelled south, reaching Miyun Yuanwu at Tiantong in the winter of 1639; in 1642 he returned to Sichuan and met POSHAN HAIMING, who struck him across the head so hard that blood ran down his face — 'Do you understand?' — and everything that had blocked him melted at once. Poshan sent him on to Xiangya. At about forty, judging that his learning was thinning as his years grew, he abandoned everything and practised as one dead; sitting one night, he heard the door creak and 'the burden fell away.' He then went to DANGSHAN YUAN at Lumen in Xiangzhou, who tallied with him 'as needle to mustard-seed' and entrusted him with the true dharma eye. He presided over four monasteries — Shuangchi, Baishui, Baoshan and finally Huanglong on Mt Baizhang, Xiangyang, which he took in 1657 — for more than twenty years.

steles.title: 奇然智禪師語錄 〈行繇〉
steles.author: self-narrated at Shuangchi, at the assembly's insistence
steles.quote: 山僧數十年東塗西抹，一具醜面孔何堪刻畫？… 予乃四川成都崇慶州人也，俗姓胡，母何氏，生於萬曆庚戌年正月十七日。九歲祝髮於灌縣中峰寺，服勤十年。二十歲朝峨眉，禮自省和尚受具足戒。
steles.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON. He opens by refusing: 'For decades I have daubed east and smeared west — what is there in this ugly face worth carving?'

steles.title: 奇然智禪師塔銘
steles.author: 方叔壯 Fang Shuzhuang, style 珂雪居士 (Kexue Jushi), dharma name 明洹
steles.author_note: A LAY DHARMA-HEIR (嗣法髮弟子) and his patron at Nanzhang — the man who installed him at Shuangchi. Signed 「頓首百拜撰文」. Cut for the press by 明林 (= Xiuye Minglin, his monastic heir).
steles.quote: 禪師諱超智，號奇然，香嚴宕山遠和尚嫡嗣，西蜀成都崇慶州。其父姓胡，母何氏… 萬曆庚戌年正月十有七日寅時生。… 乃走見襄州鹿門宕老和尚，即白悟由。宕乃與師針芥相投，即囑曰：「偶來風雨鹿門寺，今日相承賴有人。分付龜毛編就拂，撝揚四海化玄賓。」仍曰：「正法眼藏，善自護持。他日說法度人，續佛慧命。」
steles.note: ⭐⭐ 「香嚴宕山遠和尚嫡嗣」 — 'the LEGITIMATE HEIR (嫡嗣) of Reverend Dangshan Yuan of Xiangyan.' Teacher, at stele rung, in the opening line. And the transmission verse itself. Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「奇然智禪師語錄二卷…有行繇、塔銘。」

steles.title: 奇然智禪師塔銘
steles.author: unnamed (appended to his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 「萬曆庚戌年正月十有七日寅時生」…「康熙甲寅正月二十七日示微疾，二月初三日昧爽師起，沐浴服衣，索筆書偈，怡然而逝，閱世壽六十有五。」
steles.note: His stupa inscription, in fascicle 2 of his own recorded sayings, together with a 〈聯芳〉 (lineage-flower list). Cited via DILA A016286, which quotes it for both birth and death. THE HARVEST WAS RIGHT that his own 語錄 is the whole case - but the 語錄 turns out to contain a full 塔銘, which is far better than it feared.

teacher.quote: 奉為現住香嚴顯通堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十二世宕山遠本師老和尚，用酬法乳。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AT THE TRANSMISSION. 'For my ORIGINAL MASTER, Old Reverend DANGSHAN YUAN, thirty-second-generation transmitter of the orthodox Linji line, now residing at Xiantong hall, Xiangyan — to repay the milk of the dharma.' Names the man, the school, the generation and the monastery.

teacher.quote: 香嚴宕山遠和尚嫡嗣
…南嶽下第三十六世，嗣宕山遠。
teacher.note: The catalogue independently records Dangshan Yuan as a teacher with heirs at this generation.

teacher.quote: 號奇然，香嚴宕山行遠禪師法嗣…乃走見襄州鹿門宕老和尚，得法。（《奇然智禪師語錄》卷 2〈奇然智禪師塔銘〉、〈聯芳〉；《緇門世譜》卷 1）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the harvest's teacher AND EXPANDS THE NAME: 宕山遠 -> 宕山行遠 (of Xiangyan; abbot at Lumen in Xiangzhou). His 塔銘 names him, and the 緇門世譜 corroborates.

dates.quote: 生於萬曆庚戌年正月十七日 / 萬曆庚戌年正月十有七日寅時生
dates.note: ⭐ BORN 1610, 1st month 17th day — the autobiography and the stupa inscription give the SAME date independently. Death not recorded in the sources reached.

dates.quote: birth 「萬曆庚戌年正月十有七日寅時生」(1610-02-10)；death 「康熙甲寅…二月初三日…閱世壽六十有五」(1674-03-09)
dates.note: Harvest had no dates.

school.quote: 傳臨濟正宗第三十二世
sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派；法嗣有念休亮、雲海鑑、寒灰靜等三十八位禪師

bio.quote: 予回蜀參破山和尚，至方丈纔禮拜，被劈頭一棒，滿面是血，乃曰：『會麼？』予向來寶惜，一時冰釋，汗流夾背。
成都崇慶人，俗姓胡。九歲薙髮於灌縣中峰寺，年二十詣峨眉受具足戒。歷參密雲、破山、象崖諸大和尚。後隱楚雲臺孤峰頂。一夕坐至夜分，聆門響聲，豁然如釋重負

links.label: CBETA 語錄 J36nB356
links.confirms: his recorded sayings, containing the 行繇 and 塔銘

bio: Born 1638, 10th month, 2nd day. The father was Hu Yingrong, style Chunyu, the mother of the Hong clan; both were charitable people who kept a lifelong vegetarian fast, gave coffins to the poor for years and fed monks beyond counting. Before the birth the mother dreamt that an old monk with bare head and bare feet, carrying a gourd and a staff, came begging food and lodging, and was taken in. From eleven, when the mother died, the wish to leave the world took hold — but the father cursed and forbade it, and FIFTY YEARS WERE SPENT IN THE DUST, grieving night and day at not being able to go forth. In 1690 the household was abandoned at last for a hermitage; the children brought in relatives to prevent it, swearing they would fight to the death anyone who tonsured 'our mother' — so the ordination was performed with a knife, on the self. In the second month of that year came a dream of a great white ox on a mountain, which lowered its head to be mounted and flew up; the Reverend Zongyuan of Shanguang heard the dream and cried, 'Your master has come!' — for the water-buffalo is Guishan's koan, and the Reverend of Guishan had arrived at his hermitage the day before. That was GUMEI DINGLIE, thirty-fourth-generation Linji master of Great Mt Gui in Tanzhou.

steles.title: 起宗真禪師行實
steles.author: self-narrated; taken down by the secretary 力如; solicited by the disciple 力廣 and the office-holders
steles.quote: 大清康熙庚辰四月八日，弟子力廣同職事等袖香入室，請師詳說行實… 師曰：「不見佛云：『凡有所相，皆是虛妄。』我有何行實乎？」… 先君姓胡，諱應榮，字春雨，母洪氏… 崇禎戊寅十月二日，余始生焉。… 居塵五十年，日夜以不能出家為憂。至庚午年，乃捨家入菴… 遂取刀自斷其髮焉。
steles.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, dated 1700 (康熙庚辰), 4th month 8th day. He first refuses: 'Have you not heard the Buddha say, all that has form is illusion? What account of deeds have I?' Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「華嚴起宗真禪師語錄二卷…有行實。南嶽下第三十八世，嗣古梅冽。」

teacher.quote: 今對人天眾前，不免乘時拈出，供養潭州大溈山傳臨濟正宗第三十四世上古下梅先師大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON: 'for my LATE MASTER, the Great Reverend GUMEI, thirty-fourth-generation transmitter of the orthodox Linji line, of Great Mt Gui in Tanzhou.'

teacher.quote: 南嶽下第三十八世，嗣古梅冽
teacher.note: ⭐ Gives the teacher's DHARMA NAME: 冽.

teacher.quote: 定冽 / 古梅 / 古梅冽 / 古梅定冽 / 溈山古梅 — 邵陵王氏，為慧山智海禪師法嗣。有《溈山古梅冽禪師語錄》二卷。法嗣為天翼巨翔禪師。（《溈山古梅冽禪師語錄》卷上；《五燈全書》卷103）
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FULL NAME, LINEAGE AND HIS OWN 語錄 AND A 五燈全書 ENTRY. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

dates.quote: 崇禎戊寅十月二日，余始生焉
dates.note: ⭐ BORN 1638 (崇禎戊寅), 10th month 2nd day. Alive in 1700. Death not recorded.

school.quote: 傳臨濟正宗第三十四世

links.label: DILA Authority A018976 (Gumei Dinglie)
links.confirms: the teacher's full name, his own yulu, and his 五燈全書 entry

links.label: CBETA 語錄 J39nB464
links.confirms: his recorded sayings and 行實

bio: Born 1595 in Hezhou, Chongqing prefecture, Sichuan, of the Cai clan; his mother was of the Yu clan. As an infant he would retch at the smell of chicken and refuse unclean food; a physiognomist warned that he should not marry, and at ten he was sent to Jinzhong monastery in his own village and given to his uncle Daoran. He went south at seventeen (or nineteen) and spent fourteen years in the lecture-halls. In 1627 he settled at Danghu, expounded the Surangama, and sealed himself in to read the canon — but within six months nearly died of dysentery, and realising that 'a lifetime of learning is not the final matter' resolved to break out and find a teacher. A friend sent him MIYUN YUANWU'S RECORDED SAYINGS; reading the verse 'before a single thought arises — look at what it is like,' doubt seized him and he forgot food and sleep. Two more years brought nothing. Then, walking absently, HE MISSED HIS FOOTING AND FELL FROM A TOWER — and in the instant of falling, 'as one wakes from a dream,' he understood. He trained under Miyun at Tiantong and became his heir; he was abbot of Tongxuan, Qizhen and finally TIANTONG. He died in 1652, aged 58.

steles.title: 天童林野奇和尚行狀
steles.author: 曹勳 Cao Xun
steles.author_note: ⭐ A named high official of the Ming: 「明賜進士出身文林郎翰林院編修前左春坊庶子兼侍讀學士掌院事纂修國史經筵日講冊封魯藩正使正治卿中奉大夫禮部右侍郎」 — jinshi, Hanlin compiler, court lecturer, compiler of the dynastic history, and Right Vice-Minister of Rites.
steles.quote: 師諱通奇，號林野。四川重慶府，合州人。父蔡、母余，生於皇明萬曆乙未十二月廿六日。… 偶閱密雲悟和尚語錄，看至參禪偈曰：「一念未生前，試看底模樣。」頓覺疑情猛發，寢食俱忘。將從前所知所解一應拋卻，詩文註疏盡投之火。
steles.note: ⭐ 'He threw all his poems, prose and commentaries into the fire.' The birth date — 萬曆乙未 (1595), 12th month 26th day — comes from here.

steles.title: 天童林野奇禪師塔銘
steles.author: 道忞 Daomin (= 木陳道忞 Muchen Daomin)
steles.author_note: ⭐ Abbot of Wanshou Chan monastery on Mt Daochang, Wuxing — and himself one of Miyun's twelve dharma heirs, i.e. the DEAD MAN'S OWN DHARMA-BROTHER writing his stupa inscription.
steles.quote: 師名通奇，林野其字也，合州人，本姓蔡氏。… 即臨濟兒孫光明烜赫，統系相承以來，十傳則有東山演，十一傳則有昭覺勤，十五傳則有臥龍，先十六傳則有徑山範，二十四傳則有海舟慈，沿流至先師悟和尚，閱世且三十矣，復有今林野禪師。
steles.note: ⭐⭐ A LINEAGE LADDER IN ONE SENTENCE, naming 海舟慈 (HAIZHOU CI) at the twenty-fourth transmission, flowing down to 'my late master Reverend [Yuan]wu.' This independently places Haizhou Ci in the Linji trunk above Miyun — evidence bearing directly on the contested Haizhou Puci edge elsewhere in this batch.

teacher.quote: 沿流至先師悟和尚…復有今林野禪師
teacher.note: 'Flowing down to MY LATE MASTER Reverend Wu … and now there is Chan master Linye.' Written by a dharma-brother who shares the same master.

teacher.quote: 偶閱密雲悟和尚語錄…至庚午春，先師過當湖
teacher.note: 'My late master passed through Danghu.'

teacher.quote: [TEACHER] 圓悟
Miyun's twelve heirs include 林野奇

dates.quote: 生於皇明萬曆乙未十二月廿六日
dates.note: b. 1595 (lunar; 1596-01-25 Gregorian).

dates.quote: d. 順治九年三月二十九日 = 1652-05-06, 世壽五十八 (《五燈全書》卷67)

bio.quote: 偶爾散步，不覺失足墜樓。正當跌時，如夢忽覺，便會一念未生前底道理。
bio.note: ⭐ 'Walking absently, he missed his footing and fell from the tower. In the very act of falling, as if waking from a dream, he understood.' The harvest note had this; the first-person text confirms it.

links.label: DILA Authority A012053
links.confirms: dates 1595-1652, teacher Miyun, Hezhou/Sichuan, the fall from the tower

bio: Born 1614 in Zi county, Chengdu, Sichuan; his father was Zhou Chaofu, his mother of the Rao clan, a family of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard. He was a child when the She chieftain's rebellion broke out in 1621; his father, telling him that 'because the world is not level there are wars and killings,' let him go, and he was placed at Jiulong monastery in Fushun county under Xingtian. He was taught by his father and his master for twelve years, until both died in the spring of 1633 — whereupon, reflecting that 'yesterday's is gone by this morning, and the morning's gone by evening,' he went to the elder Yinxin at Fujia hermitage. He became the heir of QIRAN CHAOZHI. He was abbot of Xilai monastery at Anlu in Hubei from 1657, and in 1680 succeeded his own master at Huanglong on Mt Baizhang, Xiangyang.

steles.title: 秀野林禪師語錄 〈行繇〉
steles.author: self-narrated, winter 1660, at the assembly's insistence
steles.quote: 有何行腳可說？若說行腳，家醜外揚，你等是無事生事，專露山僧醜拙也。… 予西蜀成都資縣人也，父姓周，諱朝富，母饒氏，世族錦衣。於萬曆四十二年甲寅七月初九日辰時生。
steles.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON. 'What travels are there to tell? To tell them is to air the family's shame abroad — you are making trouble out of nothing, just to expose this mountain monk's ugliness.' Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「秀野林禪師語錄三卷…有行繇。」

teacher.kind: his own 拈香, on the anniversaries
teacher.quote: 香嚴遠師翁週忌，拈香云：「親翁三番，覿面難睹；離翁一載，難睹覿面。」… 暮春宕師翁諱日，拈香云…
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE DECISIVE INFERENCE, AND IT IS FIRST-PERSON. He burns incense for 宕山遠 (Dangshan Yuan of Xiangyan) calling him 師翁 — GRAND-MASTER, i.e. his teacher's teacher. Dangshan Yuan is Qiran Chaozhi's master (attested at stele rung: 「香嚴宕山遠和尚嫡嗣」). Therefore Minglin's own master is QIRAN CHAOZHI. The generational term 師翁 does the work; no editorship is involved.

teacher.quote: 奇然智禪師語錄二卷，清超智說，明林、明燦等編…有行繇、塔銘。
teacher.note: ⚠ CORROBORATION ONLY, NOT EVIDENCE. Minglin edited his master's record and cut the stele for the press — but EDITING A MASTER'S SAYINGS IS NOT TRANSMISSION FROM HIM. This is listed to show I am aware of it and am NOT resting the edge on it.

dates.quote: 於萬曆四十二年甲寅七月初九日辰時生
dates.note: ⭐ BORN 1614, 7th month 9th day. Death not recorded.

bio: A WOMAN — a Chan nun. From Jingmen, of Guandong ancestry, long resident in the capital. Her father was Zhou Zhixiang, who followed the founding emperor on campaign and distinguished himself repeatedly, declined office, and retired to farming and study; her mother was of the Niu clan. The parents were over fifty and childless, and prayed to the three bodhisattvas for an heir. WHEN SHE CAME OF MARRIAGEABLE AGE HER PARENTS FORCED HER TO MARRY OUT — but she was chaste by nature, coveted neither pleasure nor wealth, vowed a lifelong fast before the embroidered Buddha, and set her will on the white robe; she was tonsured under the Reverend Buren. She then investigated Chan for more than twenty years, visiting teachers who pressed her hard, until the obstruction broke. She received the seal from her master GULÜ [FAN], and came forth as abbess of Yong'an and Hong'en. Her realisation, she said, came at Wutai and in Liaoxi; she met tigers, wolves and bandits without fear, and faced fire, flood, sword and famine as things of no weight. Imperial kinsfolk and officials were moved to build monasteries for her, and she was called 'the Ferry of Compassion'.

steles.title: 子雍如禪師語錄 〈行實〉
steles.author: self-narrated at the assembly's request
steles.quote: 余乃荊門人氏，祖籍關東，流寓都門甚久。父周，諱志祥。母牛氏。開國之初，父從駕，屢著功勳，不欲受官，隱於耕讀。… 年及笄，父母迫之於歸。素性貞潔，不貪嗜欲，不戀富貴，立願長齋繡佛，奮志脫白，禮補仁和尚為師薙染。從此參究禪旨，參將二十餘載… 然後受本師古律和尚印證，出住永安、洪恩二寺。
steles.note: ⭐⭐ 「年及笄，父母迫之於歸」 — 及笄 is THE term for a GIRL reaching fifteen and marriageable age, and 歸 is the verb for a woman marrying out. THIS IS DECISIVE: the master is a woman. FIRST-PERSON.

teacher.quote: 末後三上臺山，遇著惡毒老漢，當眾勘驗，逼得如上座死而復生，怨恨難忘。爇向爐中，供養現住仁壽堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十三世上古下律大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON, AND MAGNIFICENT: 'Three times at last I climbed Mount Tai, and met a vicious old man who examined me before the whole assembly and pressed Senior Ru until she DIED AND CAME BACK TO LIFE — a grudge hard to forget. I burn this in the censer for the Great Reverend GULÜ, thirty-third-generation transmitter of the orthodox Linji line, now at Renshou hall.' The grudge and the gratitude are the same act.

teacher.quote: 專申供養現住瑞巖方丈法伯老和尚併我本師上古下律老和尚
teacher.note: '…and MY ORIGINAL MASTER (本師) Old Reverend GULÜ.' The 本師 tag, again.

teacher.quote: 子雍如禪師語錄四卷，清成如（尼）說，祖圓記錄，永潛叟序，王治跋。南嶽下第三十七世，嗣古律範。
teacher.note: ⭐ TWO facts at once: the catalogue marks her 「（尼）」 — A NUN — and gives the teacher's dharma name 範.

school.quote: 傳臨濟正宗第三十三世

bio.kind: her own 語錄, opening dharma-hall
bio.quote: 又問：「大道不分男女相，還許某甲問…」
bio.note: ⭐ A questioner in her own dharma-hall says: 'The Great Way makes no distinction of male and female form — may I ask…' Her sex is a live matter IN THE ROOM. Contextual confirmation.

bio: A Xiushui man of Jiaxing, of the Zhang clan; on the night of his birth his mother dreamt of a rooster flying from a bridge into the sky, and he was named 'Bridge.' As a boy he built shrines of tile and stone, set Buddha-images on them, and made the other children bow. HE MARRIED AND HAD A SON — and when the boy was four he was still sighing 'the dust of the world sticks fast; how shall I get out?' His schoolmaster Fang Yanshan pointed him to the sutras and then to the man himself: 'Wuqu, the old man of your own prefecture, is a descendant of Linji, THE DIRECT TRANSMISSION OF CHAN MASTER YEWENG XIAO — a genuine man of the Way. Knock on his door and he will make much of you.' He went; Wuqu said 'I have waited a long time for you.' His mother would not let him leave home, so he practised while feeding her, and only after her death was he tonsured. When he set out to build a hermitage on Jingshan, Wuqu told him: 'YOUR AFFINITY LIES BY THE WATER' — and he settled at Cart Creek (Chexi) for over twenty years. He compiled his master's recorded sayings, and in 1610 was asked to lead the Chan retreat at Jingshan. He died in 1612, aged 72. His heir Nanming Huiguang carried the line on.

steles.title: 無幻禪師行狀
steles.author: not named in the text as read
steles.quote: 師諱性沖，號古湛，禾郡秀水人，俗姓張。育之夕，母卜氏，夢橋上一雞飛而沖天，因名曰橋。… 既娶，生一子，甫四歲，每嘆曰：「塵勞膠固，曷得出離？」… 方曰：「汝郡無趣老人，臨濟兒孫也，野翁曉禪師之的傳，乃本色道流，扣之必為子之所重。」… 趣囑曰：「子緣在水邊，今姑從汝志。」
steles.note: ⭐⭐ 'YOUR AFFINITY LIES BY THE WATER' — and DILA, which never saw this text, independently records that he ended up at 車溪, CART CREEK, for twenty-odd years. Two documents agreeing across four centuries.

teacher.quote: 專伸供養敬畏庵中無趣空和尚，惟願於光明中劈開面門，現大人相，與諸人等大家描摸。」遂作女人拜
teacher.note: ⭐ FIRST-PERSON, for WUQU KONG of Jingwei hermitage — and then 'he made a woman's bow' and said 'Look, look — this mountain monk's tongue has fallen to the ground!'

teacher.quote: 師欣然往參之。趣老曰：「吾待子久矣。」
車溪無幻古湛性沖 — 昭明寺無趣如空禪師法嗣。 [TEACHER 無趣如空]
teacher.note: ⭐ DILA's alias list contains the harvest note's exact long form 車溪無幻古湛性沖 — confirming that the long name and this man are one.

teacher.quote: 臨濟第二十六世嘉興東塔野翁曉禪師／臨濟第二十七世秀州敬畏菴無趣如空禪師／臨濟第二十八世杭州徑山無幻性沖禪師／臨濟第二十九世秦溪興善寺南明慧廣禪師
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ A NUMBERED LADDER, four consecutive generations, in the corpus. It simultaneously fixes Yeweng Xiao → Wuqu Rukong → Wuhuan Xingchong → Nanming Huiguang.

dates.kind: authority record, quoting 《無幻禪師語錄》卷2
dates.quote: 1540-12-28 – 1612-01-06 (嘉靖庚子十一月廿一日 / 辛亥季冬四日, 世壽七十二)

links.label: DILA Authority A007841
links.confirms: the long name 車溪無幻古湛性沖, dates 1540-1612, teacher Wuqu Rukong, Cart Creek

bio: Dharma heir of Xiuye Minglin, and thus the fourth in the Sichuan line Dangshan Yuan → Qiran Chaozhi → Xiuye Minglin → Zhitan Zuizheng. He was resident at the Huanglong hall on Mt Baizhang, Xiangyang, which his master had taken over in 1680. His recorded sayings survive in one juan, taken down by Shangneng and Shangying.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 (per the harvest note)
teacher.quote: 秀野林 … 三十四世
teacher.note: His own incense declaration names 秀野林 as his master, thirty-fourth-generation Linji, then resident at the Huanglong hall on Mt Baizhang, Xiangyang. FIRST-PERSON — this is the load-bearing evidence.

teacher.quote: 智覃正禪師語錄一卷，清最正說，尚能、尚瑩等編。
teacher.note: ⚠ The catalogue gives him NO 嗣 tag. It is silent on his teacher.

bio: A son of the Zhuang clan of Taixing in Weiyang (Yangzhou); his father's style was Chengzhi, his mother of the Ma clan, a house that had served the Three Jewels for generations. THERE WERE EIGHTEEN CHILDREN AND HE WAS THE LAST. In the cradle he would put his palms together at a Buddha-image and retch at the smell of wine or fish. At nine his brothers, sisters, nephews and nieces all died one after another; at eleven he lost his father, the family estate emptied and the gate went quiet — and the wish to leave the world stirred. But his mother was old, and he laboured to feed her and never failed in his duty, giving away what was left over and never thinking of marriage — until his mother arranged a match in secret and forced him to wed. His hunger for the Way only grew, and he strayed into a heterodox sect and even led it, before turning back: 'This is not the true gate to the Way — how can I go on thinking myself right?' At the Lantern Festival he went into the city to see the lamps, saw a notice for a Chan retreat at Juehua hermitage, and thought: 'Here is a gate of Chan; the road of practice is not lost after all.' He carried incense to Juehua and met ZHULANG. 'Layman, where do you come from, and what for?' — 'I have come to ask for teaching. But I do not know whether a householder may practise Chan.' Zhulang laughed: 'CAN YOU EAT AT HOME?' — 'I eat.' — 'IF YOU CAN EAT, YOU CAN DO CHAN.' He later held the Huayan hall at Longshan in Fenyang, Shanxi.

steles.title: 汾陽龍山華嚴堂上傳曹洞正宗第三十一世柏山楷禪師行實
steles.author: 通睿 Tongrui of Yuantong, west of Nanjing (金陵城西圓通通睿)
steles.author_note: Signed 「頓首述」. He also contributed a preface to the 語錄.
steles.quote: 師諱德楷，字柏山，維揚泰興莊氏子。父字承智，母馬氏，世奉三寶，一乳十八人，師居其殿… 浪曰：「居士何來，來此何事？」… 浪笑曰：「你在家可喫飯麼？」師曰：「喫飯。」浪曰：「既能喫飯，便可參禪。」
steles.note: ⭐ Note the TITLE ITSELF: 「傳曹洞正宗第三十一世」 — CAODONG, 31st generation. The genre heading carries the lineage. Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「山西栢山楷禪師語錄五卷…有行實。」

teacher.quote: 耑為供養江南揚州泰興覺華堂上五住道場，傳曹洞正宗第三十世無鼻孔沒意思竹浪本師老和尚，用酬法乳。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON: 'for my ORIGINAL MASTER, Old Reverend ZHULANG — that nostril-less, senseless old fellow — thirtieth-generation transmitter of the orthodox CAODONG line, of Juehua hall at Taixing, Yangzhou, Jiangnan.' The affectionate abuse is a nice touch and a mark of authenticity.

teacher.quote: 第二回拈出，耑為供養維揚泰興縣覺華堂上傳曹洞正宗第三十世竹浪本師和尚，用酬法乳。
teacher.note: The SAME declaration a second time, in a second dharma-hall. Not a slip of the brush.

teacher.quote: 傳曹洞正宗第三十一世柏山楷禪師行實

dates.quote: 師享年七十有四，僧臘四十有二…告寂…康熙壬午三月廿二日也
dates.note: 康熙壬午=1702, 享年74 -> born 1629; own 語錄 行實.

dates.quote: 康熙壬午三月廿二日 … 享年七十四

school.quote: 傳曹洞正宗第三十世 … 第三十一世
school.note: CAODONG — stated three times, twice in his own voice.

bio: A Kunshan man of the Li clan, tonsured at Shaolong cloister under Zhixing. He met XINGZHONG ZHIREN at Yunding and received transmission from him. He was abbot in turn of Pumen, Lingyan and Wanshou in Suzhou, and finally of JINGSHAN. Summoned to the capital in the early Yongle era, he took part in the compilation of the Yongle Encyclopaedia. He was himself a lamp-historian: he compiled the Zengji xu chuandeng lu in six juan, besides his own recorded sayings in two juan, for which Yao Guangxiao — the 'Black-Robed Chancellor' of the Yongle court — wrote the preface. He died in 1418, aged 74, with 67 years in robes. His heir was Cuifeng Zongmi.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 — 南石文琇禪師語錄
teacher.quote: 奉為前住萬壽行中大和尚一爐焫却，未論報德酬恩
teacher.note: 萬壽行中 = 行中至仁; 報德酬恩 raised by 文琇 himself. First-person. ⚠ In the same enthronement he raises a further stick (0383b01) for 文海慧辯 熈怡大和尚 — that is a DIFFERENT recipient (a seat-predecessor); the transmission stick is the 行中 one.

teacher.quote: 南石文琇禪師語錄四卷　明文琇說…姚廣孝序，南嶽下第二十一世，嗣行中仁。
teacher.note: 嗣行中仁 = 嗣行中至仁.

teacher.quote: 南石文琇禪師語錄四卷明文琇說，宗謐，妙門等編，元信跋（在前），姚廣孝序，南嶽下第二十一世，嗣行中仁。
teacher.note: 21st generation, heir of Xingzhong Ren. The preface is by YAO GUANGXIAO.

teacher.quote: 字南石，為行中至仁禪師（1309-1382）法嗣
行中至仁 (1309-1382), 番陽 吳氏, heir of 元叟行端
teacher.note: Generation arithmetic checks out.

dates.quote: 永樂十六年九月二十四日 = 1418-11-01, 世壽七十四, 僧臘六十七 (《增集續傳燈錄》卷5)

bio.quote: Kunshan man, surname 李; tonsured at 紹隆院 under 智興; received transmission at Huqiu in 1371; abbot of 普門 → 靈巖 → 萬壽 → 徑山; author of 《增集續傳燈錄》六卷

links.label: DILA Authority A000178
links.confirms: dates 1345-1418, teacher Xingzhong Zhiren, Jingshan abbacy, the Yongle Dadian, his own lamp-history

bio: A monk of Yuezhang cloister in Suzhou and a dharma heir of Tuiweng Hongchu (Jiqi/Lingyan Hongchu), and thus of the Sanfeng line: Hanyue Fazang → Hongchu → Neishao Zhizhong. At his opening of the dharma hall he burned incense first for Sakyamuni, then for Mahakasyapa and down through the line to Fazang, and finally for his own master, 'Old Reverend Lingyan, thirty-second generation of the orthodox Linji line, formerly resident at Guoqing on Tiantai.'

teacher.quote: 爇向爐中，專申供養臨濟正宗三十二世原住天台國清靈嵒老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ FIRST-PERSON: 'for Old Reverend LINGYAN, thirty-second generation of the orthodox Linji line, formerly resident at Guoqing on Tiantai — to repay the milk of the dharma.' 靈巖 = 靈巖弘儲 = 繼起弘儲 = 退翁弘儲: one man, several sobriquets.

teacher.quote: 供養禪宗第一祖迦葉尊者，下洎六十八世萬峰藏禪師。伏願金襴如舊，淵源法脈無窮。
teacher.note: He burns down the whole line to 藏禪師 — Fazang, his grand-master — before reaching his own teacher. The Sanfeng descent, in his own words.

teacher.quote: 內紹種禪師語錄二卷頌古一卷，清種說，照維等記，張有譽序。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣退翁儲。
智種 / 內紹 / 內紹種 / 內紹智種 — 為退翁弘儲禪師（1605-1672）法嗣。蘇州月掌僧人。（X82n1571_p0469a12）
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE FULL DHARMA NAME. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

links.label: DILA Authority A019286
links.confirms: full name 內紹智種, teacher 退翁弘儲 (1605-1672), Yuezhang in Suzhou

bio: Born 1625 in his home prefecture, of the Cheng clan. He was tonsured at fifteen under a clansman-monk, Xiaosong, and studied the doctrinal texts with him for years; then, hearing of the teaching-wind of the Old Man of Hengshan, he went and took refuge with him. At the first knock he set to work hard on the matter, morning and evening without let, and the old man valued him and named him Lingyi. HE PRACTISED BITTERLY FOR OVER TWENTY YEARS. One day he presented a verse, and the old man said: 'Today at last I know I have not deceived you' — and handed over the responsory verses, staff and whisk that had come down from GRAND-MASTER TIE, renaming him Zhuofeng. When Hengshan travelled to Jiangnan he took charge of Qingyun; he opened the dharma at Qingyun monastery in Zhongzhou in 1680, on the forty-ninth day after his master's death. When Hengshan died his burden grew heavier still. In the autumn of 1685 the man who had promised to help him died; within ten days Zhuofeng too fell ill, and as he lay dying he took brush and paper, wrote a few lines, threw down the brush and stared, as though something were still unsettled.

steles.title: 卓峰性玨禪師塔銘
steles.author: 性統 Xingtong (= 別菴性統 Bie'an Xingtong)
steles.author_note: ⭐ A dharma-relative — signed 「高峰法弟性統撰」 — and himself the compiler of the 續燈正統, one of the major Qing lamp records. A lamp-historian writing a stupa inscription.
steles.quote: 卓峰性玨禪師，本州成氏子，生于天啟乙丑七月十九日丑時。十五歲，祝髮于同族僧笑松座下。… 聞衡老人道風揚溢，遂皈禮焉。一蒙扣擊，力究箇事，晨昏不輟，老人器之，命號靈一，苦參二十餘載。一日，呈偈于老人，老人曰：「今日始知吾不汝欺也。」即將鐵師翁所傳沿流唱和歌、拄杖、拂子付之，更號卓峰。
steles.note: ⭐⭐ 「鐵師翁所傳」 — 'transmitted from GRAND-MASTER TIE.' 師翁 = the teacher's teacher. This is the tell that identifies the whole line — see flags.

teacher.quote: 聞衡老人道風揚溢，遂皈禮焉… 老人器之，命號靈一… 即將鐵師翁所傳…付之，更號卓峰。
teacher.note: ⭐ The transmission itself: the staff, whisk and responsory verses handed over, and the new name conferred.

teacher.quote: 卷清性珏說，宗位編（丁目作客慧錄），超原序，藍理序，有塔銘。南嶽下第三十一世，嗣衡山炳。
teacher.note: 'Heir of Hengshan Bing.' Note the editorial team (宗位 / 超原 / 藍理) is the SAME as for 衡山禪師語錄 (清燈炳說) — master and disciple, published by one hand.

teacher.quote: 燈炳 / 衡山 / 沖谷 / 衡山炳 / 慶雲炳 / 衡山燈炳 — b. 1611-05-22, d. 1680-07-13. 合江人，姓馮，忠州慶雲僧人。 [TEACHER 慧機]
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE TEACHER'S FULL NAME, DATES — AND HIS TEACHER. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

dates.quote: 生于天啟乙丑七月十九日丑時 … 今歲乙丑秋七月，先師化去…旬日後，師亦示微恙…瞑然將脫
dates.note: ⭐ b. 1625 (天啟乙丑); d. 1685 (乙丑), within days of the death of Xingtong's own master. Aged about 61.

links.label: DILA Authority A016343 (Hengshan Dengbing)
links.confirms: the teacher's full name 衡山燈炳, dates 1611-1680, and HIS teacher 慧機 (Tiebi Huiji)

bio: A Meizhou man of western Shu (Sichuan), of the Wang clan, and a dharma heir of YANSHI SHANKAI of Jinshan. He was abbot in turn of Bao'en, Nengren and Jiangshan Taiping-Xingguo in Jiankang, then Huqiu at Pingjiang, then Lingyin, and finally JINGSHAN — its thirty-sixth abbot. Emperor Lizong wrote out four characters for him, 'Shixi, robe-transmitting,' and titled him Chan Master Fohai. He died on the ninth day of the sixth month, 1254.

teacher.quote: 次拈香云：此一瓣香奉為前住雲居、後住紫金掩室先師大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: His OWN dharma-milk stick (用酬法乳之恩) to 掩室 (善開). A-grade first-person. He also holds 掩室's memorial-day incense (掩室和尚忌燒香) repeatedly — 先師.

teacher.quote: 石溪心月禪師語錄三卷，宋心月說，住顯編，劉震孫序…南嶽下第二十世，嗣掩室開。
teacher.note: ⭐ Heir of YANSHI KAI — and the catalogue supplies the dharma name 開 that the corpus text withholds.

teacher.quote: 金山掩室開禪師法嗣。俗姓王。 [TEACHER 善開 (A001343)]
善開 / 掩庵善開 / 金山善開 / 掩室善開 / 掩室 — 靈隱崇岳禪師法嗣，嘉泰元年（1201）赴廬山雲居請，未幾敕補金山。編有《松源崇嶽禪語錄》二卷。 [TEACHER 崇岳] [student 心月]
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ THE LOOP CLOSES. 掩室善開 was an HEIR OF SONGYUAN CHONGYUE — who is ALSO IN THIS BATCH. And Lu You's stupa inscription for Songyuan (B34n0193 lb 0114a05) names 雲居善開 as one of the two men to whom Songyuan entrusted the dharma by letter as he died. Same man. Verified live: 人名：1 筆.

dates.quote: 寶祐二年六月初九日示寂 = 1254-07-02 (《五燈全書》卷49; 《石溪心月禪師語錄》卷1)
dates.note: ⭐ DEATH YEAR GAINED — the harvest note had none. Birth still unknown.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.quote: 理宗賜書「傳衣石溪」四字，封佛海禪師。初住建康府報恩禪寺，遷能仁、蔣山太平興國等，晚住杭州徑山。
bio.note: The abbacy list matches the harvest note's exactly, independently.

links.label: DILA Authority A013818
links.confirms: death 1254, teacher 掩室善開, the Jingshan abbacy, the title Fohai

links.label: DILA Authority A001343 (Yanshi Shankai)
links.confirms: he is Songyuan Chongyue's heir and Shixi Xinyue's teacher

bio: A Caodong master, dharma heir of Sanyi Mingyu, and thus in the line of Zhanran Yuancheng. He entered Qichang monastery at Qianxi on the eighth day of the twelfth month, 1676. His recorded sayings were edited by his disciples Zhizhi and Zhiyuan.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 at 古資聖寺 (1672)
teacher.quote: …人天眾前拈出供養，即此堂上開山第一代傳曹洞正宗二十八世愚菴先老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: THE dharma-milk stick. Here 愚菴 is BOTH the founder of the temple (開山第一代) and his dharma-father — the two roles that the brief warns can be separate happen to coincide, and it is the SAME stick that carries 用酬法乳之恩.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 at two further seats
teacher.quote: 供養曹洞正宗二十八世梵受堂上愚菴先老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。／第五回拈出，供養本山傳曹洞正宗第二十八世先愚菴老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: Three (in fact five, by his own count) separate raisings, always 愚菴, always 法乳. He separates the OTHER sticks explicitly — 「用酬鎚陶鑄之恩」 goes elsewhere.

teacher.kind: THE IDENTIFICATION — the 塔銘 inside 三宜盂禪師語錄
teacher.quote: 雲門顯聖愚菴盂禪師塔銘。敕賜太白山天童弘法禪寺弘覺禪師道忞譔
teacher.note: ⚠ THIS IS THE WHOLE CASE. 愚菴盂 = 明盂 = 三宜明盂, abbot of 雲門顯聖寺; his pagoda-inscription, written by 木陳道忞, sits inside his own 語錄. 愚菴 is simply his hermitage-name. Corroborated at J/J35/J35nB336 lb0682b21, which heads a section 「愚菴盂禪師法嗣」. So 憲's incense names 三宜明盂 — DILA's 明盂 is right, and it is now FIRST-PERSON, not external.

teacher.kind: 嘉興藏目錄 — AND ITS BLUNDER
teacher.quote: 艸峯憲禪師語錄十卷 清憲說，智質、智原同編，翠峯揆序。南嶽下第二十一世，嗣愚庵及。依駒本增入并印。
teacher.note: ⚠ CATALOGUE ERROR, DOCUMENTED. 「嗣愚庵及」 — 'heir of Yu'an JI' — makes him the heir of 愚庵智及, who DIED IN 1379. Xian was enthroned in 1672. The cataloguer saw '愚庵' and reflexively appended '及', the famous Yuan-dynasty Yu'an (whose yulu, X71n1421, is the only 愚菴 title in the canon). It also files him 南嶽下 (Linji) when he is 曹洞. Two errors in one line. NOT to be followed.

teacher.quote: 屾峰憲 / 艸峰憲 — [TEACHER] 明盂
teacher.note: ⭐ Verified live: 人名：1 筆. The only authority record for him, and it gives the teacher.

teacher.quote: 三宜盂禪師語錄十一卷明明盂說，淨範等編，道忞序，魯元寵序，有塔銘（誤訂愚庵及語錄之後，今改正。）青原下第三十六世，嗣雲門澄。
teacher.note: His teacher SANYI MINGYU is 青原下第三十六世 (Qingyuan branch — i.e. CAODONG) and heir of 雲門[圓]澄 = 湛然圓澄 Zhanran Yuancheng. This fixes Shenfeng Xian's school as Caodong. Mingyu also has his own 塔銘.

dates.quote: 師生于萬曆己未九月十五日，入寂于康熙戊申七月十三日，世壽五十，臘二十一
dates.note: 萬曆己未=1619, 康熙戊申=1668. NOTE the '春秋八十八' at 0115b26 is a 掩龕 for a different person.

dates.quote: 屾峰憲 / 艸峰憲 — teacher 明盂 (三宜盂)
dates.note: DILA carries no dates; upgraded from his own 塔銘

school.note: via his teacher. 青原下 = the Qingyuan/Caodong branch, not 南嶽下.

bio.quote: 屾峰憲禪師語錄卷二門人智質智原同編住前溪古齊昌寺語錄住前溪古齊昌寺語錄康熙丙辰歲臘月八日入院。
bio.note: Entered Qichang monastery 1676 (康熙丙辰), 12th month 8th day.

bio: A NUN — the second abbess of the Fushi ('Lion-Subduing') convent at Meixi, succeeding her teacher QIYUAN XINGGANG. On Xinggang's death in 1654 the leadership was given jointly to her and to her dharma-sister Yichuan Chaolang; when Yichuan died, Yigong was left in sole charge. Her recorded sayings survive in one juan, taken down by Mingyuan, with a preface by Gao Yiyong and a colophon by her dharma-sister Yikui Chaochen. She stands in the Linji line Miyun Yuanwu → Shiche Tongcheng → Qiyuan Xinggang → Yigong Chaoke.

steles.kind: 塔 (inscribed stupa-stone, read by a witness)
steles.title: 祗園塔院題石 — 東峙者為義公
steles.author: n/a; reported by 高以永 in his 1678 preface
steles.quote: 有祗園塔院在焉。贍禮之餘，諦視題石，則知中立者為祗園，東峙者為義公。
steles.note: Not a 塔銘 text, but an inscribed stone reported by a named contemporary who examined it. Her stupa was built by her dharma-sister 一揆超琛.

teacher.kind: preface by 高以永, reading the stupa-stones
teacher.quote: 祗園得法于石車，一揆得法于祗園…有祗園塔院在焉。贍禮之餘，諦視題石，則知中立者為祗園，東峙者為義公。義公者，梅里人，亦祗園之法嗣，一揆之同儕也。聞道最早，向住伏獅菴，歿而一揆為之建塔于此。
teacher.note: The strongest thing that survives for her: a contemporary (1678) who walked into the stupa-court, READ THE INSCRIBED STONES, and reports which stupa is whose. 'The one standing in the middle is Qiyuan; the one rising to the east is Yigong.' 義公 is 祗園之法嗣.

teacher.kind: her own 拈香 on her teacher's death-anniversary
teacher.quote: 本師忌辰拈香，指像云：「大眾！還見者老漢麼？一生性太急，初參天童，道箇杲日當空。後嗣金栗，掀翻海嶽，獨步雲霄。」
teacher.note: She calls Qiyuan 本師 and holds her memorial. Her own account of Qiyuan's line — 初參天童 (Miyun Yuanwu) 後嗣金栗 (Shiche Tongsheng at Jinsu) — matches 高以永's 「祗園得法于石車」. Consistent, and it is HER voice.

teacher.kind: 行狀 of her teacher, in the teacher's yulu
teacher.quote: 行狀：伏獅袛園剛禪師行狀。師諱行剛，號袛園，浙江嘉興府嘉興縣人。俗姓胡…
teacher.note: Her teacher's 行狀; establishes 祇園行剛's identity and seat.

teacher.quote: 伏獅義公禪師語錄一卷，清（尼）說，明元記錄，高以永序，超琛跋。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣祗園剛。
teacher.note: ⭐ 「（尼）」 — A NUN, marked as such by the catalogue; 36th generation; heir of QIYUAN GANG. The colophon is by 超琛 = Yikui Chaochen, her dharma-sister.

teacher.quote: 性別: 女. Her SEVEN heirs: 普聞授遠、怡然超宿、義川超朗、義公超珂、一音超見、古鼎超振、一揆超琛
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ 義公超珂 is listed among Xinggang's seven dharma heirs, IN HER TEACHER'S OWN AUTHORITY RECORD. This also supplies Yigong's dharma name.

teacher.quote: there is also an extant yulu for Yigong Chaoke (1615-1661), one of the two nuns [charged with leadership] ... upon the death of Qiyuan Xinggang

dates.quote: Yigong Chaoke (1615-1661)

bio.quote: Qiyuan Xinggang (1597-1654), 女; her 行狀 and 塔銘 are in 《伏獅祇園禪師語錄》卷2

links.label: DILA Authority A018946 (Qiyuan Xinggang)
links.confirms: her teacher (female, 1597-1654), the seven heirs incl. 義公超珂 and 一揆超琛, and Shiche Tongcheng as Xinggang's master

links.label: 中文維基 祇園行剛

bio: A Yuan-dynasty Linji master, dharma heir of DONGYAN JINGRI (1221-1308), and the eighteenth-generation descendant of Linji. He was abbot of Baosheng at Qingyuan from 1299, of Dingshui Chan monastery from 1313, and of TIANTONG from 1329. He died in 1357. His recorded sayings were compiled by ten of his dharma heirs, among them Zhenru Wenqi and Wuzuo Wenshu; the preface is by Xingzhong Zhiren.

teacher.quote: 平石砥禪師…師諱如砥，嗣法於東巖日。袁文清公銘日公塔，蓋師所請也。文宗至順初，住持天童…
teacher.note: 師諱如砥，嗣法於東巖日 — an explicit 嗣法 biography. Grand-teacher 無準師範 (東巖淨日 嗣無準範, B35n0194 lb0581a01). Career anchor: 住持天童 at 至順初 (1330); disciples included 木菴聰 and 恕中無慍. Credit sub-song subagent.

teacher.quote: 天童東巖日禪師法嗣　天童平石如砥禪師
teacher.note: 東巖日 = 東巖淨日. 法嗣. His own 語錄 is catalogued (B35n0194: 平石如砥禪師語錄…嗣東巖日) but the TEXT is not in this corpus. DILA A009007.

teacher.quote: 平石如砥禪師語錄一卷，元如砥說，文栖、子昶、了因等編，至仁序，正印跋。南嶽下第二十二世，嗣東巖日。
teacher.note: 22nd generation, heir of DONGYAN RI. Note the preface is by 至仁 = 行中至仁 — Nanshi Wenxiu's teacher, also in this batch.

teacher.quote: 字石平，為東巖淨日禪師（1221-1308）法嗣，大鑑下第二十三世。

dates.quote: 至正十七年 = 1357: 「臨濟第十八代孫天童平石禪師砥公示般涅槃於東堂」（《平石如砥禪師語錄》卷1〈天童平石和尚語錄序〉）
dates.note: ⭐ DEATH 1357 — from the preface to his own recorded sayings. NO BIRTH YEAR EXISTS. Do not invent one.

bio.quote: 元大德三年 (1299) 慶元保聖 → 皇慶二年 (1313) 定水禪寺 → 天曆二年 (1329) 天童寺

links.label: DILA Authority A009007
links.confirms: death 1357, teacher Dongyan Jingri, Tiantong abbacy from 1329; NO birth year

bio: Name Yunfen, style Yuzhao, sobriquet Xiaotang. Of the Wu clan of Jingling; his father Yan was a district licentiate and his mother, of the Xu clan, was widowed early and kept a lifelong fast, reciting the Lotus daily — the boy would stand beside her with folded hands and listen, and vowed to become a monk to repay her. His mother assented; his clan did not, and forced him to marry. AT TWENTY HIS WIFE DIED and he was free at last. He was tonsured under the Dharma Master Xuancui at Liantai monastery in Yingzhou and took full precepts from the Vinaya master Sanmei. In the chaos of the dynastic collapse he hid on Mt Yuquan in Jingnan and studied the sutras three years, until a passage in the Lotus — the great white ox, 'stout and strong, its pace level, swift as the wind' — stuck in him. An elder told him: 'Master the whole canon and you are still caught in the fish-trap. If the sage's mind is not penetrated, you will not escape birth and death. Chan flourishes in the south. What is a pair of straw sandals to you?' He set out — and at his own gate found his mother dying, and stayed to nurse her and bury her before going. He met TUIWENG [HONGCHU] on the road in the spring of 1650. On New Year's Day 1651, during an intensive seven-day retreat, he came forward and bowed; Tuiweng struck him; he made to speak and Tuiweng struck him again: 'Are you trying to make Buddhism out of it?' — and at that word he was through. He offered Li Bai's poem as his verse of attainment, and Tuiweng laughed: 'I rejoice with you. Today you have reached your home village.' He held Qianming on Lushan from 1657, then Chicheng, Guangxian, Tongquan, Zizhi and Dongyan, and finally revived HONGSHAN BAOTONG BAOGUO monastery at Ezhu at the governor's request. When a monastery's officers proved unruly he simply shook out his robe and left: 'I have cut open my belly and gouged out my heart for them morning and evening and cannot alter their habits. I am ashamed of my thin virtue. I dare not learn to be a viper clinging to its den.'

steles.title: 嘯堂和尚塔銘併序
steles.author: not named in the portion read
steles.quote: 師名允汾，字俞昭，嘯堂其別號也。出竟陵吳氏，父嵒，邑諸生。母許，早寡。長齋奉佛，日課蓮經。師每侍側，拱而聽。有所感，發誓為僧，以酬高厚。… 辛卯元日，會同參八九輩起精進七，師亦與焉。午後，值翁下堂，師近前作禮，翁便打，師擬伸問，翁又打，曰：「汝儗作佛法會耶？」師於言下灑然領旨。… 翁笑曰：「我助汝喜，子今得達故鄉也。」
steles.note: ⭐ The whole life, and the transmission moment. Confirmed by the canon catalogue: B35n0194 「洪山俞昭允汾禪師語錄六卷，清允汾說，上睿等編，曉青序，卷五有塔銘。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣退翁儲。」 — the 塔銘 sits in juan 5.

steles.title: 嘯堂和尚塔銘
steles.author_note: In 洪山俞昭允汾禪師語錄 卷5. His record also carries a preface by his dharma-brother describing him arriving at Lingyan 'in a worn robe, speaking Chu dialect'.
steles.quote: 康熙庚申正月十三日，泊然長逝。世壽五十有九，僧臘三十有八。
steles.note: Source of his death date. The 敘 at the same location gives the finest detail on this roster: 退翁先師心賞之…先師集群弟子於廣堂，瞬顧一匝，語和尚曰：「汾！汝堪此任。」 — the master picking him out of the assembly by name.

teacher.quote: 適退翁先師赴台州天寧之請，遇於旅次。… 師於言下灑然領旨。
teacher.note: ⭐ 退翁先師 — 'my late master TUIWENG.' The stele's author is a dharma-brother speaking of their shared master.

teacher.kind: preface (敘) by 曉青, a dharma-brother
teacher.quote: 嘯堂汾和尚挾複子上靈巖，時予在侍寮典記，見其敝衣楚音，翛然自得，絕無近世禪殼子陋習。退翁先師心賞之，俾居不租寮… 先師集群弟子於廣堂，瞬顧一匝，語和尚曰：「汾！汝堪此任。」
teacher.note: ⭐⭐ A DHARMA-BROTHER'S EYEWITNESS ACCOUNT, dated 1686. 'When Reverend Xiaotang Fen came up to Lingyan with his bundle, I was serving as recorder in the attendants' hall. I saw his worn robe and his Chu accent, and how utterly at ease he was, with none of the shabby habits of today's Chan shells. OUR LATE MASTER TUIWENG took to him in his heart.' And then, in the great hall, the master looked round the assembly once and said: 'FEN! YOU ARE EQUAL TO THIS.' A contemporary who was in the room.

teacher.quote: 南嶽下第三十六世，嗣退翁儲。

teacher.kind: 敘 to his 語錄, by a dharma-brother
teacher.quote: 嘯堂汾和尚挾複子上靈巖，時予在侍寮典記…退翁先師心賞之，俾居不租寮…椎拂之下有所證入…先師集群弟子於廣堂，瞬顧一匝，語和尚曰：「汾！汝堪此任。」…始悟其久蒙記莂。
teacher.note: An eyewitness in the same monastery: 退翁 (Tuiweng Hongchu) was his master and had long since sealed him. CONFIRMS.

teacher.quote: 為退翁弘儲禪師（1605-1672）法嗣

dates.kind: authority record citing his 語錄
dates.quote: 康熙庚申正月十三日,泊然長逝。世壽五十有九，僧臘三十有八。(J37nB389_p0522c21)
dates.note: 1622 – 1680-02-12. NEW: the roster had no dates.

dates.quote: 至庚申正月五日示微疾…至十三日泊然長逝…師世壽五十有九，僧臘三十有八
dates.note: 康熙庚申=1680, 世壽59 -> born 1622; own 語錄 塔銘.

dates.quote: 康熙庚申正月十三日…世壽五十九

bio.kind: authority record citing 塔銘 + 五燈全書

links.label: DILA Authority A014466
links.confirms: teacher, dates, the 塔銘, identity with 嘯堂

bio: Abbot of Tianyuan monastery at Nanpu (Wanxian, Sichuan) and a dharma heir of MINSHU RUXIANG, who was himself an heir of Poshan Haiming. He had at least two dharma heirs of his own, Huanzhu Ming and Chunbei De, both of the thirty-seventh generation.

teacher.kind: 破山禪師語錄 — the collected sayings of 破山海明 (1597-1666), his dharma-GRANDfather
teacher.quote: 送耳毒法孫歸寶蓮　百里乘駒破暑來，引鞭逐動寶蓮開，老僧沒卻半邊鼻，珍重吾孫袖帶回。
teacher.note: 破山海明 calls him 法孫 — dharma-grandson — and 吾孫, my grandson. A dharma-GRANDSON of 破山 is precisely the heir of one of 破山's heirs. Combined with the lamp's naming of 敏樹如相 (a 破山 heir) as his master, the generation is nailed from BOTH ends by a living contemporary. This is the strongest witness available for him.

teacher.quote: 弔耳毒法孫　大哉法道繼兒孫，水有源頭木有根，一旦不知誰薄命，獨留孤雁淚荒村。
teacher.note: 破山 mourns him as 法孫. This also DATES HIS DEATH: before 1666, when 破山 himself died.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 五燈全書 j.87
teacher.quote: 《五燈全書》卷87：「南浦天圓耳毒泰禪師……(敏樹相嗣)。」(CBETA, X82, no. 1571, p. 481, c11-22)
teacher.note: The lamp names 敏樹如相 (敏樹相) as his master directly. 嗣 is a transmission verb.

teacher.kind: his heir 幻住明's own 拈香
teacher.quote: 此瓣香，千戈林裏垂手，烽煙際內接人，此是第三回拈出，今日對眾說破，專為天圓堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十三世耳毒大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: CAREFUL — an incense stick proves the teacher of the man who RAISES it. This one proves that 耳毒 was 幻住明's teacher (and fixes 耳毒's generation as Linji 33), NOT who 耳毒's own teacher was. It is placed here as corroboration of 耳毒's identity/generation, not of his teacher.

teacher.kind: his second heir 純備廣德's own 拈香
teacher.quote: 爇向爐中，供養我現住夔府百福山天圓堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十三世耳毒先師太和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: 先師 = 'my late master' — so by the time 純備 was enthroned, 耳毒 was already dead. Same caveat as above: proves 耳毒 taught 純備.

teacher.source: harvest note, from 五燈全書
teacher.quote: 萬縣慈雲敏樹如相禪師
teacher.note: The harvest identified Minshu Ruxiang as his master. I could not locate a first-person incense for Erdu Tai himself.

teacher.quote: 幻住明禪師語錄二卷…南嶽下第三十七世，嗣耳毒泰。／純備德禪師語錄二卷…有塔銘。南嶽下第三十七世，嗣耳毒泰。
teacher.note: ⚠ INDIRECT. The catalogue never gives ERDU TAI'S OWN teacher — it gives him only as the teacher OF OTHERS. His heirs are 37th generation, which places him at the 36th, consistent with (but not proof of) descent from Minshu Ruxiang.

teacher.quote: 敏樹如相 (1603-1672): 破山海明和尚法嗣; 康熙八年(1669)返四川主持万县慈云寺; 53 dharma heirs
teacher.note: The TEACHER is solidly attested and himself an heir of Poshan Haiming — a roster node. But Erdu Tai's place among his 53 heirs is not something I could verify directly.

school.quote: his heirs are 南嶽下第三十七世

links.label: DILA Authority A010077 (Minshu Ruxiang)
links.confirms: the teacher: 1603-1672, heir of Poshan Haiming, Ciyun at Wanxian, 53 heirs

bio: A man of Minxian in Fuzhou, of the Deng clan. When KUCHAN ZIJING was teaching at Yishan he went to see him. One day Kuchan asked: 'Since once seeing the peach blossom, right up to now he has never doubted — where is it that he does not doubt?'
