He died on the twelfth day of the third month of 1707, aged 70, and was entombed to the right of Qingzhong's stupa. Thirty-three monks and eighteen laymen received his dharma.

steles.title: 竺峰敏禪師語錄 卷6〈塔銘有序〉
steles.author: 仇兆鰲
steles.author_note: Qiu Zhao'ao — Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, jinshi, principal graduate of the yichou examination, and the great commentator on Du Fu. A stupa inscription by a first-rank Qing scholar-official.
steles.quote: 欽定乙丑會魁賜進士出身翰林院侍讀四明仇兆鰲頓首撰……按狀師，西蜀酆陵人，姓徐氏，世業儒。師生而穎異，十歲薙髮，侍慶忠老人，能機辯，善偈頌。圓具後，掌記室廿有一載，而忠順世，師遂繼其席。
steles.note: Names the master (慶忠 = Tiebi Huiji), the twenty-one years of attendance, and the succession, in one sentence.

steles.title: 竺峰禪師行狀
steles.author: his disciples
steles.author_note: Sits in the same fascicle, immediately after the 塔銘.
steles.quote: 師諱幻敏，字竺峰，酆陵徐氏子，世業儒……十歲與萬峰善禪師同薙髮作沙彌，事慶忠老人……後值除夕，師獻席燈。忠書偈囑曰：「無根樹上九燈傳，果繫橘金枝葉鮮。稍稍借力油燈火，照開新舊樂人天。」命掌記室，執侍座下廿有一年
steles.note: The transmission verse itself, quoted verbatim — 'nine lamps handed down on the rootless tree'.

teacher.quote: 忠書偈囑曰：「無根樹上九燈傳……」命掌記室，執侍座下廿有一年
慶忠鐵壁機禪師語錄卷之二十　嗣法門人幻敏重編
teacher.note: He signs himself 'dharma-heir Huanmin' on the title page of his own master's discourse record, which he edited. The editor-trap inverted: here the editorship is itself signed evidence of the transmission.

teacher.quote: 字竺峰，為慶忠鐵壁慧機禪師（1603-1668）法嗣

dates.quote: 生於：明, 思宗, 崇禎, 十一年, 十二月, 十五日 / 康熙丁亥年（1707）三月十二日卯時示寂，世壽七十，僧臘六十五
dates.note: Chongzhen 11 = 1638; died 1707 aged 70. Roster had NO dates.

school.quote: 慶忠鐵壁機禪師語錄二十卷 清慧機說，幻敏重編，有行狀、塔銘。南嶽下第二十九世，嗣聚雲真。

links.label: DILA Authority A000153
links.confirms: dates, teacher, the 塔銘 and 行狀

bio: Of the Zheng clan of Yanguan (Haining); his father Qiru, his mother of the Lu clan. Born on the seventh day of the tenth month of 1587. A vegetarian from childhood, he entered Xingshan monastery at twelve under Zhouzhou and was tonsured at seventeen. Troubled by birth-and-death, he went to the old man Wuhuan at Chexi for instruction in practice, then attended Nanming Huiguang at Jingshan. Reading the Brahma-Heaven Sutra he had an insight and offered a verse; Nanming rebuked him, and he stopped writing verses. In the autumn of 1620, Nanming, gravely ill, put Xiangyan's verse to him; twice he moved to open his mouth and twice Nanming shouted him down, and when he nodded, Nanming handed him the transmission verse: 'A dharma neither given nor received, a mind neither given nor received; given to the handless one, it snaps the sinews of empty space.' He held Puming at Yunfeng in Fujian and died on the eleventh day of the tenth month of 1642, aged 56, in his thirty-ninth year as a monk.

steles.title: 傳臨濟正宗第三十世鴛湖用禪師塔銘
steles.author: 埽道人 (the 'Sweeping Wayfarer')
steles.author_note: An old friend — 'he and I met in the dharma long ago in the ruined Puming temple at Baizhu; who but I should write his last testimonial?' Commissioned by his heir Jie'an Jin, who carried his bones back from the wars.
steles.quote: 鴛湖和尚，法諱妙用，字玄微，父杭州海鹽鄭公啟儒，母陸氏……時戊申歲，南明廣禪師得法於無幻沖禪師者，其初亦從興善薙染
steles.note: The stele also resolves the teacher's OWN teacher: 南明廣 got the dharma from 無幻沖 — i.e. Chexi/Guzhan/Wuhuan Xingchong are all one man. See Nanming Huiguang's entry.

steles.title: 建寧普明鴛湖禪師行狀
steles.author: his disciples
steles.author_note: Sits immediately before the 塔銘 in the same fascicle.
steles.quote: 師諱妙用，號鴛湖，鹽官鄭氏子，生于萬曆丁亥年十月初七日酉時……庚申秋南病篤，舉香嚴偈問師。纔擬開口，南震威便喝……南即付以偈曰：「無傳無受法，無傳無受心，付與無手者，掣斷虛空筋。」
steles.note: The transmission scene and verse in full. Wanli dinghai = 1587.

teacher.quote: 南即付以偈曰：「無傳無受法，無傳無受心，付與無手者，掣斷虛空筋。」
號鴛湖，字玄微，南明慧廣禪師法嗣

dates.quote: 生于萬曆丁亥年十月初七日酉時
崇禎十五年十月十一日辰時示疾，世壽五十有六，僧臘三十有九
dates.note: Chongzhen 15 = 1642, aged 56 -> birth 1587. Confirms the roster's death year and supplies the birth.

links.label: DILA Authority A010708
links.confirms: dates, teacher, both the 行狀 and the 塔銘

bio: Of the Hu clan of Long'an in western Shu. He left home at nineteen and was fully ordained at twenty-two, then walked the Jiangnan circuit, calling at the gates of the great masters and finding an entry at each. In 1667 he visited Shaolin, passed Fengxue, and met Yun'e Xi; the connection took, and he stayed close to him for six years, receiving the seal. In 1672 he entered Qin and opened the dharma at Xingfu Chan monastery in Jingyang, then moved to Guangjiao, Qingfu, Dunhuang and Jinsu. In 1684 he took Xingshan, and in 1688 Fengxue — his master's seat. He left a discourse record and the Qiaokong yixiang, twelve fascicles each.

teacher.kind: 像讚 (portrait encomium) in his own 語錄
teacher.quote: 師諱如乾，號憨休，蜀西龍安人，胡姓。十九歲出家，二十二歲圓具，遂行腳江浙，遍參諸大宗匠之門，隨處皆有悟入。丁未遊少林，過風穴，參雲峨和尚，機緣相契
teacher.note: This is the closest thing to a life he has — a portrait-encomium at the head of his own record. No 行實 or 塔銘 is attached.

teacher.quote: 號憨休，為雲峨行喜禪師（1613-1676）法嗣……康熙丁未（1667）遊少林，過風穴參雲峨和尚，機緣相契，親炙六載，乃授記莂
法嗣有雪兆性、冲涵恒、斌雅鑑、憨休乾等多位
teacher.note: Confirmed from the teacher's end as well.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: NO DATES. Only reign-marks: active 1667-1688.

bio: Of the Xia clan of Fuling, a leading local family. He entered a monastery young and studied for years under Wansong; when Wansong died he went to Tiebi Huiji and received his transmission. He opened the dharma at two places — Huilong in Fu and Tanhua in Zhong — and died at Huilong at the age of fifty, which his stele-writer calls the kindness of dying at home. Disciples in both Fu and Zhong raised stupas for him. His record survives in a single fascicle; the man who wrote his stupa inscription admits he never met him and had not yet read it.

steles.title: 普門顯禪師塔銘
steles.author: 袁州鐸
steles.author_note: Yuan Zhoudou, principal graduate of the jiyou examination and Instructor of the Confucian school of Zhongzhou — a lay Confucian, and candid about the limits of his knowledge.
steles.quote: 師諱燈顯，號普門，開堂者二：一為涪之迴龍，一為忠之曇華。年五十示寂迴龍堂中，蓋誠得首丘之仁者。今涪、忠兩地門人各崇塔以藏不朽之骨……惜辭世早，語錄秖一卷，貽似刻行，余未獲見其人，亦尚未讀其語也。
steles.note: The stele also names his lineage: 「𭎸至忠南，獲睹吹萬大師及鐵壁和尚語錄」 — Chuiwan (聚雲吹萬廣真) and Tiebi, the grandfather and father of his house. Gives the age at death (50) but not the years.

teacher.quote: 並吹萬、鐵壁二大師未墜之統緒亦藉以顯
teacher.note: The stele frames him as the man through whom Chuiwan's and Tiebi's line is carried on.

teacher.quote: 號普門，為慶忠鐵壁慧機禪師（1603-1668）法嗣。涪陵人，俗姓夏。少從應院，初參萬松禪師有年。適松化去，參鐵壁禪師，得付法。
teacher.note: Wansong was the FIRST teacher and died; Tiebi gave the transmission. The roster has it right — but this is precisely the shape that trips roster-builders up.

teacher.quote: 普門顯禪師語錄二卷 清燈顯說，性胤錄，汪賀勛序，有塔銘。南嶽下第三十世，嗣慶忠機。

dates.quote: 年五十示寂迴龍堂中
dates.note: Died aged 50 — but the stele gives NO YEAR, and DILA says 生卒年不詳. The age is all we have.

school.quote: 南嶽下第三十世，嗣慶忠機

bio: Of the Chang clan of Puzhou in Hedong, Shanxi; his father styled Lushan, his mother of the Zhang clan. In his own words: at sixteen, looking up at the blue sky one summer evening as the sun set, he thought 'the world is so wide — why be penned in here and spoil my good roots?', and resolved to leave home. At twenty he dreamed of a flood on the Yellow River throwing up a flower ten feet high, and a wandering monk who said 'I have come to take you to my home.' He slipped away from his parents, went to Putuo, and was tonsured under Ruxiu. He served in kitchens and gardens, never sparing himself. At twenty-five he came to Miyun Yuanwu at Jinsu and vowed not to leave the hall until he had awakened; Miyun struck him across the head twice and he got nowhere. Seeing a monk reading the Wanfeng Record, he took up 'the ten thousand dharmas return to one — to what does the one return?', swept everything he had learned into the sea, and at twenty-seven put his question to his own master, then West Hall at Jinsu. He rebuilt the ruined Tang seat of Guishan, holding Miyin monastery on Mount Dawei from 1637, and died there in the spring of 1649, aged 50, passing the succession to his disciple Huishan.

steles.title: 五峰如學禪師語錄〈行實〉
steles.author: 自述 — spoken by himself in the winter of 1643 when Huishan and others begged him for his life
steles.author_note: First-person, opening 余乃山西河東蒲州人 ('I am a man of Puzhou…').
steles.quote: 癸未冬日，慧山等袖香作禮，乞師行繇。乃云：「余乃山西河東蒲州人。父常姓，字祿山。母張氏……於二十五歲，謁金粟密雲師翁……此時年二十七歲，值本師在金粟為西堂」
steles.note: FIRST-PERSON. He calls Miyun 師翁 ('grandfather-master') and reserves 本師 ('my own master') for Wufeng Ruxue, then West Hall at Jinsu. The distinction is made by the man himself — decisive.

teacher.quote: 謁金粟密雲師翁……值本師在金粟為西堂
teacher.note: 師翁 vs 本師 — grandfather vs father — in his own mouth. This is exactly the distinction the audit found the old roster collapsing elsewhere.

teacher.quote: 字養拙，為五峰如學禪師（1583-1631）法嗣……後嗣法五峰如學，居大溈山密印寺
函師靈骨奉歸大溈，養拙明公迎供建塔。癸未塔成，以不肖嘗瞻禮師足、竊附法末，養拙明公迺乞為塔銘……首度五峰
teacher.note: The disciple's office proves the bond: it was Yangzhuo who received his master's bones at Dawei, built the stupa (completed 1643), and commissioned the inscription — written by 陶汝鼐, 羊城外史, in the eighth month of 1643.

dates.quote: 卒於：清, 世祖, 順治, 六年, 正月 to 三月，50歲
dates.note: Shunzhi 6 = 1649, aged 50 -> birth c.1600. The roster's 'floruit 1637' is the year he took Miyin, not a birth.

bio: Of the Yue clan of Yongfeng village on the north road of Guozhou (Nanchong), born in 1626. His grandfather Menglong took the jinshi and served the Wanli emperor, was frugal and outspoken at court, and was reckoned a famous minister; the family kept to the Confucian line thereafter. As a boy he did not play, and was as grave as a grown man. He read a book once and put it down, yet could give back its sense in a few words that left old scholars straightening their robes. At seventeen he travelled to Mount Emei and was tonsured, and studied under Huijue Zhaoyi. He went to Yunnan and Guizhou and met the great master Zhizhi, who was sparing with approval but said only 'just so, just so' to him. Returning to Shu he met Huijue again, who likewise assented and handed him the robe and whisk: 'Take good care of it.' He was abbot at Wanshou in Renhuai, Longzhou in Jiading, Foxing in Ziyang, and finally rebuilt Xiangji at Nanchong. He died on the twenty-third day of the first month of 1667, aged 42.

steles.title: 破峰重禪師塔銘
steles.author: unnamed
steles.author_note: Appended to his own discourse record, 東山破峰重禪師語錄 卷2.
steles.quote: 師法諱普重，號破峰，果之北路永豐鄉人也，姓岳氏。其祖孟龍，登甲第，事明神宗皇帝，持己清約，在廷敢諫，以名臣稱，後嗣遂以儒傳家……年十七，出遊登峨峰，遂薙髮參慧覺和尚……去而歸蜀，復遇慧覺，慧覺亦復唯唯，如曩之遇知止者，乃舉衣拂授之曰：「珍重一祖，汝好為之。」
steles.note: The handing-over of robe and whisk, quoted. 天啟丙寅歲生 = 1626.

teacher.quote: 乃舉衣拂授之曰：「珍重一祖，汝好為之。」
號破峰，為慧覺照衣禪師（1605-1673）法嗣……徧參歸來，見慧覺和尚，得付法

dates.quote: 天啟丙寅歲生
dates.note: Tianqi bingyin = 1626.

dates.quote: 康熙六年正月二十三日示寂，世壽四十二，僧臘二十四
dates.note: Kangxi 6 = 1667, aged 42 -> birth 1626. Agrees with the stele.

bio: Of the Liu clan of Leting in Luanzhou. He would not touch meat even in the womb, and was born still and grave. His mother died when he was eleven and his father put him under Xiaokong at Hanjiadao to be tonsured. At eighteen he sealed himself in a retreat and, reciting the Lotus, stuck on the line 'the Buddha's son dwelling in this ground is already the Buddha's own enjoyment', and doubt arose. He went to Panshan and put it to Liaozong Chaojian, who simply hit him; the doubt grew fiercer and he held one phrase waking and sleeping. Watching the mid-autumn moon with the assembly, he drew a circle in the air and offered a verse; Liaozong approved it, gave him the source-record, and made him record-keeper for five years. From 1688 he was abbot of Wanshan in Luanzhou, then Shifo at Gaoshan, Huayan at Shengjing, Dizang at Ningyuan, Chaoyang at Qingshan and Shengyan at Leyi — over twenty years' teaching, a rare northern (Zhili/Liaodong) house.

steles.title: 灤州萬善暉洲昊禪師語錄 卷6〈略狀〉
steles.author: his disciples
steles.author_note: A 'brief account' — the abbreviated cousin of the 行狀.
steles.quote: 暉洲旲禪師，灤州樂亭劉氏子。胎不茹葷，誕而凝靜。十一歲母逝，父送依韓家道曉空薙髮……赴盤山參了宗見，將胸中所疑請問，見便打……見首肯之，即出源流記莂，命書記寮，五載。
steles.note: The source-record and certificate handed over by Liaozong — the transmission, named.

teacher.quote: 赴盤山參了宗見……見首肯之，即出源流記莂
字暉洲，為了宗超見禪師（1614-1688）法嗣。灤州樂亭人，俗姓劉。
teacher.note: The roster gave only '了宗'; the full name is 了宗超見.

teacher.quote: 了宗見嗣　灤州萬善暉洲昊禪師（補遺）

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: NO DATES. Only that he took Wanshan in 1688 (戊辰) and the record was sent to the canon in 1702 (康熙壬午).

bio: A Caodong master. The lamps say he was of the Zhang clan of Shangyu in Kuaiji, tonsured as a boy under Chengzhao Daoning, that he called on Zhenxie Qingliao at Changlu at twenty with some result, and then went home to Hongzhi Zhengjue at Tiantong, who acknowledged him as a true son of the inner room. He opened the dharma at Butuo in 1137, then Wanshou, Jixiang and Xuedou; in 1176 he was ordered to take Jingci monastery in Lin'an, and in 1180 retired to Xuedou. His own stupa inscription tells a different story (see below). Thirteen of his heirs are named.

steles.title: 淨慈慧暉禪師語錄 卷6〈塔銘〉
steles.author: 浪馳管子
steles.author_note: Appended to his own discourse record. NOTE this text has a Japanese transmission history, and its account diverges sharply from the Chinese lamps.
steles.quote: 師諱慧暉，金州安城人也，俗姓王氏子也……十六歲而恩遷化……乃到契禪師處……師從此依止十九年……師乃承契教而到天童，今正覺和尚盛化，眾已踰千數，你若去，乃可居第一座……隨宏智禪師一十七年……天童覺和尚者，是師之師尊也。共作證明，受二師之受印……師為僧六十八年，此中出世一十二年，七十歲即遷化。法嗣之出世人一十三人也
steles.note: *** THIS STELE CONTRADICTS THE LAMPS ON NEARLY EVERY BIOGRAPHICAL FACT. *** It says he was of the WANG clan of Ancheng in JINZHOU (not Zhang of Shangyu), that he trained nineteen years under 雪峯契 (a Fayan-line master), and that he died at SEVENTY (not 87). It agrees with the lamps on only one thing that matters: 天童覺和尚者，是師之師尊也 — Hongzhi Zhengjue was his master, and he attended him seventeen years.

teacher.quote: 天童覺和尚者，是師之師尊也。共作證明，受二師之受印
teacher.note: Even the divergent stele agrees on the teacher. This is the one claim on which stele and lamp converge — which makes it the strongest thing about him.

teacher.quote: 號自得，宏智正覺禪師法嗣……旋里謁宏智，許為室中真子
按五燈會元杭州淨慈自得慧暉禪師會稽張氏子，幼依澄照道凝染削進具，甫二十扣真歇於長蘆，微有所證，旋里謁宏智

dates.quote: 卒於：南宋, 孝宗, 淳熙, 十年, 十一月, 二十九日，87歲
dates.note: Chunxi 10 = 1183, aged 87 -> birth 1097. THIS IS THE LAMP TRADITION.

dates.quote: 師為僧六十八年，此中出世一十二年，七十歲即遷化
dates.note: *** THE STELE SAYS SEVENTY, NOT 87. *** DILA itself flags the conflict in a bracketed note: 「［《淨慈慧暉禪師語錄》卷6〈塔銘〉云：金州安城人，俗姓王。七十歲即遷化。］」 I RECORD BOTH and take neither as settled. I have listed 1097-1183 above because it is the tradition the roster and the chart already use and because the death date (淳熙十年十一月二十九日) is precise and corroborated by B16n0088 (端平二年… no — see flags); but the stele has the better claim on principle and the worse claim on corroboration.

links.label: DILA Authority A012808
links.confirms: teacher, school, and the date conflict

bio: Of the Fan clan of Jiazhou (Jiayang), born 1634. At ten he was tonsured by Huijue Zhaoyi and served him closely; seeing a corpse, he had an insight. He was abbot of Xiangguo monastery in Chongqing (Yuzhou). He edited his master's discourse record in three fascicles; his own runs to one. He died on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month of 1674, aged 40. His heir was Yitang Faxiu of Xiangguo, Chongqing.

teacher.kind: preface by his dharma-uncle 聖可德玉, written 甲寅 (1674)
teacher.quote: 佛語徹御，吾姪嘉陽范氏子也，得法於慧覺法兄和尚。御侍師終身，雖寒暑順逆百折摧而無墮容。憾其福不逮慧，未展雙桂之道而早夭。其存日，亦不喜人記錄其語。…時甲寅仲春花朝之日，華巖聖可德玉敘。
teacher.note: 得法於 — the transmission verb — written by a named contemporary who was the teacher's own dharma-brother, in the year Cheyu died. This is as close to the man as the record gets.

teacher.quote: 慧覺衣禪師語錄三卷 清照衣說，徹御等編，有行狀。南嶽下第三十五世，嗣破山明。附佛語御禪師語錄（目錄標斗葊大士錄，即徹御）…佛語御禪師語錄一卷 清徹御說，法秀等編，德玉序。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣慧覺衣。
teacher.note: Independently: he EDITED his teacher's record — a second, structural attestation of the relation.

teacher.quote: 為慧覺照衣禪師（1605-1673）法嗣。嘉州人，俗姓范。十歲禮慧覺衣禪師脫白，因觀死屍，有省……得法於慧覺和尚
佛語御禪師語錄一卷 清徹御說，法秀等編，德玉序。南嶽下第三十六世，嗣慧覺衣。
teacher.note: And the entry directly above it closes the roster's dangling edge: 「慧覺衣禪師語錄三卷 清照衣說，徹御等編，有行狀。南嶽下第三十五世，嗣破山明。」 So 慧覺照衣's own teacher is 破山海明 — the roster noted this edge 'dangles one generation short of 破山海明'; it dangles no longer.

dates.quote: 生於：+1634 / 康熙癸丑年（1674）十二月十五日示寂，世壽四十
dates.note: 1634-1674, aged 40. Roster had no dates.

bio.kind: his master's 行狀, which he edited
bio.quote: 清故湖山治平照衣慧覺和尚行錄。和尚諱照衣號慧覺。本渝之綦江縣人，俗姓熊……生於明萬曆乙巳年二月二十一日子時
bio.note: He compiled the account of conduct for his own master — an editorship that is itself evidence of the bond.

bio: Of the Zhuang clan of Jiangdu, Yangzhou; his father Jifang, his mother of the Shi clan, who dreamed an old monk lodged with her before his birth. Born on the seventeenth day of the third month of 1612. He lost his father at thirteen and, wondering where the dead go, resolved to leave home. At twenty he was tonsured at Zhongshan in Jinling; the next year he went to Ruibai Mingxue at Bianshan and asked how to settle birth-and-death. 'Who gives you birth-and-death?' — 'I don't know.' — 'What have you been practising?' — 'Reciting the Buddha's name.' — 'Who recites? And what is the Buddha?' He was left with nothing to say, and the doubt grew. Sitting the summer at Jiezhu, he looked up one night at a man lighting a lamp and broke open. Ruibai tested him hard and beat him repeatedly before acknowledging him. When lineage-forgery was rife, Ruibai had him open the canon and compile the Chuandeng zhenge, fixing the genealogy of the five houses. He opened the dharma at Yanshou in Puqi in 1654 and held Yunyan at Ningzhou, Yaoshan and others. He died on the twenty-fourth day of the intercalary seventh month of 1672, aged 61; forty men received his dharma.

steles.title: 元潔瑩禪師語錄 卷10〈塔銘并敘〉
steles.author: 淨符
steles.author_note: Jingfu of Zunsheng Chan monastery at Baiyan, Hangzhou — his dharma-brother (法弟), who says the fraternal tie left him no way to decline.
steles.quote: 塔銘并敘　古杭白巖尊聖禪寺法弟淨符拜譔……按狀：師諱淨瑩，字元潔，號睦堂，揚州江都莊氏子。父繼芳，母施氏，夢老僧託宿有妊……二十，投金陵鍾山脫白。明年壬申，走杭參弁山入就老人於報國
steles.note: 弁山 = Ruibai Mingxue's seat. The stele is built on a 行狀 written by 櫟山願公 and carried to Jingfu by Yuanjie's heir Dinggong of Gushan.

steles.title: 元潔瑩禪師語錄 卷10〈行狀〉
steles.author: 櫟山願公
steles.author_note: The account of conduct on which the stupa inscription is based.
steles.quote: 持櫟山願公所紀師行狀，索塔上銘於余
steles.note: The 塔銘 quotes it directly and at length ('按狀…').

teacher.quote: 走杭參弁山入就老人於報國……山便打，師便喝……此師資所以稱水乳契合者
瑞白明雪禪師之嫡嗣
元潔瑩禪師語錄十卷 清淨瑩說，智祥編，有行實、塔銘。青原下第三十七世，嗣瑞白雪。

dates.quote: 師生於明萬曆壬子三月十七子時，卒于清之康熙壬子又七月廿四日丑時，世壽六十一，僧臘四十有奇
dates.note: Wanli renzi = 1612; Kangxi renzi = 1672, aged 61. Roster had no dates.

links.label: DILA Authority A010055
links.confirms: dates, teacher, the 塔銘 and 行狀

bio: Of the Chen clan of Linhai, Taizhou; his mother of the Lin clan. At seven he entered the village school and never needed a lesson twice. Before he came of age he asked his parents to let him enter the sangha and was tonsured under Jizhao at Jingshan. He called on Lingshi at Jingci and on Yiyuan, then went with Mu'an Cong to Zhuyuan Miaodao at Jianyan monastery on Mount Zituo in Taizhou; barely had he opened his mouth on the 'wu' case when Zhuyuan shouted, and he awakened outright. He was abbot of Lingyan on Mount Xiang and then of Ruiyan in Huangyan. In 1374 a Japanese embassy asked the Ming court to send him to teach in Japan; nearing seventy and ill, he declined. He died on the tenth day of the seventh month of 1386, aged 78, in his fifty-ninth year as a monk, having written: 'Seventy-eight years, no dharma to speak of; the last word — the pillar wags its tongue. Bah!'

steles.title: 天台空室慍禪師行業記
steles.author: 宋濂
steles.author_note: Song Lian — the pre-eminent literatus of the early Ming, who signs it 金華宋濂再拜. The same hand that wrote Qianyan Yuanzhang's stupa inscription.
steles.quote: 天台空室慍禪師行業記……大矣哉！佛祖之道也，以心傳心。至唐之大鑑禪師，支分派別，衍於五季，盛於宋，微於元。
steles.note: Signed off at lb 0885b12: 「金華　宋濂　再拜」. A second stele is also attested — DILA cites 四明烏斯道撰行業碑, by Wu Sidao, which I did not locate in the corpus.

steles.title: 恕中和尚語錄序 and embedded biography
steles.author: 宋濂 Song Lian (金華宋公景濂)
steles.quote: 洪武七年十月二十二日翰林侍講學士中順大夫…（宋濂序）；…建石塔其上。
steles.note: Song Lian, the pre-eminent literatus of the early Ming, personally knew Wuyun ('遇休沐日必訪師劇談道妙') and wrote the preface. A stone stupa was raised over the ashes. The text also refers to 黃文獻公 (Huang Jin) being asked for a 塔銘 for the related monk 一庵 — I did not locate a separate 塔銘 for Wuyun himself.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense at enthronement
teacher.quote: 祝聖罷，次拈香云：此香已是第二回拈出，爇向爐中，供養我前住崑山薦嚴禪寺、晚年歸老紫籜峯頭西方廣院竺元大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: The dharma-milk stick, to 竺元 (Zhuyuan Miaodao), whom he places precisely at 薦嚴 monastery on Kunshan and in retirement at Zituo peak. First-person, unambiguous.

teacher.source: X/X71/X71n1416.xml, biography by 宋濂 (景濂) embedded in the 語錄
teacher.kind: 行狀-grade biography by a named contemporary (Song Lian)
teacher.quote: 偕木庵聰公、大宗興公往台州紫籜山，謁竺元道。公以看狗子無佛性話未破問，公纔開口，被一喝，師大悟，直得通身汗下。…先主明之靈巖時，夢堂噩公住瑞龍，覬師為寂照嗣。師曰：素志有在，不可奪也。一香遂為紫籜道公拈出，重得法也。
teacher.note: ⚠ THE TRAP DISARMED IN THE SOURCE ITSELF. Wuyun had a TONSURE master, 寂照端 (依寂照端公薙落), and an admirer, 夢堂噩, tried to enroll him as 寂照's heir. He REFUSED, and pointedly raised his incense for 竺元道 「重得法也」 — 'because it was from HIM he truly got the dharma'. The biography distinguishes the tonsure master from the dharma-father exactly as the evidence ladder demands. 大悟 under 竺元, precept-ordination separate.

teacher.quote: 竺原妙道（1257-1345）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十三世……往台州紫籜山謁崑山薦嚴禪寺竺元道和尚，纔擬開口問無字話，被元一喝，師豁然大悟
teacher.note: Written 竺原 and 竺元 interchangeably — the same man as the roster's 竺元妙道.

teacher.source: X/X84 增集續傳燈錄 / 五燈全書目錄 卷10
teacher.quote: 薦嚴道禪師法嗣

dates.quote: 卒於：明, 太祖, 洪武, 十九年, 七月, 初十日，78歲
dates.note: Hongwu 19 = 1386, aged 78 -> birth 1309. Roster had no dates.

bio: Of the Han clan of Yanguan (Haining), born on the thirteenth day of the tenth month of 1576. He resolved on the monastic life as a small child and was tonsured at Xingshan monastery in Zuili under Qinquan. He took the full precepts from the elder Guxin, then went into retreat at the old hermitage of Chexi on Mount Baiyun at Shuangjing and did not go out of doors for three years. One day he picked up a scrap of paper from the ground bearing the line 'Knowing the direction, one knows he has gone; but the one who goes does not arrive at a direction' — and had an insight. He brought it to the old man, who sealed him and made him head monk. He served Chexi at Jingshan for eight years, and the old man gave him the robe and a transmission verse. He then shut himself in a death-retreat at Yongqing monastery at Gaoting for four years. He made three vows: never to take a public seat, never to handle temple business, never to gather disciples. He died sitting, on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month of 1620, aged 45, in his twenty-third year as a monk. His heir was Yuanhu Miaoyong.

steles.title: 興善南明廣禪師語錄 卷1〈南明禪師行狀〉
steles.author: his disciples
steles.author_note: Attached to his own discourse record.
steles.quote: 師于徑山車溪服勤八載老人，付師衣法偈
steles.note: Quoted via DILA A010707, which cites 〈南明禪師行狀〉 verbatim. I did not open the file directly — the text is cited, not read, and is flagged as such.

teacher.quote: 時戊申歲，南明廣禪師得法於無幻沖禪師者，其初亦從興善薙染
teacher.note: *** THIS IS THE KEY. *** Yuanhu Miaoyong's stupa inscription states outright that Nanming Huiguang got the dharma from 無幻沖 — and the same text elsewhere calls the man 車溪無幻老人 (lb 0389a05: 往謁車溪無幻老人). So 車溪 (the place), 無幻 (a hao), 古湛 (another hao) and 性沖 (the dharma name) all name ONE man. The roster's 'Chexi Xingchong' is CORRECT and the apparent conflict dissolves.

teacher.quote: 古湛性冲法嗣。號南明，鹽官韓氏子……師于徑山車溪服勤八載老人，付師衣法偈
teacher.note: DILA writes the teacher 古湛性冲 while the narrative says 車溪老人 — internally confirming that the two names are the same person.

teacher.quote: 徑山冲禪師法嗣
teacher.note: The 續燈正統 files him under 「徑山冲」. As the roster already worked out, the only 徑山…冲 in the lamps is 癡絕道冲, thirteen generations too early. This is a lamp abbreviating 車溪…性沖 by his seat at Jingshan, not a second candidate. RESOLVED, not a real conflict.

dates.quote: 生於：明, 神宗, 萬曆, 四年, 十月, 十三日 / 泰昌改元庚申仲冬二十七日辰時奄然坐逝，世壽四十五，僧臘二十三
dates.note: Wanli 4 = 1576; Taichang gengshen = 1620, aged 45. Roster had NO dates at all.

bio.source: 〈南明禪師行狀〉 via DILA A010707
bio.note: Cited, not read directly.

bio: Of the Long clan of Tongchuan. His father died when he was eleven (or twelve) and he was tonsured under the old man Sanshan Denglai at Gaofeng; fully ordained at twenty-two. He heard Sanshan raise the case of Nanquan's pitcher and goose and had an insight, then worked the 'wu' case for a year until Sanshan raised Baizhang's opening of the fields and, at the words 'he spread his hands', broke through completely and was sealed. When Sanshan died in 1685 he succeeded to his seat. He restored Fayu monastery on Mount Putuo, converting it from a vinaya house to a Chan one — its first Chan abbot — and also held Yongshou at Dongyuan in Wulin. He compiled the Xudeng zhengtong, one of the very lamp records this harvest depends on, and the chronological biography of his own master. He died on the first day of the tenth month of 1717, aged 57, in his forty-fifth year as a monk.

steles.title: 《聖因接待寺》卷3〈第三十四代別庵性統禪師〉、〈塔銘〉
steles.author: unnamed
steles.author_note: In the Sheng'yin Jiedai temple gazetteer.
steles.note: Attested in DILA's mentionedIn field for A000635. NOT located in the CBETA Zen corpus — it lives in a temple gazetteer outside it. Recorded as existing, not read.

teacher.kind: 年譜 he himself compiled for his master
teacher.quote: 高峰三山來禪師年譜　南海普陀嗣法門人性統編
teacher.note: He signs himself 'dharma-heir Xingtong' on the title page of the chronological biography he wrote for Sanshan Denglai. His own hand, naming his own master.

teacher.quote: 為三山燈來禪師（1614-1685）法嗣……因三山舉百丈開田因緣至展手處，大徹，乃得印可。康熙乙丑（1685）三山歸寂，遂繼席。

dates.quote: 卒於：大清, 聖祖, 康熙, 五十六年, 十月, 初一日，57歲
dates.note: Kangxi 56 = 1717, aged 57 -> birth 1661. Confirms the roster's death year and supplies the birth.

bio: Of the Qu clan of northern Chu (Chenxi); his mother of the Wang clan. Born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month of 1618. From infancy he loved to look at Buddhist images. Coming of age, he heard a monk recite the Lotus line 'if one with wisdom hears it, he can believe and understand', and the wish to leave the world arose. In the collapse of the dynasty he abandoned his home and fled into Guizhou, where he was tonsured at the Guanyin grotto in Anshun by the elder Taixu and took the ten novice precepts; two years later he left for Hanguang and was fully ordained. Set to work on 'the face before your parents were born' he made no progress, and went to Yuechuang Chelu, who hit him twice and told him he was a dullard and to go back to the hall. He vowed to seal himself in until he understood; one night at the fourth watch, heavy with torpor, he fell to the ground and lost all consciousness — and when he came round, his limbs would not move, sweat streamed off him, and the doubt melted like a hundred-catty load set down. He came out and Yuechuang tested him on dozens of cases and confirmed him. He was abbot of Wanshou at Taiping in Annan, Puguang at Songkui, and Puxiang at Ciyun. He died in 1684, aged 67, in his forty-fifth year as a monk.

steles.title: 善權位禪師語錄 卷2〈塔銘〉
steles.author: unnamed
steles.author_note: Appended to his own record; opens with a survey of the Songkui landscape in Guizhou.
steles.quote: 權公名達位，楚北人也。萬曆戊午九月廿三日午時，毓於辰溪。父姓瞿，母王氏……尋住安南廣福寺，適幸蘭溪月幢禪師應請安龍，道經廣福，權公一見，喜自慶焉。蓋幢禪師得昭覺丈老人之傳，造詣深遠
steles.note: The stele also fixes the generation above: 月幢 received the transmission of 昭覺丈老人 = Zhangxue Tongzui. So the chain is 丈雪通醉 -> 月幢徹了 -> 松巋達位.

steles.title: 善權位禪師語錄 卷2〈行實〉
steles.author: 如純
steles.author_note: Written by his own dharma-heir Ruchun, who signs it 法嗣門人如純撰.
steles.quote: 師名達位，字善權，乃楚北人也。父姓瞿，母王氏。生於萬曆戊午九月廿三日午時……又辭光參月幢和尚……然後出關，復省覲幢。幢以數十公案驗之，師對無疑，方承印證……世壽六十七，僧臘四十五。法嗣門人如純撰
steles.note: Confirms the transmission and gives the age at death.

steles.title: 善權位禪師語錄 卷2 - 塔銘, 行實 and 分燈
steles.author: unnamed (appended to his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 「生於萬曆戊午九月廿三日午時，世壽六十七。」（〈行實〉）／（康熙）甲子仲秋廿三。
steles.note: Stupa inscription, account-of-deeds AND a 分燈 (lamp-division list of his heirs), all in fascicle 2 of his own recorded sayings. DILA A016435 cites all three. The death date is at J39, no. B469, p. 928, c17-19.

teacher.quote: 復省覲幢。幢以數十公案驗之，師對無疑，方承印證
字善權，為月幢徹了禪師（1614-1667）法嗣
teacher.note: Supplies the teacher's full name and dates; the roster gave only 月幢了.

teacher.quote: 善權位禪師語錄二卷 清達位說，大悅等編，吳之瑋序，有行實、塔銘。南嶽下第三十七世，嗣月幢了。

teacher.kind: 塔銘/行實 via authority record
teacher.quote: 字善權，為月幢徹了禪師（1614-1667）法嗣…辭光，參月幢和尚。一日經行，昏沉倒地，醒時自覺橫身輕快，疑情冰釋…省覲幢，得印證。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the harvest's teacher AND EXPANDS THE NAME: 月幢了 -> 月幢徹了 (1614-1667). The harvest flagged this edge as dangling because 月幢了 is not on the roster; the man is now identified and dated, so the node can be created.

dates.quote: 生於萬曆戊午九月廿三日午時……世壽六十七，僧臘四十五
dates.note: *** DISAGREES WITH DILA. *** 萬曆戊午 = Wanli 46 = 1618. DILA A016435 says 生於：明, 神宗, 萬曆, 四十七年 (1619). BOTH stele and 行實 say wuwu (1618) — two witnesses inside his own record against one authority entry. I TAKE 1618. Death: 1618 + 67 - 1 = 1684, and DILA's extensive note independently says 康熙二十三年示寂 (1684).

dates.quote: 「生於萬曆戊午九月廿三日午時，世壽六十七。」（〈行實〉）
dates.note: b.1619-10-29, d.1684-10-01, aged 67. ⚠ DILA's own header says 萬曆四十七年 (1619) but the quoted 行實 says 萬曆戊午, which is 1618. A one-year internal inconsistency in DILA; I take 1619, its computed value.

school.quote: sect: 臨濟宗 楊岐派；法嗣有善一如純、普渡大海等十位禪師以及王青華、龍孚世等五位居士

bio.quote: 楚北人，俗姓瞿…一日聞僧誦《法華經》至「有智若聞則能信解」之句感發出塵之念。時值世變，棄家入黔，至安順觀音硐禮太虛和尚披剃

bio: Of the Wu clan of Poyang. He was received by the monk Zhenchun Mu at Bao'en monastery at five and ordained at seven. The Central Asian monk Kongjian saw him and thought him remarkable, and sent him to Yuansou Xingduan at Jingshan, who made him record-keeper; Yuansou said of him, 'Recorder Ren is a tiger, and winged.' He came out as abbot at Yunding and Chongbao in Yuezhou, and at Huqiu and Wanshou in Suzhou. He was learned in the inner and outer canons and especially deep in the Book of Changes. In the Hongwu era he was summoned to the capital with Chushi Fanqi and Mengtang Tan'e and lodged at Tianjie monastery; his memorial pleased the Ming founder. He spent his last years at the Songlin hermitage. He died on the nineteenth day of the third month of 1382, aged 74, in his sixty-seventh year as a monk. He left the Danju shigao.

teacher.kind: 增集續傳燈錄, in the bio of his heir 文琇
teacher.quote: 洪武四年，熈怡翁說法虎丘，師謂：聞其名既久，必一見乃已。纔覿面，果契合。遂俾居侍司，升記室
teacher.note: Confirms 至仁 (熈怡翁) as a teaching/transmitting master (here as 文琇's teacher). For 至仁's OWN teacher, see DILA below.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 徑山lineage; 真牧純 tonsure from 續燈存稿 j.5
teacher.quote: REL teacher 行端 (元叟行端, A001032); REL teacher 真牧純 — 《續燈存稿》卷5：「五歲俾從州之報恩寺真牧純公受業，七歲得度。」
teacher.note: 元叟行端 is the dharma-father; 真牧純 is the TONSURE master (受業). The 行端 relation bibl is （望月）, a 20th-c encyclopedia, so this teacher edge rests on lamp tradition (roster's DILA quote: 「令參元叟行端於徑山，命掌記室」) rather than a quoted primary — held at B.

teacher.quote: 西域控空見而異之，令參元史行端於徑山，命掌記室。端嘗謂聚曰：仁書記虎而翼者也。
teacher.note: 元史行端 is a typo in the DILA record for 元叟行端 — the man is Yuansou Xingduan of Jingshan, as the roster has it. He is placed under him as record-keeper.

teacher.quote: 萬壽行中仁禪師法嗣
teacher.note: Heading — he is a teacher of record in his own right.

dates.quote: 卒於：明, 太祖, 洪武, 十五年, 三月, 十九日，74歲
dates.note: Hongwu 15 = 1382, aged 74 -> birth 1309. Matches the roster exactly.

bio.note: Cited in DILA mentionedIn; not independently read.

bio: Of the Fu (or Chuan) clan of Shangrao, Xinzhou. At eight he became a boy-attendant to the elder Chuan of Jingde monastery, who set him to bow to Guanyin; one night he dreamed the bodhisattva stroked his head, and thereafter books opened themselves to him. Struck by the Platform Sutra's phrase about fire burning the sea-floor, he went to Wuyi Yuanlai at Boshan, who set him on the Boatman Monk's case; he held it walking, standing, sitting and lying, and had an insight in the mill-shed when the millstone's nose pulled loose. He then sealed himself in for six years and reached the source; he wrote the Song of the Snow Barrier, and Wuyi, pleased, opened his door and made him head monk. He took the seat at Yingshan in 1627, and on Wuyi's death in 1631 the assembly pushed him to succeed at Boshan. In 1636 Huqiu and Miaoxing in Hangzhou invited him. Falling ill in autumn 1637 he resigned, sailed south, and reached Yingshan on the first of winter; he died on the eleventh day of the tenth month, aged 53, in his thirty-first summer.

steles.title: 信州博山能仁寺雪關大師塔銘有序
steles.author: 黃端伯
steles.author_note: Huang Duanbo — Judicial Commissioner of Hangzhou, who signs himself 法弟 (dharma-brother). A Ming loyalist who would himself be executed by the Qing in 1645.
steles.quote: 塔銘　信州博山能仁寺雪關大師塔銘有序　杭州推官法弟黃端伯稽首撰。雲巖以寶鏡三昧密付洞山，圓湛心光揀魔辨異，於是主賓互應、敲唱雙行，乃沿流至今。
steles.note: The text immediately before it (lb 0532b06) gives the death: 十月十一日，坐三十一夏，享年五十有三 — aged 53, thirty-one summers. A 傳 (〈博山雪關智誾禪師傳〉) sits in the same fascicle.

steles.title: 信州博山能仁寺雪關大師塔銘
steles.author: unnamed (in 雪關禪師語錄 卷13)
steles.quote: 生於萬曆乙酉年九月初一日 … 歿於崇禎丁丑年十月十一日
steles.note: His stupa inscription, in fascicle 13 of his own recorded sayings, cited via DILA A011738 (which quotes it for both birth and death). The same fascicle also carries a 傳: 〈博山雪關智誾禪師傳〉.

steles.title: 博山雪關智誾禪師傳
steles.author: unnamed
steles.quote: 乃參禮博山來公，山令默究船子藏身公案，行住坐臥提撕不忘，偶入槽廠見磨鼻拽脫有省。後掩關六載，始徹源底，偶作雪關歌，山見稱善，乃為開關，繼命首座。
steles.note: Cited via DILA A011738 from 《雪關禪師語錄》卷13. This is the source for the boat-monk huatou and the six-year sealed retreat.

teacher.quote: 無異元來禪師法嗣……乃參禮博山來公，山令默究船子藏身公案……後掩關六載，始徹源底，偶作雪關歌，山見稱善，乃為開關，繼命首座

teacher.note: Titled 'the Great Master Xueguan of Nengren monastery at Boshan, Xinzhou' — Boshan being Wuyi Yuanlai's seat, which Zhiyin inherited.

teacher.kind: 傳 + 塔銘 via authority record
teacher.quote: 無異元來禪師法嗣…乃參禮博山來公，山令默究船子藏身公案…山見稱善，乃為開關，繼命首座。受瀛山之請，至博山和尚遷化，眾推繼席。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the harvest's teacher. 博山來公 = Wuyi Yuanlai of Boshan. He succeeded to Boshan's own seat on his master's death.

dates.quote: 十月十一日，坐三十一夏，享年五十有三
dates.note: Aged 53. With DILA's birth (Wanli 13 = 1585) this gives death 1637.

dates.quote: 生於：明, 神宗, 萬曆, 十三年, 九月, 初一日 / 丁丑秋示微恙……十月十一日示寂，坐三十一夏，享年五十三
dates.note: Wanli 13 = 1585; dingchou = 1637. Roster had no dates.

dates.quote: birth 生於萬曆乙酉年九月初一日 (1585-09-23)；death 歿於崇禎丁丑年十月十一日 (1637-11-26)（《雪關禪師語錄》卷13〈塔銘〉）
dates.note: Both from the stupa inscription. Aged 53. Harvest had no dates.

school: Linji, Yangqi branch (22nd generation below Huineng)
bio: Of the Ge clan of Tanyang. Feeding monks at Jingci in Hangzhou one day, he happened to open the Platform Sutra and it came to him as something long familiar. When Fojian was ordered to take Jingshan, he and Tianjie Ri went together to study there and got the essentials. He then went to Duanqiao Miaolun and worked at it hard, asking for instruction eleven times; sitting bolt upright one evening he suddenly saw the lamplight in front of him and broke open. He came out as abbot of Ruiyan in Taizhou. He died on the seventh day of the first month of the first year of Zhiyuan. His heirs included Wujian Xiandu, Jingtang Gu and Yiyuan Ling.

teacher.quote: 斷橋妙倫（1201-1261）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十二世…後謁斷橋，猛力參究，請益至十一度。
teacher.note: teacher 斷橋妙倫 confirmed; 請益 x11 then transmission.

teacher.quote: 天台無見覩禪師語錄…南嶽下第二十三世，嗣方山寶。
teacher.note: his heir 無見先覩 confirms his place in the chain.

teacher.quote: 杭州淨慈方山文寶禪師，俗姓葛。斷橋妙倫（1201-1261）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十二世……後謁斷橋，猛力參究，請益至十一度
天台無見覩禪師語錄一卷 明先覩說……南嶽下第二十三世，嗣方山寶。
teacher.note: Confirms from below: 無見先覩 is his heir, exactly as DILA's heir-list says.

teacher.source: X/X84 續燈正統目錄 卷1
teacher.quote: 瑞巖寶禪師法嗣
杭州淨慈方山文寶禪師，俗姓葛。斷橋妙倫（1201-1261）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十二世
teacher.note: DILA relation type=teacher -> A000470 妙倫. Duanqiao's OWN record independently says 法嗣文寶、善靖為編《斷橋和尚語錄》 — both ends. Roster/batch CONFIRMED.

teacher.quote: 倫公之傳為方山寶公，而禪師則得法於寶公
teacher.note: Huang Jin, a leading Yuan literatus, writing the preface to Wujian Xiandu's record, states the chain 斷橋妙倫 -> 方山文寶 -> 無見先覩.

dates.quote: 至元元年正月初七日示寂
dates.note: NO YEAR-NUMBER USABLE: 至元 is ambiguous (1264 under Kublai, or 1335 under Toghon Temür). Given his master Duanqiao died in 1261 and his heir Wujian Xiandu died in 1334, the later 至元 (1335) is the plausible one — but I do NOT assert it. No birth anywhere.

dates.quote: death +1308-02-07 至元元年正月初七日（《徑石滴乳集》卷1）編按：元朝有二個至元年號，取前一個太早，後一個太晚…
dates.note: CAUTION, AND DILA SAYS SO ITSELF: there were two 至元 eras in the Yuan; the earlier gives a death before his own disciples were born, the later is too late. DILA takes 1308 while flagging the problem. I record 1308 with the same warning. Birth unknown.

dates.quote: 至元元年正月初七日…編按…疑「至元」為「至大」之訛。暫定為「至大元年」（1308）
dates.note: DISPUTED: DILA editor changed 至元 to 至大元年=1308 because 至元 conflicts with disciples' birth years. His lamp gives 閱世七十一,坐夏五十八 (X84n1585) but no anchor year -> birth ~1238 if death 1308.

bio: Of the Chen clan of Shanghai (Yunjian). Tonsured at eighteen under Wuhai Xue and fully ordained at twenty. He called on Gunan Men and Xuedou Yun, then went to Ruo'an Tongwen at Jiashan, served him long, entered the inner chamber and received the transmission. He lived in retreat at Daqian and Puti in Qizhou, then held Li'an monastery at Nanjian in Hangzhou — where over four separate terms he was the fifth and longest-serving abbot — as well as Longyou at Jinshan and Zhulin at Jiashan. He also wrote the Liangzong jueyi in the Linji-Caodong lineage controversy. He died in 1694 aged 71, in his fifty-third year as a monk, and was entombed to the right of Li'an. Thirty men received his dharma.

steles.title: 天笠珍禪師塔銘 (in 武林理安寺志)
steles.author: 毛際可 (Mao Jike), 祥符令、遂安〔知縣〕
steles.quote: 乃為銘曰：弱齡慕道，出塵之姿；遇盜不死，盜即導師…惟師荷擔…天顏大悅，法門龍象，誰續傳燈，貞珉永勒。祥符令、遂安毛際可撰塔銘。
steles.note: His stupa-inscription, preserved whole in the 武林理安寺志 (GA021). Also note his heir 夢菴格 (0240a30) and 獨超方 (0243a07) each got literati stelae — one by 和碩莊親王, one by the future Yongzheng — appended in the same gazetteer.

teacher.kind: 武林理安寺志 — full house biography
teacher.quote: 傳臨濟正宗第三十二代‧第五次住持天笠珍禪師。師姓陳氏，諱行珍，江南上海人，天笠其法號也…禮無海學公薙染，時年十八。參箬菴和尚於杭之南澗…箬菴隨命侍香夾山，於「趙州勘臺山婆子話」下，頓徹古今公案源底…箬菴印以偈云：「吹毛不犯當頭令，出窟金猊果俊哉！」又稱於眾曰：珍雖年少，悟處確實，法門令器。
teacher.note: 印 (sealed) + a transmission-verse quoted verbatim. The 理安寺志 is a gazetteer — a stele-grade house record — and it gives him a full 傳.

teacher.quote: 箬菴命掌書記，始垂記莂…丁未夏應洸禪師之請，繼南澗祖席。
teacher.note: 垂記莂 — the prediction-seal was conferred. Continued Ruo'an's own seat at Nanjian.

teacher.quote: 號天笠，為箬庵通問禪師（1604-1655）法嗣。江南上海人，俗姓陳……再參箬菴問于夾山。參禪領悟，執侍久之，得躋堂奧，遂膺付囑

teacher.source: X/X85 正源略集目錄 卷1
teacher.quote: (天笠珍法嗣
teacher.note: Heading — he is a teacher of record himself.

dates.quote: 卒於：大清, 聖祖, 康熙, 三十三年，71歲 / 康熙三十三年示寂，世壽七十一，僧臘五十三
dates.note: Kangxi 33 = 1694, aged 71 -> birth 1624. Roster had no dates but its note already carried 世壽七十一，僧臘五十三 — now sourced.

bio.note: 〈傳臨濟正宗第三十二代．第五次住持天笠珍禪師〉. Cited in DILA; outside the CBETA Zen corpus.

school: Linji, Yangqi branch (Juyun 聚雲 house; 27th generation below Huineng)
bio: A monk of Zhugong (Jiangling). He is remembered in a single exchange: coming to Wunian You, he was asked, 'Trekking county to county, roaming prefecture to prefecture — what in the end is it all for?' He said, 'The great matter of birth-and-death. I ask the master to ferry me across.' Wunian said, 'Are you a man of Jingzhou, then?' He stands in the Juyun branch's reconstructed line of Dahui Zonggao, between Wunian You above him and Tieniu Deyuan below.

teacher.quote: 荊山懷寶禪師，渚宮人。為無念有法嗣。（明清序：014；X84n1583_p0498a20）
teacher.note: *** THIS IS THE NAME EXPANSION. *** The roster carried only the sobriquet + one glyph and said 'NOT expanded'. DILA has him as 懷寶 — 荊山懷寶. His origin, 渚宮 = Jiangling, also matches the corpus exchange below, in which Wunian asks him whether he is a man of Jingzhou.

teacher.quote: 荊山寶禪師法嗣　秦嶺鐵牛德遠禪師。自印心於荊山後，菴居秦嶺。
teacher.note: Confirmed from BELOW as well: his heir Tieniu Deyuan 'sealed his mind at Jingshan'.

teacher.kind: lineage recited in a 塔銘 context
teacher.quote: 二仰欽無念有荊山寶。荊山即我授受本師也。
teacher.note: FIRST-PERSON, from the mouth of a master in the Juyun line reciting his own descent: 'Jingshan is the very master from whom I received.' The chain 二仰欽 -> 無念有 -> 荊山寶 is stated as lived transmission, not compiled genealogy.

dates.note: NO DATES ANYWHERE. DILA carries none.

bio.quote: 舉：「荊山寶和尚參無念，念曰：『躐縣遊州，畢竟為著何事？』寶曰：『生死大事，求師濟度。』念曰：『汝是荊州人麼？』」
bio.note: The only narrative scrap of his life that survives. It is his meeting with his teacher.

links.label: DILA Authority A019881
links.confirms: dharma name 懷寶, origin, teacher

school: Linji, Yangqi branch (27th generation below Huineng)
bio: Abbot of Dagang in Nanjing and of Guang'en monastery in Beijing. In 1452 he was ordered back to Dagang in Nanjing and granted the title Cishan. When Jingcheng, a monk of Puji monastery on Wutai who had worn himself out on the sutras without settling his mind, came to him for confirmation, he put a few questions that Jingcheng could not answer, set him on 'does a dog have buddha-nature', and on his awakening gave him the robe and whisk.

teacher.quote: 二十二世無際悟…二十三世月溪澄，住北京廣恩寺，景泰三年勅賜回南京大岡。
teacher.note: 月溪澄 stands as the very next generation after 無際悟 in the table — the teacher-edge (無際明悟 → 月溪澄) is CONFIRMED from the corpus, upgrading the roster's DILA-only line.

teacher.quote: 南京大崗月溪澄禪師，無際悟（1381-1446）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十七世。住北京廣恩寺。景泰三年（1452），勅賜回南京大岡，號慈善。
teacher.note: *** NAME EXPANSION: DILA carries 月溪惟澄 among his names — the dharma name is 惟澄. *** The roster carried only the sobriquet + one glyph and said 'NOT expanded'; DILA expands it, and supplies the teacher's dates.

dates.note: NO BIRTH OR DEATH ANYWHERE. The only fixed point is the imperial order of 1452 (景泰三年).

dates.quote: 壬寅，示寂於天真塔，建本山
dates.note: 壬寅: he was active 景泰3(1452, 賜號慈善), so 壬寅=成化18=1482. Reign disambiguated by documented 1452 activity. teacher 無際明悟(1381-1446).

school.quote: 臨濟宗 楊岐派 / 大鑑下第二十七世

links.label: DILA Authority A010860
links.confirms: dharma name 惟澄, teacher, seats, the 1452 order

bio: Indian monk, traditionally a prince of a south-Indian kingdom, who studied under Prajnatara and came by sea to Guangzhou. DILA's authority record has him failing to connect with Emperor Wu of Liang, crossing to the Wei, and settling at Shaolin on Mount Song, where he is said to have faced a wall for nine years; his teaching is summed up as the 'two entrances and four practices'. His named disciples are Huike and Daoyu. The dates are genuinely disputed in the sources (528, 535 or 536).

teacher.source: T/T50/T50n2060.xml (續高僧傳, 道宣, c.645 — the EARLIEST source)
teacher.quote: 菩提達摩。南天竺婆羅門種。神慧疎朗。聞皆曉悟。志存大乘冥心虛寂。…初達宋境南越。末又北度至魏。隨其所止誨以禪教。…有道育慧可。此二沙門…尋親事之經四五載。給供諮接。感其精誠誨以真法。
teacher.note: ⚠⚠ CONTRADICTION / DISPUTED. The earliest and most authoritative source gives Bodhidharma NO teacher whatsoever — I checked: 般若多羅 does NOT occur anywhere in 續高僧傳. The teacher 'Prajnatara 般若多羅' is a construction of the later lamp tradition (from the 8th-c. 寶林傳 onward) and reaches DILA via 景德傳燈錄. I do not flip the field (the tradition is what the roster documents) but mark `disputed`: for a figure this legendary the teacher edge is doctrinal, not historical, and the earliest witness is silent on it.

teacher.source: DILA A001361 (rel type=teacher, n=般若多羅)
teacher.quote: 從般若多羅學道
teacher.note: DILA cites X79n1563_p0658b18. No stele or contemporary source exists for this man; the whole biography is legend hardened by repetition.

dates.quote: 示寂年代有梁大通二年（528）、梁大同元年（535）或二年等異說。（佛光：5207）
dates.note: DILA records the disagreement rather than resolving it. I take 535 as the roster does, but this is a convention, not a fact.

school.quote: 禪宗 … 中國禪宗初祖，西天第二十八祖

bio.quote: 南天竺香至國王子…居嵩山少林，面壁九年。隨緣倡禪，弘揚二入四行。有弟子慧可、道育。

notes: First Patriarch of Chan and traditionally the 28th Indian patriarch. Born as a prince in southern India, possibly of the Pallava dynasty. Arrived in China c. 520, reportedly met Emperor Wu of Liang who asked about the merit of his works; Bodhidharma replied 'no merit.' Settled at Shaolin Temple on Mount Song, where tradition says he sat in wall-gazing meditation (壁觀) for nine years. His teaching emphasized direct transmission outside scriptures. Named Huike his dharma heir after Huike demonstrated wordless understanding.

bio: From Yongjia, lay surname Dai; ordained at eight. He trained first in Tiantai calming-and-insight, then went to Caoxi and had the single exchange with Huineng that earned him the nickname 'the One-Night Awakening' (一宿覺). He died in 713 at forty-nine. The Song Gaoseng zhuan names four disciples. The Song of Enlightenment (證道歌, T2014) and the Yongjia ji (T2013) are transmitted under his name.

teacher.kind: 〈禪宗永嘉集序〉 by 魏靜, 慶州刺史 — THE CONTEMPORARY. He personally attended Xuanjue, and he is the man who gathered the ten pieces into the 永嘉集 after his death.
teacher.quote: 唐慶州刺史魏靜述 … 大師俗姓戴氏。永嘉人也。少挺生知。學不加思。幼則遊心三藏。長則通志大乘。三業精勤。偏弘禪觀。 … 靜往因薄宦。親承接足。恨未盡於方寸。俄赴京畿。自爾已來。幽冥遽隔。 … 大師在生。凡所宣紀。總有十篇。集為一卷。
teacher.note: READ WHAT IS NOT THERE. 魏靜 says 『親承接足』 — I personally attended at his feet. He mourns him. He edits his collected works. He gives his surname, his birthplace, his training (『幼則遊心三藏。長則通志大乘。偏弘禪觀』 — Tripiṭaka study, then Mahāyāna, then above all 禪觀). AND HE NEVER MENTIONS HUINENG. Not 曹溪, not 六祖, not the one-night awakening, not a teacher of any kind. The single closest witness to this man's life — a student, an editor, a mourner — does not know the story on which the entire edge rests.

teacher.quote: 至韻陽時，謁曹溪慧能，與慧能相問答而得其印可
teacher.note: DILA cites X79n1563_p0659a01.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 佛祖統紀
teacher.note: DISAGREEMENT: DILA records a SECOND teacher, the Tiantai master Huiwei. Both are real: Huiwei/Xuanlang was his doctrinal training, Huineng the Chan seal. The roster's single 'Huineng' is right for the Chan line but hides the Tiantai formation.

dates.kind: authority record citing 宋高僧傳
dates.quote: 以先天二年十月十七日。……。春秋四十九。（T50n2061_p0758a29）

bio.quote: 俗姓戴，八歲出家，博探三藏，尤通天台止觀…著有〈證道歌〉

notes: Author of the Song of Enlightenment (證道歌). Said to have attained awakening in a single night's meeting with Huineng.

bio: Dharma heir of Mazu Daoyi. He taught at Mount Pan in Youzhou (Hebei), from which he takes his name, and was posthumously titled Chan Master Ningji. His one recorded heir is Puhua. His birth and death years are not recorded in any source I could reach — DILA states them as unknown.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, 幽州盤山寶積禪師
teacher.quote: 幽州盤山寶積禪師。…師上堂示眾曰。心若無事萬象不生。意絕玄機纖塵何立。…向上一路千聖不傳。學者勞形如猿捉影。
teacher.note: Listed in the 馬祖道一禪師法嗣 section of 景德傳燈錄 (the TOC places him among 馬祖's 18 recorded heirs). 馬祖道一 confirmed.

teacher.quote: 馬祖道一（709-788）之法嗣，居於幽州（河北）盤山
teacher.note: 馬祖道一 confirmed.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 景德傳燈錄
teacher.quote: 馬祖道一（709-788）之法嗣，居於幽州（河北）盤山
teacher.note: DILA cites T51n2076_p0251b15.

dates.quote: 籍貫、生卒年均不詳。
dates.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE ROSTER. The roster carries floruit 720 / death 790. DILA says explicitly that both his origin and his dates are unknown. I could find NO source for 720 or 790 anywhere. Both should be dropped or shown as conjecture.

bio.quote: 諡號「凝寂大師」

notes: Known for 'The mind-moon is solitary and round; its light swallows the ten thousand forms.'

bio: A Silla monk known almost solely as a link in one lineage. The stele of Master Jijeung at Bongamsa — composed by Choe Chiwon and erected in 893 — traces the line from the Fourth Patriarch Daoxin through Beomnang (法朗), Sinhaeng (信行/神行) and Junbeom to Hyeeun (惠隱) and finally to Jijeung himself. Nothing else about his life is recorded.

steles.kind: 塔碑銘 (his teacher-line named on a disciple's stele)
steles.title: 大唐新羅國故鳳巖山寺教諡智證大師寂照之塔碑銘 (the Jijeung stele, 893, by 崔致遠)
steles.author: 崔致遠 (Choe Chiwon)
steles.author_note: The great Silla literatus; he wrote the stele for Jijeung, Junbeom's dharma great-grandson.
steles.quote: 雙峯子法朗。法朗孫信行。曾孫遵範。玄孫惠隱。末孫大師也。
steles.note: Junbeom is not the subject — he is a rung on the ladder named in his descendant's stupa inscription. This is exactly the 'stele appended to an heir' pattern. Preserved in 朝鮮佛教通史 (B31n0170).

teacher.quote: 雙峯子法朗。法朗孫信行。曾孫遵範。玄孫惠隱。末孫大師也。
teacher.note: 信行 = 神行 (Sinhaeng). CONFIRMS the roster teacher, from a named stele carved within a century of the man.

teacher.kind: lineage table in 朝鮮佛教通史
teacher.quote: 【四祖派】道信下一世法明。二世信行。三世遵範。四世惠隱。五世新羅智證國師。
東京神行弟子。（全唐文．拾遺．卷四十四．…智證大師寂照之塔碑銘）

bio.note: The stele is the ONLY source. The roster's floruit 780 / death 820 is a guess from lineage position and I could source neither.

notes: Obscure link figure in the Beomnang-Daoxin lineage. Known only from the Jijeungdaesa stele at Bongamsa (893 CE, by Choe Chiwon). Transmitted the dharma from Sinhaeng to Hyeeun.

bio: Son of a cake-seller in Zhugong. He left home under Tianhuang Daowu and later built a hermitage at Longtan (Longtan Chan cloister, Lizhou, Hunan), from which he is named. He transmitted the dharma to Deshan Xuanjian — their exchange over the blown-out paper lantern is one of Chan's most-told awakening stories. His birth and death years are not recorded.

teacher.quote: 屬青原行思法系，從天皇道悟出家，得悟玄旨…傳法於德山宣鑑。
teacher.note: received lineage: 天皇道悟 (Qingyuan line).

teacher.kind: documents the 天王/天皇 dispute
teacher.quote: 權德輿馬祖塔銘．皆以天王為馬祖嗣…佛國白、達觀穎、呂夏卿、張無盡皆著辨．證傳燈之誤。
teacher.note: in-corpus record of the Song controversy over whether 龍潭's 道悟 was 天皇 (Qingyuan) or 天王 (Hongzhou).

teacher.quote: 屬青原行思法系，從天皇道悟出家，得悟玄旨
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. Note the notorious 道悟 problem: 天皇道悟 vs 天王道悟 was a live sectarian dispute, and which Daowu is meant decides whether Deshan's line is Qingyuan or Nanyue. DILA takes 天皇道悟 (Qingyuan). Flagging, not resolving.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE ROSTER, which carries 780-840. DILA says the dates are unknown. I found no source for 780 or 840.

bio.quote: 在俗為渚宮胡餅師之子…後結庵於澧州（湖南澧縣）龍潭禪院…傳法於德山宣鑑。

links.label: DILA Authority A010427
links.confirms: teacher, student, bio; states dates UNKNOWN

notes: Teacher of Deshan. Their encounter with the blown-out candle is one of Chan's most celebrated awakening stories.

contested_by.rival_evidence: Two Tang steles survive as quotations and cannot both describe one man. 丘玄素's stele for 天王道悟 (d.818, Mazu's heir): 「嗣法一人，曰崇信，即龍潭也」 -- one heir, Chongxin. 符載's stele for 天皇道悟 (d.807, Shitou's heir) lists three heirs and Chongxin is NOT among them. Same city, 11 years apart, 皇 vs 王 -- one stroke. 景德傳燈錄 welded them into one.
contested_by.kept_evidence: 景德傳燈錄 (1004), which conflated the two Daowus.
contested_by.stake: Re-parents 龍潭→德山→雪峰→雲門+法眼 out of Qingyuan into Nanyue -- about a quarter of the chart. Also THE great Chan forgery question (the 1653 五燈嚴統 war). Neither stone survives.

bio: Dharma heir of Danxia Tianran. He taught at Cuiwei in the Zhongnan mountains near the capital, hence his name. The Jingde chuandeng lu lists five heirs under him, among them Touzi Datong. His birth and death years are not recorded.

teacher.quote: 鄧州丹霞山天然禪師法嗣七人：京兆翠微無學禪師　丹霞山義安禪師…
teacher.note: Filed first among Danxia Tianran's heirs.

teacher.quote: 京兆終南山翠微無學禪師，初問丹霞：如何是諸佛師？丹霞咄曰：幸自可憐生，須要執巾𢃭作麼？師退三步。丹霞曰：錯。師即進前。丹霞曰：錯錯。師翹一足旋身一轉而出。丹霞曰：得即得，孤他諸佛。師由是領旨，住翠微。
teacher.note: 領旨 — he grasped the essential point, under Danxia. Followed immediately by 投子 (Touzi Datong) coming to HIM — showing Wuxue as teacher, not pupil, of the next generation.

teacher.quote: 鄧州丹霞山天然禪師法嗣
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.note: ⚠ DILA gives NO birth or death for him. The roster's 800-860 is unsourced; I could not source it.

bio.kind: authority record citing 景德傳燈錄
bio.quote: 京兆翠微無學禪師法嗣五人.....伏牛山元通禪師 (T51n2076_p0317a17)

notes: Dharma heir of Danxia Tianran.

bio: Lay surname Chen, of Muzhou; dharma heir of Huangbo Xiyun. He kept the precepts strictly and was learned in the canon. After decades as abbot of Guanyin cloister he returned to Kaiyuan monastery and wove rush sandals to support his mother — hence 'Chen the Sandal-Weaver'. He died in 877 aged ninety-eight. He is the master who slammed the gate on Yunmen's leg.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 index of Huangbo's heirs
teacher.quote: 洪州黃檗山希運禪師法嗣一十二人：鎮州臨濟義玄禪師、睦州龍興寺陳尊宿、杭州千頃山楚南禪師…已上六人見錄。
teacher.note: 睦州龍興寺陳尊宿 = 睦州道明, listed directly under 黃檗希運, second only to 臨濟. Upgrades the roster's DILA line to a primary lamp index.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, his heirs listed
teacher.quote: 睦州陳尊宿法嗣二人：睦州刺史陳操（一人見錄）、睦州嚴陵鈞臺和尚。
睦州陳氏，黃檗希運禪師（751-850）法嗣
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.kind: authority record citing 佛祖歷代通載
dates.quote: 乾符四年召門人曰：「此處緣息，吾當逝矣！」…壽九十八。（T49n2037_p0843a20）
dates.note: Death 877 (乾符四年) at 98 → birth c.780. The roster's floruit 800 is loose; birth 780 is the better figure.

bio.quote: 後歸開元，織蒲鞋以養母，有「陳蒲鞋」之稱。

notes: Slammed the gate on Yunmen's leg, triggering his enlightenment. Called 'Chen the Sandal-Weaver.'

bio: A nun, disciple of Yangshan Huiji. The one substantial notice of her is Dogen's: Yangshan chose her as director of the estate office (廨院主) over the objection that she was a woman, saying she had the spirit of a great man, and while serving there she took on visiting monks over the wind-and-flag koan. No dates, no lineage record of her own, no stele.

teacher.quote: 永平道元和尚曰。妙信尼仰山之弟子也。仰山選廨院主曰。信淮子雖是女流。有大丈夫志氣。正堪為廨院主。遂充之。信在廨院。與蜀僧商量風幡話。
teacher.note: 妙信尼仰山之弟子也 — 'the nun Miaoxin is a disciple of Yangshan'. Explicit teacher statement. This is 弟子 (disciple), not a narrated transmission — grade C is right. No dates survive.

teacher.kind: 禪林象器箋, quoting Dogen (永平道元)
teacher.quote: 永平道元和尚曰。妙信尼仰山之弟子也。仰山選廨院主曰。信淮子雖是女流。有大丈夫志氣。正堪為廨院主。遂充之。信在廨院。與蜀僧商量風幡話。
teacher.note: The ONLY corpus attestation of her, and it is second-hand: an Edo-period Japanese Zen encyclopedia quoting Dogen (1200-53), who is himself centuries after the fact. She has NO DILA authority record at all. Teacher = Yangshan is confirmed only at this remove.

school.note: School follows from the teacher, not from any statement about her.

bio.note: ⚠ The roster's 'defeated seventeen traveling monks' is NOT in the corpus text, which says only 蜀僧 ('monks from Shu'). The number seventeen comes from Dogen's 正法眼藏 raihai-tokuzui, which is not in this corpus; I did not verify it and have left it out. The roster's dates 830-890 are unsourced.

notes: Woman Chan master who defeated seventeen traveling monks in dharma combat.

bio: From the capital district (Jingzhao), lay surname Wang. He entered Shishuang Qingzhu's room and served him two years, then was put in charge of the North Pagoda, going about in hemp robe and straw sandals. He later taught at Mount Daguang in Tanzhou, from which he is named; the Jingde chuandeng lu lists thirteen heirs under him.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, 潭州大光山居誨禪師
teacher.quote: 潭州大光山居誨禪師。京兆人也。姓王氏。初造于石霜之室。函丈請益經二載。又令主北塔。麻衣草屨殆忘身意。
teacher.note: 初造于石霜之室…經二載 under 石霜慶諸; the 景德傳燈錄 lists him in the 石霜慶諸禪師法嗣 section (T51n2076 lb0325b22).

teacher.quote: REL teacher 慶諸 (石霜慶諸, A010581)
teacher.note: 石霜慶諸 confirmed.

teacher.kind: flat 法嗣 index in 景德傳燈錄
teacher.quote: 潭州石霜慶諸禪師法嗣四十一人 … 潭州大光山居誨禪師
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster teacher.

teacher.quote: 潭州大光山居誨禪師。京兆人也。姓王氏。初造于石霜之室。函丈請益經二載。又令主北塔。麻衣草屨殆忘身意。

dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster's corrected 837-903.

bio.quote: 潭州大光山居誨禪師法嗣一十三人

notes: Dharma heir of Shishuang Qingzhu (807-888). Dates corrected from d.950 to d.903 per lineage chronology.

bio: From Hebei; dharma heir of Xinghua Cunjiang, from whom he received transmission in 887. He taught at the South Hall (Nanyuan) of Baoying monastery in Ruzhou. His heir Fengxue Yanzhao carried the Linji line on, and it is through him alone that Linji Chan survived. He died in a 壬子 year — 952.

teacher.quote: 興化存獎禪師（830-888）法嗣…參興化禪師，大悟玄旨，密契宗風，光啟三年（887）得付法。
teacher.note: transmission verb 得付法; teacher 興化存獎 confirmed.

teacher.quote: 興化存獎禪師（830-888）法嗣…參興化禪師，大悟玄旨，密契宗風，光啟三年（887）得付法
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.quote: 壬子…南院慧顒禪師示寂。
dates.note: 壬子 in this chronology = 952 (廣順二年).

dates.quote: 南院慧顒禪師示寂壬子…慧顒住南院，壬子入滅。
dates.note: A SECOND independent chronicle, same 壬子.

dates.quote: 壬子（周太祖廣順二）南院慧顒禪師示寂。（X76n1516_p0132b24）
dates.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE ROSTER, which has death 930. Two chronicles and DILA all say 壬子/952. I take 952. The roster's 930 has no source I could find. (Scholars do dispute this man's dates; but 930 is not the sourced reading.)

bio.quote: 居汝州南院…有《汝州南院禪師語要》。法嗣有風穴延昭禪師、穎橋安禪師。

notes: From Hebei. Taught at the South Hall (Nanyuan) of Baoying Monastery in Ruzhou with an extremely strict, confrontational style. Critical link in the Linji lineage: only through his line (via Fengxue Yanzhao) did Linji's transmission continue.

bio: Dharma heir of Yunmen Wenyan, seventh generation under Nanyue. He taught at Xinkai cloister in Yueyang (Baling), from which he is named. He was known for his quickness in debate — his nickname 鑑多口, 'Jian the Talker'. Two heirs are recorded. His dates are not.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 heir-list, 雲門文偃禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 〔韶州雲門山文偃禪師法嗣上二十五人〕…岳州巴陵顥鑒大師…益州香林澄遠禪師…
teacher.note: In the SAME 25-man Yunmen heir-list as 德山緣密 (this batch) and 香林澄遠 (teacher of 智門光祚, this batch). One list, three of my men.

teacher.quote: 嶽州巴陵新開顥鑒大師，初在雲門。雲門舉雪峯和尚云：開却門，達磨來也，問師意作麼生？師曰：築著和尚鼻孔。
teacher.note: 初在雲門 — under Yunmen from the start.

teacher.quote: 岳州巴陵新開院顥鑒禪師，雲門文偃（864-949）禪師法嗣，南嶽下七世
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.note: ⚠ DILA gives NO dates. The roster's 910-970 is unsourced and I could not source it.

bio.quote: 善辯，有「鑑多口」之稱。嗣法弟子有靈澄散聖、興化興順。

notes: Direct heir of Yunmen Wenyan, taught at Xinkai Temple in Baling (modern Yueyang, Hunan). Instead of written transmission documents, he used three turning phrases to convey the essence of the Yunmen school. Appears in Blue Cliff Record cases 13 and 100.

bio: From Jiangxia, lay surname Zhang; ordained at Chongxiao monastery and awakened under Liangshan Yuanguan. When his teacher died he went to Dayang, whose abbot ceded him the seat; he held it fifty years, it is said without once crossing the threshold. He was renamed 警延 to avoid a taboo character. Dying with no heir able to carry the Caodong line, he entrusted his robe and sandals to the Linji master Fushan Fayuan with instructions to find a man — which is how Caodong survived. He died in 1027, aged eighty-five.

teacher.quote: 朗州梁山緣觀禪師法嗣一人：郢州大陽山警玄禪師（一人見錄）。
teacher.note: Sole heir of 梁山緣觀 — the roster's edge is exactly right.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, his own entry
teacher.quote: 郢州大陽山警玄禪師…曰：「未審法嗣嗣何人？」師曰：「梁山點出秦時鏡。」
teacher.note: His own words point back to 梁山 as his teacher.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 景德傳燈錄
teacher.quote: 朗州梁山緣觀禪師法嗣一人 郢州大陽山警玄禪師 (T51n2076_p0418c15)
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.kind: authority record citing 佛祖歷代通載
dates.quote: 天聖五年七月十六日陞座辭眾…『吾年八十五…』，停筆而化。
dates.note: 1027, aged 85 → birth 943. CONFIRMS the roster exactly.

bio.kind: authority record citing 補續高僧傳
bio.quote: 師以臘高無可繼法之人，一日喟然謂遠曰『洞上一宗，如懸絲欲斷，惟汝興之。』…於是以皮履布裰付遠，囑令求人。
bio.note: This is the source for the entrusting-of-the-lineage story. X77n1524_p0411c24.

links.label: DILA Authority A004661
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the Fushan Fayuan entrustment

notes: Last living Caodong lineage holder. Entrusted lineage to Linji master Fushan Fayuan to preserve the school.

bio: From Fuliang, lay surname Lin; ordained young at Baoji monastery and dharma heir of Kaixian Shanxian. He was a fine calligrapher and poet and a famous talker. Under Yuanfeng he presided at Jinshan, Jiaoshan, Dayang and Yunju — nine seats in all. Shenzong granted him robe and bowl and the title Chan Master Foyin. Su Shi, Huang Tingjian and Li Gonglin were among his circle. He died in 1098.

teacher.quote: 廬山開先善暹禪師法嗣　雲居了元禪師　南康軍雲居山了元佛印禪師。饒州浮梁林氏子。…志慕空宗投師出家。試經圓具感悟夙習。即遍參尋投機。於開先法席。出為宗匠。
teacher.note: Placed under 開先善暹禪師法嗣 (heir), and 投機於開先法席 — 'found accord at Kaixian's seat'. Teacher confirmed. 開先善暹 is himself in the Yunmen line.

teacher.quote: 開先善暹禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十世…後謁善暹得法
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster (開先善暹 = Kaixian Shanxian).

dates.kind: authority record citing 佛祖歷代通載
dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

bio.quote: 工書能詩，尤善言辯。元豐中，主潤洲金山、焦山、江西大仰、雲居等刹，九坐道場。蘇軾、黃庭堅、李公麟等文士，皆與師遊。神宗賜衣、鉢，號「佛印禪師」。

notes: Northern Song Yunmen master who served as abbot at nine major monasteries including Jinshan and Lushan Kaixian. Emperor Shenzong bestowed on him a Goryeo robe, golden bowl, and the title 'Chan Master Foyin.' Close friend and teacher of the poet Su Shi (Su Dongpo), with whom he exchanged the famous 'Eight Winds' letter.

bio: From Lu'an in Shouchun, lay surname Xia; tonsured at fourteen. He awakened under Jingzhao Chongxin (also called Changlu Chongxin) at Zisheng monastery in Jiahe, on the Liangsui/Magu koan. He went on to hold Zifu, Jiaoshan, Huilin in the Eastern Capital, Lingyan and Jiangshan, then retired to Baoshan on Lake Dongting and finally became first abbot of Yuanjue. He died in 1132 aged fifty-six. Seven heirs are recorded.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense, at enthronement
teacher.quote: 次拈香云：此一炷香當為何人？…爇向爐中，供養我長蘆　淨照禪師和尚。
teacher.note: First-person, at the transmission. The SECOND stick (the first went to the emperor) — the dharma stick — and he calls him 「我長蘆淨照禪師和尚」, MY 長蘆 Jingzhao. No other stick competes.

teacher.kind: his own words, calling the line his own
teacher.quote: 一母生兒幾百般，誰知淨照禪師家業到資福掃土而盡。
teacher.note: He speaks of 淨照's 家業 (house-business) as the inheritance he himself is spending. He also wrote a poem titled 「懷淨照禪師」 (lb 0573a16): 「一別蘆江後，千峯鴈影沉…方見老師心」 — 老師, his old master.

teacher.source: DILA A001900 (rel teacher, n=崇信 = A021139)
teacher.quote: 淨照崇信禪師法嗣…崇寧初，依淨照禪師於嘉禾資聖寺。照舉良遂見麻谷因緣問曰：「如何是良遂知處？」師即洞明。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. 淨照 IS 'Jingzhao' — DILA A021139 = 長蘆崇信 / 淨照崇信. Note this is a DIFFERENT Chongxin from Longtan Chongxin (A010427), also on this roster; the two must not be merged.

dates.kind: authority record citing 嘉泰普燈錄
dates.quote: 紹興二年四月二十日告終，壽五十六
dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

bio.kind: authority record citing 嘉泰普燈錄 卷9
bio.quote: 字慈受，號普照…壽春六安人，俗姓夏。十四割愛冠祝髮…復應王氏請，為圓覺第一祖。

notes: Northern Song Yunmen master who served as abbot of several major monasteries. Renowned poet-monk whose verse explored how nondual insight applies to ethical decision-making in everyday life. His recorded sayings (yulu) circulated widely among Song literati.

bio: A laywoman of Jinling, recorded as dharma heir of Langye Yongqi. She sold fried cakes for a living, and appears in the lamp records as a lay adept who took on monks. No dates are recorded for her anywhere I could reach.

teacher.quote: 俞道婆金陵人也。市油餈為業。常隨眾參問琅邪。邪以臨濟無位真人話示之。一日。聞丐者唱蓮華樂云。不因柳毅傳書信。何緣得到洞庭湖。忽大悟。以餈盤投地。…往見琅邪。邪望之。知其造詣。
teacher.note: 參問琅邪 + 往見琅邪 (邪知其造詣) = her transmission/confirmation under 琅琊永起. She is placed in the 琅邪永起禪師法嗣 section of the lamp.

teacher.quote: 琅邪起禪師法嗣。（X80n1564_p0025c21）
teacher.note: 琅邪永起 confirmed.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 五燈會元
teacher.quote: 琅邪起禪師法嗣。（X80n1564_p0025c21）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster (琅邪永起 = Langye Yongqi).

dates.note: ⚠ DILA carries NO birth or death. The roster's 1100-1170 is unsourced and I could not source it.

bio.quote: 金陵俞道婆
bio.note: The record is thin. Everything else told about her is koan literature, not biography.

notes: Laywoman who achieved awakening. Notable female figure in Song Chan.

bio: From Houguan in Fuzhou, lay surname Huang. He herded cattle as a boy, entered Xuefeng at fourteen, and took the precepts at twenty-four. He spent ten years on Yunmen's 'a monk's words fall short' under Laona Zuzheng at Jianfu, and awakened one day walking round a lotus pond. From about 1201 he held Shengyin, Chengtian, Wanshou, Lingyan and Wukui. He died in 1217, aged seventy-five. His heir Wumen Huikai compiled the Gateless Barrier.

steles.title: 月林觀禪師塔銘
steles.author: 陳貴謙
steles.author_note: 朝散大夫知太平州軍州兼管內觀農營田事 — a serving prefect. Calligraphy by 陳誼 (尚書禮部員外郎), seal-script by 趙伸夫 (兩浙路計度轉運副使). Three named officials.
steles.quote: 師名師觀，道號月林，福州候官黃氏子。八歲牧牛，鞭叱間忽若有省…二十四祝髮受戒具…時證老衲住澧州光孝…師徑造其室…看雲門話、墮話者又十年。一日，遶蓮池而行…豁然大悟。
steles.note: Appended to his own 語錄. Gives the whole life, the teacher, and the death date.

teacher.quote: 時證老衲住澧州光孝，道法盛行。師徑造其室…聞老衲移住饒之薦福，即徒步從之
teacher.note: The stele names 老衲 (祖證) as the master he sought out and followed. CONFIRMS the roster.

teacher.quote: 大洪老衲證禪師法嗣

dates.kind: authority record citing the 塔銘
dates.quote: 嘉定丁丑四月十三日示寂，閱世七十五（《月林師觀禪師語錄》卷末〈月林觀禪師塔銘〉）
dates.note: 1217, aged 75 → birth 1143. CONFIRMS the roster. Source is the stele itself.

links.label: DILA Authority A013182
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the 塔銘

notes: Yangqi branch Linji master. Teacher of Wumen Huikai, compiler of the Gateless Barrier. Gave Wumen the koan of Zhaozhou’s ‘No’.

bio: Dharma heir of Wansong Xingxiu. He held Wanshou in Yanjing and retired to Bao'en there. In 1281 he was the officiant who put the torch to the Daoist canon at Minzhong monastery in Dadu, by imperial order, everything but the Daodejing being burnt. He compiled two koan collections, the Konggu ji and the Xutang ji. He died the same year, aged fifty-nine.

teacher.kind: HIS OWN BOOK — 林泉老人評唱投子青和尚頌古空谷集, in his own commentarial voice
teacher.quote: 萬松先師住仰山時，閏四月旦日，上堂云：…
teacher.note: 『萬松先師』 — MY LATE MASTER WANSONG, written by 從倫 himself, in the 評唱 he composed. First-person, unambiguous, and he is quoting his master's teaching from memory of the 仰山 assembly. No lamp needed.

teacher.kind: lineage index in a 頌古 collection
teacher.quote: 燕京報恩林泉從倫禪師〈青二十三　報恩秀嗣〉
teacher.note: Corroboration: 『報恩秀嗣』 — heir of 報恩[行]秀. 萬松行秀 was abbot of 報恩寺 in Yanjing, hence 報恩秀; 『青二十三』 = 23rd generation from 投子義青, the Caodong count. Both details fit 萬松行秀 exactly and nobody else.

teacher.quote: 為萬松行秀禪師（1166-1246）法嗣…松問：「如何是向上眼？」師曰：「瞎」…松頷之。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.quote: （元世祖至元十八年）同年，從倫示寂，壽五十九。
dates.note: ⚠ MILD DISAGREEMENT: DILA gives 1223-1281; the roster has 1210-1280. Note DILA's own source here is a MODERN secondary work (水月齋主人, 元明禪宗概說), not a primary — so this is weak on both sides. I take DILA's 1223-1281 as the only figure with any citation attached.

bio.kind: authority record citing 五燈會元續略
bio.quote: 至元十八年（1281）十月二十日奉聖旨就大都憫忠寺焚燒道藏偽經，除《道德經》外盡行燒燬，主持下火…有《空谷集》及《虗堂集》各六卷行世。

notes: Primary monastic heir of Wansong Xingxiu. Succeeded him as abbot of Bao'en Temple in Yanjing. Compiled two major koan collections — Konggu ji (Empty Valley Collection) on Touzi Yiqing's verses and Xutang ji (Empty Hall Collection) on Danxia Zichun's verses. Invited to the Mongol court in 1268.

bio: From Renhe, lay surname Wang. He entered Guangyan monastery at twelve under Guangxiu and took full precepts at seventeen. He awakened under Ji'an Zongxin at Jinhua — Ji'an twisted a paper spill for a candle and asked 'when Longtan blew it out, what then?', clapping a hand over his mouth as he began to answer. He held Daci Dinghui (1313), Fuyuan, Zhongzhu, Jingci (1343) and Lingyin. He died in 1361 aged eighty-three, posthumously titled Puhui Xingwu. Among those who came to him was the Korean master Naong Hyegeun.

teacher.quote: 謁及庵信於西峰，一見器之，命居侍席。
teacher.note: dharma-father 及庵宗信 (及庵信). 廣脩 = 薙度師 (tonsure), noted separately.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 新續高僧傳
teacher.quote: 謁及庵信於西峰一見器之命居侍席 (B27n0151_p0055a10)
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. NOTE: DILA carries a SECOND teacher-relation, 廣脩 — but that one is explicitly the TONSURE master (禮邑之廣嚴寺僧廣脩為薙度師), not the dharma teacher. Exactly the distinction the audit says the old roster kept collapsing.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 五燈全書
teacher.quote: 字平山，為及庵宗信禪師法嗣

dates.kind: authority record citing 五燈全書 卷51
dates.quote: 當辛丑五月一日，世壽八十三。
dates.note: 1361, aged 83 → birth 1279. CONFIRMS the roster.

bio.kind: authority record citing 東國僧尼錄
bio.quote: 秋八月參平山。(X88n1671_p0646c9)
bio.note: Corroborates the Korean connection: 惠勤 = Naong Hyegeun came to Pingshan.

links.label: DILA Authority A016698
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the Naong connection

notes: Yuan dynasty Linji master, 19th generation (not 18th as sometimes claimed in Korean sources). Dharma brother of Shiwu Qinggong — both studied under Ji'an Zongxin. Gave formal dharma transmission to the Korean monk Naong Hyegeun at Jingci Temple in Hangzhou. Also served as abbot of Lingyin Temple. Authored Jingjuyin (淨居吟), over 200 poems. Attested in DILA Authority Database (A016698).

bio: Korean Seon master, disciple of Gugok Gagun, and a transmission link through the harshest years of the Joseon suppression. Three disciples are recorded, among them Byeoksong Jieom. Almost nothing else is recorded of him, and even his death year rests on a weak source.

teacher.kind: 海東佛祖源流 (獅巖采永, 1764), quoted in 朝鮮佛教通史 — a late lineage compilation
teacher.quote: 釋淨心，號碧溪，金山崔氏，遠嗣龜谷。又入明，傳臨濟宗下總統和尚法印而來。恭讓時辭退，後因沙汰，長髮蓄妻孥，入黃岳山，隱居于古紫洞物罕里，晦迹焉。將啟手足，傳禪于碧松，傳教于淨蓮。
teacher.note: 遠嗣 — 'succeeded from afar.' Even the tradition marks the link as REMOTE. And the same sentence gives him a SECOND transmission: he went to Ming China and brought back the 法印 of a 臨濟 'Zongtong heshang'. 李能和 comments on the very next line that 遠 must mean geographic distance, not generational distance, since Gagun and Jeongsim were contemporaries (「其云遠嗣龜谷之遠字，非謂年代先後之遠也，即謂居地距離之遠也」) — an editor visibly arguing with his own source.

teacher.kind: the lineage clause in 清虛休靜's 行狀 (c. 1604)
teacher.quote: 幻菴傳之龜谷，龜谷傳之正心，正心傳之智嚴…此實臨濟之正派。
teacher.note: Same retrospective chain as for Gagun. ~110 years after Jeongsim's death.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 禪典．禪宗法系譜
teacher.quote: 龜谷覺雲弟子。（禪典．禪宗法系譜：23）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. But note the source is a modern lineage chart, not a primary document — this is the weakest kind of teacher evidence on my batch.

dates.note: ⚠ WEAK. DILA's ONLY cited source for the death year is terebess.hu/zen/korean-lineage.html — a website, not a document. I flag this rather than launder it. Birth unknown.

school.quote: 朝鮮 / 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.quote: 法嗣: 法俊, 守眉, 智嚴
bio.note: The roster's 'active when monks were banned from cities' is context, not a sourced statement about him. I have not asserted it.

links.label: DILA Authority A031584
links.confirms: teacher, students; death year only on a weak source

notes: Transmission link during the darkest period of Joseon Buddhist suppression. Active when monks were banned from cities.

bio: The dominant figure of Joseon Buddhism. Lay surname Choe, of Wansan; dharma heir of Buyong Yeonggwan (also given as Eunam Yeonggwan). He was made supreme abbot of both the Seon and Gyo orders, and in the Japanese invasion of 1592 he raised and led the monk-militia. He died in 1604 after sixty-five years in robes. A very large number of heirs are recorded, Samyeong Yujeong (惟政) among them.

steles.title: 有明朝鮮國賜國一大都禪師禪教都摠攝扶宗樹教普濟登階尊者西山清虛堂休靜師碑銘并序
steles.author: 李廷龜 (月沙), 大匡輔國崇祿大夫議政府右議政; calligraphy/seal by 申翊聖
steles.quote: 萬曆三十一年三月初吉建
steles.note: Full text present. He is one of the best-attested men in the whole roster: at least FOUR separate steles survive for him — 李廷龜's (B31n0169 lb 0230b23; also B31n0170 lb 0400b23), 張維's 海南縣大興寺清虛大師碑銘 (B31n0170 lb 0402a16), 李雨臣's (lb 0418b26), and 徐有鄰's 紀續碑 (lb 0425a18) — plus 酬忠祠碑 and a 西山大師行錄.

teacher.kind: HIS OWN self-composed 行狀 (西山大師自抄行狀)
teacher.quote: 西山大師自抄行狀中，傳燈、拈頌、華嚴、圓覺、楞嚴、法華、維摩、般若等數十本經論，受於芙蓉大師云云
teacher.note: TOP RUNG. 自抄行狀 — the career-record the master WROTE HIMSELF. In his own hand he says he received his training 於芙蓉大師 — Buyong (Yeonggwan). First-person, from the man.

teacher.kind: his 碑銘 — 西山清虛堂休靜師碑銘并序, by 李廷龜
teacher.quote: 必得禪家頓悟法，遂聽法於靈觀大師，剃髮於崇仁長老
teacher.note: THE STELE, and it draws the line the brief demands: 聽法於靈觀 (he received the DHARMA from Yeonggwan) is held apart from 剃髮於崇仁 (he was TONSURED by Sungin). 崇仁 is the ordination master and is NOT the dharma-father. Author 李廷龜 (月沙, 1564-1635), Right State Councillor, who knew Hyujeong's heir 松雲惟政 personally ('松雲惟政即師之傳法沙門也，其渡本也數訪我於京城'); he composed it 按狀 from the 行狀 the disciples 葆真、彥機、雙仡 carried to him. Erected 萬曆三十一年 (1603).

teacher.kind: the lineage clause of the same 李廷龜 stele
teacher.quote: 李月沙廷龜撰普濟登階尊者西山清虛堂休靜大師碑銘序：…智嚴傳之靈觀，靈觀傳之西山，此實臨濟之正派，而惟西山獨得其宗云云
teacher.note: 靈觀傳之西山 — 'Yeonggwan transmitted it to Sŏsan.' The transmission verb 傳, on the stone.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 禪典．禪宗法系譜
teacher.quote: 朝鮮完山人，姓崔，西山僧人。隱庵靈觀弟子。
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster — with a naming caveat: DILA writes the man 隱庵靈觀 where the roster (and most scholarship) writes 芙蓉靈觀 Buyong Yeonggwan. Same man, different sobriquet; I did NOT treat them as two people.

dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

school.quote: 朝鮮 / 臨濟宗 楊岐派

bio.quote: 國一都大禪師 / 扶宗拊教普濟登階尊者
bio.note: His titles. The monk-militia role is universally reported but I did not find it stated in a source I fetched, so the bio states it as the well-known fact it is, flagged here as NOT independently verified by me.

notes: The most revered figure in Joseon-era Korean Buddhism, known both as a profound Seon master and as the warrior-monk who organized Buddhist militia (seungbyeong) to resist the Japanese invasion of 1592 (Imjin War). His treatise Seon'ga gwigam (Mirror for Seon Students) became the standard primer for Korean Seon practice, synthesizing Seon, Gyo (doctrinal study), and Yeombul (Pure Land recitation) into a unified curriculum still used today. At age 73, when the Japanese invasion began, King Seonjo called upon him to rally monks as soldiers; he mobilized thousands across the peninsula. He traced his lineage through Taego Bou to the Chinese Linji school, though Ahn (2019) has challenged the historicity of the intermediate links in this lineage chain. Attested in Jorgensen (2015): provides a full English translation and study of the Seon'ga gwigam.

bio: From Yixing, lay surname Jiang. He read the Platform Sutra at twenty-six and began to practise; awakened at thirty while carrying firewood over a hill, and left his wife and children at thirty to be tonsured by Huanyou Zhengchuan. His full breakthrough came crossing Tongguan peak. He held six seats — Tongxuan, Jinsu, Huangbo, Ayuwang, and Tiantong for eleven years. He died in 1642 at seventy-seven. His twelve heirs (Hanyue Fazang, Poshan Haiming, Feiyin Tongrong, Muchen Daomin, Linye Tongqi and the rest) made his line the dominant Chan transmission of the Qing — the 'Linji revival'.

steles.title: 明天童密雲悟和尚行狀
steles.author: 木陳道忞
steles.author_note: His own dharma heir, writing in the 布水臺集. An heir's account of conduct — the closest thing to a first-hand life.
steles.quote: 師諱圓悟，號密雲，荊谿蔣氏子…三十歲棄妻孥，從幻有傳和尚脫白…一日偶城歸，過銅棺山頂，豁然大悟，覺情與無情煥然等現。
steles.note: Names the teacher (幻有正傳) in the master's own life-story, written by the heir who succeeded him at Tiantong.

steles.title: 天童密雲禪師年譜
steles.author_note: In 密雲禪師語錄 卷12.
steles.quote: 嘉靖四十五年丙寅十一月十六日 … 崇禎十五年壬午七月初七日
steles.note: A year-by-year chronology; DILA takes his exact birth (1567-01-05) and death (1642-08-02) from it. I cite it via DILA — I did not open the 年譜 itself in the corpus.

teacher.kind: 行狀 by his heir 木陳道忞
teacher.quote: 三十歲棄妻孥，從幻有傳和尚脫白
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster, from the 行狀.

teacher.quote: 幻有正傳（1549-1614）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第三十四世

dates.kind: authority record citing the 年譜
dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

bio.kind: authority record citing 布水臺集 卷16
bio.quote: 嗣法弟子有五峰學、漢月藏、破山明、費隱容、石車乘、朝宗忍、萬如微、木陳忞、石奇雲、牧雲門、浮石賢、林野奇等十二人。

links.label: DILA Authority A003688
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the twelve heirs

notes: Central figure of the late Ming Linji revival. Made his line the dominant Chan transmission into the Qing.

bio: From Chaoyang in Guangdong, lay surname Lin. He began as a Confucian student, was tonsured at Kaixian on Lushan by Zhiming, and after visits to Hanshan Deqing and others went to Miyun Yuanwu at Jinsu, serving him fourteen years before succeeding him at Tiantong in 1642. Summoned to Beijing in 1659, he became Chan teacher to the Shunzhi emperor, who granted him the title Chan Master Hongjue and told him to treat him as a disciple. He died in 1674 aged seventy-nine. He wrote the 行狀 for Miyun and the 塔銘 for Ruoan Tongwen — both in his 布水臺集, and both used on this roster.

teacher.kind: his own collected works 布水臺集 — first-person prose
teacher.quote: 晦中明上座曾親炙先師密老人于天童，復為山僧監廣潤、道峰二山院事…
teacher.note: Daomin, writing in his own voice, calls 密老人 (Miyun Yuanwu) 先師 — 'my late master' — and locates him at 天童, Miyun's seat, which Daomin himself later inherited (繼席天童). First-person.

teacher.kind: his own collected works 布水臺集
teacher.quote: 悟禪耆德少參先師，往來金栗、天童，老不忍去，感而賦贈。
teacher.note: Again 先師, and named by BOTH of Miyun's seats — 金粟 and 天童. Unambiguous.

teacher.quote: 密雲圓悟禪師法嗣…親炙悟者一十四秋，日臻玄奧，繼席天童
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. DILA also records 智明 (his TONSURE master: 忞不天，依師得度) and 憨山德清 (a teacher he consulted) — neither is the transmission. The distinction matters and is preserved here.

teacher.source: DILA A003688 (Miyun's record, rel student, n=道忞)
teacher.note: Confirmed from the teacher's side too.

dates.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

bio.source: DILA A001513 (rel student, n=愛新覺羅福臨)
bio.quote: 老和尚勿以天子視朕當如門弟子旅菴相待可也 (J26, no. B180, p. 296, b26-28)
bio.note: The Shunzhi emperor's own words to him, from Muchen's record of the Beijing journey.

links.label: DILA Authority A001513
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, the Shunzhi connection

notes: First to succeed Miyun at Tiantong (1642). Summoned to Beijing as Chan teacher to the Shunzhi Emperor. CBETA: J26nB180, J26nB181.

bio: From Yuan county in Jiangzhou (Shanxi), lay surname Wang, born 1383. He was tonsured at Chongxing monastery on Mount Yuan, set out to travel in 1406, and in 1411 came to Ningran Liaogai, abbot of Shaolin, and inherited his dharma. He served as head seat (首座) at Shaolin and from 1420 was abbot of Chongxing. He died in 1452. He is a link in the Shaolin Caodong transmission.

teacher.kind: 五燈全書 biography, under the heading 少室改禪師法嗣
teacher.quote: 嵩山少室俱空契斌禪師，平陽垣曲王氏子。從重興院無相薙染，久而參方，謁凝然改于嵩山，求示心要。改曰：你向達磨未西來時道一句看。師無以對，心甚疑之，朝夕咨扣。一日，覩秦封槐，豁然契悟，徑往丈室。改一見謂曰：契斌參得禪也。師便喝。
teacher.note: Two masters again: 無相 tonsured him (薙染); 凝然了改 showed him 心要 and sealed him. 謁 alone would be association — but 契悟 + the abbot's 契斌參得禪也 is the transmission.

teacher.quote: 改傳嵩山俱空契斌。斌傳西京定國無方可從。

teacher.source: DILA A015682 (rel teacher, n=凝然了改)
teacher.quote: 明永樂九年（1411年），29歲，參嵩山少林寺住持凝然了改，嗣法。（X63n1244_p0497b20）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster.

dates.quote: 生於明洪武十六年（1383年）… 1452
dates.note: Death 1452 CONFIRMS the roster; birth 1383 is NEW (the roster had none).

bio.quote: 曾任少林寺首座…明永樂十八年（1420年），38歲，住持垣山重興寺。
bio.note: ⚠ CONTRADICTS THE ROSTER NOTE. The roster says he 'served as abbot of Shaolin Monastery'. DILA says he was 首座 (head seat) at Shaolin and 住持 (abbot) of Chongxing at Yuanshan — a different temple. Head seat is not abbot. I have written the bio to DILA.

links.label: DILA Authority A015682
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school; 首座 not abbot of Shaolin

notes: Seventh-generation Shaolin Caodong master, heir of Ningran Liaogai. Served as abbot of Shaolin Monastery in the early-to-mid Ming dynasty, continuing the unbroken Caodong transmission established by Xueting Fuyu.

bio: From Jiangling; dharma heir of Muchen Daomin. He held Longshan in Xinzhou and then Lingshan in Chaozhou, and compiled the Zhenghong ji, a collection on the Tang master Dadian. Two heirs are recorded — and DILA also records the Vietnamese monk Nguyen Thieu as having served him, which is the link by which the Miyun line reached Cochinchina.

teacher.kind: 五燈全書, his own entry
teacher.quote: 新州龍山曠圓本果禪師。上堂，問：「祖道重開即不問，如何是主中賓？」師曰：「山僧為汝徹困。」
teacher.note: A full lamp entry with recorded dialogue — upgrades the roster's DILA line. Teacher 木陳道忞 per the 五燈全書 chapter-heading and DILA.

teacher.kind: authority record citing 五燈全書
teacher.quote: 字曠圓，號碩豐，為木陳道忞禪師（1596-1674）法嗣。江陵人。（X82n1571_p0374c10）
teacher.note: CONFIRMS the roster. Corroborated from the other side: 道忞's own DILA record lists 本果 among his heirs.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳。
