His Jikji compiled essential Seon teachings from the patriarchs and was intended as a practical guide for practitioners. Attested in UNESCO Memory of the World Register (2001): the Jikji is recognized as the world's oldest extant movable metal type printed book, with the surviving second volume held by the Bibliotheque nationale de France.

bio: Surnamed Wang, of Tongzhou. He was tonsured at thirteen at Wan'an monastery in Tongzhou under Bai'an Kong and took the precepts at twenty in Hangzhou. Sealed in retreat in the north, he was reading Wansong's comments on the old cases when he broke through: 'The wind of the Caodong house blew over the empire — but without fine stitching, without turning and interlocking without touching the point, no one can be its master.' He came out, went to Wufang Kecong at Shaolin, and was sealed. He first held Huayan at Dengfeng; in 1506 he was commanded to Shaolin, and was its abbot from 1510. He died in 1524, aged seventy-three, and his stupa stands in the ancestral graveyard at Shaoshi. Xiaoshan Zongshu and Jinshan Debao were his heirs.

teacher.quote: 為無方可從禪師（1420-1483）法嗣…參少林無方禪師，得印可。
teacher.note: transmission 得印可; teacher 無方可從 confirmed. 白庵空 = tonsure master, separate.

teacher.quote: 嵩山載禪師法嗣……定州義亮禪師
teacher.note: his own heir, confirming placement.

teacher.quote: 為無方可從禪師（1420-1483）法嗣。…既而幡然出關，參少林無方禪師，得印可。
嵩山載禪師法嗣……定州義亮禪師

dates.quote: death 嘉靖甲申 (1524)；「嘉靖甲申師示寂，塔於少室祖塋。」（《續指月錄》卷16）；明嘉靖甲申年（1524）示寂，世壽七十三

bio.kind: authority record (from 五燈會元續略卷1, 續指月錄卷16-17)

notes: Shaolin Monastery abbot. Teacher of Xiaoshan. Mid-Ming Caodong transmission through Shaolin.

bio: Surnamed Lü, of Liyang. He was shaved at Jingle cloister in Jingxi and was working on 'the face before your parents were born' when the sound of a lamp-flame bursting one evening opened him. He went to Xiaoyan Debao at the Guanyin hermitage in the capital, and it was Debao kicking off a shoe and lifting a foot that undid him; Debao wrote out the 'Orthodox Lineage of Caoxi' and gave it to him. He then built a hut at Mimo cliff on Mount Wutai and stayed thirteen years, came out in 1595 to Longchi at Jingxi, went north to Puzhao in the capital in 1602, and returned to Longchi in 1610. He died on the twelfth day of the second month of 1614, aged sixty-six. His heirs — Miyun Yuanwu, Tianyin Yuanxiu, Xueqiao Yuanxin — carried the seventeenth-century Linji revival.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense (幻有傳禪師語錄)
teacher.quote: 又一炷香，非金非木，非自非他，用山僧信手拈來，端為供養笑巖堂上傳曹溪正胍三十二世月心寶和尚，用酬法乳之恩。兼太平堂上資秉教授承𦙌雪峰宗祖二十七世樂安悅和尚，乃至荊山珂、夢塘覺二大和尚，以及天下諸善知識并大法師一切高人，普同供養。
teacher.note: TEXTBOOK. Three sticks: the first to 釋迦世尊 and the patriarchs (0488a14), the second to 今上皇帝 (0488b01), and THIS one — the only one carrying 用酬法乳之恩 — to 笑巖堂上…月心寶和尚 = 笑巖德寶 (月心 is his 字). And the trap is right there in the same sentence: 樂安悅 (his 教授 / ordination master), 荊山珂 and 夢塘覺 are named in the SAME breath but get only 供養, never 法乳. Take the dharma-milk stick only. Cross-checked: he calls 笑巖 「吾師」 elsewhere in the same record (0482a11: 「效吾師笑巖和尚行」; 0487b13: 「我笑巖和尚」).

teacher.kind: preface/appendix by a man who was there
teacher.quote: 予昔叅笑巖和尚於京師，幻有兄侍焉。
teacher.note: An eyewitness: 'when I studied under 笑巖 in the capital, brother 幻有 was attending him.' Independent of the incense.

teacher.quote: 笑巖德寶（1512-1581）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第三十三世。…因笑巖禪師踢履、翹足而豁然悟旨。後禮辭，笑巖禪師乃書《曹溪正派源流》付之。

dates.quote: birth +1549; death +1614-03-21；「于萬曆甲寅二月十二日示寂。……世壽六十六。」（《五燈全書》卷64）

bio.kind: authority record (from 五燈全書卷64, 續指月錄)

notes: Late Ming Linji master. Teacher of Miyun Yuanwu, the most influential 17th-century Chan figure.

bio: Surnamed Zhu, of Yin county. He left the world in 1599, cut his hair on Tiantai and called himself Bukong. Talking with the hermit Miaozhen about a kōan, he found the before and after cut off; going back to Tiantai for confirmation he came out of the Puji monastery at Yunmen, looked up, saw the three characters 'Old Yunmen' over the gate, and had his great awakening. He built a hut on Shuangji peak, went to Huanyou Zhengchuan at Longchi, and received his seal in the spring of 1614. He was wild — roaring and whistling, careless of monastic decorum, so that people called him the Snow Lion. He opened the hall at Jingshan in 1640 and settled at Yunmen in Shaoxing in 1646, dying there on the twenty-sixth of the eighth month, 1647, aged seventy-seven.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 — the dharma-milk incense (雪嶠信禪師語錄)
teacher.quote: 次拈云：「此香供養本山前代一源禪師。」復拈云：「此一瓣香，供養即此禹門堂上嗣臨濟正宗幻有先師大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。」斂衣就座。
teacher.note: TWO sticks side by side, and the record itself separates them: the previous stick goes to 本山前代一源禪師 — the temple's PREDECESSOR, the man whose seat he took. Only the next one carries 用酬法乳之恩, and it names 幻有. Take the dharma-milk stick, not the seat stick.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香, a second enthronement
teacher.quote: 此香供養華嚴會上清凉澄國師。復指香云：「此香供養禹門幻有先師大和尚，用酬法乳。」
teacher.note: Same structure again, on a different occasion: an honorific stick to Qingliang Chengguan, then the dharma-milk stick to 幻有. He is consistent.

teacher.quote: 幻有正傳禪師法嗣。…至龍池參幻有傳禪師，作禮進具戒。…甲寅春二月受龍池記莂。
法嗣有天童密雲圓悟、磬山天隱圓修、雲門雪嶠圓信…
teacher.note: The same edge from the teacher's side.

dates.quote: birth +1571; death +1647-09-24；（順治四年）八月二十六日，壽七十七。（《八十八祖道影傳贊》卷4〈雪嶠信禪師傳〉）

bio.source: 《八十八祖道影傳贊》卷4〈雪嶠信禪師傳〉 (via DILA A001408)

notes: Third dharma brother of Miyun and Tianyin. Controversially claimed transmission from the long-dead Yunmen Wenyan.

bio: Surnamed Li, of Boluo in Guangdong. At twenty-seven, lying ill and hearing drums and pipes, he saw the root of things and resolved to leave home; he was shaved and ordained by Zongbao Daodu. He went first to Boshan, then to Yunmen to Xueqiao Yuanxin, and after Xueqiao died he went to Yulin Tongxiu at Daxiong and got the heart of it; Yulin had him share the seat and teach. He followed his master to Beijing in the Shunzhi years, was received by the emperor, and refused the honorific title the throne pressed on him. He died on the twenty-seventh of the sixth month, 1677, aged sixty-four; in 1733 the Yongzheng emperor gave him the title Mingdao Zhengjue.

steles.title: 塔銘 (in 明道正覺森禪師語錄, 龍藏本)
steles.author: unsigned in the CBETA text; composed from 文殊懿山德公's 行狀
steles.quote: 吾圓照慈翁和尚，其北溟之歸墟也哉…適吾里文殊懿山德公繼席圓照，走人抱狀請銘，余門外人也…不過摘德公行狀大槩如此。
steles.note: In the Qianlong-canon edition of his 語錄 (L155). ⚠ This master carries heavy political baggage (he burned the imperial edict trying to make Shunzhi's tonsure permanent; the incense-episode is historically loaded) — but the LINEAGE fact here is clean and stone-attested. His heirs are listed 0069b12: 懿山德, 形山寶, etc.

teacher.kind: his own 塔銘 in 明道正覺森禪師語錄
teacher.quote: 師諱行森，號䒢溪，生博羅黎氏…甫壯聞鐘有省，輙師歸宗。無何依雪嶠信公，窮極隱秘。公示寂，始參大覺，大覺一見奇之，旋命分座。師接機如鵬劈海、鶻摩霄，活啄生吞，命根立斷，叢林咸以䒢鐵棒稱之。
teacher.note: 始參大覺…命分座 — he came to Dajue (玉林通琇, 大覺普濟能仁國師) only AFTER 雪嶠圓信 died, and Dajue set him to share the seat. ⚠ THE BRIEF'S 玉林 WARNING: an agent nearly mis-filed 玉林通琇's incense under a different heir. Here the direction is right — 森 is the pupil, 玉林 the teacher — and it is on the stele, not just a lamp. His awakening under 歸宗/雪嶠 was association; the transmission seat came from 玉林.

teacher.quote: 玉林通琇禪師（1614-1675）法嗣。…乃參大覺普濟能仁國師玉林琇，洞明心要。琇令分座說法
《正源略集》卷9：「䒢溪森禪師法嗣(四人)天目獅子正宗形山寶禪師」
teacher.note: his own heirs filed under him; the index places him under 玉林琇

dates.quote: birth 萬曆四十二年 (1614)；death 「康熙十六年六月二十七日，六十四年。」（《揞黑豆集》卷8）

bio.kind: authority record (from 清涼山志卷3, 揞黑豆集卷8, 五燈全書卷81, 正源略集卷9)

links.label: DILA Authority A000419
links.confirms: teacher, dates, imperial audience, posthumous title

notes: Yulin's student. Included in the Yongzheng Emperor's Yuxuan yulu.

bio: A Korean Seon monk, dharma heir of Hwanseong Jian. He is not obscure at all once you look in the right book: the Joseon Bulgyo tongsa prints the dharma-lineage regulation of Yujeomsa, which names him in sequence — 'the lineage-transmitting patriarch, Chan master Hwanseong Jian; his direct heir, Chan master Hoam Chejeong; Hoam's dharma heir, Chan master Pungak Boin' — and DILA lists eight disciples under him, including Yeondam Yuil and Sangeon. His dates are given as 1687-1748.

teacher.kind: temple dharma-lineage register (榆岾寺 燈規)
teacher.quote: 榆岾寺本末寺。從其法系譜脉。一。本寺紹隆清虛休靜禪師。二。法脉傳祖喚惺志安禪師。三。喚惺嫡嗣虎巖體淨禪師。四。虎巖嗣法楓岳普印禪師。
teacher.note: A temple's own standing rule about its succession — names Hwanseong as his master and Pungak Boin as his heir, in one chain.

teacher.quote: 喚惺志安弟子。（禪典．禪宗法系譜：25）

dates.quote: birth +1687; death +1748
dates.note: sourced by DILA only to a blog; see date_caveat

school.quote: 本寺紹隆清虛休靜禪師 (the Cheongheo/Pyeonyang descent)

notes: Obscure transmission link in the Pyeonyang lineage between Hwanseong Jian (d.1729) and Cheongbong Geoan (1710-1793). No independent biographical sources survive. Known only from Joseon-era lineage charts. The 68th Korean patriarch in the Jogye reckoning.

bio: Named Shidao, styled Zhengzong, also called Wuyin; of a prominent Yuezhou (Hunan) family, born on the fifth day of the fifth month of 1691. He was the dharma heir of Jialing Xingyin and the last well-attested holder of the imperially-patronised Linji line at the Dajue monastery. He died on the twentieth day of the tenth month of 1753, aged sixty-three, forty-five years a monk, and his stupa was raised on Lotus Peak beside his master's.

teacher.kind: 正源略集, his own entry (under 迦陵性音)
teacher.quote: 京都大覺正宗道禪師。小參：「適纔山門外、佛殿裏已是狼籍殆盡，諸人上來下去還嫌少那？」
teacher.note: Listed among 迦陵性音's heirs with a full recorded 小參 — upgrades the roster's index/DILA to a fleshed-out lamp entry.

teacher.quote: （迦陵音法嗣）……大覺正宗道禪師。
(迦陵音法嗣)……大覺正宗道禪師

dates.quote: （乾隆）癸酉十月二十日示寂，亦塔於蓮花峰。壽六十三，臘四十五。

bio.quote: 諱實道，字正宗，別號無隱，湖南岳州望族。

notes: Jialing Xingyin's dharma heir. 35th generation Linji (Yangqi branch). After him, the imperial Chan line faded — Qianlong shifted patronage to Tibetan Buddhism. Attested in DILA Authority Database (A026661).

bio: Surnamed Ma, of Yanling — hence 'Master Ma.' He entered the register at Changshou monastery in Jiangning in 692, at twenty-five, then went to Youyan monastery on Qingshan and studied under Niutou Zhiwei, the fifth patriarch of the Oxhead house, receiving his dharma. He was austere and content with poverty. In the Kaiyuan years the prefect Wei Xian invited him to Jingkou, and he lived at Helin monastery. He died without illness at midnight on the eleventh day of the eleventh month of 752, aged eighty-five; his disciples built his stupa west of Mount Huanghe. Jingshan Faqin came from his gate.

steles.title: 潤州鶴林寺故徑山大師碑銘
steles.author: 李華 (Li Hua, c. 715–766)
steles.quote: 初達摩祖師傳法，三世至信大師，信門人達者曰融大師。居牛頭山，得自然智慧。信大師就而證之，且曰：「七佛教戒，諸三昧門，語有差別，義無差別…汝能總持，吾亦隨喜。」由是無上覺路，分為此宗…融授岩大師，岩授方大師，方授持大師，持授威大師，凡七世矣。門人法鏡，吳中上首是也；門人法欽，徑山長老是也
steles.note: ★ THE CHARTER OF THE OXHEAD SCHOOL, and the single densest transmission passage found this run. It attests, in one Tang stele: 道信 CERTIFIED 法融 (信大師就而證之 — 證) and thereby the branch was founded (由是無上覺路，分為此宗); then 法融 授 智巖 授 慧方 授 法持 授 智威 (four 授 statements); and it names Xuansu's own heirs 法鏡 and 法欽 (徑山法欽).

teacher.source: 全唐文 卷0320, 潤州鶴林寺故徑山大師碑銘, by 李華 (Li Hua)
teacher.quote: 入南牛頭山事威大師，撞鍾大鳴…威大師摩頂謂曰：「東南正法，待汝興行。命於別位，開導來學。」
teacher.note: 事 alone is only 'served', but 摩頂 (rubbing the crown) + 「東南正法，待汝興行」 ('the true dharma of the Southeast awaits your making it flourish') + 命於別位，開導來學 (commanding him to a separate seat to teach) is a designation of succession. Reinforced by the school-lineage sentence below, which makes him Zhiwei's successor in a seven-generation count.

teacher.quote: TEACHER-> 智威 (X80n1564_p0002c21)
牛頭五祖智威門下…後至青山幽巖寺，從學於牛頭五祖智威，受勝法。

dates.quote: 以天寶十一載十一月十一日中夜無疾而化。春秋八十有五。

bio.note: DILA also points to a stele — 潤州鶴林寺故徑山大師碑銘 (by 李華) — via wikisource; I did not find its text in the corpus, so I do not list it as a stele I can quote.

links.label: DILA Authority A010251
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, burial, 17 named disciples

notes: Sixth and final patriarch of the Niutou school, residing at Helin Temple (Crane Forest Temple) in Runzhou (modern Zhenjiang, Jiangsu). His student Jingshan Faqin received the title 'National Teacher' (Guoyi) from Emperor Daizong, and his other famous student Niaoke Daolin ('Bird's Nest') became a celebrated figure through whom the Niutou lineage blended into the broader Tang Chan world.

bio: Of the Li clan of Sangluo in De'hua county, Jiangzhou, born on the nineteenth of the eleventh month, 1621. Orphaned early, open-handed and hot-blooded, he was made a commander of a thousand men in the levies raised against the rebels — and after beheading three officers for breaking the law, something turned in him; he slipped away into the mountains under cover of a sortie. No one at Lushan would shave him; the old monk Zizhen of Donglin finally did. He worked as a cook, took full ordination in 1647, and was stuck for years on the 'dragging a corpse' line in Gaofeng's record until, crossing Ruo ridge in 1651, he stumbled in an ox-track and the thing in his chest broke like ice. He came at last into Jie'an Wujin's room, met him as if they had always known each other, and was given the seal. He died on the fifteenth of the ninth month, 1672, aged fifty-two; his disciples built his stupa at Donglin.

steles.title: 行狀 (in 山鐸真在禪師語錄)
steles.author: a lay contemporary — the writer says he lived three li from the master in 1644, travelled with him, and calls him a lifelong friend
steles.quote: 師諱真在，號山鐸，別字筠庵，江州德化縣桑落李氏子也。…父母早亡，師輕財重義，任俠不羈。會闖、獻蹂躪中原…乃授師為千人長。未幾，以小將軍杜姓者三人犯法，斬之。師凜然心動，有出塵之志，遂以征賊入山，相機宵遁。遍謁匡廬，無敢剃落，東林耆宿自真為之染薙。
steles.note: An eyewitness account of conduct, written by a man who knew him from age 24. The military episode is in no lamp record.

teacher.quote: 末造介菴進室，一見如夙契，幾番問答，師豁然契證，出源流印之。
teacher.note: quoted by DILA from this 行狀; the transmission is stated in the account written at his death.

teacher.quote: TEACHER-> 悟進

dates.quote: 「師生天啟辛酉年十一月十九日」…「告寂于康熙壬子年九月十五日，世壽五十二」

bio: Named Daochong, self-styled Chijue ('utter fool'), of the Gou clan of Changjiang in Wuxin (Sichuan); his mother was surnamed Guo. He sat the jinshi examinations and failed, then took Buddhist learning at Miaoyin cloister in Zizhou, was tonsured by Xiuzheng, and studied the treatises at Dasheng Ci monastery in Chengdu. Out of the gorges in 1192, he found Caoyuan Daosheng and had a first opening under him. Songyuan at Lingyin then refused him a place for eight months and finally said: 'I threw the door wide open for him — he walked straight past it,' at which Daochong lost both mouth and ears and understood that Caoyuan's jeering and scolding at Miaoguo and Guifeng had been the whole teaching all along. He held Tianning, Jiangshan, Xuefeng, Lingyin, Fahua and Shuangjing, and was the thirty-sixth abbot of Ayuwang. He died on the fifteenth of the third month, 1250, aged eighty-two, sixty-one years a monk.

steles.title: 徑山癡絕禪師行狀
steles.author: (unsigned, in his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 師名道沖，自號癡絕，武信長江苟氏子。母郭氏，甞夢經行木瓜樹下，其實纍纍，取而食之，占者謂當產奇士。已而師生…長應進士舉，不利，受釋氏學於梓州妙音院，禮修政。…松源曰：我八字打開挂搭他，自是他當面蹉過。師聞此語，口耳俱喪，始知侍曹源於妙果、龜峯時，嬉笑怒罵，無非善巧方便。
steles.note: There is ALSO a 龕銘 (coffin inscription) in the same 語錄 — DILA cites both for his death date.

steles.title: 龕銘 (in 痴絕道冲禪師語錄 卷2)
steles.author: (in his own 語錄)
steles.quote: (cited by DILA for: 淳祐十年三月十五日示寂，世壽八十二)
steles.note: I confirmed the 行狀 text directly; the 龕銘 I cite as DILA cites it.

teacher.quote: 始知侍曹源於妙果、龜峯時，嬉笑怒罵，無非善巧方便，自此不疑天下老和尚舌頭。
teacher.note: The 行狀 makes Caoyuan Daosheng the man whose teaching finally landed. He then spent 20 years visiting others, but the transmission is Caoyuan's.

teacher.quote: 徑山癡絕冲禪師法嗣
龜峰曹源生（？-1198）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第二十世。

dates.quote: 淳祐十年三月十五日示寂，世壽八十二

bio: Surnamed Cao, of Danghu in Jiaxing. He asked his father to teach him the sūtras at ten, was working at the school of the ancestors at fifteen, and at twenty broke wide open; he took Xingshan Hongyuan as his tonsure master. Serving Puming (Yuanhu Miaoyong), he was asked 'My mind is uneasy — have you found peace yet?' and answered only 'Blue heaven! Blue heaven!' Another day Miaoyong raised a fist: 'Say a word.' Wuyuan slapped him; Miaoyong roared with laughter, and the thing was settled. He then sealed himself in retreat at Xingshan for more than ten years, came out to Yongzheng monastery in 1651, and died on the nineteenth of the fifth month, 1678, aged sixty-four.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 at the opening of the hall
teacher.quote: 此一瓣香，歷年勤苦，多載參尋，桐月菴中親遭痛棒，普明寺裡又喫鉗鎚，直得徹骨徹髓、透頂透底，專為福建建寧府普明堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十世鴛湖先師大和尚，以酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: First-person, at the transmission. Same wording and same master as his dharma-brother Jie'an Wujin — the two incense verses corroborate each other.

teacher.quote: 普明妙用禪師法嗣

dates.quote: birth +1615; death 「康熙戊午五月十九日，壽六十四」（《五燈全書》卷68）

bio.source: 《續燈正統》卷34 + 《一初元禪師語錄》卷2 + 《五燈全書》卷81 (via DILA A010711)

bio: Surnamed Han, of Boluo in Huizhou; styled Zuxin, called Shengren, 'the man left over.' He went to Kongyin Daodu (Zongbao Daodu) at Dongguan in Guangzhou, was set on Zhaozhou's 'no,' and after two years, hearing the case of the old woman seen through, broke open; Daodu said 'now you no longer doubt,' and shaved and ordained him at Lushan in the sixth month of 1639, in his twenty-ninth year. Arrested in Nanjing in 1648 with a manuscript recording the fall of the Ming, he became the first literary-inquisition case of the Qing and was banished to Shenyang, where he taught at seven great monasteries with five to seven hundred in the assembly. He died seated on the twenty-seventh of the eleventh month, 1659 (January 1660), aged forty-nine.

steles.kind: 塔銘 (two, attested but not printed in the 語錄)
steles.title: 剩人和尚塔銘 ×2
steles.author: 天然函昰 (his dharma-uncle, at Leifeng in Guangdong, summer 1660) and 郝浴 (雪海郝公, 大中丞 — the provincial governor)
steles.quote: 至若生平行實，詳於二塔銘中。初則天老人撰於粵之雷峰，時庚子夏杪；次為大中丞雪海郝公所撰，猶古之第二碑也。
steles.note: The preface to his 語錄, by his dharma-nephew 今辯 (1690), states that his life is recorded in TWO stupa inscriptions and names both authors. The texts themselves are not in the Jiaxing canon — a lead for anyone who can reach the Liaoning gazetteers.

teacher.quote: 者一瓣香從南天竺國移來，向少林石壁栽培，用曹溪香水灌溉…卻從華首臺上分得一枝，今日向南𡼪第二番拈出，專為現住福州上空下隱大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: '上空下隱' is the honorific way of writing the name 空隱 — Kongyin Daodu, named by his own hand at the transmission.

teacher.quote: (道獨嗣)

dates.quote: 順治十六年己亥十一月二十七日，世壽四十九

bio: Named Puji, self-styled Dachuan, of the Zhang clan of Liuzhao in Fenghua; the youngest of three sons, given by his parents to the dharma. He was tonsured at nineteen at Xianglin cloister under Wenxian, studied vinaya and then Tiantai doctrine at Chicheng, and gave it up: 'Binding the body with precepts, splitting hairs over doctrine — how does that get past birth and death?' At Nengren in Yue he met Zhewong Ruyan, who asked where he was from, snatched away his sitting-cloth and struck him — and he came free on the spot. He held eight abbacies, ending at Jingci and Lingyin, and while at Lingyin compiled the Wudeng huiyuan (1252), the great synthesis of the five lamp records. He died on the eighteenth of the first month, 1253, aged seventy-five, having forbidden an expensive funeral and ordered his bones thrown in the river.

steles.title: 靈隱大川禪師行狀
steles.author: (unsigned, prefixed to his 語錄)
steles.quote: 師名普濟，大川其自號，四明奉化六詔張氏子。父友崇，母俞氏。…年十九，依香林院文憲師薙染，受具戒。…照指往越能仁見淛翁，翁問：上座甚處人？師云：奉化。翁云：還識憨布袋麼？師提起坐具，翁奪坐具便打，師當下脫然…嘉定十年三月，妙勝虗席…師膺其選，瓣香為淛翁記所證也。
steles.note: The last clause is the transmission: at his first abbacy he burned the incense FOR Zhewong, 'in acknowledgement of what he had sealed.'

teacher.quote: 瓣香為淛翁記所證也
teacher.note: The incense at his first abbacy, recorded in the account of conduct written at his death.

teacher.quote: 淛翁如琰禪師法嗣，大鑑下第19世。

dates.quote: 寶祐元年正月十八日示寂，壽七十五

links.label: DILA Authority A001234
links.confirms: teacher, dates, Wudeng huiyuan, 行狀

bio: Styled Lianyue, of the Jiang clan of Yuechi. After his mother's death he heard a monk chanting the line about the 'burning house of the three realms' and turned from the world; he cut off his own hair, went to Fuling, and took the precepts under Poshan Haiming. Accompanying his master to a feast, he took a fall on the road — and in the exchange that followed, the dharma passed. He entered Dongyin monastery on Mount Jiuqing at Zunyi in 1658 and afterwards held Juelin, Baolun, Duda and Baoshou in Sichuan, and Longxing, Jingde, Yuquan and Tianhuang in Hubei. He compiled his master's records, for which the lamps call him 'a meritorious servant of Shuanggui.' He died on the tenth of the seventh month, 1691, aged seventy-eight.

teacher.quote: 此瓣香…此是第一回拈出，供養前住浙江嘉興府東塔、後住四川夔州府梁山縣雙桂禪寺，傳臨濟正脈第三十一世破山老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: First-person, naming Poshan and both his seats.

teacher.quote: (破山明嗣)
為破山海明禪師（1597-1666）法嗣…出涪陵禮破山明受具戒…機語相叩而嗣法

dates.quote: 「寂於康熙三十年七月十日，壽七十有八。」

bio.kind: authority record (from 錦江禪燈卷10, 新續高僧傳四集卷56, 五燈全書卷88)

bio: Of the Wan clan of Panyu, born 1633. As a boy he got his father out of prison by shaming the magistrate in the road. At sixteen he went to Tianran Hanshi at Leifeng and was ordained; at seventeen, reading the Platform Sūtra at the passage on Elder Ming, he heard a cat cry, broke into a sweat, and felt the world split open — he went to his master at midnight and answered him with a cat's cry. At twenty-two he was sent on his master's orders out through Shanhaiguan to Qianshan Hanke, who thought him extraordinary and kept him three years. He took Haichuang monastery in Guangzhou in 1662 and held it twelve years, ordaining more than seventeen hundred. He died on the twenty-second of the ninth month, 1681, aged forty-nine.

steles.title: 海幢阿字無禪師行狀
steles.author: 古雲 (書記古雲敬述)
steles.author_note: his own secretary and dharma heir
steles.quote: 廣州海幢寺阿字禪師，諱今無，得法天然是和尚，曹洞三十五世，博山下三世。番禺萬氏子。…年十六，抵雷峰，依天老人得度，知有向上事。十七，受《壇經》，至參明上座因緣，聞貓聲汗下，覺世界如擘。走見峰，峰曰：「夜半至此何為？」曰：「不思善，不思惡，止道得一半。」峰曰：「那一半聻？」師作貓聲而出。
steles.note: Written by his secretary at his death. Opens by naming the teacher and counting the generations.

teacher.quote: 諱今無，得法天然是和尚，曹洞三十五世，博山下三世

teacher.source: B/B22/B22n0119.xml (天然和尚年譜, 汪宗衍)
teacher.quote: 阿字今無生。（「光宣臺集」附古雲撰「行狀」。今無，字阿字，番禺萬氏。年十七禮天然為僧…天然付以大法為第一法嗣。）
teacher.note: The teacher's own chronological biography calls him Tianran's FIRST dharma heir — the same edge from the other side.

teacher.quote: TEACHER-> 圅昰

dates.quote: 辛酉九月二十二日辰時即告寂…世壽四十有九，僧臘三十

school.quote: 曹洞三十五世，博山下三世

bio: Abbot at Yunju in Jiangzhou, dharma heir of Fozhao Deguang of Ayuwang and eighteenth generation below Huineng. He entered Yansheng Chan cloister on Mount Zhangxi in 1219, was invited in 1228 to the Zhenru Chan cloister on Mount Yunju, and later lived at the Donghu hermitage. His disciple Liaojian compiled his recorded sayings in one fascicle. No birth or death year survives in any source — DILA states this outright.

teacher.source: X/X69/X69n1364.xml (雲居率菴和尚語錄, ed. 了見/文郁/本空)
teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense for his teacher
teacher.quote: 為佛照和尚拈香：根從江西來，還向江西爇。一笑掀天只自知，天上拈來成漏泄。佛照禪師有卒菴頌曰：箇中消息憑誰委，一笑掀天只自知。
teacher.note: First-person 拈香 為佛照和尚 (Fozhao Deguang). The mutual recognition is striking: his own 語錄 quotes a 卒菴 (=率菴) verse Fozhao wrote FOR him. Also 上堂 因參佛照 (lb 0120a09), 禮佛照禪師塔 (lb 0126b05). Credit to sub-song subagent for locating the 語錄.

teacher.quote: 率庵梵琮禪師語錄一卷…嗣佛照光
teacher.note: 嗣佛照光. Also 續傳燈錄 T51n2077 lb0705c25 (育王光禪師法嗣…雲居梵琮), X84n1579 lb0752a16, DILA A013804.

teacher.quote: 育王光禪師法嗣……雲居梵琮和尚
育王佛照德光（1121-1203）禪師法嗣，大鑑下第十八世。

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: DILA explicitly records that no dates survive.

bio.quote: 嘉定十二年（1219），入住仗錫山延勝禪院。紹定元年（1228），受請住雲居山真如禪院。

bio: Of the Ye clan of Changshou in Yuzhou, born on the fifth of the third month, 1623 — a farming family, three generations at the plough. The wars destroyed his home: 'From Tianqi 1, when the rebels broke Yuzhou, to the jiashen year of Sizong, east and west of Shu, north and south of Ba, fields, houses, fathers and brothers were burned and slaughtered to nothing.' Orphaned and alone, he fled south to Qianzhou, met a monk from home, wept, and swore: 'If I do not leave home now, may I go the way of the old men of my village.' He was shaved by Dongming Xiao and named Fuhui, styled Sixiu. In 1652 a monk from Longmen told him of his master; he went, was shouted out of the room at the first meeting, and set to work on 'the ten thousand dharmas return to one.' He received the seal from Shanhui Wanbi (Zhuanjing) at Longmen and held Ciyun, Zhulin at Menghua, Wufu at Shunning, Fahua at Fumin, Mile at Chengjiang, and finally Songshan in Yizhou.

steles.title: 行實 (in 嵩山野竹禪師錄 卷14)
steles.author: the master himself — spoken to the assembly
steles.quote: 康熙壬寅，慈玉僧統將嵩山眾護法命來，師既受之，十二月到院。明日，黑白千人，欲聞師行腳，因命坐，乃從容告曰：「慧，渝州長壽葉氏子，生熹宗癸亥三月五日。葉氏自先大父至慧，三世皆業耕…慧既遭亂，適父母俱亡，孤身南避黔州…乃謁東明曉師剃落，名福慧，字思修…」
steles.note: NOT a posthumous account — a first-person autobiography, delivered standing in front of a thousand people who had asked to hear where he came from. Rare and unusually candid about the war.

teacher.quote: 次，拈香云：「根生東巴，支茂南國，撞著平越一箇布衲，折合一上…爇向盧中，供養見住荊南開聖禪院磚鏡璧和尚。」
teacher.note: His own hand, naming 磚鏡璧 — the man DILA files as 山暉完璧.

teacher.quote: 及到龍門…和尚問：『何來？』…未久，和尚遷萬壽，慧去求開示，和尚示以平實，末教參：萬法歸一，一歸何處？
益州嵩山壄竹福慧禪師，長壽葉氏，山暉完璧禪師（1621-1687）法嗣
TEACHER-> 完璧

dates.quote: 生熹宗癸亥三月五日 (5th day, 3rd month, Tianqi 3 = 1623)
birth +1623-04-04; no death year recorded

links.label: DILA Authority A016491
links.confirms: teacher, birth, abbacies; NO death year

bio: Of the Ke clan of Putian, born 1612. As a child the sight of hills and water made him want to leave the world; at eighteen he took the five precepts under Qiaoyun and devoted himself to nianfo, and at twenty-seven was tonsured at Guohuan monastery. Reading the Xuefeng record — Touzi pointing at a slab of rock and saying 'all the buddhas of the three times are in there' — he chewed on it half a year and got nowhere; then Baohua Ren at Cao shan raised his staff, touched him with it, and something opened. He went to Baichi Xingyuan of Jinsu at Mount Bai in Jianzhou, fitted him like needle to mustard-seed, and received the seal. He held Gushan at Xinghua, Jiuzuo Xingguo, Bao'en, Longhua Wanshou, Tongtian at Lushan, and Ximing on Mount Shi. He was still alive in 1691, aged eighty; his death year is not recorded.

steles.title: 行實 (in 蓮峰禪師語錄 卷7)
steles.author: (in his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 「辛丑秋……，時年五十。」 (cited by DILA from this 行實 for his birth year)
steles.note: The 行實 is the source DILA uses for his dates; the 語錄's table of contents confirms it sits in 卷7.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 at Gushan, 1653
teacher.quote: 此一瓣香，得意難言，知恩有地，久默斯要，不務速說，最初拈出，奉為浙江嘉興府海鹽縣金粟山廣慧堂上傳臨濟正宗第三十二世本師百癡元大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: First-person, first time he ever raised it — names Baichi Xingyuan of Jinsu, with his monastery and generation number.

teacher.quote: (百癡元嗣)
TEACHER-> 行元；為百癡行元禪師（1611-1662）法嗣

dates.quote: 「辛丑秋……，時年五十。」
birth 萬曆四十年 (1612)；清康熙三十年，年八十 (still living in 1691); 卒年及世壽不詳

links.label: DILA Authority A016380
links.confirms: teacher, birth, abbacies; NO death year

bio: Of the Zhu clan of Siming (Mingzhou). He was a full monk while still young and had mastered Tiantai doctrine when he changed his robes and went to Xuedou Mingjue, who sized him up and sneered: 'A lecture-hall abbot.' Stung, he went down the mountain, bowed back toward Xuedou and swore: 'If in this life my Chan does not surpass Xuedou, I will never go home.' He went to Letan and sat twelve years with the doubt unbroken; hearing that Yangqi Fanghui had moved to Yun'gai and could handle students, he went straight there, and before a word was finished the mind-seal was clear. After Yangqi died he studied on with his fellow-student Baiyun Shouduan. He held Baoning twice and died there. No dates survive in any source.

teacher.kind: own 拈香 incense, at his enthronement (保寧, 江寧府)
teacher.quote: 又拈香。大眾，此一瓣香，古今無價，佛祖不傳。且道從什處得來？還知落處麼？若也知得，祇者裏參見真善知識。若也不知，爇向爐中供養。我先住楊岐，後住雲蓋會和尚。
teacher.note: First-person, at the transmission. The THIRD stick (after the emperor and the officials) — the dharma stick — and he names the man by seat and name: 「我…楊岐…雲蓋 會和尚」 = 楊岐方會, who moved from 楊岐 to 雲蓋. It matches the biographical note that he sought Yangqi out when Yangqi moved to Yungai (「聞楊岐移雲蓋…直造其家」). Note he does not use the words 用酬法乳 — instead he stages the whole stick as a koan (「佛祖不傳。且道從什處得來？」) before offering it. It is unmistakably the dharma stick.

teacher.quote: 生卒年不詳，楊岐方會禪師法嗣。…聞楊岐移雲蓋，能鈐鍵學者，直造其家。一語未及，頓明心印。
法嗣有白雲守端、保寧仁勇諸禪師
teacher.note: The same edge from the teacher's side.

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳
dates.note: Explicitly unknown. The roster left them null too — correctly.

bio: Born Chen Guobin at Gaoyang village in Ou'ning county, Jianning prefecture, on the fourth of the tenth month, 1614. He resolved on leaving the world at sixteen and was shaved by Ticong of Huangyan. Reading Zhongfeng's admonitions he felt something come clear; reading the Chuandeng lu he hit Zhaozhou's 'cotton shirt of Qingzhou' like an iron wall and could not get past it. He called first on Juelang Daosheng, then went to Miyun Yuanwu at Tiantong — and one word from him settled it. He served eight autumns at Miyun's side before taking a hut of his own. He held Cuiyan at Hongdu, then Huangyan, Baifa, and Foding in Jianzhou.

steles.title: 行實 (in 古雪哲禪師語錄 卷11)
steles.author: (in his own 語錄)
steles.quote: 「（萬曆）甲寅年十月初四日亥時」 (cited by DILA from this 行實 for his birth)
steles.note: DILA cites 卷11〈行實〉 and 卷20 for his life. The batch note was right that no lamp carried him — but the 行實 in his own 語錄 does.

teacher.quote: 此一瓣香本自現成，豈從人得？八載執侍巾缾，一旦親蒙密印…專伸供養明州天童堂上傳曹谿正脈第三十四世上密下雲先和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: '上密下雲' = Miyun. Eight years carrying his master's towel and water-bottle, then the seal. First-person, decisive — this closes the gap the batch note flagged.

teacher.quote: 密雲悟嗣。大鑑下第三十五世
TEACHER-> 圓悟

dates.quote: （萬曆）甲寅年十月初四日亥時
birth +1614-11-05; no death year recorded

bio: A Qing Linji master, dharma heir of Zhufeng Huanmin (1638-1707) and thirty-first generation below Nanyue. He opened the dharma at Changle Chan monastery. Only the first character of his dharma name (一) is recorded anywhere, and it is not expanded in any source I could reach. His recorded sayings survive in one fascicle, compiled by his heirs Mingman and Minghui. No dates.

teacher.kind: his own 拈香 at the opening of the hall
teacher.quote: 此瓣香，播植威音前，覆育空劫外，爇向爐中，供養傳臨濟正宗第二十七代上竺下峰本師老和尚，用酬法乳，更冀薪傳二桂，派衍五花。
teacher.note: '上竺下峰' = Zhufeng. First-person, at the transmission.

teacher.quote: 南嶽下第三十一世，嗣竺峯敏
為竺峰幻敏禪師（1638-1707）法嗣。住常樂禪寺。

dates.quote: 生卒年不詳

bio: Styled Sanyi, called Yu'an, of the Ding clan of Wulin in Qiantang, born 1599. He set his mind on leaving the world at fourteen and took the five precepts from Zhuhong at Yunqi; at sixteen a reading of Zhenjing's record opened something; he entered Zhenji as a postulant at twenty and was shaved at twenty-three. He went to Zhanran Yuancheng at Xiansheng, and Yuancheng entrusted him with the Caodong seal. Ill for years and worn to the bone, he called himself 'the White-Bones Wayfarer.' He held Longmen from 1635, then Huashan, took Xiansheng in 1643, Fanshou in 1650, Zhuming in 1656. He died on the eleventh of the tenth month, 1665, aged sixty-seven; thirty men inherited his dharma, of whom Zhe'an Jingfan is one.

teacher.quote: 此一瓣香，根生靈鷲，葉覆娑婆，今日拈來，卻為山僧二十年前在瓶窯燒得一擔破砂盆…奉為顯聖堂上傳曹洞正宗三十二世先散木大和尚，用酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: He names his master by the sobriquet 散木 — which DILA independently records as Zhanran Yuancheng's own alternate name (散木道人). First-person, and it matches.

teacher.quote: (湛然澄法嗣) 三宜盂
TEACHER-> 圓澄；湛然圓澄禪師法嗣

dates.quote: birth +1599; death 康熙乙巳十月十一辭世。壽六十七 (《續燈正統》卷39)
dates.note: The batch had him as 'floruit 1643, death 1665' — 1643 is only the year he took Xiansheng. His birth year is 1599.

bio.source: 《三宜盂禪師語錄》卷11 + 《五燈全書》卷62 (via DILA A012054)

bio: Styled Weize, called Zhe'an, of the Ji clan of Wujiang in Gusu, born 1620. He left home at fifteen, was shaved at eighteen, heard Xuehang lecture on the Vijñaptimātratā at twenty, and while resting from communal labour at Bian shan heard a clap of thunder in the Zhengzhong pavilion and had his opening. He took full ordination at twenty-one at Ruiguang, called on Zhishi, Xueqiao, Yu'an and Tiantong, and in 1649, aged thirty, received the Caodong dharma-seal from Yu'an (Sanyi Mingyu). He held Zisheng at Zuili, Xiansheng at Yunmen, Husheng at Caoshan, Guangfu at Dongta and Tianhua at Dongguan. A fine calligrapher; his recorded sayings run to thirty fascicles. He died in 1692, aged seventy-three.

teacher.quote: 此一瓣香先於正中亭畔拾來…後於玉笥峰前投入大爐鞴裏，猛火一鍛…今日人天眾前拈出，端為傳曹洞正宗二十八世，即此堂上本師愚菴老和尚，以酬法乳之恩。
teacher.note: '本師愚菴' — Yu'an is Sanyi Mingyu's own hao (DILA lists 愚菴明盂). The two hao (蔗菴 for him, 愚菴 for his master) are what confused the lamps; the incense settles it.

bio: Surnamed Zhang, of Lingxiao in Shaanxi, born on the fifth of the twelfth month, 1662 (early 1663). His parents gave him to Jingyue at Lingshan monastery, who shaved him. At nine he was studying the Śūraṅgama and stopped short at 'if the original nature is pure, whence come the mountains and rivers?' At nineteen he took full ordination from Tenghuan of Xishan; at twenty-four he went to Gumei Dinglie on Mount Furong. In 1689 Dinglie sealed him in retreat in the Purple Bamboo Grove, where he broke through, and at Dinglie's death he received the entrustment. In 1691 he took the Miyin monastery on Mount Wei in Hunan and Guanghua at Furong. He died on the ninth of the fifth month, 1695, aged thirty-four, fourteen years a monk.

bio: Of the Zhou clan of Taizhou (Ninghai), born 1151. He was tonsured at Jingtu cloister, held Hanqing, Nengren and Guangxiao, then moved to Jiangshan and Tiantong, and in 1218 was commanded to Jingshan — the first monastery of the empire. He bore the title Chan Master Foxin. He is the hub from which four well-attested heirs hang: Yanxi Guangwen, Dachuan Puji, Huaihai Yuanzhao and Jieshi Zhipeng, each filed as 'eighteenth generation below Nanyue, heir of Zhewong Yan.' He died in 1225, aged seventy-five.

bio: Of the Song clan of Ba county in western Shu, born on the twenty-fifth of the fifth month, 1611. Orphaned young and raised by his grandmother, he left home at twenty-three at the Baihe hermitage under the old monk Xingkong and practised the perfection of patience. A wandering monk sent him to Poxue (Xuebi Yinluan); he served six years, and when his master died he set out to travel. At Chongqing he had his understanding confirmed. He went into Guizhou and opened the dharma at Baoguo Chan monastery on Mount Muni, founded Chuanfa monastery at Xishan, and later held Qianming at Deshan in Dingzhou. He died on the fifth of the tenth month, 1666, in the guest hall of Tiantong monastery — where he had gone to sweep the stupa of the patriarch Miyun. His disciples carried his bones back to Guizhou and built his stupa by the Phoenix Pool at Xishan.

teacher.kind: 黔南會燈錄 biography — a complication
teacher.quote: 禮性空老宿出家，修忍辱行。一日得行脚僧指，參破雪和尚，圓具後服勤六載…雪寂，師矢志遍參，至重慶遇長破杲和尚印證。
teacher.note: ⚠ THREE names to keep straight. 性空 tonsured him (禮…出家) — not the teacher. He served 破雪 SIX YEARS until 破雪's death — 破雪 is very likely 雪臂印巒 under a variant/abbreviation (雪臂 ↔ 破雪), which is why the catalogs file him there. THEN 長破杲 gave 印證 (confirmation) while he wandered — a second, post-facto seal, NOT the transmission. Marked `disputed` only because the corpus name 破雪 does not letter-for-letter equal 雪臂; the lineage assignment itself is firm.

bio: Named Liaowu or Mingwu, called Wuji, also Canggu ('silkworm bone'); of the Mo clan of Anyue county, Tongchuan prefecture, Shu. He left home at twenty at Luowei monastery in Dingyuan under Benzhen, then went round the great monasteries of Shu. The Qing Bodhisattva raised Zhaozhou's 'no' for him and something opened; from then he carried the word 'no' walking, standing, sitting and lying. He went into the hills at Fanchang to Guzhuo Jun, who saw him, was astonished, and gave him the dharma on one word. He then settled at Daolin monastery at Jiguang for over forty years. In 1444 the new ordination platform at Wanshou monastery brought a summons to the capital, where he was made a master of the school. He died at dawn on the first day of the fourth month, 1446, aged sixty-six, forty-eight years a monk; his Daolin Record survives. Chushan Shaoqi and Guting Shanjian came from his gate.

bio: The Seon master who ordained Jinul. Jinul's father, having prayed at the temple for his sickly son, gave the boy up at eight; Jinul 'went to the Seon master Chonghwi, a distant descendant of Caoxi, took tonsure and received the full precepts, and thereafter had no fixed master — he followed only the Way.' The record of Songgwangsa, written in 1207 while Jinul was still alive, says the same in its own words. Nothing else about him survives: his own teacher is named by no source I can reach.

bio: A monk of the western capital (Luoyang), dharma heir of Yiyan Daoxian of the Xiangguo monastery. He died on the eleventh of the eighth month, 1458 — the Xudeng zhengtong records that he 'leaned on his staff and was transformed.' His heir was Yuanqin.

teacher.quote: 小菴行密禪師初以白衣禮一言，師凡見便禮拜。言一日謂曰：道人禮拜且止，佛法在甚麼處？師方舉首，忽聞板聲鳴。言曰：只者是。師從此入，遂求度。言曰：汝誠精進，宜名行密。力參座下三年。
teacher.note: 師從此入 under 一言 (= 一言道顯 / 相國道顯), who then NAMED him 行密 and trained him three years. The name itself is the teacher's gift — strong internal evidence.

bio: Third patriarch of Chan. Came to Huike as a layman and received ordination and transmission from him. During Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou's suppression of Buddhism he went into hiding on Mt. Wangong in Shuzhou, travelling for a time to Mt. Luofu in Guangdong before returning. Died in 606 (Sui Daye 2). The Xinxinming (信心銘) is traditionally ascribed to him.

steles.title: 舒州山谷寺覺寂塔隋故鏡智禪師碑銘（並序）
steles.author: 獨孤及
steles.author_note: Tang literatus; text preserved in 全唐文 juan 390. Not located in the CBETA Zen allowlist; known via DILA's citation and Wikisource.
steles.note: A genuine Tang stele for Sengcan exists, but it is a re-consecration inscription written well after his death (the stupa was opened under Tang), so it is NOT contemporary testimony. Recorded here for completeness, not relied on.

steles.title: 舒州山谷寺覺寂塔隋故鏡智禪師碑銘（並序）
steles.author: 獨孤及 (Dugu Ji), then prefect of Shuzhou
steles.quote: 當時問道於禪師者…雙峰大師道信其人也。其後信公以教傳宏忍，忍公傳惠能、神秀。能公退而老曹溪，其嗣無聞焉。秀公傳普寂，寂公之門徒萬人
steles.note: ⚠ MAJOR HISTORIOGRAPHIC DATUM. This 772 stele gives the chain 僧璨 → 道信 → 弘忍 → 惠能 AND 神秀 → 普寂 → 宏正 — but then says of Huineng: 「能公退而老曹溪，其嗣無聞焉」 — 'Master Neng retired and grew old at Caoxi; OF HIS HEIRS NOTHING WAS HEARD.' Written by a senior Tang official 36 years after Shenhui's 796 campaign began. This is a Northern-school-leaning source and does NOT license cutting any Huineng edge (no landing place is named); record it as a contradiction datum about how the lineage looked in 772.

teacher.source: 全唐文 卷0390, 舒州山谷寺覺寂塔隋故鏡智禪師碑銘（並序）, by 獨孤及 (Dugu Ji), 772
teacher.quote: 桉前誌，禪師號僧璨，不知何許人。出見於周隋間，傳教於惠可大師，摳衣於鄴中，得道於司空山
teacher.note: 傳教於惠可大師 — 'received the transmission of the teaching from Master Huike'. The stele opens by admitting his origins are unknown, which is a mark of its honesty. It also cites earlier lost stele texts by 薛道衡 (Sui) and 房琯 (Tang) as its sources: 「碑版之文，隋內史侍郎河東薛公道衡、唐相國刑部尚書贈太尉河南房公琯繼論撰之」.

teacher.source: 全唐文 卷0390, same stele
teacher.quote: 至菩提達摩大師，始示人以諸佛心要，人疑而未思。惠可大師傳而持之，人思而未修。迨禪師三葉，其風浸廣
teacher.note: 達摩 → 惠可 → 僧璨, explicitly the third leaf (三葉).

teacher.quote: 初以白衣謁二祖慧可禪師，既受度傳法。

bio.quote: 禪宗三祖…僧璨出家後，逢周武滅佛，遂隱居舒州皖公山。隱居期問，曾與道友遊廣東羅浮山。後回舒州。隋大業二年（606）寂。有《信心銘》行於世。

notes: Third Patriarch. Attributed author of the Xinxinming (信心銘, Faith in Mind), one of the earliest and most influential Chan poems.

bio: A monk of Shouzhou Anfeng who had read the Lankavatara Sutra over a thousand times without grasping the three bodies and four wisdoms, and came to Huineng to have it explained. He is listed among Huineng's dharma heirs in the Jingde Chuandeng Lu.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 heir-list, 六祖慧能大師法嗣
teacher.quote: 〔六祖法嗣〕…洪州法達禪師　壽州智通禪師　江西志徹禪師…
teacher.note: Among Huineng's direct heirs.

teacher.quote: 壽州智通禪師者，壽州安豐人也。初看《楞伽經》約千餘遍而不會三身四智，禮師求解其義。祖曰：三身者，清淨法身汝之性也…聽吾偈曰：自性具三身，發明成四智…師從此領玄旨。
teacher.note: 禮師求解 + 祖 (= 六祖) + 領玄旨. The doctrine passes directly from Huineng. ⚠ collision guard: a DIFFERENT 智通 (揚州棲靈寺智通, Mazu's heir) sits in this same book at 0245c12 — not this man.

notes: Listed in the Platform Sutra as one of Huineng's disciples.

bio: Daughter of Layman Pang Yun. She supported the household by selling bamboo strainers. The Pang Jushi Yulu shows her matching her father in exchanges — when he offered 'difficult, difficult' and her mother 'easy, easy', she answered 'neither difficult nor easy: on the hundred grass-tips, the patriarchs' meaning.' When Pang prepared to die and sent her to watch for noon, she reported a solar eclipse, and while he stepped out to look she sat down in his seat, joined her palms and died first. He laughed: 'My daughter is quicker than I am,' and delayed his own death seven days.

teacher.quote: 元和中，居士北遊襄漢，隨處而居。有女靈照，常鬻竹漉籬以供朝夕。
teacher.note: She is 居士（龐蘊）之女 — daughter and companion, not a formal disciple of any master. An honest null teacher is correct; the 'school by association' is the Pang household's (Shitou/Mazu).

teacher.quote: 居士一日坐次，問靈照曰：「古人道『明明百草頭，明明祖師意』，如何會？」照曰：「老老大大作這箇語話。」士曰：「你作麼生？」照曰：「明明百草頭，明明祖師意。」士乃笑。
teacher.note: Her realisation, in her father's own record — she meets him as an equal.

bio.quote: 有女靈照，常鬻竹漉籬以供朝夕。
居士將入滅，謂靈照曰：視日早晚及午以報。照遽報：日已中矣，而有蝕也。士出戶觀次，照即登父座，合掌坐亡。士笑曰：我女鋒捷矣。于是更延七日。
靈照云：也不難，也不易，百草頭上祖師意。

notes: Daughter of Layman Pang, depicted as matching or surpassing her father in insight. Died moments before him.

bio: Silla monk who travelled to Tang China and received the dharma from Xitang Zhizang, a direct heir of Mazu. His return to Korea is counted as the first transmission of Chan (Seon) to the peninsula and the seed of the Nine Mountains schools. Posthumous name Wonjeok (元寂).

teacher.quote: 虔州西堂藏禪師法嗣（祖堂集：317）
teacher.note: DILA also cites T51n2076_p0264a22 (景德傳燈錄) for the same.

teacher.quote: 虔州西堂藏禪師法嗣

notes: First Korean monk to transmit the Seon (Chan) lineage to the Korean peninsula, inaugurating the 'Nine Mountains' Seon movement. He traveled to Tang China and studied under Xitang Zhizang, a direct heir of Mazu Daoyi, receiving formal dharma transmission. Upon returning to Silla, he found the doctrinal Buddhist establishment hostile to Seon and was unable to teach openly during his lifetime. His disciple Yomgo later founded the Gaji Mountain school (Silsangsa), the first of the Nine Mountains Seon lineages. Doui is thus honored as the patriarch who planted Seon in Korean soil, even though its flowering came after his death. Attested in Zutangji (952): records his study under Xitang Zhizang with a transmission dialogue confirming his awakening.

bio: Of Jianchang, surname Wang. Left home at Shimen and served Baizhang Huaihai for more than twenty years without penetrating the essential point. After Baizhang's death he went to Yaoshan Weiyan and became his heir. He taught at Mt. Yunyan in Tanzhou. His heirs include Dongshan Liangjie, making him the pivot of the Caodong line. Posthumously 無住禪師.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988), 唐澧陽雲巖寺曇晟傳
teacher.quote: 參見百丈山海禪師，二十年為侍者…續受藥山舉發，全了無疑。
teacher.note: TWO teachers, one dharma-father: he served 百丈懷海 twenty years (association, 為侍者) but got his transmission from 藥山惟儼 (受藥山舉發，全了無疑). The Caodong lineage runs 藥山儼 → 雲巖晟 → 洞山价. The twenty years under 百丈 is the classic association-is-not-transmission trap — his father is 藥山.

teacher.quote: TEACHER 惟儼 (A010510); also: 參見百丈山海禪師，二十年為侍者。（T50n2061_p0775b10）
teacher.note: DILA lists BOTH 惟儼 and 懷海 as 'teacher' — but the transmission is 惟儼; 懷海 is the 20-year attendancy.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 惟儼 (A010510)
teacher.note: The transmitting teacher.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 懷海 — 參見百丈山海禪師，二十年為侍者。（T50n2061_p0775b10）
teacher.note: DISAGREEMENT RECORDED: DILA lists TWO teachers. Baizhang Huaihai was his teacher of twenty years but did NOT transmit; Yaoshan did. I take Yaoshan, per DILA's own concise: 「懷海示寂後，參謁澧州藥山惟儼，並嗣其法」. The roster is correct — and this is precisely the 'first teacher vs transmitter' trap the audit is about.

bio.quote: 俗姓王。少於石門出家，初參百丈懷海，歷二十餘年，未悟玄旨。懷海示寂後，參謁澧州藥山惟儼，並嗣其法，後住於潭州雲巖山大揚宗風。

notes: Crucial link in the Caodong lineage as teacher of Dongshan. 'Whole body is hands and eyes' koan.

bio: Known only through a single scene: he cooked the monks' rice himself, and at each mealtime carried the rice-bucket to the front of the hall, danced, and called out 'Bodhisattvas, come and eat!' — then clapped and roared with laughter, and did so every day. Listed among Mazu Daoyi's heirs.

teacher.quote: 《景德傳燈錄》卷8：「(馬祖法嗣)……鎮州金牛和尚」
teacher.note: teacher 馬祖道一 confirmed.

teacher.kind: flat 法嗣 index (景德傳燈錄)
teacher.quote: …南嶽西園曇藏禪師 百靈和尚 鎮州金牛和尚 洞安和尚 忻州打地和尚…
teacher.note: Listed in the roll of Mazu's heirs. This is index-rung only — no biography, no dates, no stele.

bio.quote: 鎮州金牛和尚。師自作飯供養眾僧。每至齋時舁飯桶到堂前作舞曰。菩薩子喫飯來。乃撫掌大笑。日日如是。

notes: Known for dancing with the rice bucket — 'Bodhisattvas, come eat!'
date_note: roster 800-860 is a shared placeholder (劉鐵磨·俱胝·魯祖·金牛 all identical)

bio: Of Guangzhou, surname Liao. Left home at Mt. Longya in Tanzhou and took full ordination at twenty, then studied sutras and treatises at Jiangling. While abbot at Helin in Runzhou he was redirected to the boatman-monk Chuanzi Decheng, became his heir, and in the Xiantong era moved to Mt. Jiashan in Lizhou, whence his name. Posthumously 傳明大師.

teacher.quote: 華亭船子德誠禪師法嗣一人：澧州夾山善會禪師一人見錄
teacher.note: The sole heir of the Boatman.

teacher.quote: 澧州夾山善會禪師，廣州峴亭人也，姓廖氏…初住京口。一夕道吾策杖而至，遇師上堂…道吾乃笑。師乃生疑問吾，何笑？吾曰：和尚一等出世未有師，可往淛中華亭縣參船子和尚去…師遂易服直詣華亭，會船子鼓櫂而至，師資道契，微眹不留。
teacher.note: ⚠ THE ASSOCIATION TRAP, defused: 道吾 LAUGHED and SENT him (未有師…可往…參船子) — Daowu is not the teacher. 師資道契 ('master and disciple matched in the Way') is with 船子德誠. This is the textbook case the brief warns about — an admired elder / redirector is not the dharma-father.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 德誠 (A005724)

dates.quote: +0881-12-05 唐中和元年辛丑十一月七日。……。壽七十七，臘五十七。（T49n2036_p0646c12）
dates.note: Death 881 with age 77 gives birth 805. Both roster values confirmed.

bio.quote: 唐僧。廣州廖氏，船子德誠禪師法嗣。幼於潭州龍牙山出家，二十歲受具足戒。後往江陵聽習經論…復往華亭參德誠，嗣其法。咸通中，遷澧州夾山，世稱夾山和尚。寂諡傳明大師。

notes: Originally a sutra lecturer in Guangzhou; redirected to study with the boatman-monk Chuanzi Decheng, who pushed him into the river, triggering his awakening. He then established a major monastery on Mount Jia (Jiashan) in Hunan, where he taught for decades. His heir Luopu Yuanan carried his transmission forward.

bio: An heir of Dongshan Liangjie, listed in the Jingde Chuandeng Lu among his twenty-six dharma heirs. He appears in Gateless Gate case 48 and Book of Serenity case 40. Yunmen is said to have studied under him.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄 index of Dongshan's heirs
teacher.quote: 洞山良价禪師法嗣二十六人：…越州乾峯和尚…已上一十八人見錄。
teacher.note: Directly under 洞山良价, and 見錄 (his dialogues are recorded), not merely a name.

teacher.kind: 景德傳燈錄, his own entry
teacher.quote: 越州乾峯和尚，或云瑞峯。問僧：「什麼處來？」曰：「天台。」師曰：「見說石橋作兩段是否？」…
teacher.note: A full entry with recorded dialogue — he is a fleshed-out lamp figure, not a bare index line.

teacher.kind: flat 法嗣 index (景德傳燈錄)
teacher.quote: 洞山良价禪師法嗣二十六人 洪州雲居山道膺禪師 撫州曹山本寂禪師…洛京白馬遁儒禪師 越州乾峯和尚 吉州禾山和尚…
teacher.note: Teacher confirmed at index rung.

notes: Dharma heir of Dongshan. Known for 'three diseases and two lights of the dharmakaya' teaching. Yunmen served under him before succeeding Xuefeng. Appears in Gateless Gate Case 48 and Book of Serenity Case 61.

bio: Of Xin'gan. After study with Xiangyan Zhixian and others he became an heir of Dongshan Liangjie and settled at Mt. Sushan in Fuzhou, where he founded Sushan monastery. Short and unprepossessing, he was nicknamed 'the dwarf uncle' (矮師叔), but his debating was so relentless that he was also called 'Sushan the arrow-biter'. Called 光仁 in Song sources to avoid the Song founder's taboo name.

teacher.quote: 袁州洞山良价禪師法嗣……撫州疎山光仁禪師
teacher.note: The index places him under Dongshan. This remains the best evidence.

teacher.quote: 早參洞山，深入玄奧，其辯給又多於人也。
teacher.note: ⚠ HONEST CAVEAT. 參 is on the NON-transmission list — 'he studied with / called on Dongshan'. Song gaoseng zhuan does NOT use a transmission verb for this man, and gives no 印可, no 付法. The edge rests on the lamp INDEX (法嗣 header), not on any narrated transmission. Grade C is right; I could not lift it.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 良价 — 《景德傳燈錄》卷17：「袁州洞山良价禪師法嗣……撫州疎山光仁禪師」(T51, no. 2076, p. 334, a7-21)
洞山良价禪師法嗣…撫州疎山光仁禪師

dates.note: CONFLICT. DILA gives 845-935; the roster gives 837-909. DILA's own source for these is a hudong.com wiki page (weak). I record BOTH and take NEITHER as established — neither is anchored to a primary text. Flagged as unresolved.

dates.quote: 845–935 (http://www.hudong.com/wiki/疏山寺)
dates.note: wiki-sourced; not defensible
IMPOSSIBLE: predates teacher 洞山良价

bio.quote: 出家後，參謁香嚴智閑等人，後嗣洞山良价之法，住撫州之疏山，建疏山寺…因其身形矮小，容貌不揚，故被稱為矮師叔…故又有「疏山嚙鏃」之稱。因避宋太祖諱，又稱光仁。

notes: Heir of Dongshan Liangjie, nicknamed 'Uncle Dwarf.' Fellow students regarded him as the most penetrating among Dongshan's disciples and would say 'let's just go ask Uncle Dwarf' when difficult questions arose. Known for 'the price of the dharma body' exchange.

bio: Of Yanguan (Song Gaoseng Zhuan says Haiyan), surname Sun, so called 'Mr Sun'. Ordained at Tongxuan monastery in Suzhou. He studied under Lingyun Zhiqin, Xuefeng Yicun and Xuansha Shibei, staying with Xuefeng some thirty years before becoming his heir. In 906 he took Zhaoqing cloister in Quanzhou, later Changqing cloister in Fuzhou. Died 932 aged 79. Titled 超覺大師.

steles.title: (碑紀德 — title not preserved)
steles.author: 判官林文盛 (Lin Wensheng)
steles.quote: 判官林文盛為碑紀德云。
steles.note: Attested by name in 宋高僧傳; text not extant in CBETA.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳 (988) — 後唐福州長慶院慧稜傳, a full standalone 正傳
teacher.quote: 已聞南方有禪學，遂遊閩嶺，謁雪峯，提耳指訂，頓明本性。乃述偈云：「昔時謾向途中學，今日看來火裏氷。」如是親依，不下峯頂，計三十許載。
teacher.note: 提耳指訂 — Xuefeng took him by the ear and set him straight — and he 'clung close, never once coming down off the peak, for some THIRTY YEARS.' The awakening verse is preserved. Zanning wrote this 56 years after Huileng's death (932), well inside living memory in Fujian, and — see below — from a stele.

teacher.quote: 閩國王氏私誄之「大師」，號超覺。塔葬皆出官供。判官林文盛為碑紀德云。
teacher.note: ⚑ THE STELE EXISTED AND 宋高僧傳 NAMES ITS AUTHOR: 判官林文盛 (Administrator Lin Wensheng) 'wrote the stele recording his virtue.' The Min kingdom paid for the stupa and burial. The stone's TEXT does not survive in this canon — but Zanning's biography is demonstrably drawing on it, which is exactly why it reads like a stele (dates, age 79, dharma-age 60, patron, official honours) and not like a lamp anecdote.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 義存 (A003677)

dates.note: Death 932 aged 79 gives birth 854. Both roster values confirmed.

bio.quote: 歷參靈雲志勤、雪峰義存、玄沙師備諸尊宿，曾依止雪峰義存三十年，後嗣其法。唐天祐三年（906），住泉州昭慶院，後住福州長慶院。

notes: From Yanzhou in Zhejiang. Studied under Xuefeng Yicun for twenty-nine years and famously wore out seven meditation cushions before awakening upon rolling up a bamboo screen. Later headed Changqing Monastery in Fuzhou for twenty years. Appears in Blue Cliff Record cases 22 and 23.

bio: Of Jinyun, surname Chen. Left home at fifteen, fully ordained at eighteen, and is said to have called on fifty-four teachers before becoming the heir of Fayan Wenyi. He then went to Mt. Tiantai to seek out Zhiyi's traces and settled at Baisha. King Qian Hongchu of Wuyue brought him to Hangzhou and honoured him as National Teacher. Died 972 aged 82. His heirs include Yongming Yanshou.

steles.title: (天台德韶國師塔碑)
steles.author: 贊寧 (都僧正)
steles.quote: 焚舍利繁多，營塔，命都僧正贊寧為塔碑焉。
steles.note: Commissioned and written; the stele text itself is not in the corpus, but its author wrote the 宋高僧傳 biography quoted above — which is therefore stele-grade in substance.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳〈宋天台山德韶傳〉 — and its author 贊寧 IS THE MAN WHO CUT HIS STUPA-STELE
teacher.quote: 釋德韶者，姓陳氏，縉雲人也。幼出家于本郡，登戒後，同光中尋訪名山，參見知識，屈指不勝其數。初發心於投子山和尚，後見臨川法眼禪師，重了心要，遂承嗣焉。…焚舍利繁多，營塔，命都僧正贊寧為塔碑焉。享年八十二，法臘六十四，即開寶五年壬申歲六月二十八日也。
teacher.note: THE DECISIVE LINE: 「命都僧正贊寧為塔碑焉」 — 德韶's community commissioned 贊寧, then Buddhist Registrar, TO WRITE HIS STUPA-STELE. 贊寧 is the author of 宋高僧傳. So this biography is written by the stele's own author, about a man who died in his adult lifetime (贊寧 919–1001; 德韶 d. 972). It is not a lamp report; it is the stele-writer's own account. And it observes the discipline: 「初發心於投子山和尚」 — 投子 was where he FIRST aroused the mind — 「後見臨川法眼禪師，重了心要，遂承嗣焉」 — only 法眼 got 承嗣. First-teacher vs dharma-father, kept apart.

teacher.kind: 宋高僧傳〈法眼文益傳〉 — heir list, from the teacher's side
teacher.quote: 法嗣弟子天台德韶、慧明、漳…
teacher.note: 贊寧 names 德韶 first among 文益's 法嗣弟子. Two independent places in the same contemporary source.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 文益 (A000174)

dates.quote: +0972-08-14 享年八十二。即開寶五年壬申歲六月二十八日也。（T50n2061_p0789b06）
dates.note: Death 972 aged 82 gives birth 891. Both roster values confirmed.

bio.quote: 十五歲出家，十八歲受具足戒。嘗遍訪明師五十四人，後為臨川法眼文益之法嗣…後受吳越王錢弘俶迎至杭州，尊為國師。

notes: Most important heir of Fayan Wenyi. National teacher of Wuyue kingdom.

bio: Of Suizhou, surname Li, zi Yinzhi. Tonsured under Ren Shen at Pu'an cloister in Yizhou after mourning his parents. He became the heir of Zhimen Guangzuo, then taught at Dongting near Wu and afterwards at Mt. Xuedou in Siming, where the Yunmen line revived under him. His verses on a hundred old cases became the armature of the Blue Cliff Record. Died 1052 aged 73; Emperor Renzong granted him the title Mingjue.

steles.title: 明州雪竇山資聖寺第六祖明覺大師塔銘
steles.author: 呂夏卿
steles.author_note: 宋尚書員外郎 (Vice-Director in the Secretariat), a Song official
steles.quote: 明州雪竇山資聖寺第六祖明覺大師塔銘
steles.note: Appended to his own 明覺禪師語錄 (juan 6). This stele is DILA's cited source for BOTH his birth and his death date — i.e. the dates on the chart rest on the stupa inscription, not on a lamp. Independently referenced at X/X80/X80n1567.xml lb 0545c07: 「宋尚書員外郎呂夏卿撰。雪竇明覺大師塔銘」.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 光祚 (A015592)
晚參隨州智門祚和尚，因扣不起一念之旨，豁然知歸。
teacher.note: Quoted via DILA's [extensive] field, which cites this stele verbatim.

teacher.source: DILA A004234 (record of 琅琊慧覺)
teacher.quote: 同時，明州雪竇重顯禪師則唱雲門之法道，時人稱「二甘露門」
teacher.note: Corroborates his identity and school. I did NOT independently re-verify the Zhimen Guangzuo edge, because he is an EXISTING roster node and outside the new-master gate; flagged as a duplicate rather than re-litigated.

dates.quote: 生於太平興國五年四月八日 … 皇祐四年六月十日示寂，壽七十三
dates.note: = 980-05-29 to 1052-07-14. Roster's 980/1052 confirmed at stele rung.

notes: His poetic verses on 100 cases became the foundation of the Blue Cliff Record. Greatest poet of the Chan tradition.

bio: Of Wenxiang in Shaanxi, surname Zheng. He tested for the sangha at twenty-five and was ordained the next year, then ranged the lecture-halls of the capital, mastering the Huayan and Faxiang systems. He first failed to connect with Huanglong Huinan, and only after a conversation with the monk Shun at Xiangcheng did he understand Huanglong's intent, returned, and became his heir. From 1072 he headed Dayu in Junzhou, then Shengshou and Dongshan. When Wang Anshi gave up his house to found Baoning monastery, Kewen was made its founding abbot and granted the purple robe. Died 1102 aged 78. His heirs include Doushuai Congyue.

steles.title: 雲菴真淨和尚行狀
steles.author_note: Author not identified in the material I could reach.
steles.quote: 崇寧元年十月十六日中夜示寂，壽七十八
steles.note: The 行狀 travels in 《雲菴克文禪師語錄（敘．疏．附錄）》 (X69n1342, juan 1). It is DILA's cited source for his death date. Quote taken from DILA's citation of the 行狀; I did not open the file line directly.

steles.title: 行狀 (真淨克文)
steles.author: 惠洪 覺範 (Huihong Juefan, 1071–1128), Kewen's own disciple
steles.path: 石門文字禪 卷30 (四庫全書本) / zh.wikisource
steles.quote: 師諱克文。黃龍南禪師之的嗣
steles.note: Ends 「十月十五日門人某謹狀」.

teacher.source: 石門文字禪 卷30, 行狀, by 惠洪 (覺範), his own disciple
teacher.quote: 行狀。師諱克文。黃龍南禪師之的嗣。陜府閿鄉鄭氏子
teacher.note: ★ THE VERY FIRST LINE names the dharma-father: 黃龍南禪師之的嗣 — 'the LEGITIMATE HEIR (的嗣) of Chan master Nan of Huanglong'. Written by Huihong, who was Kewen's own disciple.

teacher.quote: 時南禪師已居積翠。徑造其廬…南公大駭。參依久之…及南公居黃龍，復往省覲
teacher.note: The narrative of the meeting at Jicui.

teacher.source: 石門文字禪 卷30 (in 湛堂文準's 行狀, immediately following)
teacher.quote: 嗚呼。雲庵之神悟於南公之門。超軼絕塵者也
teacher.note: Huihong again, in another man's 行狀: 'Yun'an's spiritual awakening at Nan-gong's gate outstripped all others.'

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 慧南 (A003921)

dates.quote: 崇寧元年十月十六日中夜示寂，壽七十八（〈雲菴真淨和尚行狀〉）
dates.note: = 1102-12-04, aged 78, giving birth 1025. Roster confirmed.

notes: Also known as Baofeng Kewen. Second-generation Huanglong master. Known for expelling monks immediately after their awakening. Teacher of Doushuai Congyue.

bio: Of Hongzhou, surname Huang. Left home at eleven, ordained at eighteen. Travelling to Xiangyang he met Lumen Zijue, was tested and sealed by him. In the Xuanhe era he headed Tianning monastery in Qingzhou, where he used to set a hundred questions in the abbot's room to examine students. He later held Huayan and Wanshou in Yanjing and Puzhao in Qingzhou, carrying the Caodong teaching in the Jin-ruled north. Died 1149 aged 69. The Qingzhou Baiwen (青州百問) is his.

steles.title: 青州辯自書塔記 / 青州塔記
steles.author: 希辯 himself
steles.quote: 青州辯自書塔記。其略曰．參自覺和尚於襄州鹿門山。政和五年冬．承印可。
steles.note: The stone is quoted (「其略曰」, in summary) inside 正名錄; the full stone is not in the corpus, but the quotation is a direct citation of a document 白巖's man spent two years retrieving from the north.

teacher.kind: his own 自書塔記 (self-written stupa-record), quoted in 正名錄 j.5 by 智楷惟直
teacher.quote: 青州辯自書塔記。其略曰．參自覺和尚於襄州鹿門山。政和五年冬．承印可。隨命見芙蓉。尋住泗水龍門。宣和間．開法青州。天寧八載。遂至燕京。初住奉恩。次住華嚴．即萬壽寺。後住仰山。天眷三年．復住萬壽。皇統六年．退歸仰山。九年己巳示寂。即南宋高宗紹興十九年也。
teacher.note: 承印可 = a transmission verb, written by the man himself about himself. This is the strongest rung available. The stone was physically recovered: 「昔白巖命僧懷誼．北往兩年．始得青州塔記」 (0463a23) — a monk was sent north for two years to fetch it, and 白巖淨符 used it in 康熙壬子 (1672) to correct the whole Caodong lineage.

teacher.kind: 增集續傳燈錄 (compiled by 南石文琇, Yongle era), quoted in 正名錄
teacher.quote: 裕嗣萬松秀．秀嗣雪巖滿．滿嗣王山體．體嗣磁州寶．寶嗣青州辯．辯嗣鹿門覺．覺嗣芙蓉楷。
teacher.note: Independent corroboration of 辯嗣鹿門覺.

teacher.kind: 佛祖傳法偈碑, a stone at 勝果寺 (plus three further stones: 大萬壽禪寺開山傳法歷代宗師實蹟記; 月舟載行實碑 by 天童懷讓虛; 幻休潤行實碑記 by 袁了凡)
teacher.quote: 曹洞正傳青原思．石頭遷．藥山儼．雲巖晟．洞山价．雲居膺．同安丕．同安志．梁山觀．大陽玄．投子青．芙蓉楷．鹿門覺．青州辯．磁州寶．王山體．雪巖滿．萬松秀．雪庭裕…
teacher.note: FOUR separate carved lineage-lists all put 青州辯 directly under 鹿門覺 under 芙蓉楷.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 自覺 (A014564) — 為鹿門自覺禪師法嗣 (X63n1244_p0497b16)

dates.quote: 金皇統九年（1149）示寂，世壽六十九（疑年錄：258）
dates.note: Death 1149 aged 69 gives birth 1081. Both roster values confirmed.

bio.quote: 參鹿門覺禪師，問：「如何是盡乾坤，是學人一隻眼？」覺曰：「汝被一卷經遮却也。」師擬對，覺搖手曰：「不快漆桶去！」師於言下有省，即承印可。

notes: Dharma heir of Lumen Zijue. Continued Furong Daokai's Caodong line in the Jin-controlled north while the southern branch (Danxia Zichun to Hongzhi) flourished under the Song.

bio: Of Tanzhou, surname Pan. An heir of Dawei Shanguo in the Yangqi line of Linji.

teacher.quote: 大溈果禪師法嗣，潭州人，姓潘。（T51n2077_p0695b17、p0698c11）
teacher.note: teacher 大溈善果 (善果) confirmed.

teacher.quote: 大溈果禪師法嗣，潭州人，姓潘。（T51n2077_p0695b17、T51n2077_p0698c11）— TEACHER: 善果 (A001334)
teacher.note: DILA names the teacher 善果, i.e. 月庵善果 (also styled 大溈善果). Roster's 'Yue'an Shanguo' is CONFIRMED.

notes: Also known as Dahong Zuzheng. Song dynasty Yangqi-line master. Teacher of Yuelin Shiguan.

bio: Second master of Suseonsa (Songgwangsa) after Jinul, and second of its sixteen National Teachers. Of Hwasun county in Naju, surname Choe, personal name Sik, zi Yeong-eul, self-styled 'the Man Without Robes' (無衣子). A literatus who abandoned an official career for the robe. He compiled the Seonmun Yeomsong (禪門拈頌集) in thirty fascicles, the first great Korean kongan collection. Though he never sat the monastic examinations, King Gojong appointed him Seon Master and then Great Seon Master — the first man so promoted without the examination.

steles.title: 真覺國師碑銘 (as transmitted in 朝鮮佛教通史)
steles.author_note: The 碑 text is quoted at length in 朝鮮佛教通史; I did not recover the named author from the corpus.
steles.quote: 國師諱慧諶。字永乙。自號無衣子。俗姓崔氏。名寔。羅州和順縣人也。考諱琬。鄉貢進士。母裴氏。夢天門豁開。又夢被震者三。因而有娠。
steles.note: Stele-derived biography preserved in 朝鮮佛教通史 (B31n0170), the Korean stele compendium.

teacher.quote: 曹溪山第二世真覺國師。法諱慧諶。號無衣子。輯述禪門拈頌集三十卷。
teacher.note: Placed as SECOND of Suseonsa, i.e. Jinul's successor. Jinul is named in the same passage as the founder who 「無所稟承。而從六祖壇經。及大慧書狀。獨自悟入」. Roster teacher CONFIRMED.

bio.kind: 碑銘 quoted in 朝鮮佛教通史

bio.quote: 沙門慧諶。真覺國師號無衣子雖不經選。道行甚高。高宗即位。制授禪師又加大禪師。不經選席。直登緇秩。自師始也。

notes: Jinul's foremost disciple and second master of Songgwangsa. He compiled a collection of 1,125 kongan (koans) titled the Seonmun yeomsong seolhwa (Seon Verses and Commentaries), the first indigenous Korean koan anthology. This monumental work, completed in thirty fascicles, selected cases from Chinese Chan collections and added Korean commentary, establishing an independent Korean Seon literary tradition distinct from mere importation of Chinese texts. He also expanded Songgwangsa's monastic community and received the posthumous title 'National Teacher' (guksa). His koan collection remained central to Korean Seon training for centuries. Attested in Korean Buddhist historical records: the Seonmun yeomsong seolhwa is the earliest known indigenous koan anthology in East Asian Buddhism outside China.

teacher: Cheonyeong 天英 = 圓悟國師
bio: Sixth National Teacher of Suseonsa (Songgwangsa). He entered the order at twenty-nine under Wono Cheonyeong, the fifth National Teacher, and succeeded him as head of Suseonsa. He stayed at Sangmujuam c. 1284-1286 before taking the seat. Died 1293.

steles.title: 圓鑑國師碑銘
steles.author_note: Not recovered.
steles.quote: 조계산수선사 제6세 원감국사
steles.note: EncyKorea reports that the 圓鑑國師碑銘 itself records him as 'sixth-generation National Teacher of Suseonsa of Mt. Jogye'. That stele exists but I did not locate its text; the quote is EncyKorea's report of the stele's wording, not the stele read directly.

steles.title: 曹溪山修禪社第六世圓鑑國師碑銘
steles.author: 金鳴 (奉祿大夫國學典司成文翰學士承旨臣金鳴, 奉教撰)
steles.quote: 國師諱法桓，後改為冲止，自號安庵，俗姓魏氏，定安人也。考諱紹，戶部員外郎…十九登壯元弟，奉使日域…年四十一，始住金海縣甘露社。
steles.note: A full royal-command stele, in 朝鮮佛教通史 (B31n0170) exactly as the brief predicted. Confirms the Korean chain: he was a top-of-the-class civil examinee and envoy to Japan before ordaining.

teacher.kind: his own stele — 曹溪山修禪社第六世圓鑑國師碑銘(并序), by 金鳴, 奉教撰 (by royal command)
teacher.quote: 時圓悟國師主法於禪源社，師造堂，即零染受具…丙戌二月圓悟順世，大眾舉師次繼席…入院開堂，而嗣圓悟為第六世住院。
teacher.note: 嗣圓悟 — the transmission verb, in his own stele. 丙戌 = 1286, which is exactly the death-year of 天英. 圓悟國師 IS 天英: the roster's teacher, under his 國師 title. The teacher is confirmed, and the stele also independently dates him (died 癸巳/1293, 壽六十七, 臘三十九; 諡 圓鑑國師, 塔曰寶明, 浮圖于曹溪北洞).

teacher.quote: 제5세 회당자진국사(晦堂慈眞國師) 천영(天英, 1215∼1286) … 제6세 원감국사, 충지
teacher.note: Places Chungji directly after Cheonyeong in the sixteen-master succession of Songgwangsa. Roster teacher 'Cheonyeong' CONFIRMED, and the roster's own note that he is the 6th (not 7th) is CONFIRMED.

dates.quote: 제6세 원감국사, 충지
dates.note: The succession page confirms his position; the years 1226-1293 are the standard Korean scholarly dates. I did NOT find a primary attestation of the birth year.

notes: 6th National Teacher of Suseonsa (originally numbered 7th; numbering corrected per CBETA sources).

bio: Of Yeonghae-bu, Goryeo, surname A; originally named Wonhye. At twenty a friend's death sent him to Mt. Gongdeok, where Yoyeon tonsured him. He awakened at Hoeamsa in 1344, went to Yuan China in 1348, lodged at Fayuan monastery in Dadu, and studied two years under the Indian master Śūnyadiśya (指空). He then received transmission from Pingshan Chulin at Jingci monastery, and afterwards received transmission from Śūnyadiśya as well — two lineages, deliberately held. He was ordered to head Guangji monastery in Dadu, returned to Korea in 1358, and held Sangdu-am, Singwangsa, Cheongpyeongsa and Hoeamsa. Died 1376 aged 57. His heirs include Muhak Jacho.

steles.title: 普濟尊者諡禪覺塔銘 (并序)
steles.author: 李穡 (Yi Saek, 牧隱), 奉教撰 — by royal command
steles.quote: 普濟尊者諡禪覺塔銘（并序。李穡奉教撰）玄陵在位之二十年庚戌秋九月十日。召師入京。
steles.note: The 行狀 (門人覺宏錄) begins at lb 0519a13 and runs to lb 0521 — it is the fuller document and is the one I have quoted for the transmission.

teacher.kind: 〈懶翁和尚行狀〉 by his own disciple 覺宏 (門人覺宏錄) — quoting 平山處林's OWN written charge
teacher.quote: 一日。手書囑云。三韓慧首座。來見老僧。其出言吐氣。便與佛祖相合。宗眼明白。見處高峻。言中有響。句裏藏鋒。茲以雪菴所傳及菴先師法衣一領拂子一枝付囑表信。作偈曰。拂子法衣今付囑。石中取出無瑕玉。六根永淨得菩提。禪定慧光皆具足。
teacher.note: THE CHARGE ITSELF, IN THE TEACHER'S OWN HAND. 平山 hands over the DHARMA ROBE and WHISK — physical tokens he traces to 及菴先師 (及菴宗信) via 雪菴 — with 手書囑 and 付囑 twice, and 表信 (as the token of trust). This is the 囑 verb the brief names as transmission, in a document written by the master and preserved by the disciple's disciple. Dated: he arrives 淨慈 in the 8th month of 1358 (0519b22), receives the robe, and takes leave 十一年辛卯二月初二日 (1361).

teacher.kind: institutional act by his own heir 無學自超, 1394
teacher.quote: 王師妙嚴尊者。以其先師指空懶翁掛真塔名祖派等事。奏奉王旨。 … 六月二十五日。錄載祖派于平山處林禪師之下。重刊佛祖宗派之圖。留板于難陀寺。
teacher.note: In 1394 懶翁's dharma-heir 無學自超 petitioned the throne and formally REGISTERED THE KOREAN LINE UNDER 平山處林, recutting the 佛祖宗派之圖 and depositing the blocks at 難陀寺. The closest possible party, acting officially, filed the line under Pingshan — not under 指空.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 處林 (A016698) — 《東國僧尼錄》卷1：「秋八月參平山。」(X88, no. 1671, p. 646, c9)
teacher.note: Roster teacher CONFIRMED. But see the note below: DILA's own extensive bio records him as heir of BOTH 平山處林 AND 指空 (Śūnyadiśya). The roster records only Pingshan. Both are real; the double transmission is the point of the man.

teacher.quote: 為平山處林禪師（1279-1361）及印度指空禪師法嗣 … 後投指空禪師門下，從學兩年。再至淨慈寺參平山處林禪師，得付法。再參千岩禪師，復參指空禪師，亦得付法。
teacher.note: SECOND TEACHER: 指空 (Śūnyadiśya). Recorded, not silently dropped.

dates.quote: 「以延祐庚申生。」（《東國僧尼錄》卷1）… 洪武丙辰五月十五日示寂，世壽五十七
dates.note: 延祐庚申 = 1320; 洪武丙辰 = 1376, aged 57. Both roster values CONFIRMED, and anchored to 東國僧尼錄, which is in the corpus at X/X88/X88n1671.xml.

school.quote: 臨濟宗 楊岐派 / 高麗

notes: One of the most celebrated Korean Seon masters of the late Goryeo dynasty, remarkable for having received dharma transmission from two masters of entirely different lineages. He first studied under the Indian monk Zhigong (Dhyanabhadra, d. 1363), who had come to Yuan China and gave Naong transmission in an Indian-derived lineage. He then received a second transmission from the Chinese Linji master Pingshan Chulin, a heir in the mainstream Yangqi-Linji line. This double transmission from both Indian and Chinese sources gave Naong unique authority. He became Royal Teacher (wangsa) and initiated major reforms of Korean Seon before his sudden death. Attested in Korean Buddhist records and Chinese Chan genealogies: both transmissions are documented, with his Indian lineage through Zhigong preserved in Goryeo-era inscriptions.

bio: Dharma name Jieom, sobriquet Yaro; his hall was called Byeoksong ('green pine'), whence his name. Of Buan, surname Song; his father was Boksaeng. He first studied under Gugok and it did not take (初叅龜谷不契); only later did he enter the house of Byeokgye Jeongsim. He was chosen to head Seon affairs at a moment when Seon in Joseon was, in his biographer's words, 'as sparse as morning stars', and is credited with holding the line. Died on the first day of the eleventh month of 1534.

steles.title: 碧松堂埜老行錄
steles.author_note: Author not named in the passage as transmitted.
steles.quote: 【備考】碧松堂埜老行錄云。大師法諱智嚴。號埜老。所居堂曰碧松。俗姓宋氏。父曰福生。扶安人也。母王氏。夢一梵僧。設禮寄宿。因以有娠。
steles.note: His 行錄 — the record of deeds — quoted in 朝鮮佛教通史 as a 備考 (supporting citation).

teacher.kind: 朝鮮佛教通史 (quoting his 行錄)
teacher.quote: 初叅龜谷不契。晚入登階。（碧溪正心）之家。
teacher.note: DECISIVE, and a textbook case of the audit's central error. He went FIRST to 龜谷 and it did not take; he entered 碧溪正心's house LATER. The roster names the transmitter, 碧溪正心 — CORRECT. Anyone reading 'association' as 'transmission' would have written 龜谷 here.

teacher.kind: lineage table in 朝鮮佛教通史
teacher.quote: 龜谷覺雲…碧松智嚴…碧溪正心…

dates.quote: 甲午二十九年明嘉靖十三年佛紀二五六一年十一月初一日。沙門智嚴入寂。
dates.note: 嘉靖十三年 = 1534, eleventh month, first day. Roster death 1534 CONFIRMED. Birth is NOT given — roster's 1464 is unsourced.

notes: Maintained Seon transmission during severe Joseon suppression. Name ('Green Pine') suggests mountain hermit life.

bio: Of Renhe (Hangzhou), surname Shen, zi Fohui, hao Lianchi. A licentiate at seventeen who kept the words 'the matter of birth-and-death is great' on his desk. Tonsured in 1566 by Wumen Xingtian and ordained under Wuchen at Zhaoqing. He travelled north to Bianrong and called on Xiaoyan Debao at Liuxiang; on the road home at Dongchang the sound of a watchtower drum brought him through. In 1571 he entered Mt. Yunqi and settled a derelict temple there. He argued hard for the joint cultivation of Chan and Pure Land and attacked 'wild Chan'. Died 1615 aged 81. Counted one of the four eminent monks of the Ming.

steles.title: 古杭雲棲蓮池大師塔銘
steles.author: 釋德清 (憨山德清) — contemporary
steles.quote: 參遍融、笑巖二大老，皆有開發。過東昌，忽有悟
steles.note: The primary witness. Contains no transmission verb.

steles.title: 蓮宗八祖杭州古雲棲寺中興尊宿蓮池大師塔銘并序
steles.author: (second stele, appended in 雲棲法彙)
steles.quote: 蓮宗八祖…自稱蓮池比丘
steles.note: Frames him as a Pure Land patriarch.

teacher.kind: his 塔銘 — 《古杭雲棲蓮池大師塔銘》 by 釋德清 (憨山德清), a contemporary
teacher.quote: 竟投西山無門洞性天理和尚祝髮，乞昭慶寺無塵玉律師就壇受具。…入京師，參遍融、笑巖二大老，皆有開發。過東昌，忽有悟，作偈曰：「二十年前事可疑，三千里外遇何奇。焚香擲戟渾如夢，魔佛空爭是與非。」
teacher.note: THE STELE KEEPS THE ROLES APART, exactly as 東明慧旵's does. 性天理 TONSURED him (祝髮). 無塵玉律師 ORDAINED him (受具). 遍融 and 笑巖 he merely 參'd — 「皆有開發」, both OPENED something in him — and 參 + 開發 are precisely the non-transmission verbs. His actual awakening (忽有悟) came LATER, ALONE, on the road at 東昌 — not under 笑巖. The transmission slot in this stele is EMPTY.

teacher.kind: negative evidence — verb sweep of the entire stele
teacher.quote: (zero occurrences)
teacher.note: I swept the whole stele region for 嗣法 / 得法 / 付法 / 印可 / 傳法 / 法嗣 / 嗣. NOT ONE OCCURRENCE. A stele that carefully names his tonsure master AND his ordination master AND two elders he visited never once uses a transmission verb — because there was no transmission to record.

teacher.kind: his SECOND stele, 《蓮宗八祖杭州古雲棲寺中興尊宿蓮池大師塔銘并序》
teacher.quote: 蓮宗八祖杭州古雲棲寺中興尊宿蓮池大師塔銘并序…師法諱袾宏，字曰佛慧，自稱蓮池比丘…於是南五臺性天理和尚有菩薩戒弟子矣。
teacher.note: A second, independent stele — and it frames him as 蓮宗八祖, EIGHTH PATRIARCH OF THE PURE LAND (Lotus) SCHOOL, not as a Chan dharma-heir. It too routes him to 性天理 (bodhisattva-precepts/tonsure), never to 笑巖.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 德寶 (A001697) — 《續燈正統》卷41：「謁笑巖於柳巷」 (X84n1583_p0645a10)
teacher.note: This is the roster's teacher, and it IS what DILA records — but the citation is weak: 「謁」 means he CALLED ON Xiaoyan, not that Xiaoyan transmitted to him. This is exactly the association-vs-transmission slippage the audit found elsewhere.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 徧融 (A009553)（望月‧卷六‧附錄：030）
teacher.note: SECOND teacher recorded by DILA. Recorded, not dropped.

dates.quote: 「（萬曆四十三年）至七月初四日果示微疾，面西而逝，世壽八十有一。」（《五燈嚴統》卷16）
dates.note: Death 1615 aged 81 gives birth 1535. Both roster values confirmed.

bio.quote: 嘉靖丙寅（1566）依無門性天和尚薙染，至昭慶無塵律師處受具戒。北遊參徧融禪師，後謁笑巖禪師於柳巷。辭歸，過東昌，道中聞譙樓鼓聲，忽悟。

notes: One of the 'four great monks'. Leading advocate of Chan-Pure Land synthesis.

bio: Of Jiaxing, surname Hu — one of the very few women to hold a Linji lineage in her own right. She came late: she called on a teacher at twenty-six, went to Jinsu at thirty-three, lost her mother at thirty-four and resolved on the robe, was tonsured at thirty-five and took full ordination at Jinsu. Under Shiche Tongcheng she was set to work on her original face and driven so hard that she vomited blood repeatedly without stopping; the break came one day as she shaved her head. She received Shiche's charge in the second month of 1638, aged forty-two, then withdrew to Hu'an before opening the Fushi (Crouching Lion) Chan cloister at Meixi. Died 1654 aged 58. She left seven dharma heirs.

steles.title: 伏獅袛園剛禪師行狀
steles.author_note: Author not recovered; the 行狀 and a 塔銘 both travel with her 語錄.
steles.quote: 順治甲午九月廿七日寅時，世壽五十八。
steles.note: Both a 行狀 AND a 塔銘 are appended to 《伏獅祇園禪師語錄》 juan 2 (per DILA, which cites them by name for her dates and her transmission). A stele for a woman Chan master is rare. I cite DILA's quotation of them; I did not open the 語錄 file itself, as it is not among the texts flagged in my batch.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 通乘 (A016036) — 為石車通乘禪師（1593-1638）法嗣（J39nB435_p0004c08）
teacher.note: Roster teacher CONFIRMED.

teacher.source: 《伏獅祇園禪師語錄》卷2〈行狀〉 (quoted via DILA A018946)
teacher.quote: 崇禎戊寅（1638）二月初四受乘付囑，時年四十二。
teacher.note: The transmission is dated in the 行狀 itself.

dates.source: 《伏獅祇園禪師語錄》卷2〈行狀〉 (quoted via DILA A018946)
dates.quote: 順治甲午九月廿七日寅時，世壽五十八。
dates.note: = 1654-11-05, aged 58, giving birth 1597. Both roster values confirmed at stele rung.

bio.source: 《伏獅祇園禪師語錄》卷2〈行狀〉 (quoted via DILA A018946)

links.label: DILA Authority A018946
links.confirms: teacher, dates, school, 行狀+塔銘

notes: One of the most prominent female Chan masters in Chinese history. A Linji heir of Shiche Tongcheng, she became abbess of Crouching Lion (Fuwo) Chan Monastery, which flourished under her leadership. She left seven female dharma heirs, and her recorded sayings and poems survive in full.

bio: Dharma name Seolje; of Changhwa stock, descended from Kim Bu; his father was Tae-in, his mother of the Cheongju Han clan. Born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month of 1632. He carried the Pyeonyang line — the succession running Cheongheo (Seosan) to Pyeonyang Eongi to Pungdam, and 'of these it was the Seon master Woldam who obtained the essential'. Died on the fourth day of the first month of 1704.

steles.title: 月潭堂雪霽大師碑銘并序
steles.author: 姜鋧
steles.author_note: 大提學 (Grand Academician), hao 白閣 — a senior Joseon court official
steles.quote: 【備考】月潭堂雪霽大師碑銘并序 大提學姜鋧號白閣撰。… 其狀曰。師法諱雪霽。其本昌化。其系金傅後裔。其父嘉善太仁。其母清州韓氏。崇禎壬申十二月十五日。師肇錫之辰也。
steles.note: A named Grand Academician writing at a named grave. Preserved in 朝鮮佛教通史. This is the strongest single source in my Korean set.

teacher.kind: 碑銘 (月潭堂雪霽大師碑銘, 姜鋧撰)
teacher.quote: 若清虛。鞭羊上人。踵得三昧。傳于楓潭大師。說經談玄。清眾四至。而惟月潭禪師。得其宗云。
teacher.note: The stele traces Cheongheo (清虛/西山) -> Pyeonyang (鞭羊) -> Pungdam (楓潭) -> and says that of Pungdam's people it was Woldam alone who 'got his essential teaching'. Roster teacher 'Pungdam Uisim' CONFIRMED at stele rung.

dates.quote: 崇禎壬申十二月十五日。師肇錫之辰也。
dates.note: 崇禎壬申 = 1632. Birth CONFIRMED (roster floruit 1632 is in fact his BIRTH year).

dates.quote: 甲申三十年清康熙四十三年正月初四日。沙門雪霽入寂。
dates.note: 康熙四十三年 = 1704. Roster death CONFIRMED.

notes: Bridged 17th into 18th century. Maintained the Pyeonyang lineage through deepening Joseon suppression.

bio: A mid-eighteenth-century Korean Seon master, attested in the corpus only through a disciple's account: a younger monk, having been tonsured in 1756 and having taken Seon from Hwanam Takgye, 'then went to Cheongbong Geoan for instruction', and Geoan told him — approvingly — 'I expound dead phrases; you throw yourself at the live phrase.' Beyond this the record is silent.

teacher.quote: 청봉스님은 호암체정(1687~1748)을 스승으로 모셨으며, 그 법맥은 율봉청고(1738~1823)로 이어진다. (진영은 불갑사에 봉안)
teacher.note: TAKEN, but only external. His teacher is Hoam Chejeong 虎巖體淨 (1687-1748); his dharma-uncle was Hamwol Haewon. The roster had teacher=null — this FILLS it. ⚠ external rung only: I could not find the teacher-edge in the CBETA corpus itself.

teacher.kind: 朝鮮佛教通史 — inside 栗峰靑杲's stele (Cheongbong as the PUPIL's teacher)
teacher.quote: 受禪於喚菴卓戒禪師，而遂請益於青峯巨岸大師…岸老歎曰：余講死句，子投活句，可謂茜絳藍青者此也，遂傳心印焉。
teacher.note: This proves Cheongbong TAUGHT 栗峰靑杲 (遂傳心印) — a downstream edge, stone-attested. It does NOT name Cheongbong's OWN teacher, which is why that edge stays external.

bio.kind: 朝鮮佛教通史 (in a disciple's biography)
bio.quote: 十九。乾隆二十一年投無垢大俊禪師得度。明年乞具於雲月淑敏大師。受禪於喚菴卓戒禪師。而遂請益於青峯巨岸大師。三藏奧義非不精通。惟雜華玄旨。最善游刃。不離言教。深悟別傳。岸老歎曰。余講死句。子投活句。可謂茜絳藍青者此也。
bio.note: This is the ONLY appearance of 巨岸 in the entire corpus (one hit in B31n0170), and it is inside someone ELSE's biography. It tells us he was alive and teaching after 1756 and was esteemed enough to be consulted. It tells us nothing about his own teacher or his dates.

notes: Mid-18th century Seon master in the Pyeonyang lineage. One of the few masters in the Hwanseong-to-Gyeongheo chain with attested dates (1710-1793). The 69th Korean patriarch. Carried the lineage through the deepest period of Joseon Neo-Confucian suppression of Buddhism.

bio: Of Songshan in Huangyan, Taizhou, surname Xu; hao Duanqiao, also Songshanzi. Born the seventeenth day of the eighth month of 1201. At eighteen he was tonsured by his own uncle, the doctrinal master Zongsi of Guangci cloister in Yongjia. He first met Guyuan Dao at Ruiyan, where the 'three pounds of flax' and 'dried shit-stick' cases raised a doubt that stuck in his chest. Told by a monk that if he broke through a single phrase it would beat reciting ten thousand scrolls of the Lotus, he dropped the sutra and took up 'the cypress in the courtyard', going without sleep or food 'as though sitting in a thicket of thorns'. He went to Wuzhun Shifan at Xuedou, failed thirty turning-words on the dog-and-karmic-consciousness case, and broke through on hearing the sounding-board. He headed Qiyuan, Ruiyan and Guoqing, and in 1256 was ordered to Jingci in Hangzhou. Died 1261 aged 61. He gave Gaofeng Yuanmiao his huatou.

steles.title: 斷橋和尚語錄〈行狀〉
steles.author_note: Anonymous in the text as transmitted; the 語錄 was edited by his attendants 文寶 and 善靖.
steles.quote: 行狀 師諱妙倫，號斷橋，台州黃巖松山人也，又號松山子，姓徐。母劉氏，夢空中月明，已而有娠，嘉泰辛酉八月十七日乃生。眉目秀異，性姿冲朴，絕不樂世間學。年十八，依永嘉廣慈院宗嗣論師出家，乃俗季父也，即剃髮投禮。
steles.note: Full 行狀, appended to his own 語錄 (X70n1394, marked No.1394-B). A 塔銘 also appears in the same file.

steles.title: 斷橋倫禪師塔銘 (quoted)
steles.quote: 嘗撰斷橋倫禪師塔銘曰
steles.note: A 塔銘 for him existed and is quoted elsewhere in the corpus; the full text sits in X70n1394.

teacher.quote: 還謁無準於雪竇，準以狗子因何有業識令師下語，凡三十轉不契，即竦然良久，忽聞板聲通身汗下於是始脫然矣。
teacher.note: Quoted via DILA's transcription of the 行狀. Roster teacher CONFIRMED at stele rung.

teacher.quote: TEACHER: 師範 (A004697)

dates.quote: 嘉泰辛酉八月十七日乃生 … 景定二年四月二十五日，壽六十一
dates.note: = 1201-09-22 to 1261-06-01, aged 61. Both roster values CONFIRMED at stele rung.

notes: Dharma heir of Wuzhun Shifan who served as abbot at Jingci Temple in Hangzhou, one of the Five Mountains monasteries. He gave Gaofeng Yuanmiao two of his most important huatou, including 'The myriad dharmas return to one - where does the one return to?' which triggered Gaofeng's awakening in a dream. While Gaofeng formally received transmission from Xueyan Zuqin (Duanqiao's dharma brother), Duanqiao's direct role in shaping Gaofeng's practice was indispensable.

bio: Listed in the Jingde Chuandeng Lu among the thirteen collateral heirs of the fifth patriarch Hongren, alongside Shenxiu and Mengshan Daoming. He later taught at Mt. Song and is counted a National Teacher. His own heirs number eighteen in the lamp, including Songyue Pozaoduo and Songyue Yuangui.

steles.title: 嵩山會善寺故大德道安禪師碑銘
steles.author: 宋儋 (撰兼書)
steles.path: 全唐文 卷396 (not in the CBETA corpus; the corpus preserves only descriptions of the stone)
steles.quote: （上闕）祐所（闕）識曠劫誰比次有（闕）大禪師乎？禪師法諱道安…
steles.note: Cut 開元十五年 (727), 18-21 years after his death. Survives only in a fragmentary state (heavy 闕). Verified by fetching 全唐文/卷0396 on zh.wikisource. The stone itself still stood at Songshan in the Ming, southwest of the ordination platform.

teacher.quote: 旁出一百七人 第一世一十三人：北宗神秀禪師、嵩嶽慧安國師、袁州蒙山道明禪師。已上三人見錄。
